title: Kirk Cousins: Brock Bowers is like Justin Jefferson, when he's covered, you still need to throw it
summary: Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has played with his share of big-time pass catchers throughout his 15-year career.
full_text: Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has played with his share of big-time pass catchers throughout his 15-year career. He’s now connecting with Brock Bowers on a weekly basis, with Bowers catching seven passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday’s 38-33 victory over the Jets. But even though Bowers is technically a tight end, Cousins related throwing to him to passing to an elite wide receiver. “I think what’s hard is when you play with Pierre Garçon, DeSean Jackson, or Justin Jefferson, you’re used to throwing to guys who are really open,” Cousins said in his postgame press conference. "There were times, even when they would get doubled and I would progress off of them, and [Vikings head coach] Kevin O’Connell would say to me, ‘Still throw it to Justin when he’s covered.’ I was like, ‘I don’t like throwing to covered guys. I like throwing to open guys.’ “The coaching point with Brock has been like it was with Justin, where it’s like, when he’s covered, you still need to throw it. That kind of breaks my instincts. My instincts are to progress and throw to open guys. I think you can see there are moments this year where I can be better, and then there are moments where I’m starting to figure that out. He’s made me right, if you will.” That coaching point sure seemed relevant for Cousins’ first touchdown of the game, when Bowers was covered and interfered with, but still managed to catch the ball for a 12-yard score. Through six games this season, Bowers has 41 receptions for 547 yards with five touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Von Miller defends Cowboys' coaching staff
summary: Cowboys linebacker Von Miller got his first sack in eight games with the team during Sunday's mind-boggling home loss to the Cardinals.
full_text: Cowboys linebacker Von Miller got his first sack in eight games with the team during Sunday's mind-boggling home loss to the Cardinals. After the 33-30 overtime defeat, Miller went to bat for the coaching staff. “I’m a parent," Miller said, via Jon Machota of The Athletic . "I got three kids. Sometimes you raise your kids a certain way and you teach them lessons. You expect them to act a certain way when they go out. “And sometimes the kids just go out there and do things that are not a reflection of who you are as a parent. And I use that reference for our coaching staff. We have amazing coaches that keep us prepared, ready to go mentally, physically, emotionally. They breathe life into us, and just for whatever reason, that’s the product. “The product that went out there is not a reflection of our coaching staff. This is pro sports. This is not parenting. So at the end of the day, the buck has to stop somewhere. Somebody’s going to get the blame. “But my opinion, this is just me, I don’t know nothing about football. I only played 16 years. We’ve got great coaches. We’ve got a great coaching staff. And that’s not a reflection of how they coach us and get us ready every week.” Miller's metaphor has obvious limits. For starters, it's a lot harder to disown a child than it is to bench or cut a player. If players aren't doing what they're supposed to be doing, the team needs better players. Or it needs a better General Manager. Which won't happen, because Jerry Jones continues to do the job he hired himself to do in 1989. As it relates to coaching, the fact that the players aren't performing the way they're supposed to shows that the coaching isn't working. If a coach tells the players "this is what you should do" and they don't do it, it's absolutely a reflection of the coach's inability to get the players to respond to the coaching. For any great coach in any sport, the quality of the strategies hinges on the willingness and the ability of the players to do what they are told to do. The coach's job includes not only drawing up the plays but getting the players to implement them as designed. It's that simple. And, no, it's not parenting. Parents love their children unconditionally. A coach's love is conditioned on the player doing what the player is expected to do. When the player can't (for whatever reason) or won't, the coach needs to pivot to a different player. So if the Cowboys' 3-5 record doesn't land on the shoulders of the coaching staff, where should it go? And if it goes to the overall quality of the roster, isn't the general "indictment of the whole show" (as Jones said Sunday) a specific indictment of it ringleader? If the Cowboys have the right coaches and the wrong players, it means they have the wrong G.M. And since the owner is the G.M., the cycle will continue. Offseason hype, in-season collapse. Lather, rinse, repeat. And as long as the fans keep falling for it, it will continue — year after year after year. The common denominator since the team's most recent NFC Championship appearance is the G.M. who, if he wasn't the owner, would have been fired four or five times since 1995.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Glenn says Jets aren't trading Breece Hall
summary: Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game with a quad injury on Sunday and Braelon Allen continued to shine in his absence.
full_text: Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game with a quad injury on Sunday and Braelon Allen continued to shine in his absence. Allen ran 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in the 38-33 loss to the Raiders and he's averaging just over 100 yards a game while Hall has been out of the lineup. Hall has practiced the last two weeks and he's been scratched after being listed as questionable, which has joined Allen's performance as reasons for some to wonder if the Jets might be thinking about trading Hall ahead of the November 10 deadline. At a Monday morning press conference, head coach Aaron Glenn said that will not happen. "Breece is still a part of this team ," Glenn said, via Zack Rosenblatt of TheAthletic.com. "I've said it before: We're in the business of keeping good players and he's one of our better players so he'll be here." The Jets have also reportedly rebuffed overtures from teams interested in trading for wide receiver Garrett Wilson, so it does not appear that their 2-6 start is going to lead to a fire sale over the next week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Garrett Wilson: We have to give our fans a reason to come out
summary: If someone flipped on Sunday's game between the Raiders and the Jets in the fourth quarter, they would have been forgiven for wondering if the Raiders were the home team at MetLife Stadium.
full_text: If someone flipped on Sunday's game between the Raiders and the Jets in the fourth quarter, they would have been forgiven for wondering if the Raiders were the home team at MetLife Stadium. Raiders fans were loud enough in big moments of the game to contribute to a Jets false start and the interception by Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn to seal the 38-33 win was greeted with lusty cheers by those same fans. The loss dropped the Jets to 2-6 on the season and wide receiver Garrett Wilson said after the game that it is up to the Jets to do more to convince their own fans to make that kind of an impact. “They had some fans in the building," Wilson said, via SNY. "We gotta handle it. . . . We got to give our fans a reason to come out. I get it. As a team we got to operate better, regardless of the noise.” The Jets are on their way to a 16th straight season without a trip to the playoffs and that run of futility makes it more surprising that they still have enough supporters turning out on Sundays to make it a surprise when the visiting side dominates the stands.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Bucs LB Yaya Diaby believed to have an MCL sprain
summary: The Buccaneers shut out the Falcons in Sunday's win, but their defense lost a starter to injury on the way to victory.
full_text: The Buccaneers shut out the Falcons in Sunday's win, but their defense lost a starter to injury on the way to victory. Linebacker Yaya Diaby left the game with a knee injury. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Diaby is believed to have a sprained MCL and he is set to have an MRI to provide further clarity on the extent of the injury. That testing will also provide a better idea of when Diaby is able to return to the lineup. Diaby was limited to seven snaps against Atlanta. Diaby did not land on the stat sheet during his brief time in Sunday's game, but he has 16 tackles, three sacks and an interception over the course of the entire season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Burrow: We found a way to win, we didn't do that the last few years
summary: The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they're ready to start playing football this season.
full_text: The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they're ready to start playing football this season. The Bengals spotted the Ravens that lead in the first half of Week 7 before rallying for a 35-13 win and they found themselves down 13-0 in the first quarter against the Titans this Sunday. They didn't wait until the second half to get their act together this week, but they had to struggle the whole way before finally nailing down a 43-36 overtime win. Burrow and others fielded questions about their slow starts in their postgame press conferences, but Burrow was more interested in the final scores because he feels that scrapping out wins like their last two are a sign that the team has fixed part of what has ailed them the last few years. "We found a way to win today. We're 5-2," Burrow said, via a transcript from the team. "We lose that game for the last three years. It's hard to win. You want to be great snap in snap out, but it's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and get better. You win from wins and losses and good plays and bad plays. That's what the NFL and getting better is. We'll continue to do that." Burrow threw three interceptions to go with five touchdown passes and his game-winning touchdown run on Sunday. He acknowledged the need to "be better and limit those critical mistakes," but returned often to the theme of finding ways to win when they would have fallen apart in the past.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson with right thumb injury
summary: Tyler Huntley has replcaed Jackson.
full_text: ' The Ravens have ruled out Lamar Jackson. The question is: How bad is his right thumb injury? Jackson started for the first time since Oct. 4, missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain, but he lasted one play against the Bills. The Ravens quarterback got hit on an incompletion intended for Zay Flowers and immediately left the field. The team’s medical staff took him to the X-ray room. Tyler Huntley, who was 1-2 in Jackson's absence, replaced him. He is 2-for-3 for no yards. The Bills lead 10-7 after a Josh Allen pass intended for tight end Jackson Hawes was batted into the air by Hawes and defensive lineman Broderick Washington intercepted it at the Buffalo 17. The Ravens scored on Derrick Henry's 2-yard run. Henry is only the third player in NFL history to record 40 or more rushing touchdowns with two different franchises.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaylen Warren rushes for 143 on his birthday, Steelers beat Browns 27-6
summary: The streak continues for the Steelers and Browns in Pittsburgh.
full_text: The streak continues for the Steelers and Browns in Pittsburgh. With both teams entering the contest at 5-2, Pittsburgh ran all over Cleveland to come away with a dominant 27-6 victory. The Steelers took control of the game in the first half and never really let it go, using a punishing running attack. The club had 160 yards on the ground in the first half, finishing with 201 yards in the category for the game. On his 28th birthday, Jaylen Warren led the way with 143 yards on 17 carries with a touchdown — including a 51-yard scamper. Rico Dowdle was plenty effective, too, rushing for 56 yards on 15 carries. Pat Freiermuth got into the ground game with a 1-yard tush push touchdown at the end of the first half. Aaron Rodgers wasn’t asked to do too much and did not need to, ending the game 13-of-25 for 172 yards with an interception. The pick went right off of DK Metcalf’s hands before Denzel Ward came away with it. Big tight end Darnell Washington led with three catches for 94 yards. For Cleveland, Deshaun Watson passed for over 300 yards for a second consecutive game. But he was largely stymied by the Pittsburgh defense, which produced a strip-sack on him in the first quarter that led to a touchdown. Watson finished the contest 27-of-39 for 324 yards. He was sacked eight times. Harold Fannin led with 154 yards on 10 catches. The Browns still have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003. At 6-2, the Steelers will be on their bye in Week 9. The 5-3 Browns will be on the road to face the Saints next Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cowboys had never blown a 14-point, fourth-quarter lead at home before Sunday
summary: A third-party contractor yelled "embarrassing" to Dak Prescott as he walked back to the Cowboys' locker room after a 24-16 loss to the Bucs in Week 5.
full_text: '' A third-party contractor yelled " embarrassing " to Dak Prescott as he walked back to the Cowboys' locker room after a 24-16 loss to the Bucs in Week 5. The Cowboys' 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals on Sunday was arguably worse. Before Sunday, the Cowboys were 202-0-1 when leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter at home in their history, including the postseason, according to ESPN. On Sunday, the Cowboys led 24-10 with 14:20 remaining in regulation. It matched the largest blown fourth-quarter lead in team history. In 2011 and 2022, the Cowboys blew fourth-quarter leads at the Jets and at the Packers, respectively. They are now 342-3-1 in franchise history when leading by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter. Owner Jerry Jones called in "an indictment of the whole show." "We had numerable chances to win this game and didn't do it," Jones said. "And I know everybody . . . is disappointed. We came out the second half and were a shadow of ourselves. So there's nothing to point to other than we just weren't a good team in the second half." The Cowboys became the first team in the NFL this season to lose when leading by at least 14 points in the fourth. Teams were 44-0-1 in that situation entering Sunday.
author: Charean Williams

title: The Vikings should explore a trade for Daniel Jones
summary: Kevin O'Connell's decision to punt with 3:01 to play speaks volumes about the level of trust in Kyler Murray.
full_text: At a time when the Vikings are believed to be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor, they should adjust their focal point, just a bit. The Vikings should be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for quarterback Daniel Jones. When the thought first popped into my somewhat relaxed brain on Sunday, I was mostly kidding. After reflecting on Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions — and revisiting the rare displays of frustration from receiver Justin Jefferson late in the game and, even more significantly, from coach Kevin O'Connell when talking to quarterback Kyler Murray after an ugly interception late in the first half — it's not a joke. They should immediately pivot from Taylor to Jones. The Vikings had Jones in the building two years ago, after he was released by the Giants. They wanted to keep him for 2025, more (by all appearances) than they wanted to keep Sam Darnold. (Indeed, there were whispers of a potential benching of Darnold for Jones in the 2024 postseason.) Now that the Colts are in full-blown pre-rebuild mode, trading Jones should be part of the effort to clear the decks (and stockpile picks) for the next G.M. And while the Colts have a window to avoid more than $10 million of Jones's $38 million compensation package for 2027 via a trade in the early days of the new league year in March, they could get more now from a contender that envisions Jones as an immediate upgrade. Jones obviously won't be the long-term answer in Indianapolis. And he would undoubtedly welcome the chance to move on from a team that prematurely threw in the towel last week by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. In Minnesota, Jones would be an immediate upgrade over Kyler Murray. The difference between Jones vs. Murray could be more significant than the difference between Jonathan Taylor and Aaron Jones/Jordan Mason. Which, if accurate, would result in a bigger overall bump to the offense. The Vikings have a championship-caliber defense, thanks in large part to the work of defensive coordinator Brian Flores. The grind-it-out-and-get-a-win formula had been working — until it didn't. Here's the inescapable reality. When they win with quarterback play that is inconsistent and, in turn, frustrating to people like Jefferson and O'Connell, it's easy to overlook the flaws and keep pushing forward. When they lose, the frustrations of that moment become compounded by the lingering frustrations regarding plays and points left on the field in the wins that were salvaged by the defense. Whether it's Jones or someone else (including a possible pivot to Carson Wentz), O'Connell and G.M. Nolan Teasley need to conduct a frank, candid, and objective assessment of the quarterback play under Murray. The fact that they picked Murray over J.J. McCarthy shouldn't be a factor. That's the kind of pride/ego consideration that keeps dysfunctional teams dysfunctional by doubling down on a mistake instead of admitting it and moving on. The Vikings need to realize that: (1) the defense is great; (2) the running game is good enough; and (3) the passing game is too spotty to be expected to make a big play in a big spot. Consider the decision that O'Connell made with 3:01 to play on Sunday, when the Vikings faced fourth and five from their own 33. Down four points after the Detroit running game had hot-knife-through-buttered their way to the go-ahead touchdown, why give the ball back to the Lions and let them close out the game by continuing to lean on Jahmyr Gibbs? In that moment, O'Connell thought the chances of winning were enhanced by punting — not by asking the offense to gain five yards in a gotta-have-it situation. While the choice showed unwarranted confidence in the defense, it showed NO confidence in the quarterback. Frankly, that one specific decision from O'Connell leads naturally to the next, more consequential decision that the organization must make. If O'Connell doesn't trust the offense under Murray to gain five yards with the game on the line, the Vikings should no longer entrust the offense to Murray. It's that simple. And, if the Vikings hope to avoid an outcome to the season that will result in an every-other-year playoff appearance and another one-and-done postseason, they'll make the decision that someone other than Murray should be playing quarterback. At a time when politics have become a major national focal point, this would be a so-called 80-20 issue among Vikings fans. They've seen the "just good enough is just good enough" movie for decades. With the defense the Vikings currently have, the offense needs more. If they're serious about having a snowball's chance in San Diego to get back to the Super Bowl for the first time in 50 years, they'll send Kyler to Belize and make a play for Jones. Or someone else. See if the Raiders are willing to part with Kirk Cousins (they shouldn't be, but why not make the call?) Call the Chargers about Justin Herbert. Scour every depth chart and start doing the due diligence. When Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon just before the trade deadline in 2023, the Vikings mobilized instantly to find a replacement. Based on the full body of work from Murray to date in 2026, they should be doing the same thing now — if they want to parlay their 6-0 start into the best possible finish.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Brady: Sunday's performance is the expectation for our defense
summary: The Bills allowed an average of 28.5 points per game in their first six games of the 2026 season and improving on that was a focus for the team during their bye week.
full_text: '' The Bills allowed an average of 28.5 points per game in their first six games of the 2026 season and improving on that was a focus for the team during their bye week. Sunday's return to action resulted in much better numbers. They allowed the Ravens 144 yards in a 36-10 win that moved their record to 6-1 on the season. After the game was over, head coach Joe Brady said he wants the unit to look at that performance as their standard for the rest of the season. "I think our defense should look at today and understand that that’s what the expectation is," Brady said, via the team's website. "And I'm not talking about the production. I'm not talking about the takeaways and sacks. I'm talking about the style that they played, the way that they flew around. Look, I'm just watching it out there, but I think the silent tape's going to speak loudly in terms of the way that they played for one another, the way they ran around, the communication. Everything we challenged them with coming off the bye, I thought they responded to it, and they just kept going." Brady's message was about the defense, but it's hard to ignore what was going on for the Ravens offense. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both left the game with injuries, which meant undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was pressed into action for the first time in the NFL. Fagnano was overmatched, but future Bills opponents won't be quite so hamstrung and the Buffalo defense will have to show that they are able to match that level of play against all comers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Justin Herbert has gone eight straight starts without multiple TDs
summary: As the 0-6 Chargers emerge from their bye with a "visit" to the Rams, quarterback Justin Herbert will be trying to reverse a horrible trend.
full_text: As the 0-6 Chargers emerge from their bye with a "visit" to the Rams, quarterback Justin Herbert will be trying to reverse a horrible trend. Herbert has gone eight straight games, including the postseason, without multiple total touchdowns. Via NBC Sports research, only one quarterback in Chargers history has gone at least nine straight starts without multiple touchdowns. The record is held by former first-rounder Ryan Leaf, who went 12 straight starts without multiple touchdowns from 1998 through 2000. Herbert also leads the league with 10 turnovers. The Chargers nevertheless are sticking with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, at least for now. An embarrassment against the team with which they share a stadium could change things, quickly.
author: Mike Florio

title: Baker Mayfield on zero completed passes: Whatever it takes to win
summary: The Buccaneers set a franchise-record with 324 rushing yards in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons and they made a little other history as well.
full_text: The Buccaneers set a franchise-record with 324 rushing yards in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons and they made a little other history as well. The Bucs did not have a completed pass in the game, which was a first in franchise history and it made them the first team since the Bills in 1974 to go an entire game without completing a pass. The game was played in wet and sloppy conditions that joined Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield's injured right thumb as reasons why the Bucs only tried three passes all game. “I’ll do whatever it takes to win ,” Mayfield said, via Rob Maaddi of the Associated Press. “That’s all that matters to me.” Mayfield was 7-of-11 in Tampa's Week 7 win over the Panthers and the team has called a total of 16 pass plays over the last two weeks. They've called 104 running plays and the back-to-back wins should serve as proof of concept for a run-focused approach no matter the weather in the weeks to come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dak Prescott: "Cowardice" to put blame for Sunday's loss on Brian Schottenheimer
summary: The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead and lost at home for the first time in franchise history on Sunday, so quarterback Dak Prescott may have been understating things when he called it "one of the toughest" losses of his career.
full_text: The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead and lost at home for the first time in franchise history on Sunday, so quarterback Dak Prescott may have been understating things when he called it "one of the toughest" losses of his career. Arizona scored 20 points in the final 11 minutes of regulation and then missed an extra point that would have given them a win. That reprieve did not spark the Cowboys as they went three-and-out on their only possession before the Cardinals' game-winning field goal in overtime. The magnitude of the collapse during a season that has featured other underwhelming performances has led to questions about head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job security. Prescott was adamant after the loss that all can't be put on Schottenheimer's shoulders. "It's all of us," Prescott said, via the team's website. "Don't put the blame on one person . Simple as that. I think that's weak. I think that's cowardice. This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It's never just one person's fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it's never just truly one person's fault. And so, don't take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it's about us backing him up and backing one another up and we'll have to show it." Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he’s not thinking about an in-season coaching change, but he also called the loss an "indictment of the whole show" and Schottenheimer's job puts him at the top of the pyramid. That could wind up working out well for him if the 3-5 team can navigate its way past the Giants to win the NFC East, but there's been little about their performance to this point in the season to suggest they're capable of that kind of consistent success.
author: Josh Alper

title: Frustrated Justin Jefferson didn't speak to reporters after Sunday's loss
summary: When a team is winning, it's hard for any offensive players who aren't getting the ball as often as they should to be upset.
full_text: When a team is winning, it's hard for any offensive players who aren't getting the ball as often as they should to be upset. When winning becomes losing, the frustrations can quickly surface. That happened for the Vikings on Sunday against the Lions. Receiver Justin Jefferson, who made a spectacular touchdown catch in the first half, didn't see the ball as often as he should have during proverbial nut-cutting time. After the Vikings' final drive — which curiously ended on a fourth-and-five punt with 3:01 to play at a time when the Detroit rushing game was clicking — Jefferson made a rare display of frustration. After the 19-15 loss, Jefferson declined to speak to reporters, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN. Which means that Jefferson, who has a habit of always saying all the right things, doubted that he would have been able to do that. "Obviously he's frustrated, and that's understandable," quarterback Kyler Murray told reporters, via Seifert. "He is who he is, and he has every right to the way he feels when he doesn't get the ball. That's on us to find a way to get him the ball." "We had some opportunities for [Jefferson], and there were some chances there," coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters. "But we've got to find a way to get him the ball, especially on potential chances for him on some of those sequences where we're looking to kick off some momentum. He's a great guy to do it behind, and we'll continue to find ways to get him the football. But it was a division game. These guys want to win. I don't fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form." Whatever the cause, there's clearly a problem. And Murray, who missed time early in the season due to a concussion, should be up to speed now. On Sunday, he wasn't good enough. And here's the basic reality. At some point, either en route to the playoffs or after the Vikings get there, Murray will have to make a big play in a big spot. The jury is out on whether he will. The Vikings don't have many options. They could try to make a trade, but who's out there? They wanted to keep Daniel Jones after the 2024 season; maybe, at this point, the Colts would welcome the chance to move on. If the Raiders had lost to the Jets, Kirk Cousins may have been available for a reunion. With Las Vegas now at 4-4, why would they move him? The other option would be to ride with Carson Wentz, who has shown that he can and will get the ball to Jefferson. However it goes, Sunday's game exposed the biggest problem with the Vikings. Against teams that can't be held to 15 points or less, the Vikings may not be able to muster enough points to beat them.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars expect DaVon Hamilton to miss the rest of the season with torn quad
summary: Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was carted off on Sunday, and the initial prognosis isn't good.
full_text: Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was carted off on Sunday , and the initial prognosis isn't good. The Jaguars believe Hamilton has a torn quad and will have to miss the rest of the season, according to Ian Rapoport. Hamilton will have more tests today to confirm the diagnosis. The 6-foot-4, 335-pound Hamilton has started every game and played well for the Jaguars this season. He even filled in at long snapper for a game and performed respectably. He'll be a tough player to replace. A 2020 third-round pick, Hamilton has played his entire career in Jacksonville but is slated to become a free agent after this season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lions say Jack Campbell will remain hospitalized overnight
summary: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell will be hospitalized overnight after suffering what appeared to be a serious injury on Sunday against the Vikings.
full_text: ' Lions linebacker Jack Campbell will be hospitalized overnight after suffering what appeared to be a serious injury on Sunday against the Vikings. The Lions released a statement three hours after today's game in Detroit ended to say that Campbell is being evaluated. "Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them," the statement said. Campbell was motionless on the field for several minutes after a collision, and players on both teams were visibly shaken by the injury. The Lions have said Campbell is alert and breathing but have not offered any clarification about whether Campbell has movement in his extremities.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens may explore trading for Tyson Bagent
summary: The Baltimore quarterback room was decimated on Sunday.
full_text: The Baltimore quarterback room was decimated on Sunday. With nine days left in the trading period, the Ravens could start looking for help elsewhere. Starter Lamar Jackson is heading to injured reserve with a thumb injury that could end his season. Backup Tyler Huntley has a toe injury; its severity is to be determined. One name to watch, as mentioned on Football Night in America, is Tyson Bagent. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle had that same position last year in Chicago. And the Bears have three quarterbacks. Bagent has a $4 million salary in 2026, and a $4.25 million compensation package in 2027. The Bears also have Case Keenum under contract, behind Caleb Williams. The Ravens, we're told, may explore the possibility of acquiring Bagent. We're also told that it won't be cheap to get him. That's how it goes when a team develops an in-season need for a quarterback. The price goes up, as reflected by the urgency of the effort to find a replacement. If Huntley will miss time, the Ravens need to do something. The only other quaterback on the roster is Joe Fagnone, who played after Jackson and Huntley were hurt. The Ravens have no quarterbacks on the practice squad. Diego Pavia was on the 90-man roster in the offseason; he was cut just before the opening of training camp. Austin Reed was later signed to the roster during camp, after Skylar Thompson was placed on injured reserve.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos' goal-line stand holds off Chiefs 28-24 for division lead
summary: The Broncos, who have four comeback wins this season, are 6-2.
full_text: In a game they probably shouldn't have won, the Broncos beat the Chiefs with a goal-line stand in the final seconds. Denver stopped Kansas City four times inside the 10-yard line, winning 28-24 for Sean Payton's 200th career victory, including the postseason. The Broncos lead the AFC West at 6-2, while the Chiefs fell to 5-2 with a second consecutive loss. Denver trailed 24-13 in the fourth quarter before scoring 15 consecutive points for its fourth comeback win of the season. The Chiefs uncharacteristically fell apart when it mattered most. They had a chance to pad their lead, but Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal wide right with 2:31 remaining. It came after Alex Singleton sacked Patrick Mahomes for 6-yard loss. Butker is in danger of losing his job after the Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad last week. The 10-year veteran has missed 6 of 17 field-goal attempts this season, including two misses in last week's loss to the Seahawks. Two plays, 56 yards and 35 seconds later, the Broncos led for the first time. Jonah Coleman had a 51-yard catch-and-run before a 5-yard touchdown run. The Broncos led 28-24 with 1:56 left. Emmett Johnson, the star for the Chiefs on Sunday, returned the kickoff 44 yards to the Kansas City 44, and two plays later, Mahomes found Travis Kelce for a 32-yard gain to the Denver 18. The Chiefs had first-and-goal at the 4 with 35 seconds left. Kenneth Walker ran for 3 yards to the 1 before Patrick Surtain tackled him; Mahomes threw incomplete; and Walker was stopped for no gain by safety JL Skinner. That set up a final play with four seconds left, and after a false start, Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes to end the game. The Chiefs outgained the Broncos 399 to 294 as Mahomes went 30-of-41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns. Johnson caught five passes for 128 yards and a touchdown and had a 15-yard run. Kelce added five catches for 67 yards. Bo Nix was 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, going 5-of-6 for 84 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Coleman had 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown and four catches for 63 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Andy Reid: I didn't see a false start on Jaylon Moore at end of game
summary: The Chiefs blew an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Broncos, but they were able to drive back into position to try for a game-winning touchdown in the final seconds.
full_text: The Chiefs blew an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Broncos, but they were able to drive back into position to try for a game-winning touchdown in the final seconds. That effort looked like it was successful when Patrick Mahomes flipped a pass to wide receiver Rashee Rice in the end zone with four seconds to play, but the play had been whistled dead due to a false start on right tackle Jaylon Moore. Mahomes was sacked on the next snap and the Broncos celebrated a 28-24 win. Moore's movement was minimal enough that Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said at his postgame press conference that he thought the call was incorrect. “I didn’t see it," Reid said. "That’s one man’s opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see a false start.” Moore also appeared to twitch his leg prior to the snap, which may not change Reid's opinion but it was enough for a costly penalty that helped send the Chiefs to a second straight loss.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chiefs, Steelers, Commanders have interest in Brian Thomas Jr.
summary: Contenders usually aren't sellers at the trade deadline.
full_text: Contenders usually aren't sellers at the trade deadline. But the Jaguars have a receiver who, for whatever reason, hasn't really clicked with the coaching staff that arrived in 2025. As a result, 2024 first-rounder Brian Thomas Jr. has interest in a fresh start. And multiple teams are believed to be interested in acquiring him. Currently, the Chiefs, Steelers, and Commanders have interest. The Steelers, we're told, have greater interest in Colts receiver Josh Downs. Downs, however, is Kansas City's Plan B, if they can't get Thomas away from the Jaguars. Thomas had 1,282 receiving yards as a rookie. In 2025, his output dipped to 707 yards. This year, Thomas has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns. During Sunday's 42-7 romp over the Colts, Thomas was targeted twice, catching one pass for 12 yards and the first touchdown of the day. The Jaguars have no real incentive to move him, unless they get a big offer. The problem is that their price tag doesn't reflect his current usage. Beyond the question of whether they'd trade him at all is whether they'd send him to an AFC contender. The Commanders aren't much of a contender at all this season; they'd presumably want Thomas for 2027 and, once the fifth-year option is exercised, 2028. Still, trading him carries risk. If, once he's gone, Jakobi Meyers or Parker Washington get injured, the Jaguars will wish they still had him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Larry Csonka celebrates Vikings' loss as 1972 Dolphins stand alone for another year
summary: It's celebration time for the 1972 Dolphins.
full_text: ' It's celebration time for the 1972 Dolphins. After the Vikings' loss to the Lions on Sunday, there are no remaining undefeated teams in the NFL. That means the 1972 Dolphins will remain, for at least another year, the only perfect, undefeated, untied team in NFL history. Larry Csonka, the 79-year-old fullback who was the 1972 Dolphins' leading rusher, posted a picture of himself having a celebratory cigar and a drink on social media. "CONGRATS to the #DetroitLions on the Win and a game well played today," Csonka wrote . "CHEERS to all my ‘72 undefeated teammates and #MiamiDolphin fans on our now 54 year record! Cheers!" The 1972 Dolphins finished the regular season 14-0 and then won two playoff games and Super Bowl VII to finish a perfect 17-0. Players on that team have continued to celebrate their status as the only perfect team in the NFL's 107-year history.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kyler Murray developed hamstring tightness late in Sunday's loss
summary: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray developed hamstring tightness sometime late in the fourth quarter.
full_text: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray developed hamstring tightness sometime late in the fourth quarter. He said it was late enough that it didn't affect him in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions. But Murray will undergo further evaluation on Monday. " We’ll look at it , obviously, and do what we need to do," Murray said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN. Murray went into the sideline medical tent after throwing a touchdown pass with 8:44 remaining. He was back on the field for the next drive. It is unclear whether that was related to the hamstring issue or something else. "Kyler Murray just [had] some hamstring tightness, and he was able to return late in the football game," coach Kevin O'Connell said. Murray completed 17 of 29 passes for 210 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He ran for 35 yards on four carries.
author: Charean Williams

title: Saints fire offensive run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti
summary: The Saints made a change to their coaching staff during their bye week.
full_text: The Saints made a change to their coaching staff during their bye week. According to multiple reports, they have fired offensive run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti. It's the first change to the staff since Saints owner Gayle Benson said last month that she would not accept the team's level of play as the standard. The Saints are 1-1 since those comments and 2-5 on the season. Paganetti joined the Saints as part of head coach Kellen Moore's first staff in 2025. He and Moore initially worked together with the Eagles in 2024 and Paganetti was on the Eagles' staff for the previous seven seasons as well. He initially worked for the Eagles in 2013 and 2014 and returned to the team after a two-year stint at Oregon. The Saints rank 29th in the league with 86 rushing yards per game. They host the Browns in Week 9 in their first post-bye game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni: I am not doing a good enough job, I've got to do better
summary: The Eagles' head coach took the blame after Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
full_text: '' Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took the blame after Sunday night's loss to the Commanders. The Eagles, who started the season 2-0 and had Super Bowl aspirations, lost their sixth consecutive game to fall to 2-6. Sirianni said the head coach deserves the blame when that happens. “I take everything as my responsibility that happens out on that field. Everything. Obviously I am not doing a good enough job right now. I've got to do better," Sirianni said. Asked if offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will remain the play caller, Sirianni didn't answer directly. "I'm not thinking about any of that stuff right now," Sirianni said. But Sirianni did say the ultimate responsibility for turning the Eagles around is his, not any assistant coach's. "That falls on me," Sirianni said. "With all the detail that’s not happening right now, I’ve got to try a different approach. That 100 percent is on me with how many of those issues are happening right now. I’ll do everything I can to do different things to get that point across." Sirianni said the Eagles are determined to turn their season around. "I'm pissed at myself," Sirianni said. "I know I'll fight like hell to do everything I can do to get this fixed."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Panthers hire DeAngelo Hall to coach cornerbacks
summary: The Panthers dismissed a couple of defensive coaches last week and they are bringing back one of their former assistants to help out in the secondary this week.
full_text: The Panthers dismissed a couple of defensive coaches last week and they are bringing back one of their former assistants to help out in the secondary this week. Jonathan Jones of TheAthletic.com reports that the Panthers will hire DeAngelo Hall. The three-time Pro Bowl cornerback will work with the team's cornerbacks. Hall was an assistant defensive backs coach for Carolina on head coach Dave Canales's first staff in 2024. He also held that position in 2023. Hall played 14 seasons in the NFL and made Pro Bowls while with Atlanta and Washington. The Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley after last Thursday's loss to the Packers. Todd Wash is now the interim defensive coordinator. UPDATE 8:54 a.m. ET : The Panthers have announced Hall's return to the staff.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jared Verse: I stand by everything I say
summary: Browns defensive end Jared Verse gave the Steelers some fuel ahead of Sunday's games by sharing his thoughts about the team being dirty and vowing to "make Pittsburgh ours" in Week 8.
full_text: Browns defensive end Jared Verse gave the Steelers some fuel ahead of Sunday's games by sharing his thoughts about the team being dirty and vowing to " make Pittsburgh ours " in Week 8. That's not how things played out. Verse assisted on one tackle in the Steelers' 27-6 home win. Steelers players took some pleasure in roasting Verse after the game and dropping him on his head during it, but neither the result nor the Steelers' reactions caused Verse to rethink his approach to the Browns' longtime antagonists. “I stand by everything I say, and as a man you have to naturally do that,” Verse said, via Ashley Bastock of Cleveland.com. “I think we could have definitely did more to just to present ourselves as the team that we are. I don’t know who the hell that team was that walked out there that presented themselves. We didn’t do enough across the board, from the first quarter to the last quarter.” Verse won't see the Steelers again this season unless the two teams meet in the playoffs and the Browns' chances of getting there would be improved if Verse can find a way to make an impact on the field rather than on the bulletin board. He has 18 tackles and no sacks on the season, which certainly isn't the kind of production the Browns were hoping to see from a player they had high hopes for after acquiring him in the offseason trade of Myles Garrett to the Rams.
author: Josh Alper

title: Khalil Mack trying to be where his "feet are at" amid trade rumors
summary: The Chargers slumped to another defeat on Sunday and most of the attention being paid to the 0-7 team concerns who is going to be hitting the road in the near future.
full_text: '' The Chargers slumped to another defeat on Sunday and most of the attention being paid to the 0-7 team concerns who is going to be hitting the road in the near future. Some of those conversations have to do with firing coaches and some have to do with potential trades of veteran players. Linebacker Khalil Mack is one of those players as he is playing on a one-year deal and has the kind of history of success as a pass rusher that could be appealing to a number of teams. After Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams, Mack was asked about his mindset amid the trade chatter. “You’ve got to be where your feet are man , ultimately," Mack said, via Eric Williams of Fox Sports. "That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all time. That’s kind of been my thing in years past.” The trade deadline is a week from Tuesday, so Mack, who has three sacks this season, will know where his feet will be for the rest of the season in the near future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saquon Barkley: Eagles said they won't trade me, I want to be here to fix it
summary: A report before Sunday's games said that the Eagles will not trade running back Saquon Barkley ahead of the November 10 trade deadline and Barkley said after Sunday night's game against the Commanders that he's received the same message from the team.
full_text: A report before Sunday's games said that the Eagles will not trade running back Saquon Barkley ahead of the November 10 trade deadline and Barkley said after Sunday night's game against the Commanders that he's received the same message from the team. Barkley played through hamstring and back injuries in that game and he scored a touchdown in the first quarter, but the Eagles went from being up 10-0 to losing 27-10 in Washington. The loss was the sixth in a row for a team that's reeling, but Barkley made it clear that he's not looking to jump ship and is happy that the Eagles aren't interested in parting ways. "When that message was relayed to me, it definitely does mean a lot," Barkley said, via Tim McManus of ESPN.com. "The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I'm the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it, and I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it ." The Eagles traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens last month and their tailspin would seem to make more deals a real possibility, but Barkley is set to be around for the long haul.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dan Campbell wisely declined the Vikings' intentional offsides
summary: With 2:00 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday in Detroit, the Lions had a 19-15 lead and the ball, facing second-and-2.
full_text: ' With 2:00 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday in Detroit, the Lions had a 19-15 lead and the ball, facing second-and-2. Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel jumped offside, and fans in Detroit cheered, thinking the Vikings had made a mistake. But Lions coach Dan Campbell knew better. Campbell declined the penalty because he knew the Vikings had jumped offside on purpose, wanting to concede a first down while the clock was stopped so that they could then use their three timeouts after the Lions' first, second and third-down plays and then get the ball back with time left for a comeback drive. Tom Brady, calling the game on Fox, immediately recognized what was happening. "They're not gonna accept that," Brady said as soon as Van Ginkel jumped. "They'll decline that penalty." It was obvious to Brady, but it wasn't obvious to Bears coach Ben Johnson when he faced the same situation against the Patriots. Coach Mike Vrabel told his team to jump offside to concede a first down, and Johnson accepted the penalty. That allowed the Patriots to use their three timeouts on the Bears' next three plays, forcing the Bears to kick on fourth down with 1:38 remaining. The Bears ended up winning when kicker Cairo Santos made it a two-possession game with a 58-yard field goal, but if the Bears had missed, Johnson's decision to accept the penalty could have proven costly. It's a situation that doesn't arise in most games, but it happens often enough that every coach should understand it as well as Vrabel, Campbell and Brady do: Sometimes, the smart thing for one team is to commit a penalty on purpose, and the smart thing for the other team is to decline the penalty. In theory, if the defensive team continued to jump offside and the offense continued to decline the penalties, it could reach the point where the referee would have to warn the defensive team's head coach that he could invoke the "palpably unfair act" rule, which gives the referee wide leeway to use his own discretion to enforce penalties. The referee could, for instance, charge the defensive team a timeout if it refused to stop committing intentional penalties. It didn't reach that point on Sunday, as Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell realized that Campbell was on to the intentional offside. Campbell is a smart in-game coach who recognized on Sunday what the right strategic decision was in the final two minutes.

title: Trey McBride taunts Caleb Downs as Cowboys rookie's struggles reach alarming level
summary: Dallas rebuilt its defense around first-round pick Caleb Downs, but his coverage struggles and costly mistakes were exposed
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys blew a 14-point lead twice against the Arizona Cardinals in a 33-30 overtime defeat. And owner Jerry Jones had many fingers to point during the ugly aftermath.
"It just really is glaring in a negative way how we could be where we were and end up losing that ball game," Jones said. "We had a great chance right at the end to win the game, and had everybody out there that can win games for us, and of course. didn't get it done. So it was a couple of games within the game really that was also telling, and we just just did not play well enough at all to win that ball game. Not well enough after you had the lead the way we did and had the opportunities we had to win that ball game. So it's an indictment of the whole show."
The jarring thing about Dallas' defensive collapse and their overall defensive struggles in 2026 is that the Cowboys' front office made an effort to ensure something like this wouldn't happen after their 2025 meltdown. Defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus was fired and replaced by Christian Parker. Jones traded for Rashan Gary , signed two new safeties and a new cornerback, drafted two defensive players in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft (Ohio State safety Caleb Downs and UCF edge rusher Malachi Lawrence ), and traded for Joey Porter Jr .
Yet, they still profile as one of the NFL 's worst defenses across the board.
Third down conversion rate allowed
Dallas traded up one spot to draft Downs 11th overall to be a focal point of its new-look defense, working in the hybrid nickel corner/safety role. It's a role that earned Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean a first-team All-Pro selection in Philadelphia last season. Trey McBride , a 2025 first-team All-Pro who leads the NFL with 66 catches in 2026, was far from impressed with Downs on Sunday.
After he beat Downs for a 15-yard gain on third-and-6 with 2:30 left in the first half on Sunday, McBride taunted him.
"First-round pick? You're a first-rounder?," McBride said to Downs, via Fox Sports . "For what? For what? First round for what?"
That was far from the only miscue for Downs in Sunday's loss. Downs had an angle to tackle Tyler Allgeier behind the line of scrimmage, but he took a bad pursuit angle and completely whiffed. Allgeier exploded through the Cowboys' defense for a 63-yard rushing touchdown, Arizona's first of the day. That play gave the Cardinals the belief they could actually pull off their eventual comeback.
Tyler Allgeier breaks free for a 63-yard rushing TD! AZvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PuMUPt7CLa
Downs was also bullied on a block down the field on a 52-yard run by Allgeier down the left sideline. Allgeier is now the first player this season with multiple runs of 50-plus yards in a single game.
Block in the back? Maybe Froholdt abused Caleb Downs 💀 pic.twitter.com/FO81QINMoK
Obviously, the Cowboys allowing an NFL-worst 152.8 rushing yards per game is a team effort, but Downs certainly has a hand in that effort. He did also team up with defensive tackle Kenny Clark to stonewall No. 3 overall pick running back Jeremiyah Love on a fourth and goal at the one to force a turnover on downs on Sunday. Overall, Pro Football Focus assigned Downs a 68.8 run defense grade through the first eight weeks of the season, which ranks 46th among 98 qualified safeties.
In coverage, Downs has allowed 20 of the 24 passes thrown his way to be completed (83.3%) for 230 yards and three passing touchdowns, per TruMedia. That's good for a 9.6 passing yards-per-attempt average and a 146.2 passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage. For reference, 158.3 is a perfect passer rating. Among 174 players with 20 or more passes thrown their way this season, Downs' 146.2 passer rating allowed in coverage is the third worst in the entire NFL this season. Only Baltimore Ravens safety Malaki Starks (149.3) and Miami Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr . (154.2) have surrendered a worse passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage than Downs through eight weeks.
The Cowboys have been an injury-plagued secondary. Porter Jr. suffered an ankle injury on Sunday, and Downs himself didn't finish Sunday's game after entering concussion protocol in the fourth quarter. However, Downs has as big a role as anyone on Dallas' defense in their continued struggles in the opening half of the 2026 season.

title: Lamar Jackson injury throws huge wrench into looming contract talks with Ravens
summary: Jackson's current contract runs through the 2027 season
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens suddenly find themselves in an uncomfortable position. Of course, the most immediate issue for the organization is seeing Lamar Jackson suffer a right thumb injury on his first play back from a three-game absence due to a high ankle sprain. Now, the two-time NFL MVP needs surgery and could be sidelined for the rest of the season. From a big-picture view, however, the concern is more existential: How do they handle their future with Jackson?
One of the storylines that has hovered over the franchise is that Jackson is due for a contract extension. His current deal — a five-year, $260 million contract that, at the time, made him the highest-paid player in the league — runs out after the 2027 campaign. Jackson also has no guaranteed salary remaining on his current contract beyond this season.
Since signing that deal, Jackson has earned another MVP award (2023), was runner-up for MVP in 2024, and is 34-17 over his 51 regular season starts with a 110.1 passer rating. He's also 2-2 in the playoffs over this stretch with a 105.8 passer rating. More recently, he looked great in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system, as his yards per attempt (10.1), air yards per attempt (10.9) and 70.8% completion rate in four games played entering Week 8 were all on pace to be career highs.
Those will be just some of the figures he and his camp will likely point to as they once again look to reset the market at the position, as every player of his caliber aims to do when they sit down at the negotiating table.
That said, the Ravens may have some trepidation this time around, particularly as these injuries start to pile up. Before this thumb injury that could knock him out of Baltimore's final nine games of the year, he had already been sidelined for three games with an ankle injury. Last year, Jackson missed a total of four games due to back and hamstring injuries.
Possibly resetting the market once again with a quarterback who is about to turn 30 in January and is starting to have injuries pile up is a risky endeavor for the franchise, which could result in another murky negotiation. If you remember last time around, it wasn't smooth sailing between Jackson and the Ravens leading up to their most recent agreement. In fact, Jackson requested a trade before ultimately inking his deal to remain in Baltimore, so there is some history of things getting spicy between these two sides.
With this latest right thumb injury adding to his growing list of ailments on his résumé, it throws a rather seismic wrench into these future talks.
Lamar Jackson heads to the locker room after his first pass attempt with an apparent hand injury. pic.twitter.com/JVUQYjJV8H
Along with Jackson, quarterbacks like C.J. Stroud , Caleb Williams , Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye are all due to sign extensions this offseason. Each of them will try to exceed Patrick Mahomes , who is currently the highest-paid quarterback in the NFL with an average annual value of $64 million per season. Dak Prescott is the only other quarterback currently making $60 million per season, but that will soon change with all of these signal-callers — including Jackson — up. Right now, 11 other quarterbacks are ahead of Jackson's $52 million AAV.
Does Jackson push to once again become the highest-paid player in NFL history when he signs his contract? Does he simply look to be among the highest-paid quarterbacks in the league? That distinction could be the difference between a deal getting done in somewhat quick fashion or dragging out throughout the summer.
For the Ravens, they may be painted into a corner. They'll rightfully have concerns about signing Jackson to another monster, possibly record-setting extension, but what else are they going to do? The organization is 7-14 without Jackson since his first start in Week 11 of the 2018 season (including playoffs).
It's hard to imagine Jackson playing on a lame duck contract, so they'll either need to sign him or trade him. Does the organization have the appetite to blow it up, ship the two-time MVP away and rebuild? Maybe it depends on how venomous these upcoming negotiations get.
The most likely option is that they pay him, no matter how much their hands shake as they slide the contract across the table. Whether it pays off with a deep playoff run or a Super Bowl is a different question entirely, especially as these injuries become more prevalent.

title: Cowboys biggest loser from NFL Week 8; FSU starts coaching search after firing Mike Norvell
summary: Plus, Lamar Jackson played one snap before suffering another long-term injury
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
When the Cowboys dominated the Eagles last week, they were a trendy pick to win the NFC East. That was certainly the case when they took a 14-point lead over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter on Sunday.
Then Dallas surrendered 23 points in just under 15 minutes for a 33-30 overtime loss. The catastrophic collapse was only made worse by the fact that Gardner Minshew was carving up the Cowboys like a Thanksgiving turkey.
It was a mind-melting finish, and Carter Bahns had every reason to make Dallas lead the list of Week 8's biggest losers .
Given all of that, I'm sure it won't suprise you to to learn that the Cowboys received a failing grade from our own John Breech. Even former Dallas quarterback Ben DiNucci was calling out the the team for an "embarrassing" loss .
When a team implodes like that, it's fair to question the coach's job security, but Brian Schottenheimer appears to be safe for the time being .
Of course, that was one of many wild games on Sunday, so here's everything you may have missed:
With November upon us, the college football season is reaching a crescendo. Week 9 wasn't the wildest weekend we've seen, but it delivered enough drama to tee us up for the home stretch.
Coming off a 30-18 loss to USC , Ohio State is out of mulligans, and the high-wire act begins in earnest this weekend against Oregon . The Buckeyes can't afford another loss, and they'll be starting a freshman quarterback the rest of the way. As our own Tom Fornelli explains, optimism is tough to find in Columbus these days .
Ohio State has no margin for error left, and it's fair to wonder whether it will be able to hold things together long enough to reach the playoff . There should also be some concern about the Heisman Trophy candidacy of Jeremiah Smith with freshman Luke Fahey at quarterback.
The Buckeyes aren't the only Big Ten disappointment, and it's starting to look like the conference's run of national title dominance will come to an end .

title: Cowboys should consider trading George Pickens: 5 logical NFL deadline destinations
summary: Pickens received only four targets in Dallas' historic collapse against Arizona, adding urgency to the Cowboys' decision before the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Shortly after Chad Ryland 's game-winning field goal went through the uprights to seal a 33-30 comeback, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens flew down the hallway and into the locker room by himself. No other teammate, coach, or staff member moved faster to get into the locker room and out of AT&T Stadium after Dallas made ugly history with its blown 14-point lead.
Pickens first one to the lockers, jogged down the tunnel before most media could even set up @1053thefan pic.twitter.com/RVab4T1c5M
Pickens' lack of targets was glaring. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 11 targets on Sunday while tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford was second with five targets. Pickens caught two passes for 48 yards. Four targets in a game simply isn't enough.
Pickens hasn't been bad this season: his 533 yards receiving rank as the 15th most in the NFL in 2026, just behind Trey McBride and just in front of Garrett Wilson (527) and Ja'Marr Chase (492). He is still on pace to exceed 1,100 receiving yards, but it regularly feels like the Cowboys are leaving production out on the field. Since Schottenheimer blamed Pickens' lack of vigor for run blocking for the team's struggling offense in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, he has 10 targets across the last two games.
"If I had the answer, we'd get him involved. I'm not trying to be rude or whatever it is, but he made some plays. Anytime the ball went his way, he came up with them. He had the one, unfortunately came back for a holding," quarterback Dak Prescott said. ... "I'm not sure about even how many targets he had. As I told y'all before, I go through the reads. [I] try to throw it to the open guy and stay consistent and true to that. And so, I've got to go back and look at the film and see if I missed him, see if we could have went to him more, see if we could have went to CeeDee more. I feel like it was a game that CeeDee didn't have as many catches as per usual, but we still had a chance to win and should have won it."
With the NFL trade deadline coming up in eight days on Nov. 10 and the Cowboys off to a 3-5 start and appearing to be going nowhere, it would make sense for Dallas to field trade calls for Pickens. He is playing out the franchise tag, and he will command near-top-of-the-market value on his second multi-year NFL contract. Dallas will also have to deal with balancing cornerback Joey Porter Jr. 's contract situation, since he, too, is set to be a free agent after the season.
After trading away draft capital to get Porter Jr. and Quinnen Williams, Dallas could use some additional ammunition in its 2027 NFL Draft war chest. So who could be blowing up owner/general manager Jerry Jones' phone for Pickens if word leaks out that they will listen to trade calls for their 25-year-old Pro Bowl wideout? Here is a look at five potential landing spots.
Jerry Jones has shown he doesn't care about sending a young star player to a non-divisional rival: he traded Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers . The pairing of the 49ers and Pickens makes too much sense.
San Francisco is the NFC's top seed through the first eight weeks of the season, and they have $34.98 million in cap space, the third most in the entire league, per OverTheCap.com. There are no financial barriers to this deal.
Plus, they have a glaring need for Pickens given all their wide receiver injuries. Both Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) were ruled out of their last game played in Week 7. Three wide receivers are on their injured reserve list.
Lastly, the 49ers are all in for 2026 because of their aging core. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Evans is 33, Samuel is 30, George Kittle is 33, Kyle Juszcyk is 35, Trent Williams is 38 and DeForest Buckner is 32. Both Fred Warner and Nick Bosa are healthy right now, but they're both 29 with extensive injury histories.
The Chiefs failed to score a game-winning touchdown after having a second-and-goal at the one with 15 seconds left, and Kansas City was outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter of their narrow 28-24 road loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. You know who could have made a significant difference for quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the fourth quarter in Week 8? The 6-foot-3, 200-pound Pickens.
Kenneth Walker III is starting to lose a little steam after being heavily relied upon to carry the Chiefs' offense on his back. After averaging 133 rushing yards per game and 6.3 yards per carry with six rushing touchdowns in Kansas City's first five games of the season, Walker III is now averaging 52.5 rushing yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry without a touchdown in the last two games.
That's because the Chiefs' passing game requires Travis Kelce to be their No. 1 target, something that isn't a sustainable formula over the course of an 18-week season and beyond. Also, it would be incredibly foolish to waste the rest of Mahomes' glory years. The three-time Super Bowl MVP quarterback is 31, but he hasn't been the same high-flying passer that he was with a true No. 1 wide receiver like Tyreek Hill. Without Hill since 2022, Mahomes' production has taken a notable dip.
Average air yards per pass attempt
* Ranks among 37 qualified quarterbacks since 2022
The Buffalo Bills are the AFC's No. 1 seed through the first eight weeks, and they are always in win-now mode with Josh Allen . Yes, the Bills traded for DJ Moore , but he is probably best as Buffalo's No. 2 receiver on a Super Bowl team. He missed Buffalo's last two games with a shoulder injury prior to returning in Week 8, and he hyperextended his knee in the Bills' 36-10 beatdown of the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens .
Allen hasn't had a true WR1 since the 2024 Stefon Diggs trade. Pickens could help him become the league's most efficient passer. That would probably be enough for the Bills to perhaps win their first Super Bowl in franchise history.
The Las Vegas Raiders trading for Pickens would be a case of taking care of the now and the later. The Kirk Cousins-led Raiders are 4-4 and just one game out of the AFC's No. 7 seed. Giving Cousins, whose 19 passing touchdowns rank as the second most in the NFL, Pickens to pair with Brock Bowers could really make Klint Kubiak's offense pop.
Among the players officially listed as wide receivers on the Raiders' roster, Tre Tucker , a 2023 third-round pick, is the best they have. He could also help accelerate Fernando Mendoza's long-term development. Pickens is just two years older than the 23-year-old Mendoza, so the quarterback could spend the bulk of his career with a high-caliber wide receiver in addition to the 23-year-old Bowers at tight end.
Perhaps living in Las Vegas would dull the novelty of going out on The Strip that Pickens and Lamb experienced when they visited for "Monday Night Football" last season.
Despite being 6-1 and the No. 2 seed in the NFC, the Minnesota Vikings have the sixth-lowest scoring offense (20.0 points per game) in the entire NFL. Their lack of rhythm in the passing game is a major reason for that, as their Kyler Murray-quarterbacked passing attack is averaging the second-fewest passing yards per game (165.6) in the entire NFL.
Yes, Minnesota has 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Justin Jefferson and former first-round pick Jordan Addison at wide receiver, but its offense could clearly use another weapon to help Murray find his groove as a Viking. They have been rumored to be in pursuit of Jonathan Taylor , but perhaps Pickens could also help fix the issues on the offensive side of the ball.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL Week 9 early odds: Ravens become home underdogs to Jaguars after Lamar Jackson injury
summary: A look at where the odds and spreads currently stand heading into Week 9, including a big move in Baltimore
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will likely have to go the rest of the 2026 regular season without star quarterback Lamar Jackson . The two-time NFL MVP made his return to action on Sunday after a three-game absence due to an ankle injury, but that comeback was very short-lived. On the first play from scrimmage for the Ravens offense, Jackson jammed his right thumb on Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau on a follow-through. That injury not only knocked him out of the game, but head coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that Jackson will go on injured reserve and will undergo surgery.
On top of this injury turning Baltimore's season upside down, it's also thrown the line for their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars for a loop. Not only did Jackson go down on Sunday, but backup Tyler Huntley (toe) also did, and his status for Week 9 is up in the air. That could result in undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano getting the start.
With that uncertainty under center, it's no surprise to see the Ravens go from being a 3-point favorite at home to now an 8.5-point home underdog. The total also dropped from 48.5 down to 43.5. This just shows how much a line can swing when a player of Jackson's caliber is sidelined.
While we won't see as dramatic of swings throughout the rest of the Week 9 slate, there has been some notable movement that is worth pointing out. So, as we close the book on Week 8, let's take our first glimpse at the upcoming week and who the oddsmakers have coming out on top.
Note : Pittsburgh and Tennessee are on the bye in Week 9.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Jaguars at Ravens (Thursday)
Bengals at Falcons (in Madrid)
Bengals -170, Falcons +142
Broncos -155, Panthers +130
Rams -225, Commanders +185
Texans -218, Chargers +180
Packers +124, Patriots -148
Cardinals +525, Seahawks -752
Buccaneers +205, Bears -250
As we noted in the intro, the Lamar Jackson injury has nuked this line. Baltimore is now an 8.5-point home underdog to the Jaguars after opening as a field goal favorite. The total also dropped down to 43.5 after opening at 48.5. Jacksonville is 4-3 ATS on the season, which includes a 1-1 ATS record on the road. Amid all of the QB turnover even prior to this latest Jackson injury, the Ravens enter Week 9 0-3 ATS at home.
The NFL heads back out into international waters for this matchup between the Bengals and Falcons, this time to Madrid. Cincinnati has opened as a field goal favorite as Joe Burrow and the offense are starting to find their rhythm after the Bengals QB just totaled six touchdowns in a win over Tennessee. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr . imploded for the Falcons, throwing four interceptions in a loss to Tampa Bay. The Bengals are 3-4 ATS this season, while the Falcons are 3-5 ATS. The total moved up to 51.5 after opening at 49.5, and the Over is 9-6 combined between these two teams this season.
Denver is coming off another comeback win, this time rallying to defeat the Chiefs at home to take over first place in the AFC North. Now, they'll look to win their fifth-straight game when they visit the Panthers. Carolina will have the rest advantage over the Broncos after playing last Thursday, but are home dogs. Denver is laying 3-points as a road favorite. The Broncos' 6-2 ATS record is tied for the best in the NFL, but the club is 2-2 ATS on the road. However, as a road favorite, Denver is 2-0 ATS. As a home underdog, the Panthers are 1-1 ATS entering Week 9. The total sits at 44.5, and the Under is a combined 9-6 between these squads.
New Orleans was on the bye in Week 8, so it'll be well-rested when it squares off against the Browns on Sunday. The Saints are a 3-point favorite at home and are still looking for their first ATS victory at the Superdome (0-3 ATS). On the road this season, the Browns are 2-3 ATS. With the total sitting at 43.5, it's worth noting that the Over is 2-1 in Saints home games this season.
Dallas has jumped out as a 6-point favorite after the line initially opened Cowboys -4.5. This has more to do with Indy's ongoing implosion and the possibility that it continues to sell off pieces before the deadline. On Sunday, the Colts lost 42-7 to the Jaguars and Daniel Jones was benched. It's unclear if Jones will start in Week 9. If he doesn't, Anthony Richardson would likely get the nod. Dallas is 2-2 ATS on the road, but that includes a 1-2 ATS mark as a road favorite. Indy is 1-2 ATS at Lucas Oil Stadium. The total for this game jumped up to 52.5 after opening at 51.5. The Over is 6-2 in Cowboys games this season.
The Rams have quietly stabilized after a 2-4 start to the regular season. They've won two straight to get back to .500 on the year and are now a 5.5-point road favorite as they gear up for a matchup against the Commanders. LA is 4-4 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS on the road. Both of those ATS road wins came as road favorites. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 1-0 ATS as a home underdog.
After handing Minnesota its first loss of the season, the Lions now head down to South Beach as a 7-point road favorite over the Dolphins. Detroit is 1-2 ATS on the road, which includes a 1-1 ATS record as a road favorite. At Hard Rock Stadium, the Dolphins are 2-1 ATS. The total sits at 48.5. Between these two teams this season, the Over is 9-5.
Kansas City is now a double-digit favorite over the Jets, laying 10 points after the line opened at 9.5. The Chiefs fell out of first place in the AFC West after allowing the Broncos to score 15 unanswered fourth-quarter points. That said, the Jets shouldn't present the same level of resistance. Kansas City is 2-1 ATS at Arrowhead, while the Jets are 2-1-1 ATS on the road. The total for this game opened at 43.5 but has since moved up to 45.5. The Under is 2-1 in Chiefs home games this season.
The Giants were on the bye in Week 8, so they'll be well rested for this NFC East road matchup in Philly. They'll enter Lincoln Financial Field as a 2.5-point favorite, which is up from the 1.5 points they were laying at the open. New York is 5-2 ATS entering Week 9, which includes a 2-1 ATS record on the road. Philadelphia is 0-3 ATS as a home underdog in 2026.
Houston picked up a point and a half and are laying 4.5 points on the road to the Chargers after initially opening as a field goal favorite. LA remains winless on the season after falling to the Rams on Sunday. It is 0-1 ATS as a home underdog this season and 0-3 ATS at home overall. The Texans are 1-1 ATS on the road. The total sits at 42.5, and the Under could be a popular play, with it owning a 6-1 record in Chargers games this season.
New England is a 2.5-point favorite at home over the Packers, who'll have a rest advantage after playing last Thursday. New England is 3-4-1 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS record at home. As for the Packers, they're 2-2 ATS on the road this season (5-3 ATS overall). The Under is 3-1 in Packers road games entering Week 9.
Seattle is an 11.5-point favorite despite squaring off against Arizona after playing on a short week. Given that the Seahawks still have their Week 8 matchup with the Bears to play on Monday night, this line could see movement once that game goes final. Arizona is coming off an upset win on the road against Dallas, improving to 4-1 ATS on the road this season. One thing worth monitoring with the Cardinals is their situation at quarterback. Jacoby Brissett was benched for Gardner Minshew on Sunday, so it'll be interesting to see how Mike LaFleur approaches the position going forward.
San Francisco emerges from the bye week as a 9.5-point favorite over the Raiders. The Niners are 2-2 ATS at home this season with an average margin of victory of 11 points. Meanwhile, the Raiders are 3-1 ATS on the road this season, and that 75% cover rate is tied for the third-highest in the NFL. The total, which sits at 51.5 for this game, is 6-2 in Raiders games this season and 3-4 in Niners games.
Chicago still has its Week 8 matchup to play on Monday…
