title: Steelers' Jaylen Warren is 'on fire': Why the breakout running back keeps getting better
summary: Warren tied his career high with 143 rushing yards on his 28th birthday, continuing a breakout season that has made him the engine of Pittsburgh's offense
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- On a team that includes several future Hall of Fame players, Jaylen Warren was the talk of the Steelers' locker room following a 27-6 trouncing of the Browns that gave Pittsburgh the outright lead in the AFC North division.
Warren, who turned 28 on Sunday, celebrated the occasion by rushing for 143 yards (tying his career-high) and a touchdown on 17 carries. It was the second consecutive 100-yard game and the fourth 100-yard game of the season for Warren, a former undrafted rookie who in the midst of a career year.
"Jaylen is on fire," coach Mike McCarthy said afterward. "You can't get him the ball enough."
“Jaylen is on fire. You can’t get him the ball enough.” #Steelers coach Mike McCarthy on Jaylen Warren. pic.twitter.com/b3e2gtBCbQ
Why is Warren's level of success enhanced in Year 5? It starts with his featured role. On Sunday, Pittsburgh's offensive line bullied Cleveland's defensive front to the tune of 200 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries. It was a unit that was clearly motivated to respond to Cleveland pass rusher Jared Verse's recent comments with their play on the field.
Most everyone who watched Sunday's game saw Steelers guard Mason McCormick's body slam of Verse in the first half. But just as telling was McCormick and center Zach Frazier sprinting to the other side of the field at the end of the first quarter. While his teammates were running, fellow Steelers lineman Brock Hoffman made a "feed me" reference to the Steelers' sideline, a subtle request to McCarthy to continue running the ball.
Pittsburgh's defense has also helped Warren and the offense. The Steelers' defense, which hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters, has enjoyed more time on the bench while watching Warren do his thing.
"He's a bowling ball with teeth, man," said Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt , who had two of Pittsburgh's eight sacks of Deshaun Watson . "You can't get him down. Jaylen is just funny, man. He's the guy that's out there in December when we're practicing and it's like 12 degrees, he's in a T-shirt and shorts. You're like, 'What the heck?' That's just who he is. He's a hard tackle. He's a great locker room guy. Very selfless. But man, he loves football and you can see it in the way that he plays."
Cam Heyward, the longest-tenured Steelers player, gave Warren the ultimate compliment.
"I've been blessed to play with a lot of great running backs. Jaylen is not short of that," he said. "He's every bit as advertised. Having Rico [Dowdle] as well, they do a great job of being a 1-2 punch. When they're able to sustain drives, it means we're on the sideline and we can put our feet up."
Speaking of sustaining drives, that's what Warren did on his 51-yard run that came on a third-and-13 play. The play helped give the Steelers their first double-digit lead of the day.
"To be able to call a trap on third [and long] and get a first down is pretty wild," Rodgers said. "Didn't expect that. Can't remember the last time that happened when I was out there."
Jaylen Warren just went 51 yards on 3rd and 13 😳 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YD1Naon9lN
The biggest reason for Warren's emergence, though, is the man himself, although Warren's humility would never allow him to say that himself. Warren has only gotten better during his time with the Steelers.
After a somewhat disappointing 2024 season, Warren told CBS Sports that he planned to spend more time getting treatment at the facility. That change has clearly helped. Warren ultimately ran for a career-high 958 yards in 2025 and is currently on pace to have the most prolific rushing season by a Steelers running back since Le'Veon Bell.
"It's definitely paying off," Warren said on Sunday when asked about his extra time at the recovery table.
“I’d say it’s definitely paying off.” #Steelers Jaylen Warren on some of the changes that have led to his success. pic.twitter.com/J6JV2Gm0s5
Lastly, Warren's intangibles are another reason for his success. His team-first attitude has made him a locker room favorite. His teammates want him to succeed, which is evident every time he makes a big play and whenever his teammates are asked about him.
“Love having him on our team. He’s a fantastic teammate, and he’s making a lot of plays.” #Steelers Aaron Rodgers on Jaylen Warren. pic.twitter.com/RtCUght8GR
For Warren, it's about being the best player he can be so he can help the Steelers achieve their Super Bowl goals. That mindset helped him make the Steelers' roster as an undrafted rookie, and it's serving as the main catalyst for his breakout season.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Seahawks vs. Bears how to watch, prediction, odds: Caleb Williams faces toughest test yet
summary: The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses
full_text:
In the Week 8 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Seattle Seahawks host the Chicago Bears . Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs , snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night.
Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening.
Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset?
Chicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests.
For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores.
Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league.
The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground.
The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III . D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box.
The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year.
Seattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's .
Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual.
The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions.
Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head.
Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel , and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.)
The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price . Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league.
Seattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home.
Prediction: Seahawks 24, Bears 20
author: Jared Dubin

title: Wilson's 2027 NFL mock draft: Browns trade up for QB, five passers land in Round 1
summary: Jets, Titans and Browns all have multiple first-round picks
full_text:
Hey, fun story: Remember when the 2027 QB class was supposed to be loaded? We spent the summer talking about six or seven potential first-rounders , including two names — Dante Moore and Arch Manning — who entered the season as my QB1 and QB2. Two months later, Moore's season is over after suffering a concussion vs. USC in late September, and Manning has been so inconsistent we're wondering whether he should even enter the draft .
And, now, for the third straight draft cycle, the preseason QB hype hasn't come close to matching what we've seen on the field. That doesn't mean there aren't first-round passers in this class; it just means figuring out which ones deserve to be there.
Darian Mensah is my QB1 , and while the competition Miami has faced leaves some (possibly many) questions unanswered, he's been consistently outstanding. Meanwhile, Drew Mestemaker has gone from a quarterback few people were talking about to the most buzzworthy one after a hot start in Stillwater. I wrote about him after he outplayed Moore and Oregon early in the season , and we'll have to see if he decides to return to school for 2027.
And it's worth remembering that my preseason First-Round Readiness Score (FRED) model was higher on Mensah, Mestemaker and Jayden Maiava (all first-rounders in this mock draft) than some of the bigger names in this class. Meanwhile, Moore and Manning entered the season with more questions than their preseason draft projections might have suggested. Two months through the season, and what we've seen on the field has largely backed up what the model was telling us.
Of course, there's one name we haven't talked about, and he happens to be the best player in this class. He's also not a quarterback. The last time a non-QB went No. 1 overall was in 2022 when the Jaguars took pass rusher Travon Walker. The last time a wide receiver was the first overall pick? Thirty-one years ago, when the Jets selected Keyshawn Johnson. Which brings us to Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, who has been dominant since the day he arrived in Columbus.
I wrote back in September about why passing on him might be taking a bigger risk than drafting him high . He's big, physical, can win at all three levels and makes ridiculous catches look routine. Think Julio Jones or Terrell Owens or Calvin Johnson.
And yes, the still-winless Chargers (and current holders of the top pick in the 2027 draft) already have Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey, and they've invested plenty of draft capital at receiver in recent years. Doesn't matter. Because if you have the No. 1 overall pick and no one willing to trade up, you're taking Smith a million times out of a million. This isn't about filling the biggest need on your roster; it's about adding the best player in the draft. And when that player is that much better than everyone else, why overthink it?
So where does that leave us? With five quarterbacks in this first-round mock, no Manning for the second straight mock draft , and plenty of questions left to answer. As for the non-QB positions, offensive tackle leads the way with six players in this mock draft, followed by wide receiver with five.
Keep reading to see how all 32 picks shake out.

title: Cover 32: Why Jets have every reason to trade Breece Hall, plus Week 8 games balls, gaffes
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into the biggest items from Week 8, including Joe Burrow's six-touchdown day and Chad Ryland's redemption
full_text:
The New York Jets set the NFL ablaze at last year's trade deadline. The club made a couple of seismic moves, shipping away corner Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams for a collection of draft picks. Fast-forward about 12 months, and they're being eyed again as a seller. For the most part, folks have pondered the possibility of star wideout Garrett Wilson being available, but the organization has slammed that door shut .
The door that should be kept wide open, however, is trading running back Breece Hall .
Following the Week 8 loss to the Raiders , New York is 2-6 on the season and will travel to Kansas City to face the Chiefs in Week 9 before the Nov. 10 deadline rolls in. In all likelihood, they'll have accumulated seven losses over their first nine games once they reach the deadline. That's a recipe for a team to look itself in the mirror, realize the 2026 campaign won't bear any fruit, and move pieces to build for tomorrow.
Hall fits the bill as a player who is more valuable to them as a trade asset rather than a contributor on the field. That's thanks, in part, to the emergence of fellow running back Braelon Allen .
As Hall has been sidelined with a quad injury, Allen has flourished in the starting role. Over the last five games with Hall on the shelf, Allen has started in each contest and has rushed for 504 yards on a 5.4 yards-per-carry average and has two rushing touchdowns. Allen is also averaging 3.92 yards per carry after contact over this stretch, which is elite. For reference, that's better than Derrick Henry (3.11) and Jahmyr Gibbs (3.39) this season.
In the loss, Allen remained one of the bright spots for the Jets, rushing for a career-high 147 yards on a 7.0 yards-per-carry clip.
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
With Allen, a 2024 fourth-round pick, under team control through 2027 and on his rookie contract, Hall becomes an expendable piece that the Jets should exploit before the deadline.
When healthy, Hall is an electrifying piece out of the backfield, notching his first-ever 1,000-yard rushing season last year for the Jets. In three games this year, before missing time with this quad injury, he's posted modest numbers, totaling 265 yards from scrimmage. Still, he would garner plenty of interest on the trade market if New York puts him on the block, especially as he nears a return to the field. Despite not playing in Week 8, Hall was limited in practice all last week, signaling he's close.
There are a slew of teams interested in adding a back at the deadline, but the supply may be running thin. Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley have been two big names circulating in the rumor mill, but neither may end up being moved. The Eagles effectively shut down any talk of them moving Barkley, while the Colts are not actively shopping Taylor and would likely need to be blown away with an offer to deal him.
This creates quite the opportunity for the Jets to cash in with Hall. They could deal him to an RB-needy team, further strengthen their treasure trove of draft capital, and turn the keys of the backfield over to Allen permanently.  They'd also get out from under Hall's contract, which runs through 2028 and sees his base salary jump from $5.16 million in 2026 to $13.1 million in 2027 and $14.1 million in 2028.
It makes too much sense to explore a trade and ship Hall to the highest bidder.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Joe Burrow needed to throw it all over the yard in Cincinnati's overtime win over the Titans on Sunday. The Bengals quarterback was clutch down the stretch, throwing an 18-yard touchdown to Tee Higgins to tie the game at 36 with just over a minute left in regulation. Then, he scrambled for what proved to be the game-winning touchdown. Burrow became just the second player in NFL history with at least 450 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown in a game (Norm Van Brocklin, 1951).
Joe Burrow today (passing + rushing): - 472 total yards - 6 total touchdowns 📺 CBS & @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/OSGgAriSWT
Allgeier was the key cog in Arizona's upset win over the Cowboys in Dallas. Amid a quarterback change midgame as the Cardinals went from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew , Allgeier was the steady presence out of the backfield. His 63-yard touchdown run at the end of the third quarter began the late rally, and he had another explosive run (52 yards) that set up another touchdown. Allgeier is the first player this season with two rushes of 50-plus yards in a game.
Tyler Allgeier breaks free for a 63-yard rushing TD! AZvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PuMUPt7CLa
Bowers remains one of the biggest mismatches in the NFL and found paydirt twice in Las Vegas' victory over the Jets. This was his third career game with multiple touchdowns and his 11th career game with at least 90 yards receiving. That's tied for the second most by a tight end age 23 or younger.
Just throw it up to Brock Bowers LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3XvS9rjBy2
The Steelers defense smothered the Browns en route to a 27-6 win in Pittsburgh. Queen was key among the star figures on the defensive side of the ball, leading the team with 12 total tackles and accounting for 1.5 of the eight total sacks they piled up on Deshaun Watson . He also forced a fumble by Watson on Cleveland's second possession of the game, which set up a Steelers touchdown.
Sack and a fumble forced by the Steelers defense 😤 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gDaB2D1rl9
Anzalone was one of the early tone setters for the Buccaneers as the defense shut out the Falcons , 16-0. As a unit, they created four turnovers, all of which were interceptions by Michael Penix Jr . Anzalone tallied two of those picks, and each of them came in the first quarter.
Alex Anzalone intercepts Michael Penix Jr. for the second time in the first quarter ATLvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jWgIqEE7Ye
Tuten emerged from the Jaguars bye week and continued his ascent with a stellar two-touchdown showing in the blowout win over the Colts. The second-year back became the third player in franchise history with at least 100 yards rushing, 50 yards receiving and two total touchdowns in a game, joining Fred Taylor and Maurice Jones-Drew .
BHAYSHUL TUTEN RUNNING THROUGH DEFENDERS FOR A 39-YARD TD INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d2MvvxMdPw
All in all, Cam Ward had one of his better days as a pro, throwing for 304 yards and two touchdowns in a loss to Cincinnati. Despite that, he still showed some warts at the worst possible time. After Joe Burrow knotted the game at 36 apiece with just over a minute left in regulation, Ward led the offense to the Cincinnati 45-yard line, and it felt like the Titans were in a position to attempt a game-winning field goal.
However, after a seven-yard run to set up third-and-3, Ward did the only thing he couldn't do in that situation. The former No. 1 overall pick was sacked for a 13-yard loss, eliminating the possibility of a field goal attempt altogether.
Dexter Lawrence takes down Cam Ward for a sack in the final minute 💪 TENvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/V2ju4flSe1
Tennessee punted the ball away; the game eventually went to overtime, and the Bengals pulled off the victory.
Despite putting up 27 points in a win over the Browns, Steelers wideout DK Metcalf was essentially a non-factor, catching just one pass despite seeing a team-high six targets. Not only that, but he had one of the biggest gaffes of the slate in the third quarter. title: Five things we learned as Broncos stun Chiefs, seize first place in AFC West
summary: Denver's quarterback delivered another remarkable finish, while a vastly improved defense and two emerging running backs helped the Broncos take control of the AFC West
full_text:
The Broncos got one of the best wins by any team this season, coming back from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Chiefs 28-24. Denver got massive, heroic efforts from its offense and its defense, especially in the fourth quarter.
Sean Payton and the Broncos moved to the top of the AFC West at 6-2 and erased the head-to-head advantage the Chiefs had entering the game. The Broncos have won four straight games, surviving a brutal opening stretch; they have already faced the Chiefs (twice), the Jaguars , the Rams , the 49ers and the Seahawks . A winning record would have been a success, but 6-2 is a resounding one.
It's not just a big result for the division and potential playoff implications, but for what is says about both teams. Games like these -- postseason-caliber matchups -- teach us a lot about where both clubs are and where they could be headed. These are the five lessons we learned.
One didn't need to watch the first three quarters to comprehend how Bo Nix was playing. The boos on the broadcast told the story. Such is life for a quarterback: goat in the eyes of fans one minute, GOAT the next.
Entering the fourth quarter, Nix was 15-for-26 for 153 yards. Just seven of his 26 attempts had gone for first downs, including just one of eight on third down. It was ugly, and it looked like what Nix had put on display much of the year: very conservative, with little downfield. The boo birds were especially prominent when consecutive drives ended with punts after Nix completed short of the sticks on third down.
And then the fourth quarter came. Nix went 5-for-6 for 84 yards. Was it anything magical? No. But Nix took advantage of a pair of coverage busts in crucial moments. First, this touchdown to Nate Adkins :
Wide open 🙌 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/jvXNVepHSu
Then this quick pass to Jonah Coleman :
THE ROOK BREAKS FREE! 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/lC66or5Z0i
Since entering the NFL in 2024, Nix has ...
The Broncos have averaged 8.1 points per fourth quarter under Nix, the highest rate for any starting quarterback since at least 1950.
CBS' broadcast team of Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt explained that when they met with Nix, he couldn't explain his late-game exploits, but it's certainly better to start slow and finish strong than to start strong and finish slow. That much is true.
Of course, Nix owes the fact that he even has a chance in the games he starts slow to his defense being excellent. And it very much was Sunday. The last-second goal-line stand is what will get the most plaudits, but Denver's stout defense throughout the game was crucial.
That starts with stopping the run. In Week 1, Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards in a 31-10 Chiefs win. There were missed tackles all over the place -- 24 in total -- and just way too many wide-open holes. Walker had 7.8 yards per carry after contact in Week 1. In Week 8? There were still 16 missed tackles, but Walker had just 2.1 yards per carry after contact. He finished with just 69 yards total.
This has been a season-long improvement for Denver.
Yards after contact per rush
For an offensive-minded head coach with one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time, Andy Reid has had some extremely conservative moments as a coach. Sunday, he had another one. Up three with under three minutes left, Mahomes took a bad, bad sack. It wasn't a great play call, but we can't blame Reid for Mahomes taking a rare awful sack.
We can blame Reid for kicking on fourth and 8 from the Denver 36-yard line. Harrison Butker missed (very) wide right. He is now 2 for 7 from 50+ yards this year.
The execution of the play obviously wasn't what Reid had hoped for, but his thought process there is extremely poor. As I wrote in our weekly overreactions and reality checks:
Mahomes is actually better at converting fourth-and-8 to fourth-and-12 in his career (3 for 6 -- 50%) than Butker is at kicking from 50+ this year. So yes, even though fourth-and-8 looks bad, it might not have been. And Mahomes had been rolling all game. Speaking of ...
The Chiefs' collapse will overshadow an otherwise outstanding game from Mahomes. He was 30 for 41 for 321 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. He took just two sacks against a fearsome pass rush and made several terrific plays while under pressure. His 0.16 EPA per dropback was his best mark since Week 3 and, considering the opponent, it might have been his best game of the year.
On third downs, Mahomes was 6 for 10 for 113 yards and a touchdown. Four of his six completions went for first downs, including conversions of third-and-10 and third-and-12.
But the Chiefs must upgrade their receiving corps. The Chiefs' leading receiver was running back Emmett Johnson (more on him in a bit) with five catches for 128 yards. Tight end Travis Kelce had five catches for 67 yards. Wide receiver Rashee Rice had seven catches but for just 53 yards, and he is very much a quick-pass and YAC guy.
Ever since Tyquan Thornton's injury, Kansas City's deep passing game has evaporated. He has not had a single completion on a throw 20+ yards downfield in any of the past three games, since Thornton's injury. That's tied for the longest streak of his career. (He had seven in the three weeks before that, for comparison's sake.)
Whether it's a big name ( George Pickens , perhaps?) or a smaller one, Kansas City must add some downfield firepower. Rice doesn't provide it. Xavier Worthy , for all his speed, doesn't provide it. The rest of the guys are young late-round picks or former UDFAs. More downfield pop would help the run game, too.
Both the Broncos and the Chiefs added mid-round running backs in this year's draft. Both were expected to play complementary roles: The Broncos already had J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey , and the Chiefs already had Walker.
But it's clear that Jonah Coleman and Emmett Johnson deserve more love than the "complementary piece" title suggests. Coleman, in fact, led the Broncos in carries (11), rushing yards (41) and receiving yards (63). He also scored the game-winning touchdown. With Harvey out, he looks like a lead back.
JONAH COLEMAN GIVES THE BRONCOS THE LEAD KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uK6gM9pjU4
Johnson, meanwhile, also found the end zone. In addition to his 128 receiving yards, he had a 15-yard carry and a 44-yard kick return. He looked like Walker was making would-be tacklers miss on a consistent basis. This was an excellent play design, and look at how Johnson finishes it.
THE ROOKIE EMMETT JOHNSON WITH A 73-YARD TD KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sGCPC0rJYU
The Chiefs can't run Walker into the ground. Expect Johnson to continue to see significant action.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Andy Reid questions controversial false start that erased Chiefs' apparent winning TD
summary: A controversial false start on Jaylon Moore wiped out a go-ahead touchdown before Malcolm Roach sealed the win with a sack on Patrick Mahomes
full_text:
The Denver Broncos secured first place in the AFC West with a thrilling come-from-behind victory against the rival Kansas City Chiefs that required a goal-line stand.
After a 24-13 lead flipped to a 28-24 deficit in the fourth quarter, Patrick Mahomes took the Chiefs offense all the way down to the Broncos' 1-yard line with 15 seconds remaining. On second-and-goal, Mahomes couldn't find a receiver and threw the ball away. On third down, Kenneth Walker III was stuffed by JL Skinner -- who made a fantastic tackle. That set up a fourth-and-1 for the game.
It appeared Mahomes hit Rashee Rice across the middle for the game-winning touchdown -- but there was a flag on the field. The officials called a false start on right tackle Jaylon Moore . That moved the Chiefs five yards back to the 6-yard line, where Mahomes was sacked by Malcolm Roach to end the game.
PATRICK MAHOMES TO RASHEE RICE FALSE START 77 pic.twitter.com/Anx556Z2bG
This was a controversial penalty for a couple of different reasons. It looked like Moore shifted in his stance just a bit with 10 seconds remaining on the play clock. Then, he turned his head to the left. Which action drew the whistle?
In his postgame press conference, Chiefs coach Andy Reid was asked about the false start. He simply said he didn't see it.
"I didn't see it," Reid said with a chuckle. "But that's one man's opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn't see a false start."
Moore wasn't sure if he committed a penalty either when speaking to reporters in the locker room.
"I mean I've got to go back and look at it, still haven't got a chance to look at it," Moore said. "But regardless, I've just got to be better."
Moore's alleged misstep wasn't the only reason the Chiefs lost on Sunday. Earlier in the fourth quarter, when the Chiefs were up, 24-21, Mahomes took an avoidable sack on a third-and-2. Reid decided to send kicker Harrison Butker out to attempt a 54-yard field goal instead of punting the ball or going for it. Butker missed wide right, and the Broncos scored what ended up being the game-winning touchdown just two plays later.
The Chiefs have now lost two straight games following their 5-0 start. Sunday marked Mahomes' third career loss when holding a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter, including playoffs. He's now 80-3 in those situations.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Former Cowboys QB rips Dallas for 'embarrassing' loss to Cardinals: 'They stink'
summary: The loss was bad enough, but the way the Cowboys crumbled did not sit well with the 2020 draft pick
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have never won a game against the Arizona Cardinals inside AT&T Stadium. With their Week 8 loss, they fell to 0-5 in such contests. The 33-30 overtime defeat was undoubtedly the most disappointing result of the bunch. In fact, former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci chalked it up as an "embarrassing" loss.
Despite holding a 10-point lead with 3:54 to play in regulation, the Cowboys lost for the third time in the last four weeks. They led by as many as 14 points in the fourth quarter and for the first time this century lost a home game with that kind of late advantage. They had won each of their last 69 such games. It was as disheartening of a showing as any across the NFL .
"This was absolutely embarrassing today," DiNucci said on CBS Sports HQ . "They stink. I'm lost for words, honestly. They have so much talent on both sides of the ball, and year after year, week after week, all we see is just letdowns from them. I'm not sure what needs to change. … But at some point, the same old, same old in Dallas for the Cowboys, it's not cutting it. Something needs to change. Somebody needs to look themselves in the mirror. I don't know who it is, but that was an embarrassing loss for them."
Dallas was fortunate to even have a second chance at winning the game in overtime, because if not for a missed extra point on the Cardinals' final touchdown, they would have almost certainly lost in regulation.
Adding insult to injury, Arizona sparked its comeback with a backup quarterback. Gardner Minshew entered in relief of Jacoby Brissett and instantly elevated the offense with some help from running back Tyler Allgeier . What's more, the Cardinals may be destined to finish the year in last place in the NFC West. That is the caliber of opponent the Cowboys need to defeat in order to accomplish their goal of winning their own division, which remains fully up for grabs.
"It comes down to effort for the Dallas Cowboys," DiNucci said. "When you turn on the tape week in and week out -- and I honestly hate questioning guys' effort in the NFL because all of us understand what goes on on a day-to-day and week-to-week basis inside those locker rooms and organizations -- but the effort is not there for the Cowboys. You never know what team you're getting week in and week out. You can tell run play from pass play based on what effort guys are giving on offense."
The changes that DiNucci called for might not include a coaching change. Team owner Jerry Jones indicated that firing Brian Schottenheimer in the middle of the season is not on the table. If not that, then what? There are only so many ways to spark a meaningful turnaround when a team is seemingly at rock bottom.
DiNucci understands the pressure that comes with wearing the Cowboys star, having spent the 2020 and 2021 seasons as the team's backup quarterback, and he said the star veterans need to step up and change the culture.
"At some point, something inside that locker room needs to change," DiNucci said. "The leaders, whoever it is: Dak Prescott , Quinnen Williams , CeeDee Lamb . Whoever it is, somebody needs to take control of that locker room and say, 'Guys, whatever we're doing right now is simply not working. We need to scrap this thing. We need to ignore the outside noise.'
"I think a lot of the problem in Dallas is there's so much going on outside the game of football there. It's hard for guys to compartmentalize football from what's going on off the field. I can say that. I was there for a couple of years. I saw it firsthand on Mondays and Tuesdays; when I'm working out on off days, they're running tours through the facility, letting people see us work out and meetings and this and that. There's just a lot that comes with being a Dallas Cowboys football player, and I wonder if that at some point starts to take a toll on guys."
There are a few get-right opportunities in the near future for Dallas with the Indianapolis Colts , Tennessee Titans and Philadelphia Eagles representing three of their next four opponents. If a week off is what this team needs, though, that will not come until a Week 14 bye.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Andy Reid backs decision to trust Harrison Butker despite Chiefs kicker's struggles
summary: Butker's late miss helped give Denver an opportunity to complete its comeback and intensified questions about Kansas City's kicker situation
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs have a kicker problem. Harrison Butker missed yet another kick on Sunday, a 54-yarder that would have extended Kansas City's lead over the division rival Denver Broncos to six points but instead set up the game-winning touchdown drive by Denver.
The Chiefs led by three points when they drove down to the Denver 30-yard line and faced third-and-2 from there. Patrick Mahomes dropped back to pass, but he was sacked for a six-yard loss, which turned what would have been a 48-yard field goal attempt into a 54-yarder, and Butker missed his kick wide to the right.
The kick is no good and the Broncos will take over down 3 👀 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VRZzs9NNwG
It was the third significant miss in two weeks for Butker, whose job already appeared to be on thin ice after the Chiefs signed former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad earlier this week. Tucker had been out of the league since 2024 after he was accused by multiple women of sexual misconduct, as originally reported by The Baltimore Banner . After the game, Andy Reid defended the decision to send Butker out to try the deep field goal attempt.
"Those are hindsight. It ended up being what it was," Reid said, via FOX 4 Kansas City . "But it's within Harrison's range."
Here's the thing, though: 54 yards isn't really within Butker's range anymore. It may have been during his prime, but these days, he is not nearly consistent enough from that distance to justify trying that kick.
Here's what we wrote just last week , for example, when Butker missed a pair of field goal attempts in the Chiefs' loss to the Seattle Seahawks :
Through 2023, he made 89.1% of his total field goals, and 28 of 40 (70%) from beyond 50 yards. Since then, though, Butker has made just 82.2% of his kicks, and only 8-of-18 (44.4%) from beyond 50 yards. He missed one of those 50-plus-yard kicks short by several yards in this game, making him just 1-of-5 from 50-plus this year, and he missed another from 45 yards out, pushing it wide to the right.
Whether you agree with the decision to kick the field goal or not, it's clear that the Chiefs can't trust Butker in big spots anymore. And that means his time with the Chiefs could soon be coming to an end, whether Kansas City turns to Tucker or somebody else.
author: Jared Dubin

title: NFL Week 8 winners and losers: Cowboys suffer epic collapse, Joe Burrow delivers historic heroics
summary: Burrow produced a historic six-touchdown performance, while the Cowboys squandered a late lead and the Ravens endured another devastating Lamar Jackson injury
full_text:
Many weeks in such an unpredictable league as the NFL , the football world witnesses something so historically improbable that it is difficult to believe. There were two such occurrences in Week 8, with the Dallas Cowboys enduring as miserable a fourth-quarter and overtime sequence as any in the last 25 years of franchise history and Joe Burrow delivering a stat line that no other quarterback has posted since the merger.
The highs of Burrow's career day and the lows of the Cowboys ' blown lead exemplified everything that makes the NFL such a successful entertainment product. What more could fans seek than late-game drama and excellence from the greatest football players in the world?
Of course, there are two sides to every outcome. The Arizona Cardinals celebrated at the Cowboys' expense. The Tennessee Titans were left bewildered by the quarterbacking they witnessed from their opponent.
Here are the biggest winners and losers from Week 8 in the NFL.
Brian Schottenheimer left his offense on the field on fourth-and-1 from his own 32-yard line in the first quarter, and the Cowboys turned the ball over on downs. That was the first sign that Sunday was not going to be their day. Coaching and offense failed them in that moment, and the defense failed them the rest of the afternoon in surrendering 33 points to the Cardinals in a stunning three-point overtime loss. The same defense that has not held a single opponent under 20 points all year, that is.
At home against a Cardinals team that might finish the year at the bottom of the NFC West, the Cowboys blew a 10-point lead with 3:54 to play in regulation and gave up a game-ending field goal in overtime. They were fortunate to even get to the extra period, because it took an Arizona missed extra point with six seconds remaining for regulation to end level at 30-30.
Arizona is now 5-0 all-time at AT&T Stadium. This loss for the Cowboys stings as much as any of the previous four. The most painful part might be that the 30 points they allowed in the second half and overtime came with backup quarterback Gardner Minshew on the field for Arizona. Or maybe it is the unfathomable splits in two-score games, where since 2000, the Cardinals were 1-174-1 when trailing by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter and the Cowboys were 69-0 at home when leading by 14 or more in the fourth ( according to ESPN Insights ). If they cannot close out a game against that kind of opponent, then the Cowboys essentially cannot be trusted against anyone.
Ideally for the Cincinnati Bengals , they would not have needed Burrow to shoulder such a heavy load against the Titans. Their opponent, after all, entered Week 8 with just one win. It was one of those situations, though, where they should have felt fortunate to have such a premier quarterback on their side, because most signal-callers are not capable of playing hero to the degree Burrow did in a 43-36 overtime triumph. The three-time Pro Bowler became the second quarterback in NFL history with 450 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown in the same game and the first such player in 75 years.
Joe Burrow today (passing + rushing): - 472 total yards - 6 total touchdowns 📺 CBS & @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/OSGgAriSWT
To be clear, Burrow would have been a major reason why the Bengals lost had they come up short. He threw three interceptions. However, the Cincinnati defense mostly stood tall after those turnovers and limited the damage to just one field goal. In essence, Tennessee only gained one net point off of turnovers, because one of its ensuing possessions resulted in a safety.
The five touchdowns matched a career high. The 462 passing yards were his third-most in a game.
The last thing the Baltimore Ravens could have expected when they reinserted Lamar Jackson into the starting lineup was that Joe Fagnano would wind up spending more time under center than any other quarterback on the roster. A pair of injuries thrust the undrafted rookie into action, however, as the Ravens lost Jackson to a thumb injury and backup signal-caller Tyler Huntley to a toe issue. Fagnano was the Ravens' emergency third quarterback and shockingly made his NFL debut in the second quarter of the 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills .
To lose Jackson on his very first play back from a sprained ankle is the most cruel luck possible for a Baltimore offense that desperately needs him to stay healthy. The unit has not scored more than 13 points in any of its last three games, all losses. A team with Super Bowl aspirations now stands at .500 and in last place in the AFC North, and with Jackson out for at least four weeks as he undergoes surgery , it will be difficult to turn things around.
The moral of Sean Payton's tenure with the Denver Broncos is that if his team is in a close game, it is destined to win. The Broncos' 28-24 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs marked their 15th consecutive win in one-score games dating back to last season, which tied the NFL regular-season record. They are also now 5-0 in games decided by seven points or fewer this year alone, which matches the best record through Week 8 since 2000.
It takes immense clutch fourth-quarter efforts to stay unbeaten in tight situations, and the Broncos displayed plenty of timely play in their latest triumph. They trailed the Chiefs by 11 points with just under nine minutes to play and scored a pair of touchdowns to take the decisive lead. They received a bit of help in the way of a Harrison Butker missed field goal, but they also stepped up on both sides of the ball on their own and ended the game with a fourth-and-goal sack of Patrick Mahomes .
The Broncos’ win probability fell to 10.2% early in the fourth quarter and was just 11.9% with 2:44 left in regulation in their comeback win over the Chiefs. Denver’s chances of winning the AFC West are now 64%. With a loss, they would have been 24%. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/yTc9UFmuQx
That was far from the first time the Broncos grasped victory from the claws of defeat during the 15-game streak. At this point, it is hard to say it will be the last.
Who needs completed passes? The 1974 Bills did not, and neither did the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8. Those are the last two teams to win a game without a single completion. Baker Mayfield went 0-for-3 in the Buccaneers' 16-0 shutout victory over the Atlanta Falcons. The run game did all the work with Bucky Irving racking up 170 yards and the game's lone touchdown and Kenneth Gainwell adding 139 yards. Mayfield scampered for 14 of his own.
Tampa Bay is now on a two-game winning streak with a total of 59 points in that span. Mayfield completed only seven throws for 64 yards in the previous victory.
The quarterback on the other sideline had an even worse day. Michael Penix Jr . completed just eight of his 24 attempts and threw four interceptions. Two of those picks came in the first quarter when Alex Anzalone came down with both of them, and by halftime, Penix had more turnovers than completions. He ended the day with more interceptions than in any game of his college or professional careers.
Mostly to blame for the offensive disaster was the torrential downpour that persisted throughout the contest in Tampa Bay.
This is how bad the rain is coming down here. Could be a long nasty game in Tampa. #Falcons pic.twitter.com/Hu4nc0C0cp
It took two months for the obligatory reminder to arrive: The 1972 Dolphins are the only team in NFL history to complete an undefeated season. They will continue to stand alone. The Minnesota Vikings lost on Sunday, and thus there are no unbeaten teams left. The NFC North leaders entered the week at 6-0 and as the only perfect squad in the league and left it with a divisional loss to the Detroit Lions . They fell, 19-15, in another one of their patented defensive battles.
Could the Vikings make a play for a quarterback at the trade deadline? This loss exemplified how the lack of a proficient offense…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Week 8 overreactions: Time for Vikings to bench Kyler Murray? Colts should fire Steichen?
summary: Plus, does the NFC South run through the Buccaneers?
full_text:
For much of the first seven weeks of the season, the predominant question around the Minnesota Vikings was: "Can they really keep winning this way?"
And the answer was yes, six times over. Sure, Minnesota's 10 touchdowns were the fewest by any 6-0 team in more than 100 years, but wins are wins, and Minnesota was stacking them.
This week, that ended. The Lions grounded out an impressive 19-15 win, a crucial result in the cutthroat NFC North. Jahmyr Gibbs had 168 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown, and Jared Goff gutted through a tough day overall to throw the game-winning touchdown to Jameson Williams .
There were major, uncomfortable questions during the Vikings' winning streak. Those questions just came to the forefront even more with a loss, and the Vikings must find answers immediately. The most important question revolves around the most important position.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
I gave Murray a lot of grace early this year. He was on a new team and in a new system. He suffered a concussion moments into his Vikings debut. It was about as inauspicious a start as possible, and even as he struggled after he returned, I was willing to give him some time to figure it out.
That time is over. Murray was dreadful again Sunday: 17-for-29 for 210 yards, one touchdown and one interception, with three sacks taken. He also ran four times for 35 yards, which was a team high (more on that in a bit). His touchdown pass was a miraculous Justin Jefferson catch.
JUSTIN JEFFERSON OH MY MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DUTDY0f59E
But Murray was so wildly inaccurate that he often didn't even give his teammates chances to make otherworldly catches or routine catches. According to TruMedia, five of Murray's 29 passes (17.2%) were off-target. He missed Jefferson up the seam on what would have been a touchdown. He missed Jefferson on a rollout, firing the ball several feet above his superstar wide receiver. He dirtied a ball when Jefferson was open on a slant, a play that left Jefferson shrugging as if to say, "What happened?"
Then, there are far too many throws that have an extremely low likelihood of being completed anyway. He throws a ton of perimeter passes that are 50/50 balls at best, and usually, they're closer to 10/90 balls because Murray is so inaccurate on those, too.
He also rarely finds or takes easy answers. His 3.20 average time to throw is by far the highest of his career, even though he is also having the slowest time to pressure this season. Only three players — Caleb Williams , Malik Willis and Drake Maye — have a longer time to throw, on average. But Murray isn't the playmaker or physical force Williams or Maye are.
It's a huge surprise to see Murray play this poorly. Even at his worst in Arizona, he was an average or slightly below average quarterback by most metrics. But this season, he has been so much worse than he's ever been.
Kyler Murray career worsts this season
Murray's mobility and pocket management have declined, too. He can still move as a runner, but his sack rate and sack-to-pressure rates are way up.
Simply put, it's time for the Vikings to look elsewhere, whether that's in-house ( Carson Wentz is the backup) or via a trade. Frustration is bubbling up — Jefferson declined to speak to the media after Sunday's game — and in his postgame press conference, Kevin O'Connell mentioned multiple missed opportunities.
#Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell on getting Kyler Murray comfortable in the offense: “I don’t necessarily believe it’s going to be one tell all thing. I think it’s how we continue to put together the plan of where he’s most comfortable in his alignment, then marrying the offense from… pic.twitter.com/Cf3RjlWVc1
O'Connell can only do so much, though. Murray hasn't been close to good enough for a team with a championship-level defense, and Minnesota simply can't keep the status quo much longer.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
The Colts played one of the worst excuses you'll see for a football game Sunday, falling to the Jaguars 42-7. Indianapolis' first-half drive chart was as follows:
Trevor Lawrence threw for 210 yards and three touchdowns on 14 attempts, a ridiculous 15 yards per attempt — the highest rate by any quarterback in any game (min. 10 attempts) in the last two seasons. The Jaguars also averaged 5.5 yards per carry, and only one of their 33 carries went for negative yards.
The offense was similarly embarrassing.
The trick play goes awry and the Jaguars get it back! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AinguLvhQi
Yes, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner this week and fired GM Chris Ballard the week before. Yes, the season has gone off the rails. But the Titans traded Jeffery Simmons this week and took the Bengals to overtime. The Colts, on the other hand, didn't look interested in playing. This wasn't acceptable in any way, shape or form, and it falls on Shane Steichen.
One issue in the Colts’ locker room right now is a lack of players with the standing to check their teammates and keep it real. Jonathan Taylor is trying, but he isn’t naturally a vocal leader. I commend his effort here. pic.twitter.com/xbXVJwHlSQ
Speaking of Taylor, the Colts reportedly aren't actively shopping him , but not trading him would be a massive mistake. Indianapolis is facing a multi-year rebuild. They have no competent quarterback and likely no way to find one in the draft due to the Sauce Gardner trade. Taylor is reportedly commanding significant offers. The Vikings would be a great fit, as their running game continues to stink.
Indianapolis must move their star running back, and it must move on from Steichen, too. If not, it's a damning mismanagement by Carlie Irsay-Gordon at an absolutely critical junction early in her ownership.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Just kidding! But boy, a 27-6 loss was a rough dose of reality for the Browns , who haven't won a regular-season game at the Steelers since 2003.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Speaking of a rough dose of reality for the Browns, Watson was once again pretty poor Sunday. Though the passing box score stats look good (27-for-39, 324 yards), he took eight sacks. He has now taken 22 sacks in his last four games, a completely unsustainable number. This has been an issue throughout his time in Cleveland, and after a better start to the year avoiding sacks, he has fallen back significantly. He has had a negative EPA per play in three of his past four games, too.
But the Browns don't have a better answer. Shedeur Sanders had major sack problems last year. The offensive line is in rough shape. Watson may be back on his downward trajectory, but Cleveland is still 5-3, and Watson has had some good moments in clutch time. All five of the Browns' wins are by four points or fewer. Plus, there's not a better alternative. If there were, Sanders would be starting.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Baker Mayfield did not complete a single pass in the Buccaneers ' 16-0 win over the Falcons on Sunday, a game played in an absolutely downpour. Let's take a little history lesson.
Mayfield only attempted three passes. The week before, he only attempted 11 (completing seven) in a 43-13 domination of the Panthers . Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards in that game.
The Buccaneers cannot win this way forever, clearly. But they don't have to be that far off. The offensive line has really come together after a rocky start, and Bucky Irving looks absolutely excellent. The bigger factor here is the defense, which held Michael Penix Jr . to 8-for-24 passing for 125 yards and four(!) interceptions.
WIDE OPEN JACOB PARRISH ‼️ 📺: #ATLvsTB on FOX pic.twitter.com/LcZ3BpvEul
Penix was absolutely atrocious, but this isn't a one-off occurrence. Tampa Bay absolutely dominated Carolina with a relentless pass rush the week before, and this defense has been stupendous all season:
It's not like the bar is that high in the NFC South, and the…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Why is Ashton Jeanty not getting carries? Another Raider emerges as Vegas' top RB in Week 8
summary: Jeanty's rushing workload continues to decrease on a weekly basis
full_text:
This is not how Ashton Jeanty was supposed to develop when the Las Vegas Raiders made him the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft . The former Heisman Trophy finalist projected as an eventual superstar, but to reach that heralded potential, he needs to improve upon his play in 2026. Not only is Jeanty on pace to regress statistically from his promising rookie year, but he is also experiencing a role decrease.
The Raiders got into a shootout with the New York Jets in Week 8, yet Jeanty carried the ball just twice in the 38-33 win. He saw a greater workload as a receiver with three catches on four targets than he did as a rusher. The five total touches were the fewest of his young career.
Jeanty's downturn in opportunities is a trend. He opened the season with a fantastic effort against the Miami Dolphins and amassed 102 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns across 29 touches. Since then, his carry total has diminished on a weekly basis. It reached a new low on Sunday when Mike Washington Jr. , conversely, set a career high with 38 snaps.
The road game at MetLife Stadium also marked the first time this season that Washington started over Jeanty.
"That's my call," Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said postgame of the snap distribution at running back. "Ashton's still going to be a big part of our team. He had a huge catch. He's going to be a huge part of our run game going forward. We just wanted to give Mike a few more opportunities today. I think both of those guys are going to be a huge part of our rushing and passing success moving forward."
It is more than just the reduction in opportunities that contributes to Jeanty's underwhelming sophomore NFL campaign. He is not nearly as efficient of a runner as he was last year, either. Jeanty averages 0.6 fewer yards per carry in 2026 than in 2025. His success rate is nearly identical to a year ago, but the overall yardage simply is not there. And he is on pace to come up shy of last season's five rushing touchdowns despite playing on a much higher-scoring offense.
It's possible the offensive revitalization (and the coaching behind it) is the crux of this downturn. Jeanty remains the same highly skilled ball carrier who was nearly untackleable at Boise State, but this is now his fifth consecutive year with a new play caller dating back to his freshman year with the Broncos.
His running style seems to clash with Kubiak's system, and he now plays for a coach who has a history of splitting carries rather than utilizing a bellcow back.
"We won," Jeanty said to ESPN . "It doesn't matter how I feel about how [many] times I get the ball. Whatever it takes for the team to win, I just want to win. That's all."
This week's dramatic reduction in carries did not have anything to do with the comments Jeanty made ahead of the game about the Jets' defense, Kubiak said. During a locker room media availability at the Raiders' facility, Jeanty took a dig at individual players on the opposing team.
"I think we can definitely get the run game going, get back on track and just really get after these guys," Jeanty said . "Couple guys out that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."
That remark was widely received as being in poor taste. Former Jets coach Rex Ryan was among those who called Jeanty out for taking a dig at the New York defense.
Rex Ryan on Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty saying that there are a couple of Jets who look like they don’t want to tackle: pic.twitter.com/zoXmTnwQpK
Jeanty said after the game that the coaching staff gave him advance notice that he would receive fewer touches in Week 8 than in previous games, but he said he did not know whether the comments were the reason behind that decision.
While Kubiak said Jeanty's two carries were not the result of discipline, the timing of that role reduction and his comments about the Jets' defense do indicate that they could be related. It is also entirely possible that the coaching staff simply felt Washington gave them a better chance to beat New York as a ball carrier. Even if it was a one-game situation, a rebound in opportunities next week may not take Jeanty all the way back to his Week 1 workload or that of his rookie season. There is enough of a sample size beyond this one game to suggest the Raiders would prefer to use him more sparingly.
Kubiak did not say whether Sunday's roles — with Washington as the early-down back and Jeanty entering on third downs and passing situations ‚ would continue. Instead, he said that the staff would review the film and that it has "two runners that we believe in."
Barring any changes, Jeanty will be more of a receiving threat than a rushing threat. That is a job he can specialize in, as he proved in Week 1 when he scored two receiving touchdowns and in the seven following games when he crossed the 50-yard mark four times. But it is not remotely what he was drafted to be. As one of the top running back prospects of the decade, if not the absolute best, Jeanty figured to become an every-down featured back.
As Washington continues to carve out a job of his own, this could also trend more toward how Kubiak deployed Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet during his tenure as the Seattle Seahawks ' offensive coordinator. He essentially used them as co-starters and schemed up opportunities for Walker to thrive in space while using Charbonnet on inside runs, in pass protection and as a red-zone weapon. Jeanty would fit the Walker mold with Washington playing more a la Charbonnet.
The best-case outcome is that Jeanty improves his per-snap efficiency, makes the most of a smaller workload and flirts with the same rushing numbers that made his 2026 season a promising one. Paired with the clear year-over-year uptick in production as a receiver, that would make him a well-rounded and highly impactful running back.
But if Jeanty keeps picking up only 3.1 yards per carry, he may cede further touches to Washington and settle in as a passing-game specialist. That would be a monumental disappointment given the investment the Raiders made in him at the draft.

title: Why Jerry Jones 'doesn't see' firing Brian Schottenheimer midseason after disaster Cowboys loss to Cardinals
summary: Dallas squandered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead in its overtime loss to Arizona, but Jones says he is not considering an in-season coaching change
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys (3-5) did the unthinkable in their 33-30 overtime home defeat against the Arizona Cardinals (3-5).
Dallas led by 14 points twice, including 24-10 with 14:20 left to play, yet still lost. Sunday marked the first loss in Cowboys history when Dallas led by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter. Previously, the Cowboys were 202-0-1 at home when leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter, including the playoffs. Dallas' five games with 30-plus points are tied for the most in the NFL with the Buffalo Bills (6-1), but the Cowboys joined the Houston Texans (2-5) as the only two teams with multiple losses when scoring 30 or more points in 2026. The Cowboys defense has now allowed 20-or-more points in 15 consecutive games, which is the longest active streak in the entire league.
What does that mean for Brian Schottenheimer? Jerry Jones faced those questions head-on when speaking immediately after Sunday's grisly loss.
"Yeah, we're not going to get into anything. That's not in my mind at this time. But the main thing that's in my mind is we tee it up for those kinds of spots to win it," Jones said when asked about a coaching change. "We really do want those situations to call for it, bring it on. And we got it and didn't get it. ... None of us are getting it done, and that should be my concern. So I'm not pointing at Schotty. I'm not pointing to anybody, but none of us have it done. I haven't been involved in too many games that we should have wanted, and we had the opportunities we had to win this game. So that is a big snapshot that we want to put above our mirror."
Jones has only made one in-season coaching change in his 38 years owning the Cowboys, and that was when he fired Wade Phillips during the 2010 season. Schottenheimer won't be joining Phillips on that list at this time.
"I made a change, and I don't want to mention it because I'm not proud of it," Jones said. "But I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season, and I don't see that here."
Dallas is 10-14-1 in the Schottenheimer era and has yet to put together a winning streak in 2026. Jones, however, pointed fingers at everyone and not just his coach.
"It just really is glaring in a negative way how we could be where we were and end up losing that ball game," Jones said. "We had a great chance right at the end to win the game, and had everybody out there that can win games for us, and of course. didn't get it done. So it was a couple of games within the game really that was also telling, and we just just did not play well enough at all to win that ball game. Not well enough after you had the lead the way we did and had the opportunities we had to win that ball game. So it's an indictment of the whole show."
Despite the lack of consistency under Schottenheimer, firing Schottenheimer during the 2026 isn't on his mind at the moment because he feels the inconsistency this season has to do with the entire organization, not just the head coach.
"Well, I will say that a lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said. "So for whatever criticism we want to have with Brian, we can all get in line. And that was a total team loss to use a cliche. That was a total team effort out there for us. And we have to be better for our fans, have to be better than that when we got our hands on the win and then drop the ball."
Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott was quick to point fingers at himself and many others in addition to the criticism for Schottenheimer.
"It's all of us," he said. "Don't put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that's weak. I think that's cowardice. "This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It's never just one person's fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it's never just truly one  person's fault. And so, don't take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us, and it's about us backing him up and  backing one another up and we'll have to show it."
Schottenheimer himself took accountability for the defeat but also deflected to the positive takeaways from Sunday's overtime loss.
"I'm going to always own my part of this as a head football coach. It starts with me and there's certainly things that I need to do better," Schottenheimer said. "But as a football team in all three phases, I can point out three, four, five, six plays right off the top of my head; I'm not going to, about that. And so, a lot of football left, and again, no different than Philadelphia, where you have to come out of that game and say, okay, hey, we didn't reinvent the game. You got to come out of this game and find the positives. There's going to be positives, the way we played in the first half. Quinnen Williams got some pass rush. So  that's what we'll do."
Defensively, Dallas' defense allowed backup quarterback Gardner Minshew to come off the Cardinals' bench to become the first player in the NFL this season with at least three passing touchdowns in the fourth quarter of a game. Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier exploded for 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns with a career-high 147 yards rushing on just 11 carries. He ran for a 63-yard score and also added a 52-yard run down the left sideline. That made him the first player in the entire league in 2026 with multiple 50-yard runs in the same game.

title: Bengals wild overtime win ends with final score that's never happened before in NFL history
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, we have a scorigami!
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals and Tennessee Titans played one of the wildest games of Week 8, and it ended with the two teams combining to make some NFL history. The Bengals beat the Titans 43-36, which is notable because that exact score had never happened before in the 107-year history of the NFL.
With under four minutes left to play, it didn't look like the scorigami would happen. The Titans were leading 36-29, and if that had been the final score, it wouldn't have been a first-time final score. Enter Joe Burrow . The Bengals quarterback engineered an 81-yard scoring drive that was capped by an 18-yard pass to Tee Higgins that tied the game with just 1:17 left to play.
Once the game got to overtime, Burrow was at it again. The Bengals got the ball first, and Burrow immediately led them down the field for a touchdown. Burrow went 4-of-4 for 51 yards before capping the drive with a nine-yard TD run that put the Bengals ahead 43-36, which officially gave us the 1,098th unique final score in NFL history.
TEN 36 - CIN 43 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1098th unique score in NFL history, and the 3rd of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/oRigwLSJDE
Burrow did throw three interceptions against the Titans, but he also became just the SECOND PLAYER in NFL history with at least 450 passing yards, five touchdown passes and one rushing TD in a single game. Overall, Burrow ended up throwing for 462 yards to go along with his five touchdowns.
Burrow utilized his two favorite weapons, Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, both going off for more than 140 yards.
As for the scorigami, you usually need something crazy to happen to get a final score that the NFL has never seen before, and that happened here. With the game tied at 21, the Bengals picked up a safety in the third quarter that gave them a 23-21 lead. That got the ball rolling on our bizarre score.
The Titans scored a touchdown to go up 28-23, and the Bengals followed that up by getting their own score to retake the lead at 29-28. On Cincinnati's touchdown, the Bengals went for two but didn't convert.
For the Bengals, this marked their first scorigami in four years. The last one they were involved in came back in 2022 when they beat Bill Belichick's Patriots 22-18. On Tennessee's end, this marked the Titans' first scorigami since 2020 when they beat the Lions 45-26.
Overall, this was the third scorigami of the 2026 season, but the first two both happened back in Week 1 , so it had been nearly two months since we had gotten a new final score in the NFL. As more final scores get knocked off the list, scorigamis become rarer, so there's no guarantee we'll see one again this season. Last year, there were just four scorigamis, so just one more in 2026 will match that total.

title: Lions' Jack Campbell placed on backboard, carted off field after suffering serious injury
summary: The All-Pro linebacker suffered what appeared to be a serious injury vs. the Vikings
full_text:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field after appearing to suffer a serious injury during the team's Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings .
Following the 19-15 victory, Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters he had no further information on Jack's status, other than that he was receiving medical care. He stayed in the hospital overnight for evaluation, and the team announced it would provide more information when it had it available.
On the first play of the fourth quarter, Campbell and teammate Eric O'Neill combined to tackle Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson . Campbell then went limp. While lying prone, Campbell was not seen moving before trainers reached him. After about 10 minutes, Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field.
Prayers up for Jack Campbell. pic.twitter.com/dZsTw6zEj1
The Lions announced that Campbell was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.
It was an emotional scene at Ford Field. The entire Lions team went over to see their teammate off, while the defense gathered for a moment to rally after seeing one of their leaders go down.
The Lions defense takes a moment after Jack Campbell was carted off. @ErinAndrews has more. pic.twitter.com/uvy9PfrITI
In seven games this season, Campbell recorded 57 tackles, two QB hits and a fumble recovery. Just six months ago, he signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL .
Campbell was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Iowa, just six selections after the Lions drafted running back Jahmyr Gibbs . The 26-year-old had a career year in 2025, recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended. He was named a First Team All-Pro and earned his first Pro Bowl bid.

title: Lamar Jackson headed for injured reserve: Ravens QB to undergo surgery after injuring thumb vs. Bills
summary: Jackson made his first start on Sunday after missing the last three games
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens probably feel like they're living in a nightmare right now. In Lamar Jackson's return to the field on Sunday, the two-time NFL MVP got knocked out of the game after suffering a thumb injury on Baltimore's first offensive play against the Buffalo Bills .
Following the Ravens' 36-10 loss, the news went from bad to worse with head coach Jesse Minter revealing that Jackson would be placed on injured reserve.
"That will be a surgery deal," Minter said . "He'll go to IR."
Putting Jackson on IR means he'll miss at least four games. Here's a look at Baltimore's upcoming schedule:
Week 9: Jaguars (Thursday night) Week 10: Chargers Week 11: at Panthers Week 12: at Texans Week 13: Bye Week 14: Buccaneers
With Jackson now on injured reserve, the earliest he can return is for that Week 14 game against the Bucs on Dec. 13. Jackson has already missed three games this season due to injury, and this will bring his total to at least seven.
The thumb injury happened on Baltimore's first offensive play of the game. On a first-and-10 play, Jackson threw a pass to Zay Flowers , but as he threw the ball, his hand hit a defender's arm, and after that happened, Jackson was in immediate pain.
Lamar Jackson heads to the locker room after his first pass attempt with an apparent hand injury. pic.twitter.com/JVUQYjJV8H
Jackson clearly didn't feel right, because he quickly ran to the sideline, and at that point, the Ravens' training staff took him into Baltimore's locker room at Highmark Stadium.
The showdown between Jackson and Josh Allen was supposed to be one of the highlights in Week 8, but instead, it turned into a blowout win for Buffalo after Jackson left the game.
The Ravens have already played three games without Jackson this year, and if those were any indication, things could get ugly over the next few weeks.
With Jackson on the field during their first four games, the Ravens averaged 29.8 points per game while going 3-1. However, with Jackson out over the past three weeks, they went just 1-2 while averaging just 17.7 points per game. And now, you can add another loss to that tally in a game where the Ravens managed to score just 10 points.
For Thursday's game against Jacksonville, it's still not clear who the starting QB will be. Not only did Jackson get hurt, but Tyler Huntley also had to leave the game after injuring his toe. If Huntley isn't ready to return, that means QB Joe Fagnano will be getting the first start of his career.
Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn, went 10-of-12 for 91 yards with an interception while playing about 2.5 quarters against the Bills.
For Jackson, there's no guarantee that he'll return as soon as he's eligible to come off IR. A thumb injury on the right hand is a brutal one for a quarterback because it impacts their ability to grip the football. Jackson will need that to fully heal before he can return, and since he has to undergo surgery, he likely won't be back on the field until late December.
At 4-4, the Ravens will need to keep their head above water until then, or it could be a lost season for Baltimore.

title: Baker Mayfield, Buccaneers complete win against Falcons with statistics not seen since 1933
summary: Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield didn't complete any of his three throws in a 16-0 win
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) pulled off a 16-0, rain-soaked home victory against the Atlanta Falcons (3-5) on Sunday with a method not seen since 1945.
With quarterback Baker Mayfield not completing any of his three passes, the Buccaneers are now the first team with no completions in a game since the 1974 Buffalo Bills , who won their completion-less game 16-12 against the New York Jets . Tampa Bay is also the first team since the 1945 Pittsburgh Steelers to win a game by double digits without having a completion. Those Steelers beat the Cardinals 23-0 in that game. Finally, the Buccaneers became the first team to produce no completions and over 300 yards rushing (324) in a game since the Boston Braves, now the Washington Commanders , in 1933.
Mayfield returned from a three-game absence because of a right thumb dislocation in Tampa Bay's 43-13 road win at the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and with the heavy rain in Tampa on Sunday, the Buccaneers chose to lean exclusively on their ground game. They racked up 324 yards rushing, with running back Bucky Irving leading the way with 170 yards rushing and a touchdown on 27 carries. He also averaged 6.3 yards per carry. No. 2 running back Kenneth Gainwell also chipped in another 140 yards rushing on 25 carries for a 5.6 yards-per-carry average. Mayfield added 14 yards on the ground on four carries.
Irving and Gainwell are now the first teammate duo in NFL history to each have 25-plus carries and 125-plus rushing yards in the same game.
Incredibly, the Buccaneers have now won consecutive games against their NFC South division rivals, with Mayfield completing seven of his 14 throws for 64 yards and a touchdown in the last two weeks. They have survived a malfunctioning passing game because of their run game and smothering defense. In Week 7, they forced four Panthers turnovers, including a 32-yard fumble return touchdown.
On Sunday against the Falcons, they forced Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr . into a career-high four interceptions, and he completed just eight of his 24 throws for 125 yards. This is the first time a Falcons quarterback has thrown four interceptions in a game since Penix Jr.'s predecessor, Kirk Cousins , in a 17-13 Week 13 loss against the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2024 season.
The Panthers stayed in first place in the NFC South with a 3-4 record entering Week 9, with the Buccaneers (3-5) and the Falcons (3-5) right behind them. The New Orleans Saints sit in last place at 2-5 and are on a bye in Week 8. Through the first half of the season, the NFC South remains the most wide-open, wacky division in the NFL.
