title: Who is Ravens' Joe Fagnano? Baltimore turns to third QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries
summary: Baltimore is down to its third-string quarterback, an undrafted rookie
full_text:
The Ravens ' quarterback issues went from awful to somehow even worse in a hurry in a crucial Week 8 meeting against the Bills . After Lamar Jackson , in his first game back from an ankle injury, injured his thumb on Baltimore's first offensive play of the game, backup Tyler Huntley got hurt in the second quarter. The Ravens had to turn to emergency third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano , a rookie undrafted free agent out of UConn.
Jackson hit his thumb on Gregory Rousseau and immediately went to the locker room. Huntley, who started the Ravens' previous three games with Jackson sidelined, then got his foot caught/rolled up on by Ed Oliver .
Here’s a look at #Ravens QB Tyler Huntley injuring his right toe on the tackle by Ed Oliver. Pretty classic turf toe mechanism. https://t.co/2qpBBQTJCV pic.twitter.com/GHRY4WufeN
Huntley is officially questionable to return. In his place, Fagnano finished 10-of-12 for 91 yards with an interception while playing about 2.5 quarters against the Bills.
Though Fagnano is making his NFL debut Sunday, he has played a lot of football. A rare 25-year-old rookie, Fagnano started his collegiate career as a walk-on at Maine, an FCS program, in 2019. He earned the backup quarterback job — and a scholarship — quickly, though. Like his NFL debut, his college debut came after the starter got hurt. One week later, in his first collegiate start, Fagnano threw five touchdown passes in an upset win over FBS program Liberty.
The Black Bears only played four games in the 2020 season due to COVID-19, and Fagnano got hurt in 2021 and only played in four games. After a solid 2022 season, he transferred to UConn.
After suffering a season-ending shoulder injury two games into his debut season at UConn, Fagnano played most of 2024. He got on NFL radars with an outstanding 2025 that included 28 passing touchdowns, one interception and 3,448 passing yards.
The Ravens invited Fagnano to a rookie tryout, where he beat out Diego Pavia for an opportunity to spend the summer with Baltimore. He capitalized with a strong preseason that included a nearly 75% completion percentage, three touchdowns and one interception.
Now, all of a sudden, he's trying to halt Baltimore's two-game losing streak. According to the CBS broadcast, running back Justice Hill would be the emergency quarterback to the emergency quarterback if Fagnano gets injured as well.

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Cowboys Winners & Losers: Arizona’s offense comes alive in second half in 33-30 win
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are at the point of the season where they need wins. Huge stats and highlight reels are nice, but victories are sorely needed. Today’s game against the Dallas Cowboys comes at a time when Arizona will either have a decent year or be picking in the Top-5 once again in April’s NFL […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals are at the point of the season where they need wins. Huge stats and highlight reels are nice, but victories are sorely needed. Today’s game against the Dallas Cowboys comes at a time when Arizona will either have a decent year or be picking in the Top-5 once again in April’s NFL Draft. RELATED: CARDINALS OFFENSE MOVES WHEN BRISSETT BENCHED The game might be the final for DE Josh Sweat and S Budda Baker, both of whom have been speculated as trade bait ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline. In this game, Arizona used their backup QB, backup RB, backup RT, their WR3, and their kick returner as another receiver. The injury list this upcoming week isn’t going to be pretty. At the final gun, the Cardinals won 33-30 in overtime. The Cardinals have beaten Dallas now five times in a row. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS Defensive stops – Dallas went for it on fourth-and-one from their own 32-yard line in the first quarter. Trot out the punter, right? The Cowboys, basking in their own glory while playing a two-win team, went for it. LB Mack Wilson read the running play by RB Javonte Williams and stuffed him for a two-yard loss. . @MackWilson forces the turnover on downs 😈 #AZvsDAL | @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/RuVK9s9Vy2 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 LB Zaven Collins came off the edge for the sack on QB Dak Prescott, which forced Dallas to punt. L.J. Collier’s timely sack forced a Dallas punt late in the fourth quarter. Making the Cowboys have a three-and-out on their only possession in overtime was a huge series of downs. Josh Sweat had a decent second half, including a sack late that forced the Cowboys to think field goal instead of seven. S Andrew Wingard was very active and had several key stops and finished with seven total tackles. Frame it 🖼️ pic.twitter.com/f2k1wE2PgV — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 WR Michael Wilson – Holy smokes. Where was Wilson in the first half? He destroyed the Dallas secondary in the final two quarters. His 17-yard jet sweep in the extra period was the catalyst to get into field goal range. On the final drive before the regular time ran out, he snagged a 21-yard pass and then the game-tying touchdown, with both feet dragging. Quiet first half, but finished with 15 targets, 8 receptions for 111 yards, and one TD. LB Jack Gibbens – Seems like every week Gibbens is leading the Cardinals in total tackles. Against Dallas, that trend continued with 11 tackles. He reads the run very quickly, then makes up his mind and finds the correct gap. 63-YARD HOUSE CALL FOR 22 📞 #AZvsDAL | @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/a5VMl6P8WU — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 RB Tyler Allgeier – When Allgeier is told he is the lead back and isn’t going out of the game, he balls out. Both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight sustained injuries in the first half, so it became the Allgeier Show. He had very few carries and yards in the first half, but made up for it after the half. Exploded for runs of 63 yards and 52 yards and was the difference in the game. Finished with 11 carries for 147 yards, a 13.4 yards-per-carry average, and scored two TDs. All in pretty much two quarters. This week’s “NFC Offensive Player of the Week.” QB Gardner Minshew – Here on ROTB , we ran an article and suggested that perhaps it was time to see what the other quarterbacks on the roster had to offer. After all, QB Jacoby Brissett has a 3-15 record as Arizona’s starting quarterback, so it can’t be any worse. So, you are the backup quarterback and come into the game in the third quarter. What do you do? Well, for one, you use all of the playmakers. That is what Minshew did with Allgeier, Wilson, and, of course, McBride. He didn’t spend a lot of time looking for other receivers and focused on the speedier Wilson and the sure-handedness of McBride. A DOT FROM GARDNER MINSHEW TO MICHAEL WILSON TIES THIS UP WITH :06 ON THE CLOCK! #AZvsDAL | 📺 Fox pic.twitter.com/xYLhtBVW3i — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 Lo and behold, the offense not only moved, but it also scored actual points. No, really, like touchdowns. What a sparkplug. Arizona scored 20 points in the final stanza, and moved the ball down into field goal range in the overtime period to get into field goal range all on Minshew’s arm and accuracy. In the end, the Cardinals not only had a win, but also totaled 467 yards in total offense. Minshew went 17 for 23 for 188 yards with three TD throws against zero picks or fumbles, was sacked just once, and had a 137.3 QB rating. Second half adjustments – You have to admire a head coach who can identify what isn’t working and offer changes for the second half instead of just cashing it in or staying with the game plan that obviously isn’t working. QB Jacoby Brissett had one series in Quarter 3 before he was yanked. The offense just wasn’t moving, and when it did, it could not score. The defense also blitzed a safety or a linebacker more in the second half, which made Prescott have to throw the ball earlier than in the first two quarters. And the ball was being distributed more to the Cardinals’ playmakers, Wilson and McBride, on a more frequent basis. Josh Fryar came in for the injured Jayden Williams at right tackle and held his own. And the long ball was incorporated, which made the Dallas cornerbacks back off the line pre-snap and helped the short passing game. DT L.J. Collier – Collier was immediately placed on the cow dung list when he pushed LT Tyler Guyton and got a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty. What happened was a pile of players was clustered from the previous play, which was a failed third down for Dallas. As players were getting up, Guyton shoved LB Gibbens, and Collier saw it. He then went over and body-slammed Guyton with both hands. Naturally, the referee only saw the second offender. Instead of setting up the punt return team, the Cowboys had a fresh set of downs. It was a knucklehead play. But Collier more than made up for it. With 3:58 remaining in the game, he batted a pass on a third-and-11. He sacked Prescott with 2:09 left in the game, and then halfway through the extra period, he was able to bat the pass down that became a Cowboys punt. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS First-quarter offense – QB Jacoby Brissett airmailed four passes in the opening quarter. RB Jeremiyah Love had minimal gains on the ground, then walked off with an injury. A beautiful nine-play drive was stuffed at the one-yard line on both third and fourth downs, with Arizona getting zero points. Then TE Elijah Higgins pops the ball up as Dallas LB Shemar James makes an interception and runs it all the way down to the Cardinals’ five-yard line. Two plays later, the Cowboys are up 7-0, but only because S Andrew Wingard doesn’t land on the fumble caused by the S Budda Baker hit on RB Javonte Williams. Only 22 rushing yards for Arizona, and the offense’s best pass catcher, McBride, had one catch for five yards. First-quarter possessions: punt, downs, INT. Missed opportunities – The Bam Knight fumble came as the second quarter was winding down, as the offense was getting near field goal range after WR Simi Fehoko hauled in a 17-yard pass. Not scoring any points after the offense got to the one in Quarter 1. Cardinals got the ball on the Cowboys’ 30 after the failed fourth-down attempt and scored no points. The missed PAT would have won the game outright. Missed tackles – Budda Baker, Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson, Andrew Wingard, and Denzel Burke. CB Denzel Burke – He missed the tackle on WR CeeDee Lamb that should have been a loss in the second quarter, but ended up converting a first down instead. On the Cowboys’ second touchdown, WR Ryan Flournoy was his man as Dallas was inside the five-yard line, yet Burke played off him instead of pressing tight with such a limited field. The catch was uncontested and increased the lead to 14-0. In the third quarter, he…

title: Arizona Cardinals bench Jacoby Brissett and offense immediately takes off in win over Cowboys
summary: It is hard to quantify things, because you never want to lay all the blame on one player. But after today, Jacoby Brissett will finish his career as the Arizona Cardinals starting quarterback at 3-16 and a 0.158 win percentage. That is the worst in Cardinals history for any starter with 10 or more starts. […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II (15) celebrates a touchdown pass with tight end Trey McBride (85) during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It is hard to quantify things, because you never want to lay all the blame on one player. But after today, Jacoby Brissett will finish his career as the Arizona Cardinals starting quarterback at 3-16 and a 0.158 win percentage. That is the worst in Cardinals history for any starter with 10 or more starts. And in today’s win, the Cardinals made the change with 1:35 left in the third quarter, and the Cardinals trailing 17-3. Then Minshew Mania, Minshew Magic, whatever you want to call it, came to life and the offense followed suit in the Cardinals improbable 33-30 overtime win. Four touchdowns drives in regulation took the game to overtime thanks to a missed Chad Ryland extra point that would have won the game. Instead, we dealt with overtime, and an Arizona Cardinals win that seemed improbable. However, this offense looked completely different in terms of ability to execute with Minshew at the helm. One thing we will want to see is if the Cardinals offense was good out of desperation, or if the quarterback’s inability to move was holding them back. Either way, the Arizona Cardinals are 3-5 and the team looked juiced to have some sort of hope once again on offense. Brissett in nearly three full quarters: 10/23 119 yards one interception Minshew in a little under two quarters: 17/23 (three incompletions were spikes to stop the clock) 188 yards three touchdowns What do you make of this? Well, for one game, the Arizona Cardinals are victorious and showed signs of life.

summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cardinals fans and fans across the country. Fans are… not confident. And it makes sense. When you have 12 attempts in a goal to go situation in a game and score only three […]
full_text: Oct 25, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) warms up before the game against the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cardinals fans and fans across the country. Fans are… not confident. And it makes sense. When you have 12 attempts in a goal to go situation in a game and score only three points, it is hard to have confidence in the direction of the team. That’s why only 16% fans are confident in the direction of the team. They tried to improve the offense with a coaching hire and some assets along the offensive line and at running back and we’ve seen no difference, and in fact things have gotten worse in the scoring department. So, it also makes sense that fans are overwhelmingly ready to see Carson Beck at the quarterback position, with the offense not clicking under LaFleur and with Jacoby Brissett at the helm, you have to exhaust all options before you land on… the head coach is the problem (since he is the play caller). The Commanders game is really the sweet spot at this point to me, but I get why fans would want to stop the madness with Brissett. I also understand why the Cardinals continue to be underdogs week-in and week-out on FanDuel Sportsbook , with this week they are a full touchdown underdogs. The Cowboys give up 25.7 points per game and the Cardinals team total for the week is 23.5-points. No one is buying this offense, and fans want to know for sure the problem isn’t Brissett, and they would rather do it with someone like Beck than going to another Brissett in Gardner Minshew.

title: Falcons – Buccaneers Week 8 recap: Defeated in a downpour
summary: The rain made the field sloppy, the rain made the Falcons sloppy. In the end, they couldn’t beat a completely one-dimensional Buccaneers team on the road that barely even tried to pass the ball and seemed to relish how embarrassing that became as the game wore on. By the time the dust settled, the Bucs […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Zach Harrison #96 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rain made the field sloppy, the rain made the Falcons sloppy. In the end, they couldn’t beat a completely one-dimensional Buccaneers team on the road that barely even tried to pass the ball and seemed to relish how embarrassing that became as the game wore on. By the time the dust settled, the Bucs became the first team in over 50 years to win without completing a pass, and the Falcons made unfortunate history in multiple ways before it was over. If you’ve followed me for any length of time, you know that I believe one game is one game, and it’s best to patiently build the picture of what a team and/or players are over the course of a season. I get caught up in big days and big moments like anybody else and that bleeds into Sunday and even Monday, but then I try to make myself take stock of the bigger picture. I’ll be doing that again this week, but it rarely feels as tough as it does after this one. Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions and legitimately could’ve thrown three more, and he badly missed other passes that might’ve made a difference in this one. The offensive line didn’t do a great job of protecting Penix or opening lanes on a consistent basis. Tommy Rees and company called doomed screens, chose to pass on the rare occasions when the Falcons had short yardage situations and could’ve run, and just generally seemed ill-equipped to put together a working offense in a rainstorm. Jeff Ulbrich’s defense basically had one job—defend the run—and allowed the Bucs to gash them for over 300 yards even so. Nick Folk missed his field goal try and clearly isn’t going to be trusted in adverse conditions or beyond 50 yards the rest of the season, and Atlanta’s return game was once again basically nonexistent as the team struggled with field position. It’s incredibly difficult to find positives because there were so few in a game the Falcons lost 16-0 and barely seemed competitive in. Again, it’s one game, but the Falcons are now 1-2 against the division and that’s likely to matter down the line. It’s one game, but the Falcons may be asked to play again in the rain or snow or cold, and this will make you wonder if they can handle that. It’s one game, but the Falcons have a tough assignment against the Bengals abroad next week. It’s one game, but it’s at least the third time this year the Falcons have found themselves down early, struggling, and unable to come up with any answers to avoid the game turning into a legitimately blowout. It’s one game, but it’s a game that feels like the absolute worse games of the late Mike Smith era, the mid-to-late Dan Quinn era, the Arthur Smith era, and the Raheem Morris era. It’s one game, but it’s just about as terrible a game as you can imagine the Falcons playing. The Falcons, of course, can’t linger on it. They won’t be playing in driving rain in Spain a week from now, and may not actually have to deal with wet conditions the rest of the way, and they know that game was the outlier of all outliers in terms of their run defense having to put up with nonstop running and Penix playing about as poorly as he can possibly play. There’s only so much you can take away from a game you may not see again for a decade, in terms of conditions and opponent game plans, and getting stuck trying to fix what ailed them on this specific Sunday is unlikely to be a great use of their time. They have to get ready for a pass-first script from Joe Burrow and the Bengals and the weakest run defense they’ve faced in weeks, which will drastically change how they approach the next game. It pays to have a short memory in the NFL, and the Falcons will under a head coach as even-keeled as Kevin Stefanski. For those of us in the stadium and at home, though, this will linger and should linger. It’s the latest sizeable dent in the notion that this Falcons team is (or even can be) different than the many hapless ones that preceded it; the Falcons in the past few eras were capable of truly astonishing wins against teams they weren’t expected to contend against but fell to earth in dispiriting ways the following weeks. For these Falcons to truly be different, they have to have something more than a deeply inconsistent team that follows a dominant week or two with horrors that would make Stephen King blush. If this isn’t rock bottom for the Falcons by a mile, this season is over, no matter how grim the NFC South may be. Whether they continue to “same old Falcons” or find their footing, the Falcons can’t dwell on their ugliest losses this year. Unfortunately, it’s difficult for us not to do so. On to the full recap. The Good Bijan Robinson’s balance was such an asset on a very wet field. Over and over again, he went into the pile or survived an early onslaught to pick up extra yardage, something that would’ve been impossible for a lesser back with lesser ability. His ugly drop was the only significant stain on a quality (if somewhat quiet by his standards) day, especially because the Buccaneers run defense has long given him fits. If only Bijan had not been mothballed on critical late game short yardage situations, eh? Jahan Dotson had the biggest play of the game on offense, underscoring how dangerous he can be. He took a risky Penix pass, went around a defender, and turned on the jets for a 76 yard gain that should have set up Atlanta’s first scoring drive had the team not frittered it away. No other Falcon had more than 10 yards and Dotson had 95 on two receptions; it’s safe to say he bounced back this week even if he’ll always likely be inconsistent from week-to-week. Jessie Bates is on fire right now, and he made the play of the game in this one. With Baker Mayfield escaping the pocket after a busted play and flipping it backwards to Bucky Irving, the Bucs running back had a clear lane to the end zone…right up until Bates arrived and chopped hard at the ball. That forced a fumble that landed out of bounds, and per NFL rules, that meant Atlanta got the ball. It was a massive, six point swing when the Falcons would’ve been down 10-0, and exactly the kind of play that makes Bates worth every penny. Mike Hughes had a tremendous play on the first drive, with Baker Mayfield’s end zone bomb to Ted Hurst looking caught…until Hughes chopped it out of his hand at the exact right time to prevent a score and force Tampa Bay to settle for three. We’ve been justifiably hard on Hughes this year, but credit where it’s due. Maason Smith’s third down stop with the Bucs driving and threatening to move the game from “likely out of reach” to “entirely out of reach” was a huge play. I wished it had mattered more. Jake Bailey had a solid day at the office, pinning the Bucs inside their own 20 twice and averaging nearly 50 yards a punt. Paired with stingy work from Falcons special teams—they only allowed two punt returns for a combined eight yards—the punting game did its job. The Ugly Michael Penix Jr. had done a good job of taking care of the football, but he had been fortunate not to throw a couple of picks over the past few weeks that bounced off defender’s hands. That hot streak ended in this one in excruciating fashion, as Penix threw two first quarter interceptions right at Alex Anzalone, who he appeared not to see on both occasions. It was a gruesome performance that got worse, with Penix badly missing a wide open Kyle Pitts after shrugging off a sack attempt and then throwing his third interception on a half-hearted fourth down attempt in the second quarter. He then threw a fourth interception on another ill-advised throw to Charlie Woerner that was picked off by a leaping Zyon McCollum. The Falcons clearly planned to stay balanced despite the wet field conditions, and sticking with…

title: Week 8 Snap reactions: Falcons get stuck in the mud
summary: The Atlanta Falcons got buried in the mud by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A team hasn’t won a game without completing a pass since 1974; here are the Week 8 snap reactions. Penix Melts in the Rain It was a complete meltdown for the 3rd-year quarterback, who threw four interceptions on the day. We’ll talk […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: A'shawn Robinson #91 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers knocks down a pass attempt by Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons got buried in the mud by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . A team hasn’t won a game without completing a pass since 1974; here are the Week 8 snap reactions. Penix Melts in the Rain It was a complete meltdown for the 3rd-year quarterback, who threw four interceptions on the day. We’ll talk about the staff’s role in this, but these interceptions were awful decisions and clear misses. You can’t reasonably explain any of them, just pure unfiltered poor quarterback play. Kyle Pitts was ready to snag his explosive play of the day against Tampa Bay, and Penix missed him with no one around. After playing one of the best games of his career, Penix’s homecoming was a major letdown. A tough day at the office, and while Penix has been playing well this season, no one’s future is guaranteed. Michael Penix vs Bucs 6-16 41 Pass Yards 4 INT 6.2 Pass Rating pic.twitter.com/oEPfEZl9mt — PFF (@PFF) November 1, 2026 Run Game issues persist Earlier in the week, I called out the Falcons poor running game , which was surprisingly met with some resistance, but this issue is now undeniable for Atlanta. The Falcons have more money tied up in their interior OL than most franchises and can hardly generate a push. Matthew Bergeron has not lived up to his extension; run blocking was never Neuzil’s strength, and Lindstrom can only do so much on his own. Without his 30-yard carry, Bijan was held to 2.6 yards per carry on 18 touches. Weather can’t be an excuse given how well the Buccaneers ran the football, and excusing these performances cause they’re happening against good run defenses isn’t sound reasoning either. If you can’t perform against the best, then you aren’t as good as you think you are. Something has to change. Poor weather highlights poor coaching Did the Falcons coaching staff not read the weather report this week? Baker Mayfield attempted 3 passes and didn’t complete one of them. That’s the kind of game the Falcons needed to play, but they came out throwing in this monsoon. Rees’ stubbornness to do so proved to be the Falcons demise. Bijan has stalled, and Rees has no answers for this drought. The Falcons screen game can’t get going, the passing game folds under pressure, and the defense was continuously let down. If you need everything to be perfect to succeed, then you won’t make it long in this league. When Rees’ offense has faced adversity this season, it folds like a washcloth. Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers become the first team since 1974 to win without completing a pass pic.twitter.com/MbFNyOdPPm — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 1, 2026 Defense gets gashed I won’t be too hard on the defense; it’s hard to build any momentum when your quarterback is giving the opposing offense endless opportunities, but the Buccaneers were able to win without completing a pass, something you’ll see maybe a handful of times in your existence. This attacking front has pinned its ears back in most games because the score was close, but Tampa Bay exposed that aggression and ripped off run after run in this mud bowl. Harold Perkins Jr. has been sensational in coverage, but the defense couldn’t hide him in the run today, and he had a rough game. The defense still gave the offense a chance, but they didn’t get any help from that side of the ball. Baker Mayfield recovers a dropped snap and flips it to Bucky Irving, who fumbles just before the end zone! Falcons ball! 📺: FOX/ FOX One pic.twitter.com/Aonn0k5Qlg — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 1, 2026 It’ll take a while to wash this loss off. It’s easy to blame a performance like this on the weather, but the Falcons have too many red flags to ignore. The Falcons bungled their chance to take control of the division and are 3-5 at the season’s halfway point.

title: Falcons – Buccaneers instant recap: The rain washes away any shine from our favorite team
summary: We hoped and prayed the Falcons would buck a seemingly ancient trend of falling down after a major win against a contender, and we hoped and prayed in vain. Our favorite team went to Tampa Bay in a downpour that turned into a drizzle and washed away their hopes of taking possession of the NFC […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We hoped and prayed the Falcons would buck a seemingly ancient trend of falling down after a major win against a contender, and we hoped and prayed in vain. Our favorite team went to Tampa Bay in a downpour that turned into a drizzle and washed away their hopes of taking possession of the NFC South lead with an embarrassing effort that undermined almost every positive the Falcons have put forth in recent weeks. Let’s be honest about what we saw Sunday: It was an ass kicking where Atlanta was entirely out-coached, out-played, and out-hustled. Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass, yet the Buccaneers didn’t care because they ran for 300 yards. The Falcons had Bijan Robinson, but somehow that didn’t matter because the Falcons got down after throwing too much and then started throwing nonstop late. The Falcons were within striking distance—or at least not dead—all day, but yet could not turn in a single point. There is nothing that can be said about the caliber of performance the Falcons put on the field today that is positive, and aside from a handful of strong individual performances, Atlanta was humiliated and humbled by their rival. Now 3-5, the Falcons are back down with the Buccaneers and the division is a muddle, and Atlanta’s highs are matched by their lows as they continue to be defined by inconsistency and utterly baffling performances after stunningly good ones. This loss is impossible to justify and tough to swallow, and this is the kind of doubt-sprouting performance that the Falcons will now be combating the rest of the year. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. I suggest not bothering to read it, but thanks for stopping by. 1st Quarter Bijan picked up three yards on first down, then Michael Penix Jr. hit Jahan Dotson for 19 yards. Bijan picked up three and then Penix hit Kyle Pitts for five yards, and then Bijan got a yard. Penix went up the gut on fourth down to convert. Bijan then went two yards and then was stalled for no gain, and Penix couldn’t connect with Drake London. In the rain from 53 yards, Nick Folk’s field goal attempt went wide left. The Buccaneers took over near midfield, and then Bucky Irving took it almost 20 yards. Irving got a yard on first down. After three yards, Kendal Daniels got Irving out of bounds. Baker Mayfield then bombed it downfield and threw it a bit behind his receiver, who had it knocked loose by Mike Hughes, who arrived with excellent timing. Chase McLaughlin’s field goal try was good to make it 3-0 Buccaneers. Zachariah Branch took it to about the 28, and an illegal formation call on the Buccaneers gave Atlanta five more yards. On the next play, Penix simply missed the defender and threw an interception right to him, with Drake London picking up a 15 yard penalty for unnecessary roughness on the same play. Buccaneers ball. Irving took it five yards on first down. Then in a wildly bewildering sequence, Baker Mayfield got out of a busted situation, scrambled, flipped the ball to Bucky Irving, and Irving was galloping toward the end zone…only to have Jessie Bates come in and chop the ball out of his hands, where it landed out of bounds in the end zone. Falcons ball! Bijan Robinson got called for a first down, and then picked up five yards. Penix didn’t see anything downfield on second down, and tried the outlet to Bijan, who dropped it. Then Penix threw another interception, again to Anzalone. Buccaneers ball. Irving was stopped for a loss by Brandon Dorlus. Irving then got three yards. Mayfield missed badly on third down, setting up a McLaughlin field goal. 6-0 Buccaneers. Branch slid down past the 25 yard line. Bijan then took it for four yards. Bijan then cut it inside for another four. Penix evaded the pressure, but wildly overthrew Pitts. The Jake Bailey punt rolled to the 13 yard line. Bucky Irving then picked up 12 yards on first down. Baker fumbled the snap and handed it to Irving, who got a yard. Irving then got a couple more yards on second down. Gainwell was then quickly tackled after maybe a yard. 2nd Quarter Dotson called for a fair catch on the Falcons 39 yard line. Bijan then appeared to run into the pile for a minimal gain, but emerged on the other side for almost 15 yards. Then he picked up two yards. Penix then made a dangerous arcing throw to Dotson, who had it bounce off his hands. Khalil Herbert then ran into the pile for maybe a yard. The Falcons then went for it on fourth down, and Penix threw an interception again. Bucs ball. Irving spun his way to five yards, and then Mayfield scrambled for a first down. Irving then picked up another five yards. Irivng was tripped up by Daniels for another four yards. Irving got another first down and five yards, and followed that up with six yards. Irving was then tackled by Zach Harrison on second down just shy of a first down. Maason Smith then got Gainwell, but not before he squeezed past the line for another first down. Gainwell then took it almost 20 yards. Gainwell went up the middle for a yard or two. A false start on the Bucs backed them up five yards. Mayfield had the ball flip out of his hand and then ran for five yards. A carry for Gainwell then went for three yards, setting up a field goal try. McLaughlin hit it again to make it 9-0 Buccaneers. A one yard gain by Bijan gave way to a nice, physical run where he picked up nine yards and a first down. Herbert then picked up two yards. Penix then sort of threw it away to the sideline in the direction of a receiver. Bijan somehow then managed to bully his way to a first down on 3rd and 8, but on booth review he was ruled down after a six yard gain. On fourth down, they gave it to Bijan, who came up a little short of a conversion. Bucs ball. Irving then rolled for 13 yards on first down. C.J. Henderson then got Irving after a couple of yards. Irving then got two more, and Stefanski surprisingly called a timeout. Gainwell was hit by Cameron Thomas and got a yard, with Atlanta spending their last timeout. Ryan Neuzil’s snap bounced off Matthew Bergeron’s leg. Half over. 3rd Quarter The Bucs returned it to about the 28 yard line, and then Irving went two yards. Irving then picked up three yards. Baker Mayfield’s pass to Gainwell was tipped and ultimately dropped by the running back. Punt, and it went over Jahan Dotson’s head and rolled back inside the 10 yard line. Bijan was stonewalled on first down. Bijan then took it about seven yards. Pitts then caught a short pass and took it just shy of a first down. Punt. Mayfield faked a pass and scrambled for three yards. Irving then ran into a brick wall. Mayfield tried to scramble and was brought down for a loss. The Falcons get the ball back after a penalty and a touchback. Bijan rolled forward for a yard, and then picked up another yard on second down. A quick pass to Herbert went for five yards. Punt, and Mike Ford Jr. got Tez Johnson inside the 10 yard line. Irving took it eight yards on first down. Irving then got loose and ran to the Falcons 35 for 46 yards. Kenneth Gainwell then went one yard. Gainwell then got loose, evading multiple tackle attempts and picking up 28 yards. Irving was smothered after maybe a yard. Irving then powered through contact to pick up a touchdown. 16-0 Buccaneers. Herbert took it to about the 35 yard line on the kickoff return. Penix then felt pressure and threw it at Herbert’s feet, but a roughing the passer call gave the Falcons life. Herbert then took it almost nine yards. Herbert then got tackled for no gain, with one defender latching on to his ankles. Bijan was then stuffed. On fourth down, Penix scrambled for a first down. Austin Hooper then made a leaping roll on a catch for nine yards. Penix then had to throw it away on second…

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Bucs
summary: As Week 8 follows on the heels of Halloween, the Atlanta Falcons hope to avoid a house of horrors at Raymond James Stadium in a high-stakes NFC South clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. After a 0-4 start, the Bucs’ season looks resurrected with recent wins, and the Falcons hope to end their hopes in […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 27: Kyle Pitts #8 of the Atlanta Falcons scores a touchdown during the first half of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Week 8 follows on the heels of Halloween, the Atlanta Falcons hope to avoid a house of horrors at Raymond James Stadium in a high-stakes NFC South clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . After a 0-4 start, the Bucs’ season looks resurrected with recent wins, and the Falcons hope to end their hopes in a nightmare scenario. But to survive the scares in Tampa Bay, the Falcons will need to summon some supernatural performances from five key players. Michael Penix Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will need to pack his holy water and grip his crucifix tightly as he attempts to exorcise the blitzing demons of Todd Bowles’ defense. The Bucs love to bring the heat, and Penix has shown poise under that extra pressure, posting the 6th-best DVOA according to FTN Fantasy . However, when those blitzes actually create pressure, the script flips into a horror movie: Penix ranks 31st against pressure per the same source. To banish demonic doubts, Penix must use his quick release to attack the soft spots over the middle before Tampa’s ghoulish pass rushers can drag him down. Kyle Pitts While Tampa Bay prepares its haunted house, tight end Kyle Pitts enters Week 8 as their ultimate recurring nightmare. Like a classic horror-movie villain in a hockey mask, no matter how many times the Bucs think they’ve stopped him, Pitts always comes back. In eight career games against Tampa Bay, Pitts has terrorized their defense with six touchdowns while averaging over 78 receiving yards per game. Considering he averages roughly 40 yards per game against all other opponents and a third of his career touchdowns have come against Tampa Bay, Pitts channels a slasher-flick energy against the Bucs. If he wields the machete again on Sunday, Atlanta’s offense will be in great shape. Ryan Neuzil Pitts isn’t the only monster haunting this matchup. The Bucs feature a terrifying creature in 350-pound nose tackle Vita Vea. That places the onus squarely on Falcons center Ryan Neuzil to gather his silver bullets and hold the line against a beast that ravenously devours run plays. If the Falcons hope to establish the ground game against Tampa Bay’s second-ranked run defense, Neuzil and the interior offensive line will need a heroic, monster-slaying effort. Gervon Dexter On the other side of the trenches, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter will need to play the Grim Reaper. The Bucs boast a dangerous rushing attack, and Dexter must help control the line of scrimmage. But his soul-harvesting duties don’t end there, as quarterback Baker Mayfield has also struggled under pressure this season. If Dexter can help the Falcons’ front collapse the pocket, they can force Mayfield into grave mistakes and collect crucial takeaways just like they did in last week’s win over the San Francisco 49ers . Kendal Daniels For the second straight week, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels will don the green dot to lead the defense in Divine Deablo’s absence . Stepping into the caller’s role, Daniels will have to haunt the A- and B-gaps to help Dexter and the defensive line bury the Bucs’ run game. If the rookie phantom can diagnose plays quickly and fill his assignments without giving up the ghost, Atlanta’s defense will be well-positioned to stop the Buccaneers. Surviving a road trip to Tampa Bay on Halloween weekend won’t be easy, but the Falcons are well-equipped to pull off another frightful upset. If they can, they’ll take complete control of the NFC South. Can you name any other Falcons that will be tricked or treated in this matchup?
author: Aaron Freeman

title: Falcons vs. Buccaneers: What will Week 8’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: Just when it looked like hope in the season was about to start getting drained out following a 2-4 start and a meeting against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on tap, the Falcons had an unexpected victory in dominating fashion to give this roller coaster ride another swing upwards, as has been their MO for […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 11: Kyle Pitts Sr. #8 of the Atlanta Falcons scores a touchdown in front of Kindle Vildor #22 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium on December 11, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just when it looked like hope in the season was about to start getting drained out following a 2-4 start and a meeting against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on tap, the Falcons had an unexpected victory in dominating fashion to give this roller coaster ride another swing upwards, as has been their MO for years. Of course, Falcons fashion would be losing the next game after an exhilarating victory to let the fanbase down and send this ride going the right back down the other way. If they want to be taken seriously, it’s imperative that they buck the trend this weekend against the Buccaneers. Atlanta makes the trip down to Florida for its first game against the Bucs of the season and it may well be the most important one of the campaign up to this point. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They would climb back up to .500 at about the halfway mark of the season which, given the schedule and the 0-2 start behind Cooper Rush, would feel like a minor miracle. Back to back victories against the 49ers and Buccaneers would have much of the fanbase buying back in. They would also have weathered the eight game storm without the suspended James Pearce Jr., who is eligible to return next week. With Carolina’s defeat against the Packers on Thursday Night Football (I guess beating Green Bay on TNF isn’t for everybody), the Falcons would move into sole possession of first place in the NFC South, and would drop Tampa Bay and New Orleans to two games behind them in the win column, solidifying this as a two horse race for the time being. The algorithm at playoffstatus.com currently gives the Falcons a 17% chance of winning the division and a 37% chance of making the playoffs as of today. Those numbers would increase to 23% and 46%, respectfully, which I know don’t seem like much, but that’s huge movement when dictated by just one game in the middle of the season. The Birds would continue a recent period of success against the Bucs, winning their sixth meeting in the last eight against Tampa Bay, dating back to 2024. If the Falcons lose Then it will be another case of “typical Falcons,” with another big let down following a euphoric victory. No matter the head coach or front office over the last decade, this will continue being the groundhog day type plague that continues tripping this franchise up. To make matters worse, this would also be Atlanta’s second divisional loss in three games. You don’t have to look further than last season to realize how detrimental these divisional losses can be as the Falcons wound up tied for first in the NFC South but were mathematically eliminated a month before the end of the season because of their inferiority when it came to the tiebreakers. The Falcons would remain a half game behind the Panthers and would actually fall to third in the division due to the head to head tiebreaker Tampa would possess while sitting at an identical 3-5 record. Carolina, remember, also owns the tiebreaker over the Birds as of this moment. Atlanta’s odds at the division would fall from 17% to 15% and their overall playoff odds would fall from 37% to 28%, as any hope of even potentially fighting for a wildcard spot would take a major blow. Their next two games are against the Bengals and Chiefs, which could take things from bad to worse in a hurry.
author: Adnan Ikic

title: Top takeaways from the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills
summary: The Baltimore Ravens stacked insults upon injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s top takeaways from the worst game of the 2026 season: So many questions, so little time. Lamar Jackson’s right thumb injury will no doubt spark a new round of questions about his long-term future in Baltimore. But […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on from the sideline against the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens stacked insults upon injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s top takeaways from the worst game of the 2026 season: So many questions, so little time. Lamar Jackson’s right thumb injury will no doubt spark a new round of questions about his long-term future in Baltimore. But the Ravens do not have any time to think about offseason contract situations right now. They need to take stock – particularly at the quarterback position – and figure out who is starting on Thursday night against the Jaguars. Reports of a turf toe injury to Tyler Huntley indicate that will likely be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. His potential backup is not currently on the Ravens’ roster. And then there’s the trade deadline in just nine days. Baltimore is 4-4 at the bottom of the AFC North; Jackson’s injury could effectively knock them out of playoff competition. Can Eric DeCosta make – or rather, take – the tough calls to part ways with valued veterans in exchange for future draft capital? These are the first of a series of tricky decisions the Ravens will have to navigate in the coming days, weeks, and months. Tyler Loop’s time is up. The Ravens have got to start holding players accountable for poor performances, and it should start with Loop after he missed a chip-shot field goal and landed the opening kickoff out of the bounds against the Bills. Kickers in the modern NFL should be able to be trusted on kicks under 50 yards. There may not be many better options on the street right now to replace Loop, but Baltimore has to start sending messages about what happens if you fail to do your job. – Dustin Cox The Ravens need a complete offensive line overhaul. Much has been made this season about the Ravens’ offensive line inconsistencies and struggles. While they’ve had poor injury luck and their ideal starting five has almost not played together at all, the offensive line’s performance in Buffalo was abysmal – and indicative that the Ravens need a full makeover up front. Roger Rosengarten, who is supposed to be a building block at right tackle, was dominated all afternoon by Gregory Rosseau. Ronnie Stanley continues to be penalized often and Cam Jurgens missed blitz pickups in the middle. Lamar Jackson couldn’t even go one play without being hit immediately on a play action. Poor pass protection has been a factor in Jackson’s injury struggles and now both backup quarterbacks picked up injuries in this game as well. Vega Ioane is clearly a long-term fixture, Jurgens was just traded for so the Ravens can’t give up on him too early, and maybe Rosengarten can turn things around. Nevertheless, the Ravens need heavy investment this offseason to infuse more talent on the offensive line to protect their franchise quarterback. – Frank Platko It’s going to be a long few months in Baltimore. Even if Jackson can return this year – and if the Ravens can keep their playoff hopes alive in the meantime – there will be virtually no margin of error to close out the season. Given the circumstances, a postseason appearance would qualify as some sort of a success, but it is clear that the Ravens, as currently built, are not a Super Bowl team. That was the expectation coming into the season, and anything short of that will be seen as a distinct failure in Jesse Minter’s first year as a head coach. Then comes the offseason, and along with it a host of tough roster decisions on overpriced, underperforming veterans. Sunday’s loss in Buffalo might have been a new low for the Ravens, but just because things can only go up from here doesn’t mean that they will anytime soon.

title: Ravens QB Tyler Huntley could miss TNF vs. Jags with suspected turf toe
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are evaluating backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley for a suspected turf toe injury, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. An MRI on Monday will shed further light on his status for Thursday night’s matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Huntley, 28, entered Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills after starter Lamar Jackson injured his […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens throws the ball as he's getting tackled during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are evaluating backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley for a suspected turf toe injury, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. An MRI on Monday will shed further light on his status for Thursday night’s matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Huntley, 28, entered Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills after starter Lamar Jackson injured his throwing hand on the first snap of the game. He faced constant pressure and was hit multiple times before leaving the game in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the game under center while taking several shots of his own, though he “hopes” to be ready to play on Thursday. Jackson is set to land on injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, which will sideline him for at least four games. Huntley would be in line to start in his place, as he did in Jackson’s three-game absence following a Week 4 high ankle sprain. However, confirmation of his initial turf toe diagnosis will almost certainly keep him from playing in Week 9 – and potentially longer. Instead, it will likely be Fagnano making an unlikely first start of his NFL career vs. the Jaguars, who boast an elite run defense but have struggled against opposing passers this year. The former UConn starter could only complete 10 of his 21 passing attempts for 91 yards and an interception on Sunday afternoon, good for a paltry 4.3 yards per attempt and a 40.0 quarterback rating. Getting reps with Baltimore’s first-team offense will give him a chance at a better showing against Jacksonville, but Fagnano will clearly be facing an uphill battle. Huntley largely struggled in his five appearances this year. His numbers through the air are at or above league-average, but his underpowered arm limited the Ravens’ downfield passing game. He was not helped by a leaky, banged-up offense line that slowed the run game and far too often allowed rushers right in his lap. Turf toe injuries can linger, especially for a quarterback whose game is built on his mobility. Huntley could miss not only Thursday night’s game, but more contests after that, potentially positioning Fagnano for multiple starts. The Ravens will already need to add quarterback depth just to get through the week, but a longer-term absence from Huntley could force them to make a more substantial move.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson to undergo thumb surgery, will land on IR
summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be placed on injured reserve to undergo surgery on a right thumb injury suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Jesse Minter announced after the game. Landing on IR will sideline Jackson for at least four games, but his absence figures to be much longer. Minter […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks down at his thumb while walking off the field against the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be placed on injured reserve to undergo surgery on a right thumb injury suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Jesse Minter announced after the game. Landing on IR will sideline Jackson for at least four games, but his absence figures to be much longer. Minter said that the injury could “potentially” be season-ending. Jackson injured his thumb on his first snap back from a three-game absence due to a high ankle injury. He dropped back to pass off play action, hit Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau on his follow-through, and quickly left the field cradling his throwing hand. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley entered the game, but hurt his toe partway through the second quarter and was ruled out shortly after halftime. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, Baltimore’s emergency No. 3 quarterback, played the rest of the game despite taking several hits from a ferocious Buffalo pass rush. Minter said that the Ravens effectively have 24 hours to figure out their quarterback situation ahead of a short week before a Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Jackson, obviously, will not be available. Minter did not have an update on Huntley, who left the stadium with a boot on his injured foot, per NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe . Fagnano acknowledged that he was not at 100% after some “bumps and bruises,” but “hopes” to be ready to play on Thursday. In any event, Baltimore will need to add at least one quarterback in the coming days, but at this point of the season, their options are extremely limited. They may have to scour practice squads for an available arm and even consider a trade ahead of next week’s deadline.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens discussion: Reactions to demoralizing Week 8 loss to Bills
summary: The Baltimore Ravens entered Week 8 in good spirits thanks to the return of Lamar Jackson, which was hopefully going to cure their recent offensive ailments and give them a chance to get upset win over Buffalo Bills. Instead, Jackson took the field for just one play before suffering a thumb injury and exiting without […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Landon Jackson #94 of the Buffalo Bills sacks Joe Fagnano #12 of the Baltimore Ravens during the first half at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens entered Week 8 in good spirits thanks to the return of Lamar Jackson, which was hopefully going to cure their recent offensive ailments and give them a chance to get upset win over Buffalo Bills. Instead, Jackson took the field for just one play before suffering a thumb injury and exiting without return. Tyler Huntley also exited early, and the Ravens were forced to play the majority of the game with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center. While the Ravens played competitively in the first half and made some good defensive plays, the wheels eventually came off and resulted in another blowout loss, 36-10. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the team’s third consecutive defeat. What an awful day. To get Lamar Jackson back just to lose him to the first play of the day to a freak football play injury. It’s all too common to see quarterbacks hit their hands on their follow through when throwing and this one turned disastrous. Then the offensive line proceeded to get bullied all day, resulting in Tyler Huntley getting hurt and Joe Fagnano getting harassed in his NFL debut. The defense wasn’t much better and was heavily aided by Buffalo mistakes that kept Baltimore in it longer than they should have been. The only positive from today was the defense did play with energy, even after Jackson went down, getting multiple turnovers but it didn’t amount for much as they still got shredded. At this point, I’m done with this roster. Only people that should be safe are Kyle Hamilton, Vega Ioane, Nnamdi Madubuike, and Lamar Jackson (if they can find a way to convince him to stay after so many years of disastrous lines). Eric DeCosta’s seat is red hot at this point and Jesse Minter might not get much of a leash if DeCosta is ousted before 2027. I do think Minter should get a chance to build the roster his way before moving on from him but a new GM might not think so. — Zach Canter Obviously, it’s a bad situation in Baltimore right now. Lamar Jackson injured his thumb on their first offensive play which is just a cruel joke from the football gods. I was however, very impressed with the fight the defense showed. Buffalo sports one of the best offenses in the league and the Ravens limited them the best they could considering the ineptitude of the offense. We don’t know the extent of his injury or how long he’ll be out, but without Lamar Jackson, it will be a long season for the Ravens. Injuries have plagued the team all year but Eric DeCosta simply hasn’t been able to solve the issues across the line of scrimmage. It was clear in Buffalo today – regardless of who was at QB – that the home team had a far superior offensive and defensive line. It’s a tried and tested Super Bowl formula, but for whatever reason, the Ravens have generally chosen to money ball those positions in recent years. Lastly, it seems like this current nucleus of veterans has run its course. Expect players like Andrews, Smith, Humphrey and more to be gone next year, and for the Ravens to hit the reset button on the team around Lamar Jackson. Even without Jackson, it’s shocking to see how bad the rest of the team looks which is a direct indictment on DeCosta. The decision to resign Mark Andrews might’ve been a fireable offense on its own. The question now becomes- do you trust Jesse Minter and Eric DeCosta to pull off a quick rebuild? — Stephen Bopst This game was over the second Lamar Jackson left the game on the Ravens’ first offensive snap. This team simply does not have the talent to overcome losing their superstar quarterback. The offensive line is in the spotlight right now after a horrible performance that led to all three quarterbacks getting banged up. I don’t know how Jesse Minter can rally the troops on a short week to play a Super Bowl contending Jaguars squad. His defense played better this week, but they were unable to hold up for four quarters without any help from the offense. It’s hard to say that the season isn’t lost after another injury could sideline Jackson for several more weeks. Baltimore may very well become sellers at the trade deadline, although it will be difficult to get much of anything for some of their bigger name players considering their play this season and cap ramifications. I don’t know where this team goes from here. — Dustin Cox Looking at this schedule over the next few weeks, I’d wondered if the Ravens could shift from being buyers to sellers at the deadline in a worst-case scenario. Folks, I’d call this a worst case scenario. Lamar Jackson’s immediate injury appears to be one that would have him down at least a month, whether it’s a dislocation of the thumb or something worse. Even so, with the deficiencies shown by the rest of this team, they can’t afford to be without LJ for a month and expect to contend for the postseason. I don’t think any single player, coach or member of the front office can solely shoulder blame, but that makes the road moving forward even more complicated. It might be time to bite the bullet, shed some of these larger contracts where you can and hope you can build forward with draft capital in a stacked 2027 class. — Kevin McNelis
author: Stephen Bopst

title: Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 8 matchup vs. Bills
summary: The Baltimore Ravens will take on the Buffalo Bills today in a much-anticipated Week 8 contest. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for the game. Dustin Cox The Ravens have often responded with big wins in previous seasons when their backs were against the wall. That was with John Harbaugh at the helm, however, so we […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 07: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens runs the ball for a touchdown during the second quarter against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will take on the Buffalo Bills today in a much-anticipated Week 8 contest. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for the game. Dustin Cox The Ravens have often responded with big wins in previous seasons when their backs were against the wall. That was with John Harbaugh at the helm, however, so we will have to see if Jesse Minter is able to rally the troops the same way. This game heavily hinges on how healthy Lamar Jackson is behind a shaky offensive line. If Jackson plays to the level he was performing to start the season, then Baltimore has a legitimate path to victory on Sunday. The Bills defense has struggled against the pass, so Jackson and Zay Flowers could do some real damage through the air. If Buffalo is able to get quick pressure and Jackson isn’t healthy enough to evade rushers as usual, then it could be a long day for Declan Doyle. Continuing to scheme up easy plays to Flowers and letting him make plays after the catch will be needed to ease the burden on Jackson in his first game back. X-Factor: Trenton Simpson. The Ravens defense will have their hands full with Josh Allen. Simpson has been one of the best players on Baltimore’s defense to start this season, and his speed could come in handy when Allen inevitably escapes the pocket looking to make a big play through the air or as a runner. Simpson tracking down Allen on extended plays could make a huge difference if he is able to force Allen into a quicker decision with the ball. Score Prediction: Ravens 31, Bills 30 Nikhil Mehta Baltimore’s secondary is already on skates heading into a matchup with Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson is back just in time to face one of the NFL’s worst passing defense. This could be a shootout of epic proportions, and it’s going to come down to turnovers. The Ravens have a poor record in that regard against the Bills, but Allen isn’t always careful with the ball either. Vega Ioane’s absence and Jackson’s still-ailing ankle will, I think, ultimately keep Baltimore’s offense from making all of the plays they need to in the fourth quarter, and the defense will be inches away from the game-changing turnover that never comes. This is an opportunity for the Ravens’ highest-paid defenders to step up and lead by example – can anyone deliver? X-Factor: Nate Wiggins. Wiggins doesn’t fall into the aforementioned group above, but he’s extension-eligible next offseason, and he hasn’t proven where he ranks among the league’s corners. The key? Playmaking. He needs to use his speed not just to be sticky, but to break on passes, create turnovers, and maybe even rack up some return yardage. Score Prediction: Bills 38, Ravens 34 Frank Platko There is a lot riding on this game for the Ravens. While they aren’t necessarily in desperation win-now mode yet and can technically afford another loss, a victory would go a long way for both positive vibes and playoff hopes. A win over the Bills on the road could serve as a turning point for the team to turn a new page with Lamar Jackson coming back. Obviously, the Bills are going to get their share of points no matter how well the Ravens’ defense can play. Josh Allen and Buffalo’s offense is as dangerous as any in the NFL and they have an established offensive floor. We’ve yet to see Jesse Minter’s defense really dominate a game from start to finish and exceed expectations. They were just embarrassed by the Bengals last week in the second half. How will the Ravens’ defense respond against another elite quarterback? This a “play for your pride” type of a spot. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson. The Ravens signed Hendrickson with the idea of him being the needle-moving pass rusher that can help the team close out victories. While he’s been playing through a finger injury, we’ve yet to see Hendrickson consistently make game-changing plays and convert pressures to sacks. The Ravens could use him to come through against Allen and make a big play or two. Score Prediction: Bills 29, Ravens 27 Zach Canter The Ravens are knee deep in “can’t lose” territory heading up to Buffalo. The Bills, much like the Bengals, are coming off a bye and boasts the best offense in the NFL statistically. They also have one of worst defenses overall, so it looks like this will turn into a shootout. Under different circumstances, I’d probably take the Ravens. I think the offense is capable of going shot for shot with the Bills and the Ravens defense is good enough to deliver one more stop than the Buffalo’s is. However, Lamar Jackson is returning from injury and probably isn’t 100%. They are going to be missing their first-round guard Vega Ioane and the Bills are coming off a bye week. So, I think the Ravens fall just short in this one. The offense will have just a couple missteps in Jackson’s first game back, and the defense just won’t be able to do enough to limit Josh Allen to support the offense while they get back in rhythm. X-Factor: Mike Green. If the Ravens do want to win this game, the defense is going to have to find a couple spots on the Buffalo offense. Trey Hendircskon will have his hands full working against Dion Dawkins and Madubuike winning inside will be important. But Bills right tackle Spencer Brown is expected to miss this one. Mike Green beating a backup tackle to put pressure on Allen and not letting him escape to his arm side is going to be vital to avoid those back breaking plays Allen is capable of delivering. Score Prediction: Bills 34, Ravens 24

title: Greg Rousseau passes Darryl Talley on Buffalo Bills’ all-time sack list
summary: Greg Rousseau has another milestone to add to his growing résumé with the Buffalo Bills. The outside linebacker recorded a sack against the Baltimore Ravens giving him 39 for his career and moving him past Darryl Talley into eighth place on the franchise’s all-time sack list.  Talley spent 12 seasons in Buffalo and was part […]
full_text: Greg Rousseau has another milestone to add to his growing résumé with the Buffalo Bills. The outside linebacker recorded a sack against the Baltimore Ravens giving him 39 for his career and moving him past Darryl Talley into eighth place on the franchise’s all-time sack list. Talley spent 12 seasons in Buffalo and was part of the Bills teams that went to four consecutive Super Bowls in the early 1990s. He finished his time with the team with 38.5 sacks in 188 regular-season games. Rousseau, meanwhile, needed just 85 games to move past that total. Not bad for a player who is only in his sixth NFL season. And this season, Rousseau has been making that climb a little faster. With Jim Leonhard taking over as defensive coordinator under new head coach Joe Brady, Rousseau has moved from defensive end to outside linebacker. The change has given him different opportunities to get after opposing quarterbacks, and the results have been hard to miss. Rousseau recorded two sacks in each of Buffalo’s first three games before being held without one against New England. He entered Monday night’s game with six sacks, already within reach of the career-high eight he recorded in both 2022 and 2024. Now, with Talley behind him on the leaderboard, Rousseau has another name to chase. Mario Williams, who played four seasons in Buffalo from 2012 through 2015, sits seventh with 43 sacks. Greg Rousseau records his 7th sack of the season and becomes the 4th Bill with a sack today. https://t.co/aU5vkSctnG — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 1, 2026

title: Takeaways from Bills win over Ravens
summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the Ravens 36-10 in Week 8 at home. Baltimore used three quarterbacks in the contest as Lamar Jackson got hurt his first offensive play of the game and Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury later. Nonetheless, the Bills are now 6-1 entering Week 9. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills beat the Ravens 36-10 in Week 8 at home. Baltimore used three quarterbacks in the contest as Lamar Jackson got hurt his first offensive play of the game and Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury later. Nonetheless, the Bills are now 6-1 entering Week 9. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. The defense did what it should have given the circumstances Of course, I’m not expecting Buffalo’s defense to allow 144 points at 2.9 yards per play very often. Playing a third-string quarterback made things exceptionally easier for that unit in this game. BUT… Buffalo’s defense did exactly what it should hav against an undrafted rookie quarterback thrust into an emergency relief appearance. That’s a positive sign. Even Derrick Henry was held in check — only 11 carries for 53 yards — and Zay Flowers did not have a catch. Joey Fagnano demonstrated some moxie on a handful of throws yet none were completed to the receiver who entered this game with the NFL’s highest yards-per-route-run figure among all qualifying wideouts. So while it’s absolutely correct to mention the caveat regarding this performance from the Bills defense, it was placed in a no-win situation because of the competition level it faced at quarterback. This contest was a reminder that it’s a 60-minute game The Bills have an incredible ability to put forth a C+ / B- performance and either score 30-plus points and/or win by more than one score, both of which happened in this game. Despite the 16-7 lead at the half, Buffalo absolutely squandered quality scoring chances and made mistakes in the first two quarters. The end of half clock management wasn’t ideal. Worked. But the process was off. Overall, it was very disjointed. No doubt. The Bills went from a somewhat pedestrian 2.0 points per drive in the first half to a massive 4.0 points per drive in the second half. And the vibe of Buffalo’s offense and ease at which it moved the football matched those splits. In the third and fourth quarters, the Bills ran it more efficiently and got more pass-catchers involved at all levels of the field. In the end, Josh Allen finished 21-of-34 for 289 yards — 8.5 yards per — with two passing touchdowns, one interception, one sack, and a respectable passer rating of 96.3. While, yes, a team’s own offense does have an impact on the defense, it’s not as if the Ravens third-string unit was out there against Allen and Co. Welcome, back DJ Moore + Ed Oliver Finally, the Bills had one of their receivers make a spectacular grab in a low-percentage situation. Moore’s 49-yarder down the middle of the field was a thing of beauty we frankly haven’t seen much of from Buffalo’s pass-catching group over the past few seasons. His four snags, 82 yards and a score were a jolt to Buffalo’s aerial attack. On the defensive side, Oliver finished with four pressures on 18 pass-rush snaps — good for a whopping 22.2% pressure rate. His bull rush was outstanding throughout, and his first-step quickness gave Baltimore’s interior blocking unit problems all game. The Bills were playing without two key pieces on either side of the ball in Los Angeles and Las Vegas, and their impact was certainly felt in this win. I still think the WR corps needs a boost Despite Moore’s production — and outrageous catch on the long ball — it still feels like, collectively, the Bills receivers aren’t moving the needle enough on a regular, drive-to-drive basis. Now, sure, there’s Dalton Kincaid at tight end, who had an up-and-down contest, James Cook on the ground and through the air and Ty Johnson making something happen on a critical third down. But this offense still doesn’t want to feature Khalil Shakir — despite his awesome dependability — and Coleman disappeared in this game with one catch for four yards. And now, Josh Palmer is working through another injury. I highly doubt the Bills make a move at receiver before the trade deadline. But I would love for them to at least explore that position. As a last resort, how about some Greg Dortch in the offense? I want Allen to be able to lean on his collective of wide receivers a little more this season. There’s the Jim Leonhard we expected (possible springboard?) Leonhard likely was licking his chops when Huntley entered the game, and his eyes probably lit up when Baltimore’s undrafted rookie quarterback was forced into action. Those developments could’ve skewed Buffalo’s defensive philosophy in this one. But nonetheless, Leonhard went blitzing berserk in this victory, and I view that as a positive sign. The Bills blitzed on 64.5% of dropbacks against the Ravens in Week 8, their highest blitz rate since 2021 and the highest blitz rate Ravens quarterbacks have faced this season, according to @NextGenStats . Their blitz rate had not exceeded 39% in any of their previous six games. — Lance Lysowski (@LLysowski) November 1, 2026 Interestingly, Leonhard decided to call the game from the box for the first time this season as well. Should we expect the Bills to blitz on over 50% of the opposition’s dropbacks every week? Probably not. But remember, before this game, Buffalo had the NFL’s 20th-highest blitz rate at just 27.9%. Those blitzes were more creative against Baltimore and, sure, Jackson likely could’ve made some defenders miss in the pocket, but Leonhard’s blitz designs regularly got a free runner to the quarterback. Overall, Fagnano was pressured on 56% of his dropbacks. Huntley was pressured on four of his five dropbacks, and Jackson was pressured on his only one in this game. I wonder — and will be tracking — if this game acts as a springboard for a genuinely aggressive, blitz-heavy defense the rest of the way.
