title: Bills vs. Ravens Week 8 instant analysis: Buffalo defeats depleted Baltimore
summary: The Buffalo Bills moved to 6-1 with a 36-10 win over a Baltimore Ravens team that lost quarterback Lamar Jackson on its first play from scrimmage and finished the game with its third-string quarterback. A chaotic game for most of the afternoon, the Bills regained focus to turn a tight game into a blowout win […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Greg Rousseau #15 of the Buffalo Bills reacts after making a sack against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills moved to 6-1 with a 36-10 win over a Baltimore Ravens team that lost quarterback Lamar Jackson on its first play from scrimmage and finished the game with its third-string quarterback. A chaotic game for most of the afternoon, the Bills regained focus to turn a tight game into a blowout win versus a short-handed, overmatched Ravens team. Here are my notes as the game happened, with final game stats in parentheses. 1st Half Great 1st drive. Starting at the 40 helps, but good to see the offense in rhythm from the get-go against a talented defense that has played really well in 1st halves. (Khalil Shakir caught three passes for 49 yards on the opening drive.) Great to see Josh Allen willing to take the checkdown early. Pass could’ve been better, but I’d like to see James Cook catch that ball. A lot of green in front of him if he does. (Cook dropped a pass on the first play of the game and finished with two catches for 21 yards.) Dion Dawkins with a false start with the Bills ready to open the score. Not good. Thankfully the Bills offense is too much for this Ravens defense to deal with inside the red zone. An extra handful of plays and it’s Bills 7-0. (Allen finished the drive with a 1-yard touchdown run.) Ouch, this Ravens team is cursed. Lamar Jackson injured his hand on his first pass attempt, hitting Greg Rousseau’s hand hard as he released the ball. Looked like a thumb injury. Straight to the dressing room for X-rays, probably. Questionable to return. Defense quickly leaves the field not allowing points. (Jackson threw one pass all day.) Bills O back and starting the drive with a pass to Dalton Kincaid again. I love Joe Brady getting Kincaid involved early in games, should make the passing offense’s job easier going forward. Bills go for a 4th and short, Josh completes the pass to DJ Moore (it’s so good to have him back) but an illegal shift penalty denies the conversion. Tyler Bass (barely) stays 100% for FGs this season. Bills 10-0. (Bass’s 56-yarder went in off the left upright.) Bills defense starts really strong. No Lamar helps (listed as out now) but we can’t deny the job they have done. Containing the run and getting to Tyler Huntley. Ball will be back with the O. (Baltimore finished with 76 rushing yards on 19 carries.) Bills billsying. Jackson Hawes not only drops the ball but taps it up, almost like asking Baltimore’s defense to intercept it. Everything until this point of the game went in favor of Buffalo, and then they put the Ravens in the game again. (Broderick Washington Jr. made the interception, the first of his career.) Two Derrick Henry runs later, TD Ravens. Unbelievable. Can’t allow what became an easy game to turn into a tough one because of their own mistakes. (Henry’s 2-yard run was Baltimore’s only touchdown of the game.) Bills’ offensive turnover killed the team’s momentum , gave hope to a Ravens team that was clearly shaken by their QB1 injury, and also killed their own defense’s momentum, as they were perfect until that point. Gotta come back on track real quick. (Buffalo finished with two giveaways, this interception and a Moore fumble; Baltimore finished with three.) Buffalo’s O in trouble , but DJ Moore draws a holding penalty and a 1st down. He impacts this O beyond his numbers. (Moore finished with four catches for 82 yards and a touchdown.) Josh tries Joshua Palmer deep , but he seems hurt midway through his route. Looks like a muscular problem. It’s sad at this point but it’s tough to defend Palmer still ahead of rookie Skyler Bell. Awesome scramble by Josh , shakes the defender out of his shoes for another 1st down. (Allen finished with seven carries for 30 yards and a touchdown.) Another drop, now Dawson Knox. It’s tough for Josh to trust his guys on those short passes when they keep dropping with a lot of green in front of them. (Knox, Kincaid and Hawes each dropped a pass in the first quarter.) Defense back on track , containing the run and forcing obvious passing situations. Safety blitz works with Cole Bishop getting home. Fumble forced and recovered by the Bills, already in the red zone. (Bishop finished with two tackles, a sack and a QB hit; rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr recovered the fumble.) 4th and short , after failing to convert a tush push early in the game, Joe Brady finally calls an option out of the fake tush push. Needed a challenge flag but got the 1st. 3rd down , this time at the goal line, another speed option out of the tush push formation. This time Josh keeps it with Knox as the option, but Baltimore’s D is all over it. Loss of yards and FG. 13-7 Bills. (The designed Allen sweep lost four yards before Bass kicked a 22-yard field goal.) Those fakes being run to the left is straight dumb, IMO. Josh normally sneaks to the left already, run the fake to the right, give Josh an option to throw, I don’t get it. Ravens get a great return , but now Huntley is also out. (Baltimore returned eight kickoffs for 218 yards, with a long of 59.) Obviously, their 3rd QB starts shredding our defense in the 1st two passes. (Baltimore’s quarterbacks finished 12-of-26 for 91 yards with one interception, four sacks taken and a 39.1 passer rating.) Landon Jackson welcomes Joe Fagnano to the NFL with a sack. Nice stunt game by the DL. (The Bills finished with four sacks and 12 QB hits.) Bills D does its job, and Tyler Loop misses from 34 yards. Still Bills 13-7. (Loop made one of two field goals.) Three and out by the offense , with Josh missing Keon Coleman wide open, deep, for a touchdown. It’s not a good game by 17 so far, in a day when everything has cooperated toward a Bills W. They’re still allowing the Ravens to hang around. Defense is playing well. Stopping the run, doing what they should. Getting to the QB on 3rd downs. Some nice blitzes. Bills will have the ball again with 4 mins left. (Buffalo forced five three-and-outs.) A long drive ending in points would be good now to close the half. Bills O has struggled , but this Ravens defense has been really good in 1st halves this season. They’ve been ugly on 2nd halves, though. We’ll see today. James Cook with his first explosive run of the day , followed by a 6-yard run. 3 mins left in the 1st half. (Cook’s longest carry went for 16 yards; he finished with 21 carries for 80 yards.) 3rd and short, Josh had the 1-on-1 versus Roquan Smith and chose to throw. Ball got tipped by the Ravens LB, making Moore drop it. 4th down. (Smith finished with 11 tackles.) Bills go for it on their own side of the field. Swing pass to Ty Johnson with blockers ahead, 1st down and more. 2-minute warning. Josh completes a dart to DJ Moore, who fumbles it. Refs say he was down by contact but he wasn’t. Great punch by Roquan Smith. Ravens ball. Another mistake by the Bills offense. Baltimore has a chance at a double dip, 1:51 left in the 2nd quarter and they’ll get the ball back to start the 2nd half. Greg Rousseau with the sack and, as crazy as it sounds, the defense is saving the day. (Rousseau finished with one sack, one tackle for loss, three QB hits and two passes defensed.) Bills D forces a 3rd down and calls a timeout. Brady clearly wants another shot at points before the half. The Ravens get the 1st down. Missed tackle by Davison Igbinosun in space. A few plays later, IGB makes up for it. Geno Stone drops the INT but the rookie was there to secure it. 1:08 left, ball at the 33-yard line. Huge opportunity for the offense. (Igbinosun’s first career interception went for 17 yards; Stone finished with six tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass breakup.) The 1st half is close to an end and Zay Flowers is a no-show. title: Buffalo Bills improve to 6-1 with blowout win over Baltimore Ravens
summary: Winning in the NFL is incredibly tough, parity or not. That the Buffalo Bills are now 6-1 with a rookie head coach in Joe Brady all while facing a difficult schedule to begin the season is no small feat. Winning is, however, expected with Josh Allen playing quarterback. That also means being willing to admit […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Winning in the NFL is incredibly tough, parity or not. That the Buffalo Bills are now 6-1 with a rookie head coach in Joe Brady all while facing a difficult schedule to begin the season is no small feat. Winning is, however, expected with Josh Allen playing quarterback. That also means being willing to admit that it really isn’t how a team wins, but that it continues doing so in the face of adversity. ESPN Bills beat reporter Nick Suss put it best after Buffalo’s latest win was official, saying “(a) lot of first-world problems to address coming out of this one, but when your ‘ugly wins’ are 26-point bludgeonings of fellow contenders, allow yourself a few smiles. There was also this gem from Sal Capaccio of WGR 550 stating, “I feel like I say or tweet something like this just about every week. Bills now have 36 points and I have no idea how.” Those are two statements that properly encapsulate Buffalo’s mystifying Week 8 win. Sometimes fans need to be reminded that it’s okay to enjoy winning, allowing concerns to settle in during a later time. It’s also true that the Bills continue confounding many folks. Brady’s first go as the lead man after a bye deserves an incomplete at best. Yes, his team won, he gets the victory, but it was anything other than a commanding performance. One will likely wonder how this game unfolds if quarterback Lamar Jackson doesn’t get injured on Baltimore’s first offensive play. The Bills were a revelation on defense — which deserves both applause in what defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard was able to scheme up, but also a dose of reality in remembering that Buffalo faced an emergency quarterback named Joe Fagnano after Jackson and then backup quarterback Tyler Huntley were lost to injury. That isn’t to take away from what the defense did, specifically what the defensive backfield did to completely erase wide receiver Zay Flowers from the game. Also notable is the fact that Leonhard was in the booth and calling plays from upstairs for the first time as DC. Flowers was wholly irrelevant to the game’s outcome. Sure, some of that is due to enduring two changes at quarterback. Yet, Bills defensive back Te’Cory Couch played a masterful game against Flowers regardless of the situation. Then there was the mighty Derrick Henry. Buffalo has a complicated history with the certain future Pro Football Hall of Famer, but their latest effort against him went mostly their way. Henry finished with 53 yards on 12 carries, adding a touchdown run, and having a second one called back by penalty. You can’t ask for much more than that in working to limit Henry’s damage. A truly bizarre game, this is one where the defense carried the day until the offense began to click late. In the modern NFL, holding any NFL team to 10 points is a heck of an accomplishment. Optics matter, and that means recognizing how Jackson’s loss affected Baltimore’s game plan. Still, it’s great to see the Bills play a solid game on defense, all things considered. There’s plenty of work to do, as Nick Suss stated, and the team will continue being evaluated against a higher standard, where even the slightest flaw will be dissected against what their chances are in postseason play and, hopefully, a fruitful path to the Super Bowl. Buffalo must get better play in all phases. Today’s effort smelled a lot like a team struggling to re-focus after a bye, at least in the first half. Playing one half of football may catch up with Allen and the Bills in time. Right now, 6-1 looks fantastic on Buffalo. Up next is a primetime date with the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings and their fearsome defense.

title: Buffalo Bills stock up, stock down in big win over Baltimore Ravens
summary: What a weird game that was. The Buffalo Bills and the Baltimore Ravens matched up in what was supposed to be a showcase of two marquee quarterbacks. Instead, Baltimore’s Lamar Jackson left after one play, Buffalo’s Josh Allen struggled for much of the afternoon, and we all learned the name Joe Fagnano. The undrafted rookie […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a weird game that was. The Buffalo Bills and the Baltimore Ravens matched up in what was supposed to be a showcase of two marquee quarterbacks. Instead, Baltimore’s Lamar Jackson left after one play, Buffalo’s Josh Allen struggled for much of the afternoon, and we all learned the name Joe Fagnano. The undrafted rookie from UCONN entered to play quarterback after Baltimore’s backup quarterback, Tyler Huntley, suffered a toe injury in the second quarter to knock him out of the game. It was all part of a wild afternoon where Buffalo’s defense dominated, Baltimore’s defense kept the game close for as long as they could, and Josh Allen earned yet another major career achievement. Was it perfect? Definitely not. However, the Bills will take a 36-10 win over the Ravens as they head into a Monday night matchup with the Minnesota Vikings next week. Here are our horns up and horns down for the Bills’ blowout victory. _____________________________________________________________________________ Horns Up: Cole Bishop Bishop made a big play in the first half, speeding through on a blitz to sack Baltimore quarterback Tyler Huntley. Bishop’s big hit forced Huntley to fumble, and after a scrum, rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr recovered to give the Bills great field position. While the team would only convert a field goal, it was points, and it was Bishop who set it up. He played well throughout the game, as he covered Mark Andrews tightly in man looks and also patrolled his zone with authority. Bishop finished with two tackles, a sack, and a QB hit. Horns Down: Tight Ends In the first quarter alone, all three of Buffalo’s tight ends dropped a pass. Dalton Kincaid’s drop, at least, could have been a pass breakup, as he was unable to secure a contested catch against cornerback Chidobe Awuzie. Dawson Knox had one hit him right in the hands on a crossing route and he dropped it. However, the worst drop came from Jackson Hawes, as he had a middle screen hit him right in the bread basket. He couldn’t secure the catch, but worse still, he batted the ball high into the air almost as if he were a libero passing to his setter. This isn’t volleyball, but he put the ball up softly enough where Baltimore’s Broderick Washington Jr. easily secured the first interception of his seven-year career. It set up a short field and an easy touchdown for the Ravens. Later, Kincaid made a nice catch on a deep ball in the fourth quarter, but he immediately followed it up with a wide-open drop. It was a microcosm of the kind of day Buffalo’s usually dependable tight end group had. Horns Up: Tyler Bass With the offense stuck in neutral for much of the first half, it was Bass providing much of the scoring for Buffalo. He doinked a 56-yard field goal in off the left upright to give the Bills a 10-0 lead. Then, he hit a 22-yard field goal after a questionable play call turned what should have been a tush-push attempt at a touchdown into a four-yard loss on a designed Josh Allen sweep. Then, with 14 seconds left in the first half, Bass was good from 51 yards out to push Buffalo’s lead to 16-7 at halftime. Bass was perfect on field goals, hitting all three of his tries, and he was also perfect on his three PAT attempts. It’s been a phenomenal season so far for Bass. Horns Up: Geno Stone The veteran had a pretty terrible preseason with the Bills, as it was clear that he wasn’t going to make the 53-man roster from a fairly early time in the summer. However, in his first action of the season as a practice squad call-up, Stone made his presence known. He made a stop on third and long on the first drive, planting Justice Hill for a one-yard loss. Then, late in the first half, Stone played the “robber” role and fooled third-string Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano into thinking he had Zay Flowers open. He didn’t, and Stone nearly intercepted the pass. His deflection pushed the ball up into the air, which allowed rookie Davison Igbinosun to secure his first career interception. That led to the aforementioned 51-yard field goal from Bass. Of course, the caveat here is that Baltimore’s quarterback situation today was dire, but Stone was sound in his assignments and strong in his play all day long. He finished with a team-high six tackles, one tackle for loss, and one pass breakup. Horns Down: Head Coaching Decisions Why are we straying from the Allen QB sneak in one-yard situations? Baltimore stopped it once. Good for them—make them do it again! While the play call ultimately worked, what was the deal with the clock management at the end of the first half? The result was positive, as Josh Allen scrambled for 14 yards on a beautifully designed run, but the better move was likely to run a play and keep their timeout to set up a field goal on the next play. Instead, head coach Joe Brady let the clock run down to 18 seconds before burning the timeout. The play calling on offense was shoddy at times in the first half, as nothing Buffalo did looked easy. It shouldn’t be that hard for Buffalo to find rhythm on offense, especially with all of their playmakers healthy, but Buffalo made a middling Baltimore defense look elite at times. Yes, they settled in as the game went on, but the Bills won’t be playing too many third-string quarterbacks from here on out, so they likely won’t have that kind of time to find their footing in future games. Horns Up: Khalil Shakir Yes, he leads the Bills in targets, is tied with Dalton Kincaid in receptions, and is second to Kincaid in receiving yards after today’s game, but I still feel like he’s someone who needs the football more. Shakir is dynamic in space, so finding ways to put the ball in his hands at all levels of the defense should be a priority. Today, it looked like that was an early priority, as Shakir caught three passes for 49 yards a near-touchdown on the Bills’ first drive. However, he went quiet for the better part of the next few drives. When Josh Allen went back to him, the offense moved the ball. DJ Moore might be the clear alpha receiver, but Shakir is still Allen’s security blanket. He’s also one of the NFL’s most dynamic playmakers in space. Joe Brady needs to make sure to continue feeding No. 10, who finished today’s game with five catches for 64 yards on six targets. Horns Up: Greg Rousseau Rousseau made arguably the biggest play of the game, and it was the first play from scrimmage for Buffalo’s defense. On Baltimore’s first offensive play, Rousseau hit quarterback Lamar Jackson’s throwing hand, tipping the pass and mangling the star quarterback’s thumb. That was Jackson’s only play of the game, and it was the first of multiple tipped passes at the line for Groot. Rousseau had a sack and three quarterback hits to go with two tipped passes through the first three quarters of the game. While he didn’t add to that stat line in the fourth quarter, much of the reason why is that the Bills expanded their lead to the point where Buffalo had as many reserves in the game as they could. It was a very good day for No. 15 and the Buffalo pass defense. Horns Down: Penalties You know what? I normally would say that the penalties are indicative of a lack of discipline. Today, though, it felt like Ross Tucker sighed and called the penalty weak after nearly every flag. There were holding calls that looked like nothing, and then there was contact with no flag. Case in point: On Allen’s first touchdown, linebacker Roquan Smith tried to rip his head off. It’s the day after Halloween, sure, but Allen’s helmet went around like Linda Blair in The Exorcist with no call. I don’t think it was a good day for the zebras, who certainly contributed to the game’s lack of flow. Horns Up: Te’Cory Couch and Damar Hamlin Yes, I…

title: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly for Bills touchdown record
summary: Josh Allen has spent much of his career rewriting the Buffalo Bills’ record books. On Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens, he claimed another piece of franchise history, moving past Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Jim Kelly for the most career touchdown passes, including the postseason.  Allen entered the game tied with Kelly at 258 […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen has spent much of his career rewriting the Buffalo Bills’ record books. On Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens, he claimed another piece of franchise history, moving past Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Jim Kelly for the most career touchdown passes, including the postseason. Josh Allen connects with DJ Moore on his 259th career passing TD (including playoffs), surpassing Jim Kelly (258) for the most in franchise history. pic.twitter.com/zkxVUT79R9 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 1, 2026 Allen entered the game tied with Kelly at 258 touchdown passes. His 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the fourth quarterback gave him No. 259, putting him alone at the top of a list that Kelly had led since his retirement following the 1996 season. Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Just two weeks earlier, Allen had pulled even with Kelly during Buffalo’s 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. A nine-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Khalil Shakir brought him within one of the record before a 12-yard backhanded shovel pass to wide receiver Keon Coleman tied the two quarterbacks at 258. The record includes both regular-season and postseason touchdowns, a distinction that matters when comparing the two quarterbacks. Kelly still holds Buffalo’s regular-season record with 237 touchdown passes, while Allen entered Sunday’s game with 229. Allen has reached the combined mark considerably faster than his predecessor. Kelly played 177 games over 11 seasons with Buffalo, including 17 postseason appearances. Allen entered the Ravens game having played 149 games, including 15 in the playoffs, putting him 28 games behind Kelly when he matched the Hall of Famer’s total. With half a season still on the calendar, and Allen just needing just eight touchdowns to move his name onto the top line under the title “Franchise leader for regular season touchdown passes,” the watch for Allen to take another category is on.

title: Tyler Bass sets Bills record for consecutive field goals made
summary: Buffalo Bills kicker Tyler Bass has put his name at the top of the franchise record books, connecting on his 19th consecutive field goal on Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens to break a record that had stood for nearly 19 years.  Bass entered Sunday’s game having made 18 straight field goals, tying the franchise record […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 18: Tyler Bass #16 of the Buffalo Bills kicks a field goal against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills kicker Tyler Bass has put his name at the top of the franchise record books, connecting on his 19th consecutive field goal on Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens to break a record that had stood for nearly 19 years. Bass entered Sunday’s game having made 18 straight field goals, tying the franchise record set by Rian Lindell during the 2007 season. His 56-yard field goal in the first gave him sole possession of the record, moving him past Lindell for the longest streak of consecutive successful regular-season field goals in Bills history. Bass’s streak dates back to the 2024 season and has continued through his return to the field this year after missing the entire 2025 season with an injury. Today’s field goal wasn’t the cleanest kick, but it ended on the right side of the goal post and that’s all that matters. A doink make from 56 yards out for Tyler Bass & the Bills! BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/62oTe44wZb — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Bills kicker entered Sunday’s matchup a perfect 13-for-13 on field-goal attempts in 2026. He made four against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6, helping Buffalo secure a 33-30 win before heading into their bye week. The week before, against the Los Angeles Rams, he connected on a 45-yard field goal in overtime to give Buffalo a 37-34 win. While Bass has missed two extra-point attempts this season, he has yet to miss a field goal with today’s 56-yarded being the longest. Lindell’s streak ran from October 21 through December 9, 2007. During that stretch, he tied Steve Christie’s previous franchise record of 17 consecutive field goals before extending the mark to 18. Lindell wasn’t the only kicker that Bass was compared to after the kick. The 56-yard boot was Bass’s sixth straight kick of 50+ yards – a mark that tied him with Stephen Hauschka (2017) for the Bills’ franchise record. His 51-yarder in the second quarter broke that tie.

title: What’s next?
summary: The 3-4 Carolina Panthers held on to first place in the NFC South thanks to a16-0 win by the 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers over the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons that featured 324 yards rushing and -2 yards passing by the Bucs. This is the company that we keep. The company we don’t keep anymore includes former […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers runs to the sidelines against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 3-4 Carolina Panthers held on to first place in the NFC South thanks to a16-0 win by the 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers over the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons that featured 324 yards rushing and -2 yards passing by the Bucs. This is the company that we keep. The company we don’t keep anymore includes former defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and former defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. The defense has been a point of contention for Panthers fans in recent years as a sort of chicken or egg scenario. Limited investment and limited success have made it difficult to fully evaluate Evero’s work on a game-by-game basis. The full course of his tenure in Charlotte, however, clearly left head coach Dave Canales dissatisfied. Some will say this firing is overdue. Others will question the timing and ultimate purpose of it at this point in the season. Regardless, we shouldn’t hold our collective breathe in anticipation of major changes for the Panthers porous defense. The fact remains that with Jaelan Phillips in and out of the lineup with injuries and Cam Jackson, Mike Jackson, Jaycee Horn, Akayleb Evans, Nic Scourton, and Thomas Incoom all on injured reserve, the Panthers are basically playing preseason football out there. That is not to say that the defense is the only problem unit the Panthers have. Their offensive line has been a specific and obvious weakness for some time. Starters Taylor Moton, Ikem Ekwonu, and Damien Lewis have all been sorely missed throughout their various injuries. Free agent acquisitions Rasheed Walker and Luke Fortner have simply been complete disappointments. Right guard Robert Hunt’s play and mental focus may have you questioning if he ever actually did return from his 2025 torn bicep. Rookie offensive tackle Monroe Freeling, meanwhile, is doing his best out there. He could be worse, the unit as a whole however could hardly be. They helped prove two weeks in s row that the Panthers cannot win a shootout if they don’t let their quarterback shoot. Enter the 6-2 Denver Broncos, a team with twice as many wins as any team in the NFC South. The Panthers’ Week 9 opponent has a capable passing game and a relatively fearsome defensive line that sacked Patrick Mahomes twice yesterday afternoon. While they only have ten sacks on the season, they may expect to double that total against a Panthers offensive line that has surrendered 11 sacks in the last two games. They are, in short, a competent, competitive NFL team who will provide a solid test for the Panthers. The Broncos are probably the best team the Panthers have faced so far. Early season success against backup quarterbacks may have falsely inflated expectations for Carolina, but they still have limited talent on both sides of the ball. There is enough talent that they could steal a few games if they can shore up their obvious weakenesses at corner, right guard, center, left guard, and left tackle. That will be the test that they have to pass against a hungry Broncos team that is looking to build on their own divisional lead. What us next, in this context, is that test. The next few weeks will be an inflection point for these Panthers. Either they will pull themselves together through adversity or they will squander the hottest start they have had in a season since Sam Darnold was here. I’m not saying that they have to beat the Broncos to save their season, but they absolutely have to look like they belong on the same field as them. If they can do that then they can at least play a competitive December, further injuries permitting.

title: Chicago Bears @ Seattle Seahawks: Week 8 Players to Watch
summary: After captivating the league’s attention (if they weren’t already on notice), the Chicago Bears once again have an elite Primetime matchup with another Super Bowl contender – if not outright favorite – in the current defending champion Seattle Seahawks. Chicago will not only have to tighten up some mental mistakes that have led to 21 […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts after a play against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After captivating the league’s attention (if they weren’t already on notice), the Chicago Bears once again have an elite Primetime matchup with another Super Bowl contender – if not outright favorite – in the current defending champion Seattle Seahawks. Chicago will not only have to tighten up some mental mistakes that have led to 21 penalties over the last two weeks, but also deal with arguably the most talented roster in the league at the most difficult stadium in the league. Ben Johnson and Co. have their work cut out for them in what many are saying may be a preview of the NFC Championship game. Let’s get to which players from Seattle will have my attention on both sides of the ball. Offense: Quenton Nelson, #53 – G Anytime you add an All-Pro talent mid-week, he is going to get quite a bit of attention. Fortunately for Chicago, they, too, added an All-Pro talent in the form of Jeffery Simmons – the former Tennessee Titan who played against Nelson’s Colts twice a year. All in all, these two have played each other 13 times over the course of their careers but never surrounded by the talent these two have around them this time. Nelson being added to the Super Bowl champs is the definition of the rich getting richer. Considered by many as the best Guard in the league, Nelson is and has been a dominating force in the middle and figures to provide a jolt to the struggling Seahawks run game while assisting in keeping Sam Darnold clean in the pocket. Considering the offensive line is the one position group in the game of football that relies more on cohesiveness than any other, I am expecting a few hiccups in his first game action, especially within his first 7 days as a Seahawk, but Nelson still has the ability coupled with opportunity to make quite an impact Monday night. If Dennis Allen and his shiny new toy can cause some confusion up front and get after Sam Darnold, Chicago’s secondary will have a chance to create some critical turnovers and give Chicago a chance. If Nelson fortifies the Seahawks OL and helps keep Darnold clean whilst simultaneously opening holes in the run game – it will be a humbling experience for Chicago this week. Defense: Nick Emmanwori, #3 – S When it comes to the former 2nd-round pick out of South Carolina, his impact simply cannot be measured in the box score. And yet, out of all the bona fide ballers on the Seahawks’ vaunted defense, #3 is the one player who keeps opposing offenses up at night more than anyone else. Think of Kyler Gordon but 3 inches taller, 20lb heavier, and runs a 4.3 forty instead of a 4.5. And like Spidey, Emmanwori is deployed all over the defense, presenting unique challenges for any offense. According to Sumer Sports’ Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes), Emmanwori has been deployed in the slot 36% of his snaps, at Linebacker 34%, and 27% at Edge. I love Nick Emmanwori so much pic.twitter.com/DVaSay5Olx — Pete (@thefilmwatcher_) October 5, 2026 How Chicago manages this demon will be crucial. And like I said, they have multiple difference makers on that side of the ball that are capable in wrecking games. From Devon Witherspoon (arguably my FAVORITE Corner in the league) to Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy Jr. (best DT duo in the league) to pass rushers Derrick Hall and Uchenna Nwosu, these Seahawks likely have more than 11 defenders who would start on most teams. That’s not even taking into account dependable veteran difference makers like Safety Julian Love, LB Earnest Jones IV, and DT Jarran Reed. And yet – Emmanwori is more worrisome than them all. If Caleb Williams can avoid Emmanwori and the Bears offense can get a body on him in the run game – Chicago has enough talent on offense to put up points against anyone – Seattle included. But if Emmanwori can confuse the offense, make Bears TE Sam Roush look like the rookie he is, and nullify the impact of Colston Loveland, then Chicago is in trouble. Big game Monday night! Who on Seattle’s squad will you be watching most closely?

title: Chicago Bears Trade Deadline Rumors on Khalil Mack and Tyson Bagent
summary: On the Sunday Night Football pregame show, Mike Florio speculated that the Baltimore Ravens, who lost their two top quarterbacks today, could be in the market for a quarterback ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline, and he mentioned the Chicago Bears’ Tyson Bagent. Perhaps it’s just logical dot-connecting by Florio, since Baltimore’s offensive coordinator, Declan […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 29: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears throws a pass during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 29, 2023 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the Sunday Night Football pregame show, Mike Florio speculated that the Baltimore Ravens, who lost their two top quarterbacks today, could be in the market for a quarterback ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline, and he mentioned the Chicago Bears’ Tyson Bagent. Perhaps it’s just logical dot-connecting by Florio, since Baltimore’s offensive coordinator, Declan Doyle, spent 2025 with the Bears, but it would make sense for them to check with Chicago about Bagent’s availability. The Ravens are 4-4 and still in contention in a competitive AFC North, and with QB1 Lamar Jackson heading to injured reserve with thumb surgery, and QB2 Tyler Huntley dealing with turf toe, they’re left with rookie undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano. In their loss today, Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards, 1 interception, and a passer rating of 40.0. He was also sacked 3 times, rushed for 3 yards, and lost a fumble. Sports Illustrated’s Jason La Canfora (yeah, I know, JLC’s track record with Bears scoops has been bad) is reporting that the Ravens have already reached out to the Bears. The Ravens top pursuit is Bears back-up quarterback Tyson Bagent, according to multiple high-ranking NFL personnel execs. They have reached out to Chicago, but are in a desperate position, DeCosta already got fleeced trading a second-round pick for a concussed and suspect offensive lineman. Multiple league sources told me through the summer that the Bears were rebuffing all overtures for Badgent (who makes $4M this year and $4M next year), who they believe can be a valuable back-up in Ben Johnson’s system. “Chicago doesn’t have to trade him,” one NFL GM told me. “They like him … Wonder how hard they squeeze DeCosta?” There were offseason rumors that the Bears received calls on Bagent, but the desperation of two injured quarterbacks and a deadline may be what they need to get an offer they can’t refuse. The other Bears-related rumor that popped up on Sunday was a familiar one. NFL Insider Ian Rapoport talked about Chicago’s big trade for Jeffery Simmons this morning on NFL Game Day , then added, “The Bears may not actually be done. I’m told they are still calling around. Still looking on the edges of their defense. Wouldn’t be surprised if a Khalil Mack trade was in the offer here. A possible reunion for Mack and the Bears.” Mack’s current team, the Los Angeles Chargers, just lost to the Los Angeles Rams, dropping to 0-7, so if they aren’t ready to deal the 35-year-old Mack, they never will be. Mack played a season-low 35 snaps in the 24 to 9 loss to the Rams, making 2 tackles. In 7 games, all starts, Mack has 21 tackles, 5 tackles for loss, and 3 sacks. Mack was asked about the trade rumors today, and he said ( via FOX Sports’ Eric Williams ): “You’ve got to be where your feet are, man, ultimately. That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all times. That’s kind of been my thing in years past.” The Chicago Bears play tomorrow on Monday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks, and the NFL’s trade deadline is November 10.

title: Bears vs. Seahawks – Game Picks and Predictions
summary: Hello Chicago Bears fans! Monday night in Seattle is the biggest road test yet for a 5-2 Bears team that has looked like a legitimate contender. full_text: CHICAGO, IL - DECEMBER 26: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello Chicago Bears fans! Monday night in Seattle is the biggest road test yet for a 5-2 Bears team that has looked like a legitimate contender. Chicago’s league-leading rushing attack and a Caleb Williams-led offense that just put up 30 on the Patriots run into the defending Super Bowl champions, a 4-3 Seahawks squad coming off a dominant 20-3 win over Kansas City. Both teams have added significant pieces before the deadline, with the Seahawks adding All-Pro guard Quinton Nelson, and the Bears adding All-Pro defensive tackle Jefferey Simmons. Seattle is favored by about three points at Lumen Field, but the Bears’ recent form and ability to control the ground game give them a real shot at a statement win. What follows are our score pick, winner, and projected stat lines for a prime-time matchup that could shape the NFC race. Kickoff: Monday, November 2, 2026, at Lumen Field in Seattle at 7:15 p.m. CT (8:15 p.m. ET) TV: ESPN (national); in the Chicago area, it also airs on The U (WCIU-Channel 26) because ABC is carrying Dancing with the Stars . ESPN2 has the ManningCast with Peyton and Eli. Streaming: ESPN app and NFL+ Radio: ESPN Chicago (1000 AM / 100.3 FM HD2) National broadcast team is Joe Buck (play-by-play) and Troy Aikman (analyst), with Laura Rutledge on the sideline. Local Bears radio is Jeff Joniak, Tom Thayer, and Jason McKie. Pick and Predictions Josh: In the first game without Cole Kmet, the offense struggles to move the ball for three quarters. Jaylon Johnson limits JSN to 120 yards and a touchdown, which seems nearly miraculous. Caleb tries and fails to stage some late-game heroics. It comes down to a throw Darnold should never have tried and a Thieneman pick-6. Chicago steals one 24-20. Sam : Realist take. This is one you probably mentally put as a loss when the schedule came out in the spring. I’m not sure anything has changed for me. If it were in Chicago it’s a different story. The Seahawks defense just showed their teeth against Patrick Mahomes. We know Ben and Caleb will get theirs, but this game is going to be a slugfest, worthy of the playoff implications it will likely carry. Seahawks 27, Bears 26 after a potential Chicago game-winning 2-point conversion attempt is knocked incomplete with less than 2 minutes to play. Gary : I had this penciled in as an L back when I did pre-season predictions. Defending Superbowl champions, best defense in the league on the road in one of the most hostile environments. The deck is stacked against us. With the way the offense has performed, even without the benefit of a rushing attack that was leading the world the first 4 weeks, it gives you some hope, but you can’t win every game, and a road loss to the defending champs is an honorable death. 27-21 Seahawks. Edit: Jeffery Simmons is a Bear, 400-0 Bears. GOOCH : After the Hawks added Nelson, I had concerns, especially since we are on the road in a stadium legendary for how difficult it is for the opposition. But then Poles decided to bring us the best defensive tackle in football. The Hawks’ defense is tough. They’re going to accumulate at least three sacks against Caleb, who is still working his way back to 100% from the hamstring pull. But my optimism meter is overflowing, and I believe that Guy will be back playing on Monday night, and we will have our two-headed monster at running back again. The Bears do what they do, control the clock, run the ball, and put up 150 yards on the ground between Swift and Monangai, with KM getting a touchdown in his return. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland notch TDs, while Rome puts up 80+ yards. Meanwhile, the Bears have Sam Darnold and the Hawks offense on their heels all night. They can’t get a consistent running attack, and Darnold is sacked by Simmons, Sweat, and Booker while throwing an ill-advised pick to T.J. Edwards, who drops into coverage in his return to the lineup. Bears 27, Seahawks 17.

They also dive into the Bears v. Seattle Seahawks game and what it will take for the Bears to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 4: Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks in action during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Lumen Field on October 4, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll is joined by former Chicago Bears cornerback Jerry Azumah to talk about the newest Chicago Bears player, Jeffery Simmons, and the immediate impact he’ll have on this defense. They also dive into the Bears v. Seattle Seahawks game and what it will take for the Bears to upset the defending champion on the road. Taylor is then joined by Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times, who shares the Seahawks’ perspective after they made a big trade for Quenton Nelson to try to spark their run game and protect Sam Darnold. Taylor and Bob chat about all things Seattle, plus this possible chess match between Ben Johnson and Mike Macdonald, and how Macdonald’s defense will attack the Bears. “They don’t blitz a ton. You know, traditionally, they’re not the biggest blitzing team ever. What they do more is try to bring pressure from different spots than you’ll see,” Condotta said. “So, it’s not always necessarily bringing like six guys, but it’s bringing four or five guys, but not from spots you necessarily thought those guys were coming from.” Condotta then discussed Seattle’s biggest X factor. “And that’s where Nick Emmanwori has become such a factor because he’s basically, essentially a strong side linebacker, but people make a big deal out of the Seahawks always playing nickel because they look at Emmanwori being listed as a safety, but you know, essentially a strong side linebacker. But you know, they can put him on the defensive line, and he’s just like a rush end.” ”It makes it kind of hard to know what they’re doing with him on this play, where what is he going to do, and you know you can rush him and drop someone else, and that’s where I think McDonald is really at his most dangerous is devising things like that.“ Besides previewing the game, Azumah also got into the big Simmons trade, and what else he’d like to see the Bears do. “I would like to see a defensive back, particularly a corner, to go over to the Chicago Bears,” he said about another possible trade. “I think that they could use the depth. There’ve been some issues in the secondary, but you know, Dennis Allen, he runs a very precise system, and the DBs have to basically match up to the wide receivers, and sometimes they lose. So I think that with Simmons being there, I think that that’s going to help out the secondary tremendously, but I wouldn’t mind seeing a depth move at corner.” Check out the full show in either of the embeds below, or anywhere you get your podcasts. This week’s Reacts results are pretty much the same as a week ago, when confidence was at 92.7%. I’m sure we have some visiting voters from the SB Nation sites that cover the Packers, Lions, and Vikings in the poll trying to sway things negatively, but if there are still disgruntled Bears fans out there voting no, I need to know: why? If a (5-2) record one season after an (11-5) NFC North Championship team that beat the Packers in the Wildcard round and narrowly lost in the Divisional round isn’t enough for you to be confident the Bears are heading in the right direction, then what are you waiting for? Perfection? Now, to be fair, most of these votes were tallied before the Bears made the all-in move of trading for Jeffery Simmons. So maybe some of your hesitation in voting yes was that you were waiting for the defensive line to be addressed. Well, it’s been addressed in the biggest way, and the baddest defensive tackle in the NFL now resides in the Windy City. Simmons goes from the one-win Titans to the high-profile Bears, who have two prime-time games up next, and a bigger media presence can only help his chances at the Defensive Player of the Year Award. Simmons is a force multiplier, and the entire defense will benefit from his presence in the middle of the Bears’ d-line Chicago’s defense has been generating pressure by blitzing, but Simmons will let them drop more into coverage, which could help their struggling corners. Nickelback Kyler Gordon is tied for the team lead with 4 sacks in just 2 games, but the Bears may not have to send him off the edge as much with Simmons pushing the pocket. On Monday night, the Bears play the Seattle Seahawks and one of the best wide receivers in the game, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and when he runs routes out of the slot, Gordon could be counted on to cover. Do you think Gordon can cintnue his surprisinly impressinve play?

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ overtime win over the Titans
summary: That’s the second game in a row where the Cincinnati Bengals fell behind 13-0. Only this time, it came against a seemingly outmatched opponent, the Tennessee Titans. This was one that Cincinnati easily could have lost, and that would have been a disaster in a tight AFC North. Instead, it resulted in a thrilling overtime […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - NOVEMBER 1: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II #97 celebrates with teammates after recovering a fumble in a game between the Tennessee Titans and the Cincinnati Bengals on November 1, 2026, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images That’s the second game in a row where the Cincinnati Bengals fell behind 13-0. Only this time, it came against a seemingly outmatched opponent, the Tennessee Titans. This was one that Cincinnati easily could have lost, and that would have been a disaster in a tight AFC North. Instead, it resulted in a thrilling overtime victory that taught us a lot about how the team (especially the defense) has grown. Here’s what we learned. 1. There’s no stopping this offense once it gets going Against the Baltimore Ravens two weeks ago, the Bengals got 35 points in the second half. Then, against Tennessee, the Bengals scored zero points in the first quarter but ended up with 43. Tee Higgins got the ball rolling, and Ja’Marr Chase led the way late. But the engine was, of course, Joe Burrow, who finished 38-of-48 for 462 yards, with five touchdowns, three interceptions, and a rushing touchdown. To put that into perspective, Burrow became the first quarterback since 1951 to get 450 yards, five touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown in the same game. (The fact that the Bengals QB did something that got “Norm Van Brocklin” trending 43 years after his death is saying something.) So when the defense did what it has done so often in recent years (give up long plays and turn borderline starting QBs into superstars), the offense didn’t blink. Burrow and the Bengals just continued to fire downfield, not letting interceptions get in the way, because they know they can outlast anyone. 2. Tee Higgins has gone all the way beast mode It’s not just the 10 catches for 155 yards. It’s the fact that Tee Higgins looks more dominant than he ever has before. He’s manhandling defensive backs, catching in traffic, catching over the top of their heads, and not showboating afterwards. He knows who he is: one of the very best in the game. What’s really noticeable is how easy it seems to be for him. Higgins doesn’t even seem to be going full speed, but he’s getting right by guys because of how confident he is in his route running, hands, and big body, which is always going to win. Higgins now has totaled 148 yards or more in three of seven games. He’s on pace for 104 catches, 1,763 yards, and 10 touchdowns, which has only been done six times before . Forget the WR2 or WR1A talk. Just enjoy the fact that the Bengals have two supremely talented receivers, and neither of them can be contained for an entire game. 3. The defensive line gives them a chance to win games they never used to Burrow pointed out that this Titans game was precisely the kind of contest they’d lost the last three years. And it looked bound to happen again, with Cam Ward driving to get near field goal range with under a minute left. But then Dexter Lawrence got a monstrous sack, grabbing hold of Ward and slamming him to the ground . It was the most dominant sack these eyes have seen since Geno Atkins propelled Deshaun Watson into the air back in 2017. That play brought the Bengals back to life. And it was the kind of play that was missing, especially from the interior of the defensive line, for so many years. It was the result of a beautiful collaboration with Boye Mafe. According to Paul Dehner Jr ., “Lawrence and Mafe gave each other a look” and then we had “Mafe banging into Lawrence’s blocker, helping free the 350-pound wrecking ball to slam Titans quarterback Cam Ward to the ground for a sack.” The two combined for another huge play in the third quarter, when Mafe strip-sacked Ward, and Lawrence picked up the ball and returned it eight yards (he was tragically tripped before he could take it all the way—that would have been an all-time highlight). Those two plays, along with Demetrius Knight Jr. shooting through the gap to tackle Tony Pollard for a safety, showed you precisely the kind of game-changing plays that are possible when you’re consistently winning in the trenches.

title: Best available NFL free agent cornerbacks the Bengals could target if DJ Turner misses significant time
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since 2021, when they won the AFC Championship Game and went to their third Super Bowl berth in franchise history. Unfortunately, they may have lost cornerback DJ Turner, who suffered an ankle injury in the fourth quarter against the Titans on Sunday. The Bengals came into […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since 2021, when they won the AFC Championship Game and went to their third Super Bowl berth in franchise history. Unfortunately, they may have lost cornerback DJ Turner, who suffered an ankle injury in the fourth quarter against the Titans on Sunday. The Bengals came into the 2026 season dangerously thin at the position, opting to focus on safety and the defensive line. If Turner does miss some time, it’s unlikely they’ll be able to just absorb the injury and move forward with the next man up. So, here are some free agent corners the Bengals could bring in for a workout before they head to Spain for their Week 9 game against the Falcons. Jeff Okudah Former Buckeye standout Jeff Okudah could be an interesting option for the Bengals. He was the No. 3 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft by the Detroit Lions, but he struggled to live up to that draft position, largely because of injuries and inconsistent play. He most recently played for the Vikings, appearing in six games in 2025 before multiple concussions landed him on IR. The 6-foot-1, 205-pound cornerback has the size and speed to play on the outside, and he could be looking to prove he can put it all together on the field. He’s relatively young, and the Bengals could do worse if they need urgent help. Adoree’ Jackson Jackson could be one of the more realistic options for the Bengals to reinforce the secondary. The former first-round pick spent the ‘25 season with the Eagles, starting 10 games in which he recorded 55 tackles, 11 passes defended, and an interception. Previously a member of the Titans and Giants, Jackson has experience at outside corner and has the athleticism to match up with some of the league’s better wide receivers. Despite being 31, he has a better recent track record than many younger corners still available. Marshon Lattimore The 11th-overall pick out of Ohio State in the 2017 NFL Draft, Lattimore would bring a wealth of experience to the Bengals defense, though there hasn’t been much reported on him since he appeared in 11 games last season in Washington before suffering a torn ACL. Even before the injury, it was clear that the 30-year-old Lattimore was well past his prime, earning a career-low 53.2 PFF grade before the injury. Even so, you won’t find many free agent cornerbacks out there with his experience and talent. Might be time to give him a call and see how his rehab is going. Artie Burns Former Steelers first-round pick Artie Burns is another veteran cornerback available on the market who could draw interest from Cincinnati. The 31-year-old has appeared in 90 career games with 39 starts and has spent time in Pittsburgh, Chicago, and Seattle before he was signed by the Dolphins in 2025. Burns tore his ACL during training camp last summer, which ended his season before it began, which means he hasn’t seen a snap since the 2024 season. He does have experience in the slot and on the outside, but there are younger and more reliable options. Mike Hilton The former Bengals cornerback is still a free agent after spending the 2025 season on the Colts’ practice squad. Hilton would offer the Bengals familiarity, but there’s been little mention of him since last season, and it’s possible the 32-year-old cornerback isn’t considering a return to the NFL. But if he is, the Bengals should give Hilton a call. He may be well past his prime, but there aren’t many guys out there who can come in and have at least a decent feel for the team’s defensive scheme. Jalyn Armour-Davis The former Ravens and Titans corner could be an intriguing option for Cincinnati, especially considering his relatively young age and recent starting experience. The 27-year-old former Alabama standout started 10 games for the Titans in 2025 before suffering a torn Achilles in December. He has excellent size and speed for an outside cornerback, but injuries and inconsistent play have prevented him from establishing himself as a dependable NFL starter. He reportedly is fully healthy and worked out for the Bills and Chargers in October, though he wasn’t signed by either team. Kyu Blu Kelly This could be one of the more intriguing options for the Bengals, especially if Kelly is fully healthy. He’s only 25 years old and enjoyed his most productive season in 2025 for the Raiders. He recorded 40 tackles, defended six passes, and intercepted 3 in 13 games before he suffered a ruptured Patellar tendon in December. Kelly worked out for the Falcons in September, which suggests he has recovered from his injury, but he remains unsigned. Kelly, a former fifth-round pick by the Ravens out of Stanford, could be a solid addition if he’s fully healthy. Trevon Diggs Former Cowboys All-Pro cornerback Trevon Diggs is on the Seahawks’ practice squad and could be signed to the Bengals’ active roster should they go that route. He led the NFL with 11 interceptions in 2021, but struggled with injuries and some inconsistent play in recent years, ultimately leading to his departure from Dallas. At only 28, Diggs still possesses ball skills and the experience to contribute on the outside for the Bengals should they lose Turner for any extended period of time. His aggressive play style sets him up to occasionally give up big plays, and his injury history is a bit of a concern, but he could be looking to prove he still belongs in the league and get a fresh start. Marco Wilson A familiar face could be an option for the Bengals. Wilson is currently on the Panthers’ practice squad and was a member of the Bengals through parts of the ‘24 and ‘25 seasons before he signed with the Dolphins in free agency. Miami released him before the regular season, and he eventually landed on Carolina’s practice squad. The 27-year-old cornerback has 37 career starts in his career, and his familiarity with Cincinnati could make him a potential target if Turner’s injury forces the Bengals to look for outside help. Tre’Davious White Another former All-Pro and another practice squad target, White is currently on the Bills’ practice squad. The 31-year-old veteran was once one of the league’s top corners, leading the league in interceptions in 2019. He has gone through some serious knee and Achilles injuries, but still started 16 games for the Bills in 2025, recording 40 tackles, 10 passes defended, and an interception. He’s not who he once was, but he could be a dependable option for Cincinnati, which also has familiarity with AFC competition in the regular and postseason.

title: Tee Higgins is on pace for a historic season

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals pulled off an overtime win on Sunday as they knocked off the Tennessee Titans. Led by the offense, the team fought back from three Joe Burrow interceptions to pull off the much-needed win. Now firmly set on the right side of the playoff bubble, as The Athletic gives the team an 84% chance to make the playoffs , it was Ja’Mar Chase and Tee Higgins who helped the Bengals pull off Sunday’s win. Higgins continued his impressive season for the team as he is now on a historic pace after posting 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns. That pace? 104 catches for 1763 yards and 10 touchdowns. Would only be done for the 6th time ever in NFL history. Tee Higgins pace: 104-1763-10 For context, that's been done 6 times ever. — Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 1, 2026 People talk a lot about how this Bengals squad has two No. 1 receivers in Chase and Higgins. Now with Tee healthy, we are seeing that sentiment to be true as they both continue to dominate. They have the offense to compete for a Super Bowl. Now all we can hope is that the defense finds a pulse to complement this team’s offense.

title: Bengals News: DJ Turner and Cashius Howell Injury Watch
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals may have some serious issues pop up after their escape from the Tennessee Titans yesterday. Two pretty big names were declared out with injuries fairly quickly after exiting. That doesn’t always mean something, but it could. That is what the watches are for. The biggest name was DJ Turner exiting with an […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals may have some serious issues pop up after their escape from the Tennessee Titans yesterday. Two pretty big names were declared out with injuries fairly quickly after exiting. That doesn’t always mean something, but it could. That is what the watches are for. The biggest name was DJ Turner exiting with an ankle injury after helping on a tackle with Tony Pollard. This hurts for two reasons. The most obvious is that Turner may be one of the best players on the defense, period. He has been super consistent in coverage and has been one of the better tacklers in space. The other reason is that the Bengals have proven their depth at corner has been an issue. The other player is rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell. He may not be the most productive player in the box score, but he gets pressure at a pretty good rate. He has also proven to be a big part of the rotation on the defensive line this season behind Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. Will these two miss major time, or can they get back out there soon? These are major storylines to follow this week for the Bengals. Bengals News Bengals DE Shemar Stewart Active for Titans After Being a Healthy Scratch vs. Ravens It is good to see that it truly looks like it was an isolated incident that Stewart was inactive last week despite being healthy. However, at some point this guy may need some snaps in games to actually improve. That was supposed to be a reason Al Golden was brought in after Lou Anarumo, right? Postgame Quick Hits | Joe Burrow’s Bengals Grind To Thrilling OT Win: ‘I Looked At Him And Told Him He Was Legendary’ It is rough that it took this kind of effort to defeat the Titans, but any given Sunday a team can come out and really put up the fight of their life. It is frustrating to watch this team try to sleepwalk through lesser teams. The opposing team gets some momentum, and that can carry an entire game if you let it, like it did today. Luckily, the Bengals had just enough to pull out a win at the end of the day. ‘Ask Zac.’ Ja’Marr Chase on how Bengals can avoid slow starts Zac Taylor gets credit for this team’s Super Bowl run and has done some nice things to change the culture in the building. It might be fair to say that this team could benefit from a fresh voice and new ideas. These slow starts have been so consistent that it is hard not to watch and think Taylor and his staff have something to do with it. NFL News Ravens QB Lamar Jackson to undergo surgery on right thumb, will be placed on IR Bengals fans know how bad a season can turn after losing your franchise quarterback to injury. Jackson threw one pass before hitting his hand on a defender’s helmet. It certainly looks like at least one AFC North team will be losing pace with the top of the division now, though. Buccaneers’ Todd Bowles on zero-completion win over Falcons: There’s a ‘first time for everything’ Truly one of the more remarkable things is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulling out two wins where they basically called on running back Bucky Irving and the running game to weather the load. The weather had a massive impact on the play calling here, but it certainly isn’t something you will see happen again in a long time. Lions LB Jack Campbell carted off field, evaluated for neck injury at hospital It is always scary to see a player leave in that fashion. It is certainly good that he is receiving the care he needs. Just always helps to remember how violent this sport truly is and that the guys playing it are humans as well. Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! title: Bengals vs. Falcons odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup in Madrid
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals needed a spectacular performance from Joe Burrow to escape with an overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but oddsmakers aren’t expecting the same kind of offensive fireworks when Cincinnati faces the Atlanta Falcons next weekend. Still, with the Bengals’ defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals needed a spectacular performance from Joe Burrow to escape with an overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but oddsmakers aren’t expecting the same kind of offensive fireworks when Cincinnati faces the Atlanta Falcons next weekend. Still, with the Bengals’ defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially high-scoring affair. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta, with the Bengals listed at -225 on the moneyline and the Falcons at +188. The opening over/under was set at 49.5 points. The latest FanDuel odds show Cincinnati remaining a 3.5-point favorite, although the price has shifted to -102 for the Bengals and -120 for the Falcons. The Bengals’ moneyline has moved to -184, while Atlanta’s stands at +154. The over/under has increased by one point to 50.5. The Bengals enter the matchup following a wild 43-36 overtime victory over Tennessee that featured five touchdown passes and three interceptions from Burrow, who ultimately delivered the winning score by scrambling nine yards around left end for just the second offensive overtime touchdown in franchise history. But while Cincinnati’s offense once again demonstrated its ability to put points on the scoreboard, the defense raised serious questions. The Bengals surrendered 36 points in regulation to a Tennessee team that entered Sunday’s game with just one victory, delivering a performance that looked disturbingly similar to the defensive struggles that plagued Cincinnati throughout last season. Atlanta, meanwhile, is coming off a 16-0 shutout loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that did not complete a single pass. That sets up an intriguing matchup between a Falcons offense that couldn’t find the end zone and a Bengals defense that had difficulty keeping the Titans out of it. Cincinnati and Atlanta are scheduled to meet Sunday, November 8, at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. Eastern time. Who Dey! title: Scorigami: Bengals and Titans combine for a final score that’s never happened
summary: The 43-36 final score of the Cincinnati Bengals and Tennessee Titans has never happened before in the history of the NFL. The final is the 1098th unique score in NFL history. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami. Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Wide receiver Elic Ayomanor #5 of the Tennessee Titans makes a catch against safety Bryan Cook #6 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the first quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 43-36 final score of the Cincinnati Bengals and Tennessee Titans has never happened before in the history of the NFL. The final is the 1098th unique score in NFL history. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami . Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. In this game, the Titans converted a two-point conversion to make it 21-21 — a very normal score. But then a Bengals safety started making things weird at 23-21. The Bengals couldn’t get a two-point conversion on a later touchdown after the Titans scored, making it 29-28. Then the Titans got a two-point on their next score to make it a seven-point lead at 36-29. The Bengals scored and kicked an extra point and the game sat at 36-36 at the end of regulation. That tie at 36-36 would have also been a Scorigami but 39-36 would not have been. It should also be noted that an overtime touchdown would have won the game without an extra point before this season and 42-36 has also happened before. We had two Scorigamis on September 13th but haven’t had one since. The NFL averages around four of these per season and we already have three halfway through the season. 2026 NFL Scorigamis September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37 September 13: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22 November 1: Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 During the 2025 season we saw four Scorigamis: Bills beat Ravens 41-40 Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 Texans beat Jaguars 36-29 Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 Our friends at Secret Base have done extensive work on Scorigami. If you want to see it, it is fascinating.

title: The Bengals offensive line has been REALLY good this season
summary: It’s so interesting how when there’s a problem, whether on your favorite sports team or in everyday life, you complain non-stop about it. Then when it’s remedied, you don’t say a peep, maybe not even acknowledging that not only is it remedied but also working really well. The Bengals’ offensive line fits that exact description. […]
full_text: It’s so interesting how when there’s a problem, whether on your favorite sports team or in everyday life, you complain non-stop about it. Then when it’s remedied, you don’t say a peep, maybe not even acknowledging that not only is it remedied but also working really well. The Bengals’ offensive line fits that exact description. For years, Bengals fans complained about the team’s offensive line. Sometimes unfairly, but the criticism was fair more often than not for the first six years of Joe Burrow’s career. But over the last four years, the Bengals have quietly built what is now one of the NFL’s best offensive lines. Through six games, the Bengals have allowed just 10 sacks. And this is the heart of their success this season: Five of those sacks came in Week 2 against Houston. That means, in the other five games, Joe Burrow has only been sacked an average of one time per game. One time per game. That’s it. It’s been four years since the Bengals were in the Playoffs. The last time they played a playoff game was in the AFC Championship Game in January of 2023. They did so with three backup offensive linemen taking the field that night at Arrowhead Stadium. That night, the Bengals gained zero yards in the first quarter, and Joe Burrow was sacked on the Bengals’ final offensive play of the game. Less than two months later, the Bengals swung big and signed the best left tackle in free agency in Orlando Brown Jr.. Brown has signed multiple contract extensions with the Bengals since then. After Week 2, there was concern about him, and rightfully so. He had a rough preseason and training camp. But since Week 2 against Houston, have you even noticed him? It was worth keeping your stock in him. With the 18th pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, the Bengals drafted Amarius Mims out of Georgia. There was concern over his limited playing time in college, but that’s not at all the conversation now about the Bengals’ franchise right tackle. He looks like the second coming of Willie Anderson. Watch the play where Burrow stepped up in the pocket and found Tee Higgins for a 44-yard gain Sunday. At the outset of the play, Mims erased Ravens edge rusher Mike Green completely out of the play. It was impressive. How about the interior of the Bengals’ offensive line? Ted Karras is the only starter from the Bengals’ offensive line from that 2022 AFC Championship still with the team. He’s as solid as they come and a true leader on this team. Dylan Fairchild is unnoticeable at left guard. Yes, he’s had a couple of key holding penalties this season, but he’s playing really well in his second season. He looks like a home run who the Bengals drafted in the third round of the 2025 Draft. Dalton Risner signed with the Bengals last August, just a week before the season started. He’s blocking incredibly well both in the passing and running games. Since becoming the full-time starter at right guard in the middle of last season, the Bengals’ offense has been much more fluid upfront. In the second half Sunday, Joe Burrow had clean pockets every time he dropped back to pass. When was the last time you saw the Bengals control the line of scrimmage like that, especially in a division game? The Bengals finally have a really good offensive line in front of Joe Burrow. They deserve their credit, even if they want to go through life anonymously. Fans complained about the Bengals’ offensive line for years and, more often than not, rightfully so. But now, fans aren’t talking about the Bengals’ offensive line even though they deserve a lot of credit. That’s a good thing. Still, though, the Bengals’ offensive line is playing really good football heading into November.

The NFL trade deadline is just over a week away, with the New Orleans Saints next up on the Browns schedule in Week 9. J. Paganetti, sources say. Run-game issues have plagued the team this year. pic.twitter.com/yBPAkbzG9c — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 2, 2026 Paganetti’s run game last year was also among the worst in the NFL, but the Saints averaged 94.3 yards per game on the ground in 2025, with a strong drop-off this season. Paganetti was brought over with HC Kellen Moore after their shared time with the Philadelphia Eagles. No news on who will take over New Orleans’ run game or why it took the entire bye week for the decision to be made, but Cleveland could see some new wrinkles from the Saints’ rushing attack in Week 9.
