title: Week 8 proves Browns aren’t there yet, but CLE split the season series with the Steelers
summary: “You win some, you lose some, but you live. You live to fight another day.” I use this quote specifically because it applies to the Cleveland Browns. Yes, the Browns got bullied by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8. Head coach Todd Monken said the team earned the loss (they did); however, it isn’t the […]
full_text: “You win some, you lose some, but you live. You live to fight another day.” Willie Jones (also known as Mr Jones from the movie Friday) I use this quote specifically because it applies to the Cleveland Browns. Yes, the Browns got bullied by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8. Head coach Todd Monken said the team earned the loss (they did); however, it isn’t the end of the world. 6-2 and alone in the AFC North would’ve been nice, but you would settle for 5-3 in a year in which no one thought the team would be ahead of schedule. 1st Down: Young teams are often the most inconsistent teams As everyone knows, the Browns have one of the youngest teams in the NFL. The difference is clear when you pay close attention. Going into Pittsburgh and winning was going to be a tough task, but Cleveland didn’t make things easier for themselves at all. The Steelers essentially did what the Browns did to them when the two teams played on Thursday night this season. Granted, the score wasn’t as close this time around, but Cleveland looked like the young team that they are. It’s not necessarily a bad thing, but it’s just the reality of the situation. As far as the game goes, not much went right for the Browns. Most, if not all, of Cleveland’s players did their best to downplay the history of the team not winning in Pittsburgh, only to extend their losing streak and miss out on an opportunity to sweep the Steelers in a season series. 2nd Down: Jared Verse is doing more harm than actual good Leading up to the game, Browns defensive end Jared Verse had some choice comments about the Steelers going back to their last meeting. Some fans liked it (because why not), and others like myself weren’t necessarily annoyed by it but just don’t understand why Verse continues to run his mouth despite not having a sack this season. #Browns Jared Verse on the Steelers and Cam Heyward’s comments this week: pic.twitter.com/c3n2nqNmJz — Ashley Bastock (@AshleyBastock42) October 29, 2026 It’s obvious that the Steelers were aware of it, and judging by the postgame comments by many Steelers players, they don’t respect Verse at all, and honestly they shouldn’t. Jaquan Brisker on Jared Verse’s trash talk earlier in the week prior to the Steelers topping the Browns 27-6 “He should have kept his mouth shut. All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles, that’s bad.” “He’s gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better.” pic.twitter.com/tp6WH6Iw9O — Ashley Wenskoski (@AshleyWenskTV) November 1, 2026 Do I understand why Verse is trash-talking? Yes, he’s trying to be apart of the “culture changing” but I would rather have you back up your talk and be productive than talk and be a liability. It’s fair to question if the team picks up his option if the production doesn’t get better but sometimes it’s best to not say anything. 3rd Down: Defense needs to get healthy, OL has bad outing The Browns don’t have their bye week for a few weeks, but the defense has to get healthy to some degree. If you have played any iteration of EA Sports College Football video game, you are likely aware of the Wear and Tear feature. It appears some of Cleveland’s defensive players are in the red area. Defensive tackle Mason Graham isn’t quite 100%, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger hasn’t been healthy all year. The run defense was an issue last week, and it was an issue on Sunday. Defending against trap runs has been an issue for a while, but by the time adjustments were made, the game was already out of reach. After having a stout outing last week, the Browns offensive line had a bad outing. I don’t think the Steelers defensive line is that dangerous, but the Browns offensive line struggled throughout the day. Quarterback Deshaun Watson didn’t help due to him holding the ball for too long trying to extend plays, but the entire offensive line had their fair share of struggles. 4th Down: Browns aren’t a good team… yet but they aren’t a bad team The Cleveland Browns are 5-3. Yet, the conversation will be whether this team is as good as their record may indicate. I’m not sure the Browns are a good football team, guys. — Danny Cunningham (@RealDCunningham) November 1, 2026 Are the Browns a great football team? No, at least not at this moment. Let’s put things in perspective. The team is 5-3 Of the 5 wins this team has, they weren’t favored in 4 (they were favored against the Titans) The team is ahead of schedule Considering how most, if not all, analysts predicted that this team would be one of the worst teams in the league before the season started, the fact that they are 5-3 is impressive. Yes, the team has flaws, but this team is also one of the youngest teams in the league. Look at the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers are winless and have looked objectively awful. You think Los Angeles would like to be in Cleveland’s position right now? Albeit the expectations might be different, the point remains. Yes, Week 8 was terrible, but I don’t believe that should change your view on this team. It could be a lot worse. Extra Points The Browns are more likely to trade for an edge rusher before the deadline, from what I was told (the YaYa Diaby smoke has some traction) Cleveland’s taunting penalties felt as if they were instigated by the Steelers. Tight end Harold Fannin had a career day. Watson had another 300-yard game, but most of the yardage came from YAC or underneath route concepts The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2, but I am not moved; I am just waiting for the shoe to drop. A day later, what are your thoughts on the Browns’ Sunday big loss to the Steelers? Join the conversation! title: Browns, Steelers winners and losers: Cleveland was never in the game
summary: The Cleveland Browns versus the Pittsburgh Steelers in the rubber match had plenty of incentive. Both clubs were tied for the lead in the AFC North Division with identical 5-2-0 records. The winner would sit on top of the division on their own. The Browns won the first game 27-24 in Week 4, which was […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns versus the Pittsburgh Steelers in the rubber match had plenty of incentive. Both clubs were tied for the lead in the AFC North Division with identical 5-2-0 records. The winner would sit on top of the division on their own. The Browns won the first game 27-24 in Week 4, which was played in Cleveland. But the Browns are 0-10 playing regular season games in Pittsburgh in the past decade. That says quite a bit. RELATED: STEELERS VS. BROWNS RECAP Pittsburgh came into this game with the league’s #7 run defense. It just so happens that the Browns found their running game last weekend against the Tennessee Titans, so this would become one of the game’s hot topics. In the end, Cleveland was dominated by the Steelers and lost 27-6. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES – Winners TE Harold Fannin – While Cleveland’s offense could not sustain any drives, Fannin was a single shining star for all four quarters. Early in the second quarter, the Browns were faced with a third-and-six down 10-3. Fannin snagged a 12-yard pass to give the Browns a new set of downs. Steelers bring pressure on 3rd down but Watson finds Harold Fannin over the top for a big gain. Browns down inside the Steelers' five . — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) November 1, 2026 On the very next play, he secured a short pass, then rumbled for 22 yards to the Steelers’ 44. As the third quarter was winding down, QB Deshaun Watson found Fannin for a 15-yard gain. Fannin gained 37 yards on the second play of Quarter 4 before being tackled at Pittsburgh’s 39-yard line. With 6:51 remaining, Watson connected with Fannin for 27 yards and, two plays later, for another 10 yards. 12 targets, 10 receptions for 154 yards with a 15.4 yards-per-catch average. on the board thanks to Andre 🙂‍↕️ @meijer | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/CavYG1jgPv — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 1, 2026 Kickers – Punter Corey Bojorquez had four kicks for 199 yards and a 49.8 average, including one for 58 yards. K Andre Szmyt nailed both field goal attempts. S Ronnie Hickman and S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren – Hickman had a fine game. Midway in the first quarter, he tracked down RB Rico Dowdle from behind after a nine-yard gain. When Freiermuth was open for 28 yards in the second quarter, it was Hickman who took him down instead of the player whose duty it was to cover him. Both players ganged up on Washington after a 12-yard gain early in the fourth quarter. On kickoff coverage, McNeil-Warren had two tackles. He read the run and then nailed Dowdle for a two-yard gain in the third quarter. He tackled Warren, forced a fumble, and then recovered the loose ball that was then overturned. He blitzed when Pittsburgh had the ball at their own five and was able to stop Warren after just two yards. For the game, Hickman had seven total tackles while McNeil-Warren had nine. FROWNIES – Losers The play that lost the game – Cleveland had mounted an 44-yard drive that culminated in a 49-yard Szmyt field goal to cut Pittsburgh’s lead to 13-6. 45 seconds remained before halftime. Pittsburgh QB Aaron Rodgers has made a career out of getting a lot with so little. RB Jalen Warren gashed up the middle for 23 yards. A two-yard completion. Next, 28 yards to a wide-open TE Pat Freiermuth for 28 yards, which placed the ball in field goal range. Rodgers, not wanting to go into the locker room with three points, tossed a short pass to WR Germie Bernard for 15 yards with sloppy coverage by DB Denzel Ward to the one-yard line with five seconds remaining. This one play was the difference going into the locker room, 16-6, and made a defensive stand, or the ensuing touchdown run, which put Cleveland down 20-6. Absolutely the dagger going into the locker room. Penalties – Ahhhh!!!! Every game, the penalties are drive killers. Seven were called in the first half, with five accepted. Nine total for the game for 85 yards. And nothing changes. Seven were called on the offensive line, including two holding calls on rookie OT Spencer Fano. Run defense up the middle – The Steelers rarely ran to the corners. Why? Because they gashed the Browns over and over and over and over up the gut. All day long, MLB Carson Schwesinger was blocked out or moved to the side. All of the defensive tackles for Cleveland struggled to maintain gaps, and the Steelers offensive line just moved bodies anywhere they decided. DT Mason Graham had one tackle for loss, but with 1:56 left. 5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 DT Mike Hall got a one-yard stop on RB Rico Dowdle in the second half, and not much in the other three quarters. In the second quarter, DT Maliek Collins got RB Warren for minus two, then he celebrated like that isn’t his job on all of the other downs. Pittsburgh had 200 yards on the ground, with most of that on the legs of Warren, who gashed the middle of the Browns’ defense for 143 rushing yards. When safeties are being called on to make the bulk of tackles, there is a huge problem. No pass rush – Rodgers sat back in the pocket all day and got to go through most of his progressions. Where was the pressure? DT Adin Huntington got the only sack of the day, as Cleveland had just two QB hits. Otherwise, nobody got into the face of Rodgers. DE Jared Verse got a QB hit! Yoohoo! Missed tackles – Denzel Ward, Carson Schwesinger, Tyson Campbell, Grant Delpit, Mike Hall, Quincy Williams. These were just the most obvious. Run game – The Steelers came into this game ranked #7 against the run. So, what happened? The Browns tried to run the ball for 34 total yards. All game long, Pittsburgh had seven in the box and, on occasion, eight. Offensive line’s new nickname: Jailbreak – From the opening drive, the Steelers played an all-out pass rush. In the end, there were eight sacks. But in fairness to Deshaun Watson, his escape routes from the pocket, as it was beginning to implode, were not good. On three of those sacks, he simply ran into a Pittsburgh defender trying to escape. Which offensive linemen, you ask? Yes. Offense first half – With 6:34 left in the first quarter, the Browns had lost two turnovers, had four accepted penalties called, allowed three sacks, and had minus one yard. Their first first down was at the 12:40 mark of the second quarter. At halftime, eight rushing yards. Red Zone, third-down efficiency, fourth downs – The Browns got into the Red Zone three times all game, and went 0-3. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh was 3-5. Cleveland was 4-13 on third downs versus 4-11 for the Steelers. The Browns went for it twice on fourth down and did not convert either. All three categories for the Browns provide a glimpse into why the failures occurred. Milk Bones – There is a fine line between fishing and just standing on the shore like an idiot Punch it in @ricodowdle 😤 pic.twitter.com/HUqIExGBY7 — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 CB Denzel Ward – On Pittsburgh’s second possession in the first quarter, they drove down to Cleveland’s nine-yard line. On a second-and-one, Dowdle took it up the middle and met Ward, who had read the play. Ward hit him high at the eight-yard line, rode Dowdle for three yards, and then just let go. On the short pass to Bernard for 15 yards right before the half, Ward had no clue where Bernard was and left him wide open. Ward did secure the interception, but his man, WR D.K. Metcalf, was open and then bobbled the catch, which ultimately landed in Ward’s lap. Two total tackles with two batted passes. TE coverage – The Steelers’ tight ends didn’t have a banner day, but were a very important aspect of their offense and had several long gains. BIG MAN ON THE MOVE 😤 @_Dwfootball11 pic.twitter.com/7QrUrLG0uf — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 Most notable was the 58-yard catch-and-run by Darnell Washington, who had beaten Schwesinger badly from the get-go. He caught the pass at the Browns’ 45-yard line with a seven-yard lead on Schwesinger, and…

title: Cleveland Browns news: What the hell was that?
summary: Another year, another disastrous road trip to Pittsburgh for the Cleveland Browns. Cleveland played its annual game against the Steelers in Pittsburgh on Sunday and lost for the 23rd consecutive time. That ties the NFL record for most consecutive regular-season road losses against one team in NFL history, as the Browns now join the Detroit […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another year, another disastrous road trip to Pittsburgh for the Cleveland Browns. Cleveland played its annual game against the Steelers in Pittsburgh on Sunday and lost for the 23rd consecutive time. That ties the NFL record for most consecutive regular-season road losses against one team in NFL history, as the Browns now join the Detroit Lions, who lost 23 consecutive road games to the Green Bay Packers from 1992 to 2014. It is fitting that the Lions are involved, as Detroit and Cleveland are the last two NFL teams to go 0-16 in a season. Perhaps the one saving grace is that the Browns will have to wait a year to claim the record for themselves. It was all downhill from the start as the Browns turned the ball over on their first two offensive possessions and never were able to get anything going from there. Quarterback Deshaun Watson was sacked eight times, the running game totaled just 34 yards, and the Browns were just 4-of-13 on third down. Basically, Cleveland looked like a team that had never played the game before. Which is par for the course when they face the Steelers on the road. The loss drops the Browns to third place in the AFC North, and looking to pick up the pieces from an embarrassing afternoon. It was also so very, very, exhausting. There is not much more to say, so let’s just move on to today’s edition of the Daily Dawg Chow. title: Browns TE Harold Fannin joins Hall of Famer after big day
summary: The Cleveland Browns had their annual very bad road trip to Pittsburgh on Sunday as they dropped another game to the Pittsburgh Steelers.  The offense was horrible, the defense couldn’t get anything going, and it resulted in the 23rd consecutive regular-season road loss for the Browns in Pittsburgh. If you are looking for bright spots, […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 1: Harold Fannin Jr. #44 of the Cleveland Browns runs the ball during the fourth quarter of a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns had their annual very bad road trip to Pittsburgh on Sunday as they dropped another game to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The offense was horrible, the defense couldn’t get anything going, and it resulted in the 23rd consecutive regular-season road loss for the Browns in Pittsburgh. If you are looking for bright spots, they are hard to find, but there was at least one in tight end Harold Fannin Jr. After a stellar rookie season, Fannin’s second year has been a bit of a slow build as he entered Sunday’s game without a 100-yard receiving game to his name. There were also some questions about how he caught just two passes for 13 yards combined in the games against the New York Jets and Baltimore Ravens. Fannin said he was not worried about his production because the Browns were winning and he knew his time would come soon enough. Things started to turn around last week against the Tennessee Titans when Fannin had six receptions for 91 yards. That solid day was overshadowed by wide receiver KC Concepcion going off for 129 yards, one of the 10 best days by a rookie in franchise history . Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. recorded a career-high 154 receiving yards today, becoming the first Browns tight end with 150+ receiving yards in a game since Ozzie Newsome in 1984. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 1, 2026 But there was no overshadowing Fannin’s performance on Sunday as he finished with a game-high 10 receptions and 154 yards, making him the first Cleveland tight end to surpass 150 receiving yards in a game since Hall of Famer Ozzie Newsome had 191 yards on 14 receptions against the New York Jets in 1984. Those 154 yards and 10 receptions are career highs for Fannin, surpassing the 114 receiving yards and eight receptions he had against the Titans in 2025. For the season, Fannin now has 35 receptions for 411 yards, which puts him on pace to surpass his rookie numbers. It may not be much in the wake of another embarrassing performance by the Browns in Pittsburgh, but at least there was one bright spot to come out of the day.

title: Browns, Steelers Week 8: 15 key takeaways from AFC North domination by PIT
summary: In what felt like a replay of Week 1’s loss, the Cleveland Browns were blown out by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. A matchup of the top two teams in the AFC North, the Steelers controlled the game from start to finish, with Cleveland struggling on both sides of […]
full_text: In what felt like a replay of Week 1’s loss , the Cleveland Browns were blown out by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. A matchup of the top two teams in the AFC North, the Steelers controlled the game from start to finish, with Cleveland struggling on both sides of the ball . While not a major impact on the game, and both returned to the contest, a few injuries on the defense didn’t help the Browns’ cause . A few key takeaways, few positive, from the train wreck that was Week 8 for Cleveland: Young teams are inconsistent Not an excuse, but important to note that the Browns are a very young team facing a veteran-laden Steelers squad for the second time this year. Cleveland was also on the road in a very tough place to play. Deshaun Watson’s early struggles with quick decisions Simply put, quarterback play in the NFL is all about going through the first two reads while in your drop back and throwing the ball when you hit your back foot. Even at his best, that has not been Watson’s game, which leads to more sacks and what looks like “running for your life” plays. Those plays will happen, at times, throughout the league, but most quarterbacks are throwing passes as players are in their break or before; Watson is often waiting until they are out of their breaks. Was this game all on the quarterback? Not at all; problems were all over the place. Just notable that it seems like Watson isn’t getting protection, but his style of play doesn’t help either. Ronnie Hickman’s poor angle leads to 2 big gains 51 on third and long and 23 yards late in the 2nd quarter to get Pittsburgh near midfield, leading to a late first-half touchdown were both because Cleveland’s safety took horrible angles in run support. This is not the first time Hickman’s lack of run discipline caused the Browns problems. Trying anything for a kick return spark Nothing really popped, but interesting that Isaiah Bond took the first kickoff, then it was Malachi Corley , followed by Dylan Sampson . It was obvious that Cleveland’s coaches knew they needed something to spark a win in Week 8 and were willing to try a few different things Bad start followed by few adjustments Early in the game, the Browns looked bad again. Unlike the past few weeks, whatever adjustments the coaches tried just didn’t work. The Steelers were not going to be fooled again by changes made by Cleveland as they did in Week 4. Harold Fannin has second straight big game One of the few positives from Week 8, Fannin had 10 catches for 154 yards. While the second-year tight end fumbled early in the game, he was one of the lone bright spots from the Browns offense. Carson Schwesinger injured? The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year just didn’t look like himself. While he’s fought through his ankle injury for the last few games, Schwesinger was out of place, physically manhandled and “led” a Browns defense that gave up 200 yards rushing. Defense’s redzone success kept Browns in the game in 1st half While the overall performance by Cleveland’s defense wasn’t good, a few key stops (forcing a punt and 2 redzone field goals), made the game seem within reach (until Pittsburgh’s touchdown drive to end the first half). Horrible defense leads to giving up TD at end of 2nd quarter Including Hickman and Schwesinger mistakes, the Browns allowed the Steelers to drive 69 yards in 44 seconds to turn a seven-point halftime deficit into a 14-point hole that would not be overcome. A very deflating possession by Cleveland’s defense after the offense had just driven for three more points. Allow Darnell Washington big gains on the same play twice Something good coaches do: Pittsburgh ran the same play that broke tendencies and found their huge tight end for big plays on both. Often, Washington is used as a blocker on wide receiver screens. Twice, the Steelers set up what looked like a WR screen, but Washington leaked out instead for big gains, beating Schwesinger. Forcing fumbles still, recoveries are mostly luck Cleveland’s defense forced two more fumbles, but were not able to capitalize with possession at the end of the play. DC Mike Rutenberg preaches going after the football, and the Browns have bought into doing so. Unfortunately, data shows that fumble recoveries are just random with an oblong ball that bounces in many different ways. Denzel Ward having a career year Tied his career high with three INTs already; big hustle play with DK Metcalf wide open; took the ball away from the Steelers’ big receiver. With a big contract extension this offseason, Ward has made GM Andrew Berry look good on that decision. Jared Verse conversation continues Listen, the Browns are not trading Verse, but another game where Verse’s name was rarely said by the broadcasters in any positive way and just one assist in the box score is concerning. There are tons of things that Verse does to help the defense, but the lack of impact plays is problematic, especially as he continues to trash talk. 2 taunting, 1 late roughness penalties while down 21 points Sam Williams and Quinshon Judkins just have no reason to taunt when their team is down that much. Quincy Williams got into the act in the fourth quarter, getting called for unnecessary roughness after a play. Jaylen Warren was the expected star; couldn’t stop the run, just like last week It is one thing when a player has a big game coming out of nowhere. Coming into the game, it was obvious that Warren was the most important player on the Steelers offense. Did Cleveland load up to stop the run? It didn’t seem like it, and it didn’t work if they did. Warren had 143 yards on just 17 attempts with one touchdown. Backup RB Rico Dowdle added 56 yards on the ground as well. What are your takeaways from the Browns getting destroyed in Week 8 by the Steelers? Join the conversation! title: Cleveland Browns vs. Pittsburgh Steelers recap: Streak lives on, as Cleveland dominated and loses division lead
summary: The Browns have lost grasp of the AFC North division lead. It comes at the hands of the Pittsburgh Steelers, who made it a 23-game winning streak over Cleveland in their home stadium with a 27-6 dominant victory. It certainly wasn’t Cleveland’s day, as they turned the ball over on the first two drives, and […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 1: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of a game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Browns have lost grasp of the AFC North division lead. It comes at the hands of the Pittsburgh Steelers, who made it a 23-game winning streak over Cleveland in their home stadium with a 27-6 dominant victory. It certainly wasn’t Cleveland’s day, as they turned the ball over on the first two drives, and the defense couldn’t stop Pittsburgh’s rushing attack between Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle . It looked like the Browns might keep it competitive when they added a field goal with less than a minute to go in the first half to make it 13-6, but the defense let Pittsburgh get a touchdown drive in that short span, and they basically double-dipped after the half to go up 27-6. The Browns’ offense had some opportunities, but turned it over on downs in a goal-to-go situation, and Deshaun Watson was sacked 8 times. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Steelers The Browns received the opening kickoff, and after a run by RB Quinshon Judkins , QB Deshaun Watson was sacked on second down when his quick read wasn’t there. On 3rd-and-7, Watson sailed a short pass to WR KC Concepcion for an incomplete pass, but Pittsburgh was flagged for roughing the passer for going high on Watson to give the drive new life. Watson had to exit to be checked for a concussion, bringing QB Shedeur Sanders in. Cleveland had back-to-back ineligible downfield penalties called because the Browns called simple screen passes that Pittsburgh was all over, so Sanders held the ball longer than needed. Later, on 3rd-and-13, Sanders checked it down to TE Harold Fannin to give way to P Corey Bojorquez — but then Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy threw a red challenge flag, and replay showed that the group of Steelers stripped Fannin of the ball before he was down. That gave Pittsburgh the ball at the Browns’ 42 yard line. CB Tyson Campbell knocked QB Aaron Rodgers first quick slant attempt away, as he tried to hit WR DK Metcalf . RB Jaylen Warren carried for a few yards to set up 3rd-and-7. Rodgers overshot Warren on a crossing route, so K Chris Boswell came on to try a 57-yard field goal. He missed it wide left, and ironically enough, Cleveland took over pretty quickly with better field position than where the turnover had happened at their own 47-yard line, with Watson returning. Judkins got the handoff to midfield. Then on second down, Watson was collapsed on, and then tried fumbled as he tried to throw the ball away, with Pittsburgh recovering right back at the Browns’ 45 yard line. Sack and a fumble forced by the Steelers defense 😤 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gDaB2D1rl9 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Pittsburgh fared better on their second drive, first with a swing pass to WR Germie Bernard for a first down, and then RB Rico Dowdle getting a burst of 15 yards up the middle before he was touched. A pitch play to Dowdle then went for 9 yards, setting up 2nd-and-1 at the 9 yard line. Dowdle then took it in on the next play for a 9-yard touchdown, as CB Denzel Ward tried going for the ball instead of the tackle, to put Pittsburgh up 7-0 with 7:57 to go in the opening quarter. Rico Dowdle breaking tackles on his way to the end zone! CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XuFdbhhI61 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 After the play, a personal foul penalty was called on a Steelers’ offensive lineman for extracurricular activity against DE Jared Verse , no doubt in relation to the words that were had during the week. That was enforced on the kickoff, helping WR Malachi Corley to return it out to their own 37 yard line. #Browns DE Jared Verse has been talking plenty of trash about the #Steelers …. Well, Steelers G Mason McCormick just did this to him. 😳😳 pic.twitter.com/OP1iknS4JP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 1, 2026 Watson ran a playaction on the next drive, and missed a wide open WR Denzel Boston for what would have been a 15-20-yard gain. A short connection to WR Tylan Wallace made it 3rd-and-7, and Watson was drilled from behind for the third sack of the game, and leading to a punt (which is technically better than a turnover I guess). Bojorquez’ punt was fair caught at the 11 yard line. After Warren picked up a first down on the first play, a screen play to Bernard was shut down by S Grant Delpit for a loss of 3 yards, setting up 3rd-and-13. They ran a quick-hitting run with Warren, and it was wide open up the middle and then bouncing to the outside for a gain of 51 yards, all the way to the Browns’ 25 yard line. 5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 Two plays later, another pitch out to Warren gained 8 yards to the 13 yard line for a fresh set of downs. A pass to TE Pat Freiermuth set up 3rd-and-2 at the 5 yard line. They gave it to Dowdle, who easily got 3 yards to the 2 yard line on the final play of the first quarter. 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Steelers On 1st-and-goal at the 2 yard line, a fade to Metcalf had no shot. On second down, Rodgers threw the ball away after a low snap. On third down, Rodgers handed to Warren, and the play was stuffed for no gain. The defense held strong for a big stop, as Boswell came on for a short field goal. He hit from 20 yards out to put the Steelers on top 10-0. Watson began with an 8-yard dumpoff to Fannin, and then Judkins moved the chains with a run for the team’s first first down that wasn’t via penalty. Then, on 3rd-and-7, Fannin got the ball again quickly for 12 yards and a first down to the Steelers’ 44 yard line. Off of playaction, Fannin got the catch for 25 yards to the Steelers’ 19 yard line. After a 1-yard run by Judkins, RT Tytus Howard had a false start to make it 2nd-and-14. A quick screen to Fannin gained 9 yards to set up a manageable 3rd-and-5. Watson had to throw the ball away after he couldn’t find anyone and was being hit, so K Andre Szmyt came on for a 32-yard field goal, and it was good to make it a 10-3 game with 8:43 remaining in the second quarter. Pittsburgh began their next drive at the 35 yard line. Rodgers got the Browns to bite on a fake screen, with TE Darnell Washington streaking upfield for a 24-yard gain. Then, Dowdle, after looking bottled up, broke free for 16 yards. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-3 at the 12 yard line, Rodgers handed to Dowdle for an easy first down to the 9 yard line. Like last time down here, Rodgers tried throwing the ball and had no where to go, making it second down. On second down, they tried throwing again, and it was blown up again for an incomplete pass. On third down, DT Adin Huntington got the sack for a loss of 10 yards, forcing another field goal. Boswell hit from 37 yards, to make it 13-3 with 3:27 left in the half. Adin comin' up big 💪 #CLEvsPIT on CBS pic.twitter.com/fGx5EuNluk — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 1, 2026 With the Steelers set to get the ball at the start of the second half, the offense needed another score to help draw closer. Beginning at the 25 yard line, Watson hit Boston for 5 yards, but then a false start by LG Zion Johnson made it 2nd-and-10. A run to Judkins went for 6 yards, but he had a hole and was just barely tripped up, preventing a bigger play. That made it 3rd-and-4 heading into the two-minute warning. Watson found Concepcion down the seam just before he got hit for a 24 yard gain. Boston then caught a timing pass to the outside for 12 yards, now at the Steelers 32 yard line. Watson laid one out for Boston in the end zone, just before he got hit again, but Boston couldn’t locate it and it fell incomplete. Watson got sacked by DE T.J. Watt for a loss of 8 yards on the next play, as pressure came…

title: Browns injuries: 2 key starters head to locker room in 1st half of Week 8, return in 2nd half
summary: The Cleveland Browns had a difficult start to their Week 8 matchup with AFC North rival Pittsburgh Steelers. The Browns defense gave up over 150 yards rushing in the first half and were down 20-6 heading into halftime, with the Steelers getting the ball to start the third quarter. Cleveland’s offense had its own struggles, […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns had a difficult start to their Week 8 matchup with AFC North rival Pittsburgh Steelers. The Browns defense gave up over 150 yards rushing in the first half and were down 20-6 heading into halftime, with the Steelers getting the ball to start the third quarter. Cleveland’s offense had its own struggles, with multiple fumbles to start the game. The Browns couldn’t convert their positive drives into touchdowns either, as penalties and sacks caused a number of issues throughout the first half. Injuries were also part of the problem. QB Deshaun Watson left the game for four plays , three of which included penalties, after a late hit led to Cleveland’s quarterback having to be evaluated in the blue medical tent. Late in the second quarter, DT Maliek Collins went to the locker room and was announced as questionable to return due to an elbow issue. As Pittsburgh was driving late in the second quarter, CB Tyson Campbell made a tackle but stayed down on the field before also being taken to the locker room. Collins returned after halftime, while Campbell is questionable to return with a neck injury and is being evaluated for a concussion. Campbell was back on the field for Cleveland’s second defensive possession of the second half.

title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals Stock Report: Brian Schottenheimer’s offense shrinks
summary: The Dallas Cowboys played down to the moment on Sunday, there is no doubt about that. With a sizable lead in hand, the Cowboys seemed to start envisioning what life would be like at 4-4 and with Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak with the team (after 25 career games, mind you). While they were daydreaming […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys played down to the moment on Sunday, there is no doubt about that. With a sizable lead in hand, the Cowboys seemed to start envisioning what life would be like at 4-4 and with Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak with the team (after 25 career games, mind you). While they were daydreaming the Arizona Cardinals were rallying. Arizona, a moribund team in today’s NFL, seemed inspired and invigorated while the Cowboys were lost in thought. In the end the Cardinals were winners at AT&T Stadium (why wouldn’t they be?) and the Cowboys were forced to take yet another hard and long look in the mirror. This is that mirror. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer I’m not sure which was worse, Schottenheimer the head coach or Schottenheimer the offensive play-caller. You don’t lose a game, let alone blow a huge lead to this season’s Arizona Cardinals team, unless you are a special type of bad. Schotty the head coach allowed for the team to get far too comfortable, but Schotty the play-caller called a timid game in the second half and kept leaving the door more and more open. It has been a long time since it felt like Dallas had an advantage at head coach. Who knows when the next time will be? Stock Down: Dak Prescott As a whole the Cowboys offense was given the ball six times by their defense and ultimately scored just twice. What’s more is that the offense had 12 true possessions (discounting the kneel down at the end of regulation) and failed to net double-digit yardage on seven of them. 7 of 12! Dak Prescott was under some duress (more on that in a moment), but there is no excuse. The franchise quarterback has to do more. Stock Down: Christian Parker How do we say this again ? What amalgamation of words can we use that hasn’t already been offered? Christian Parker is in some truly historic company in the worst kind of way. His unit did deliver the stops early on as noted, but they allowed the Cardinals to gash them all throughout the end of this game. What’s more is that they allowed Arizona to waltz all the way down at the end of regulation to tie, even though they should have won then. Stock Down: Rashan Gary What are you doing committing obvious roughing the passer penalties in critical moments? Rashan Gary was supposed to be among the leaders that the Cowboys were able to bring in to the defensive side of the ball. Game in and game out he seems to offer more questions than answers these days, and he had terrible judgment in a critical moment that was key in the loss. Stock Down: Offensive line This is not about discounting credit and/or blame from Dak Prescott. We have established this. But my word the Cowboys offensive line got pushed around. Perhaps the book is out as we all discussed/feared following the Buccaneers and/or Packers losses, but they were not able to hold on for much against Arizona and in the process a lot of what they wanted to do on offense was jumbled. For a group that had really been turning it around as of late, this was not good. Stock Down: Javonte Williams Keep in mind that one of the touchdowns that the mighty Cowboys offense scored only happened because a Javonte Williams fumble was recovered in the endzone. The offensive line struggled, but so did Williams. This has to be better. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey Nobody is trying to say that a 61-yard field goal is easy. But Brandon Aubrey is expected to make those. What’s more is that the Cowboys lost this game in overtime; had he made that kick near the end of regulation you can argue that things never come down to that. The inches matter. Stock Down: DaRon Bland Like with Christian Parker as a whole, this is the same story. DaRon Bland continues to get picked on every week. On some level maybe the Joey Porter Jr. trade created a new and worse kind of problem in that sense. Obviously the contract situation is what it is. This is just a huge bummer. Stock Up: Caleb Downs It goes without saying that we hope that Caleb Downs is alright as he entered concussion protocol near the end of this game. Downs was having arguably his best game as a professional early on. He was huge in many respects and was the primary tackler when Dallas held Arizona on fourth-and-goal early in the game. He is living up to the hype. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy We have all been very excited about Ryan Flournoy for some time, and as of late he is proving why. It is strange how the Cowboys cannot seem to get George Pickens going consistently, but Flournoy is more than making up for it himself. He did have a tough drop, and he has become a reliable receiver for Dak.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys loss to the Cardinals
summary: Wow. It’s hard being a fan of the Dallas Cowboys these days, and those difficulties reached a new level after an indescribable 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals. While most of us were guarded against these pesky Cardinals due to the history between these teams, our guard was lowered just long enough to raise […]
full_text: Wow. It’s hard being a fan of the Dallas Cowboys these days, and those difficulties reached a new level after an indescribable 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals. While most of us were guarded against these pesky Cardinals due to the history between these teams, our guard was lowered just long enough to raise our hopes so they could be snatched away yet again. This one was a tough one, and here are 10 thoughts on this really sad Sunday morning showing. 1. The streak continues Another game against Arizona, another loss. It’s just not in the cards. For reasons as mysterious as the Loch Ness monster, the Cowboys cannot beat this football team. Even when it looks like the Cardinals are dead in the water, they find a way to rise up and defeat Dallas. The losing streak now sits at five straight and nine of the last 10 games. It’s frustrating, it’s peculiar, and it’s downright tiring. 2. Getting all the breaks What’s even weirder about this loss is that so many things went in the Cowboys’ favor. They won the turnover battle, they won the penalty battle, and when loose balls were flying around, they were landing in the Cowboys’ hands. Jonathan Mingo muffed a punt. No problem. Javonte Williams fumbled in the end zone. Don’t fret; still a touchdown. Early in the game, the Cardinals receivers were dropping passes left and right, and it just felt like everything was working in the Cowboys’ favor. Little did we know what lay ahead. 3. Sneaky suspicious When the Cowboys get backed up deep in their own territory, they love to waste a down and QB-sneak it. They did it last week against the Eagles, and they did it again on Sunday. Both times resulted in a quick possession, as the Cowboys were forced to punt. Brian Schottenheimer clearly values safety over extending the drive. His team. His choice. If he likes to sneak so much, then why didn’t he do so when he decided to go for it on 4th-and-inches at his own 30-yard line? Instead, he opted to run, and Williams was stuffed behind the line of scrimmage. 4. Other weird stuff The playcalling was weird sometimes, but some of the logic behind the Cowboys’ choices was equally puzzling. Going for it at your own 30-yard line is certainly a choice. In that moment, he chose to be aggressive. We get it. That’s what makes his other passive moments really confusing. Late in the first half, the Cowboys had a shot at a field goal, and they chose to run the ball to get a little closer for Brandon Aubrey, but even still, it was a 60+ yard field goal attempt? Just because he’s capable of booming those kicks doesn’t mean you shouldn’t at least try to get closer. It didn’t seem like a whole lot at the time, but those three points would’ve come in handy later. 5. Second half collapse The Cardinals aren’t viewed as a strong offensive team, but for the Cowboys to still hold them to just three points in the first half was impressive, especially considering the Dallas offense turned the ball over on downs in their own territory. Nice recovery, defense. But as good as they were in the first half, they were equally disastrous in the second half. They surrendered four second-half touchdowns, including three in the fourth quarter alone. The defense allowed two 50+ yard runs from Tyler Allgeier and couldn’t make a stop to save their lives. It was a complete meltdown. 6. One first down, please Despite the late comeback, the Cowboys still had a chance to ice the game. After a failed onside kick, Dallas was sitting in great shape. All they needed was one first down, and the game was over. The Cardinals only had one timeout left, and Mike LaFleur opted to use it on the plus side of the two-minute warning after a running play that went nowhere. This dared the Cowboys to pass on second down because the clock would stop after the next play no matter what. Dallas took the bait; only Prescott took the conservative approach and cautiously fell into a sack after his first read wasn’t there. This resulted in a sack and gave them no chance to get a first down and run out the clock. 7. Another gift After the Cardinals scored a touchdown with just six seconds left, the life was sucked out of AT&T Stadium. The only thing left was for Arizona kicker Chad Ryland to hit the extra point and leave Dallas with another victory. Shockingly, he shanked it, missing his first extra point since 2024, and giving the Cowboys another chance they didn’t deserve. 8. A wasted stop Despite transforming into a red-carpet defense in the second half, the Cowboys surprisingly forced the Cardinals to go three-and-out in their first possession of overtime. It set up a perfect opportunity for the Cowboys’ offense to take control of the game and move into Aubrey range for the game-winner. They never got close. The offense’s final possession was pathetic. It was a quick three-and-out, and they went backwards. The Cowboys punted the ball away and never got a chance again. The defense just didn’t have it in them to make another stop. 9. Under pressure It feels less exhilarating now, but there was a time when it was exciting to see Jacoby Brissett repeatedly succumb to pressure. The Cowboys sacked the Cardinals’ quarterbacks five times, with two coming from Quinnen Williams, and one each from Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, and James Houston. Defensive tackle Elijah Garcia almost had another one, but Brissett was able to get rid of it at the last second. While most of the damage happened in the first half, it was good to see the Cowboys’ pass rush show some life. 10. Brissett still undefeated Entering the game, Brissett remained the only quarterback from Prescott’s draft class in 2016 whom the Cowboys have yet to beat. They have faced seven quarterbacks from that draft, including Jared Goff, Carson Wentz, Cody Kessler, Nate Sudfeld, Brandon Allen, Jeff Driskel, and Brissett. All of them have fallen to the Cowboys at some point over the years, with the exception of Brissett, and it looked like they would finally be able to check him off the list as well. They had his number so well that he was benched and replaced with quarterback Gardner Minshew. The veteran came to the rescue and kept Brissett’s winning streak against Dak and the Cowboys alive and well.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas gets upset, embarrassed by Cardinals in OT
summary: It was a game the Dallas Cowboys needed to win. After winning against the Eagles in a decent performance last week, Dallas had the opportunity to gain ground in the division with the Giants on bye. And against a 2-5 Cardinals team, winning seemed like an entirely doable task. For most of the game, it […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images It was a game the Dallas Cowboys needed to win. After winning against the Eagles in a decent performance last week, Dallas had the opportunity to gain ground in the division with the Giants on bye. And against a 2-5 Cardinals team, winning seemed like an entirely doable task. For most of the game, it looked like Dallas was going to get it done, but they didn’t. Dallas Cowboys suffer embarrassing 33-30 defeat against Arizona Cardinals- Mark Heaney, Inside The Star It was a game that was a good summary of the season. Dallas looked good at times, but in a game the Cowboys should have won, the defense couldn’t get the job done. Unfortunately, that momentum didn’t last; after another Dallas punt, backup RB Tyler Allgeier broke free for a 63-yard touchdown run, cutting the lead to 17-10. Offensively, they finally responded: a 37-yard connection between Dak Prescott and George Pickens, followed by a pass interference penalty, set them up at the goal line. Game Recap: Dallas shocked in OT, 33-30- Staff, DallasCowboys.com At this point, there is enough evidence to believe that the Cardinals simply have the Cowboys number. Even after losing eight of the last nine, this one simply should not have happened. The Cowboys won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. And the unit quickly took care of business by forcing the Cardinals to go three-and-out. But Dallas could do no better and punted on their first try as well. Given a second chance, Arizona did what they had to do, crossing into Cowboys territory and setting up Ryland to redeem himself. This time the kicker split the uprights from 42 yards out to give the Cardinals a shocking 33-30 win. 5 instant reactions to Cowboys’ soul-crushing overtime loss to Cardinals- Michel Haney, The Landry Hat It’s tough not to feel as though the season may be coming to an early end. If you can’t beat the Arizona Cardinals at home as a 7.5-point favorite, there isn’t much hope for the tougher games remaining. Defense is too sloppy to hold up against good teams In the first half alone, the Cowboys were flagged for offsides three separate times, all because of Brissett hard counts. Daron Bland was called for defensive pass interference on a quick slant that might not have even been catchable for Michael Wilson. Schottenheimer’s stubborn offensive strategy doomed Cowboys from start- Reid Hanson, Cowboys Wire In a loss this embarrassing, fingers can be pointed in a lot of different directions. However, it’s tough not to start with the defense and head coach. Dallas’ run-pass distribution fell 39-29 in the running game’s favor; the Cowboys were successful on only 32 percent of those runs, garnering an EPA/rush average of -0.26. These numbers spread out over the course of a season would rank Dallas 31 st in both EPA and success rate, yet, for some unexplainable reason, Schottenheimer stuck with it. 3 things we learned about the Cowboys from the Cardinals game- Dyllan Rivers, Blogging The Boys After this game, fans have a pretty good idea of who the 2026 Cowboys are. The offense is decent but wildly inconsistent; the defense has its moments but is largely useless, and the coaching is abysmal. It’s possible for the Cowboys defense to start fast but can’t finish Dallas forced a punt and had a goal line stand on the Cardinals first two drives, respectively. On the third drive, Shemar James snagged the first interception of his young career, creating a seven-point opportunity on the Cardinals five-yard line.

title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals: The good, the bad, and ugly from Week 8
summary: It would have been shocking to see the Dallas Cowboys lose to the Arizona Cardinals in the way they did on Sunday afternoon, if it wasn’t so predictable. They had the game in hand only to let it slip from their grasp at the end of regulation, which was only prolonged into overtime after the […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images It would have been shocking to see the Dallas Cowboys lose to the Arizona Cardinals in the way they did on Sunday afternoon, if it wasn’t so predictable. They had the game in hand only to let it slip from their grasp at the end of regulation, which was only prolonged into overtime after the Cardinals missed extra point attempt. It’s yet another example this team is just bad this year. Once again, there are more negatives than positives after the Cowboys Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. THE GOOD – DT Quinnen Williams It’s difficult to think of many positive things that occurred in the embarrassing overtime loss to the Cardinals Sunday afternoon, but Quinnen Williams’ play stood out. He’s been playing really well as of late and had multiple sacks in the game (2) in this Week 8 matchup against Arizona. He’s really been a bright spot on defense for the Cowboys this year, and the most consistent force recently. He’s been well worth the price Dallas paid to acquire him. He’s a centerpiece they can continue to build around and still probably better than anyone the Jets will draft in 2027 with the first of Dallas’ two first-round picks. THE BAD – HC Brian Schottenheimer Brian Schottenheimer’s playcalling duties have been a matter of discussion for the majority of the season and will likely remain to be so until they’re either taken away or he relinquishes them. With the playmakers he has at his disposal, the Cowboys offense should be one of the best in the league. Instead, they are struggling to have consistent outings. And, if that wasn’t enough, Schottenheimer’s in-game decision-making is costing the team wins. He played it way to safe at the end of the game, which allowed Arizona time to drive the field and scored TD that should’ve ended the game if not for the missed extra point. THE UGLY – Christian Parker’s defense It was a tale of two halves Sunday afternoon for Christian Parker and the Cowboys defense in the Week 8 matchup with the Cardinals. In the first half they looked pretty good by only allowing three points, but things changed dramatically for the worse in the second half. They allowed RB Tyler Allgeier to rush for 147 yards and score two touchdowns, also allowing QB Garner Minshew to throw for 188 yards and three TDs in the third and fourth quarter. Whatever was working well for them before halftime completely changed in the second half. They allowed a big play after big play in both the running and passing game and ended up costing them the “W”.

title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys from the Cardinals game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost a heartbreaker to the Arizona Cardinals. Here is what we learned. It’s possible for the Cowboys defense to start fast but can’t finish Dallas forced a punt and had a goal line stand on the Cardinals first two drives, respectively. On the third drive, Shemar James snagged the first interception of […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys lost a heartbreaker to the Arizona Cardinals. Here is what we learned. It’s possible for the Cowboys defense to start fast but can’t finish Dallas forced a punt and had a goal line stand on the Cardinals first two drives, respectively. On the third drive, Shemar James snagged the first interception of his young career, creating a seven-point opportunity on the Cardinals five-yard line. The offense would go on to score a touchdown on a wild fumble recovery by newly elevated James Mitchell. Tyler Allgeier, however, decided it was time to explode in the third quarter after the quarterback switch to Gardner Minshew. It was exceptionally confusing considering the state of the Cardinals offense. Jeremiyah Love was out, the offense just switched to the backup quarterback. Injuries were ravaging the Cardinals. But once Arizona finally put up a touchdown, they were not stopped again until the first drive in overtime. It was certainly a disappointing finish on the day for a defense that started out strong as strong as they did. They just can’t put a complete game together. Sticking with the run still didn’t work Brian Schottenheimer and the offense once again kept the ball on the ground at a high rate for the second straight week. The offense left some points on the board, and the run game wasn’t explosive, but the balance allowed them to be efficient enough through most of the day, putting up 30 total points. That should have been enough. Somehow, it wasn’t. When the defense allowed Allgeier to break off a massive touchdown run in the third quarter, the Cowboys didn’t panic. They continued to run the ball and pass the ball at nearly a 50/50 ratio on the following touchdown drive. When the defense again gave up a touchdown on the next drive, the Cowboys offense immediately stepped in and chewed up nearly seven minutes, finishing with a field goal and going up by two scores. They ran the ball nine times on that drive. That’s the kind of offense you can run to shut out games on any normal week. Unfortunately, as we know, games against the Cardinals are far from normal. It’s hard to quantify just how Dallas lost this game. The Cardinals are going to Cardinal This two decade long Cardinals nightmare continued the day after Halloween. It looked like Dallas was going to run away with this one, going up 24-10 in the fourth quarter. Then again at 27-17 and just 3:54 to go in the fourth, the game should have been locked up. But the Dallas defense rolled over and allowed the Cardinals to score four back-to-back touchdowns in the second half, tying the game at 30-30 (thanks to a missed Arizona extra point). And then in overtime, after forcing an Arizona three-and-out, the Cowboys offense had one last shot to go put the game away. They returned the favor by going three-and-out themselves. The defense completely fell apart again on the ensuing drive, allowing a game-winning field goal to the Cardinals. This was a game that Arizona had no business winning. Yet, as we know, this 2026 Cowboys team just isn’t good enough to trust in any game situation. And with that loss, the Cardinals curse continues.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals: 4 losers and 3 winners from the game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys returned home looking to show they could grind out back-to-back wins after last week’s dismantling of the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas’ defense played with considerably more physicality and creating turnovers until the late game disappointment. Offensively, a couple of unlikely names provided important moments, although the running game and self-inflicted mistakes caused a […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys returned home looking to show they could grind out back-to-back wins after last week’s dismantling of the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas’ defense played with considerably more physicality and creating turnovers until the late game disappointment. Offensively, a couple of unlikely names provided important moments, although the running game and self-inflicted mistakes caused a massive fourth quarter collapse, eventually losing 33-30 in overtime. We have four losers and three winners from the game, but the damage done to the season is absolutely the biggest loser. Loser: Cowboys running game One week after Javonte Williams ran wild against Philadelphia, Dallas wasn’t able to reproduce anything close to it, and against this Arizona defense that’s most frustrating. Williams totalled 56 yards on 24 carries, averaging only 2.3 yards per attempt, while Tyler Goodson had 14 yards on seven carries, easy maths there on yards per carry. Arizona consistently won around the line of scrimmage and Dallas struggled badly in short-yardage situations. When Dallas was leading in the fourth quarter, that was exactly when the Cowboys should have been able to lean on their running game and drain the clock. Instead, Prescott had to continue carrying too much of the offensive responsibility, which made hard work closing the game out and gave Arizona the chances it needed to get the win. Loser: Cowboys defense versus Tyler Allgeier This one is difficult to explain. Tyler Allgeier entered Sunday with just 176 rushing yards on 61 carries this season, averaging only 2.9 yards per attempt. Against Dallas, he explodeded for 128 yards on only six carries, and he was the third running back on their depth chart. The biggest damage came on a 63-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter that suddenly turned a comfortable 17-3 Dallas lead into a one-score game. Allgeier then hurt the Cowboys again through the air, catching a five-yard touchdown from Gardner Minshew in the fourth quarter to make it 24-17. That meant a player averaging fewer than three yards per carry coming into the game suddenly became Arizona’s biggest offensive weapon. The Dallas defense gave up 128 rushing yards on six attempts, that’s more than 21 yards per carry, to a backup running back and that is simply unacceptable. Loser: Rashan Gary There are bad penalties, then there are penalties like Gary did. Arizona faced third-and-10 from the Dallas 29 with 2:23 remaining and Dallas leading 27-17. Gardner Minshew’s pass fell incomplete. The Cowboys should have been walking off the field with Arizona facing fourth down. Instead, Gary was called for roughing the passer, 15 yards and an automatic first down. On the very next snap, Minshew found Trey McBride for a 14-yard touchdown, suddenly making it 27-24. It was an terrible penalty at one of the worst possible moments that helped cost the team the game. Loser: Brian Schottenheimer This loss is on the head coach. Dallas led 24-10 in the fourth quarter and somehow lost the game. The most frustrating part was how passive the Cowboys became once they had something to protect. Dallas put together a 15-play drive that consumed nearly seven minutes, but once it reached Arizona territory the aggression disappeared. The Cowboys eventually settled for a field goal to make it 27-17. Dallas recovered the onside kick later in the game at the Arizona 20 with just over two minutes remaining and had another chance to finish the game. What followed was painfully conservative. Williams ran for no gain. Prescott was sacked. On third-and-16, Dallas handed the football to Williams for three yards and happily settled for another Brandon Aubrey field goal. That made it 30-24, but it left Arizona 1:09 to drive for a touchdown. Arizona then went 80 yards, scored with ten seconds remaining and would have actually won the game in regulation had Chad Ryland not missed the extra point. Dallas then got another chance in overtime and still couldn’t finish it. Arizona eventually kicked the winning field goal. Schottenheimer spent the closing stages coaching trying not to lose rather than coaching to win. There is a difference between intelligently managing a lead and becoming afraid to attack, this was the latter. Dallas had multiple opportunities to finish an inferior opponent and repeatedly chose the safest possible option. It was scared football, and eventually Arizona made them pay Winner: James Mitchell What a way to make your first touch of the football this season count. Javonte Williams appeared to be crossing the goal line for Dallas’ opening touchdown when Budda Baker knocked the football loose. Instead of disaster, James Mitchell was waiting in the end zone, recovering the fumble for the touchdown. Mitchell was elevated with Dallas dealing with injuries at tight end and immediately made his opportunity count. Being alert enough to follow the play and turned what could have been a costly turnover into seven points, making his first touch of the ball for Dallas a touchdown. Now that’s efficiency. Winner: Ryan Flournoy Ryan Flournoy continues making a case for a bigger role. Flournoy caught a nine-yard touchdown from Prescott in the second quarter and had three receptions for 38 yards, including a big 17-yard gain. After producing 70 yards against Philadelphia, Flournoy has followed it with another useful performance. Dallas already has Lamb and George Pickens, but Flournoy is becoming an increasingly dependable third option. Winner: Cowboys pass rush The Cowboys’ pass rush showed some real signs of life today. James Houston got Dallas started with a first-quarter sack of Jacoby Brissett, while Rashan Gary’s pressure helped create one of the biggest defensive plays of the game. Gary got into Brissett’s face on third down, hurried the throw and Shemar James stepped in front of it for the interception before returning it 33 yards. Then came back-to-back sacks when Donovan Ezeiruaku got to Brissett, which then followed a huge 16-yard sack by veteran, Von Miller. Adding to the total was Quinnen Williams and this defense left the day with five sacks for 42 yards.
author: Mike Poland

title: Jerry Jones on potential coaching change: ‘Not in my mind at this time’
summary: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a particularly embarrassing loss on Sunday. At one point in time the home team led 17-3 against a moribund Arizona Cardinals team. Picking up Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak with the team, in his 25th career game as head coach no less, seemed inevitable. The Cowboys always find a way. Dallas […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys suffered a particularly embarrassing loss on Sunday. At one point in time the home team led 17-3 against a moribund Arizona Cardinals team. Picking up Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak with the team, in his 25th career game as head coach no less, seemed inevitable. The Cowboys always find a way. Dallas collapsed and did so in truly Dallas Cowboys™ fashion. They lost the game, are now 3-5, and naturally one question is at the top of everyone’s mind: Are they going to fire Brian Schottenheimer? Cowboys owner Jerry Jones: “This is an indictment of the whole show … This is a criticism of everyone.” On making a change on the coaching staff: “That’s not in my mind at this time.” — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 1, 2026 Jerry Jones said following the game that staff changes are not in his mind at this time. Firing head coaches is not something that the Cowboys have become known for, the last time they did it was in 2010 with Wade Phillips, but they are seriously underperforming and in danger of the season becoming rather meaningless for them. The Cowboys have already rearranged the deck chairs, so to speak, once this season by bringing in Mike Pettine to help Christian Parker on the defensive side of the ball. Who could help Schottenheimer? Why does a head coach even need help? These are all questions that everyone is going to be hearing and facing for some time.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys caught by Cardinals in horrific collapse of a loss
summary: There were multiple times where it seemed like it was going the other way. At least 2 or 3 times… it felt like the Dallas Cowboys had done enough to beat the Arizona Cardinals. That’s a Cardinals franchise that hasn’t dominated anyone as of late… except for the Cowboys. That’s a Cardinals team that was […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 01: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer looks on before kickoff against the Arizona Cardinals during an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images There were multiple times where it seemed like it was going the other way. At least 2 or 3 times… it felt like the Dallas Cowboys had done enough to beat the Arizona Cardinals. That’s a Cardinals franchise that hasn’t dominated anyone as of late… except for the Cowboys. That’s a Cardinals team that was down big and changed quarterbacks in the second half. They didn’t pivot to the number one overall pick making his debut, they pivoted to an NFL journeyman who was undrafted originally. But it’s the Cardinals and it’s the Cowboys. For whatever reason… things just have to go one way. This really went that way. The Cowboys dropped Sunday’s game to the Cardinals in a manner that puts up it up there with some of the most disastrous losses they have had in recent memory. They are now 3-5 and look like they have no business being buyers at the trade deadline. How could this happen? First Quarter The Cowboys won the toss and deferred. Defense was up first. Credit where it is due as they stood tall and forced a punt. It was really more that Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson couldn’t wrap one in, but a stop is a stop and the offense had a chance to get to work for the first time. It appeared as if Dak Prescott picked up a third down on the ground, but the initial ruling was that he did not. Brian Schottenheimer challenged that ruling and the Cowboys lost, but then he decided to go for it on fourth and short. What happened next was an absolute nightmare. nightmare pic.twitter.com/8qJoQ3Rzvf — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 The general reaction was disgust and wonder as to why the Cowboys did not sneak it with Prescott. Sigh. Obviously this gave Arizona a short field to work with. And it wasn’t looking good. The Cardinals began to move and everything felt dark. They got right on the edge of the goal line and decided to roll the dice themselves on 4th and Goal. Caleb Downs said no, though! CALEB DOWNS!!! pic.twitter.com/2OJIuwoWbD — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 Dallas was unable to do much with such short field position and ultimately punted the ball away. It was a bummer, but at the very least the Cardinals hadn’t scored obviously. Arizona’s next offensive possession was hardly better for them. They were struggling to move the ball and then a miracle happened. A tipped pass wound up in the hands of Shemar James for the interception! SHEMAR JAMES INT!!! pic.twitter.com/Gyh6PabBUY — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 Jake Ferguson returned for this possession after previously heading to the locker room so that was great to see. Dallas was unable to punch the ball in and when it seemed like Javonte Williams was about to… it was miracle time once more. Williams had the ball jarred loose… but James Mitchell recovered it in the endzone for a Cowboys touchdown! Still counts lol pic.twitter.com/sKzd5Rfpfv — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 The period ended with Arizona holding the ball. Second Quarter The Cardinals gained more yards on the possession in question than any to date, but it was still south of 30 and not enough to really move the needle. Notably the Cowboys sent pressure on its final third down, sacked Jacoby Brissett, and they forced another punt. The next drive was easily the best of the game for the Cowboys offense. Prescott had been a bit under duress earlier, but he had a bit more time to work here. CeeDee Lamb got involved and then things really started to flow. It all ended with an incredible one-handed touchdown catch from Ryan Flournoy to put Dallas up 14-0. FLO TD! pic.twitter.com/aSK8gWyQOa — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 The Cardinals went on to match the Cowboys with a score of their own, but it was only a field goal. Still, points are points, and suddenly it was 14-3. This was the case with 1:13 left in the half. It appeared that Dallas had a real opportunity to double-dip. Unfortunately the Cowboys lost four yards in three plays and punted the ball away. But after the Cardinals took back over and started to move a bit… DeMarvion Overshown jarred the ball loose with a huge hit on Arizona running back Bam Knight. Knight needed help to get off of the field which stalled things. We certainly hope he is alright. Dallas had the ball at Arizona’s 47-yard line, 11 seconds left, and a timeout in their pocket. Brian Schottenheimer ran it and the team picked up 4 yards. He settled for a 61-yard Brandon Aubrey field goal that was pushed right. The Cowboys took a 14-3 lead into the locker room. Third Quarter The Cowboys moved the ball on their opening possession of the second half, but it was a little bit like pulling teeth. It was fairly obvious that Arizona was successfully generating pressure that was bothering Dak Prescott on some level. Still though, the offense was able to get within easier field goal range than their last time out and had to settle for one that Brandon Aubrey converted this time around. Dallas stretched their lead to 17-3. The Cardinals really struggled on their next drive. They did technically get a little bit going, but Donovan Ezeiruaku and Von Miller provided back to back sacks that essentially ended it. The Cardinals punted and Dallas took over with a chance to really go put the game away. Dallas responded by picking up a single yard over their next possession. Obviously they punted. Arizona then surprised everybody by benching Jacoby Brissett and putting in Gardner Minshew. Perhaps that was enough to wake everybody up as right away the Cardinals got back in the game with a 63-yard touchdown from Tyler Allgeier. Gross pic.twitter.com/gUtp8Axzuo — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 The quarter ended right after the Cowboys picked up a huge pass interference on their next possession. It appeared imminent that they were going to score again themselves. Fourth Quarter It took a couple of plays for that to happen, but it did nonetheless. On 3rd and Goal the Cowboys saw Dak Prescott tuck the ball and get into the endzone. It felt like this was going to be enough. DAK! pic.twitter.com/J4vlyn6OUi — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 1, 2026 It was more of the same in the worst way. Tyler Allgeier broke yet another big run and given the fact that almost all of the fourth quarter was left… anything was possible. Arizona seemed to feel that way themselves. They got down near the goal line and Gardner Minshew was able to hook up with Tyler Allgeier who made a critical reach for the goal line on 3rd and Goal and scored: 24-17, Dallas. The Cowboys offense took over with a chance to go put the game away. After falling short on a third down shy of midfield it seemed like they had failed. Thankfully Arizona committed an after-the-play unsportsmanlike conduct penalty that gave Dallas new life. Ultimately the Cowboys were able to get points out of the drive, shout out to L.J. Collier who committed the penalty, by way of a field goal. This put them up by 10 with under 4 minutes to go. Arizona refused to go away, though. They quickly got within striking distance, partly thanks to a roughing the passer penalty that went against Rashan Gary. In fact, just one play after Gary’s penalty Gardner Minshew found Trey McBride for a touchdown to narrow the deficit to just a field goal. It was tense. The Cardinals declared an onside kick was coming and did not recover it. Dallas took over, partly due to a penalty from it not traveling far enough, at Arizona’s 20-yard line with 2:07 left. Dak Prescott was sacked on second down which happened before the two-minute warning. The Cowboys ultimately settled for a field goal to take a 6-point lead and gave…
