title: Game balls for the Broncos comeback win over Chiefs in Week 8
summary: The Denver Broncos pulled off yet another insane comeback win to wrest control of the AFC West from the Kansas City Chiefs. Down 24-13 in the fourth quarter, the Broncos scored 15-unanswered points and put down one of the craziest goal line stands in recent memory. Even now, on Monday morning, I’m still processing how […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: JL Skinner #34 of the Denver Broncos stands on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos pulled off yet another insane comeback win to wrest control of the AFC West from the Kansas City Chiefs. Down 24-13 in the fourth quarter, the Broncos scored 15-unanswered points and put down one of the craziest goal line stands in recent memory. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Even now, on Monday morning, I’m still processing how it all went down. Two fourth down conversions for touchdowns. The missed Harrison Butker field goal. It’s wild. It’s the Bo Nix experience. People keep expecting that ride to end, but it keeps rolling. Nix now has one fourth quarter comeback every 3.5 games started and one game-winning drive for every 2.8 games started. Second place on that Hall of Fame-filled list is a mile . It’s a long mile. No one has ever started their career with such “luck” in the fourth quarter. Maybe its time we all just accept that the Bo Nix experience might be here to stay. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to from the Broncos wild win over the Chiefs: Bo Nix The Broncos quarterback just makes magic happen in the fourth quarter. It may not be pretty the first three quarters, but he finds a way to deliver when it matters most. For the game, Nix finished 20-for-32 passing for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Perhaps the most important stat: no turnovers. With Nix at quarterback, the Broncos have now won 16 consecutive one-score games. It gets better: Nix improved to 12-12 in his career when trailing at any point in the fourth quarter (.500), the best record by any QB since 1970. That’s ahead of Patrick Mahomes (23-33) (minimum of 20 games). As Nix said to Tracy Wolfson on CBS after the game, “Something’s magical about this place. I don’t know. I can’t explain it.” Nix plays a big role in that Mile High Magic. – Ian St. Clair Bo Nix has a 118.9 passer rating when down 1-8 points in 4th quarter (playoffs included). That ranks first among 169 QBs with 75+ attempts in that scenario since 1991 — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) November 2, 2026 Bo Nix in the 4th quarter in his career 63%, 4,025 yards, 33 TDs, 9 INTs — Liam Hammer (@itshammersports) November 2, 2026 Jonah Coleman Jonah Coleman hit the ground running right off of injured reserve last year and took advantage of the bigger workload, getting all the running back work in the second half and turning it into 100+ yards from scrimmage, the first Broncos back over 100 yards this year. He made it count when it mattered most, ripping off a big play on a swing pass to setup the team in scoring position and then showed great vision at the goal line to punch in his second ever NFL touchdown. He already leads the running backs in first downs, despite spending half the season so far on IR. Trade rumors may continue to swirl, but I think Denver has found their starting running back for this season and into the future. – Jeff Essary JONAH MFING COLEMAN!!! pic.twitter.com/PgsLaqppkH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Devon Key, Taylor Rapp, and JL Skinner When both starters go down, it takes a village sometimes to keep the unit together. That village at the safety positions came from Devon Key, Taylor Rapp, and JL Skinner. The defense faltered at points yesterday, but I don’t remember a single time when I felt like it came from any one of these three dudes. When the game came down to a third down and goal from the one, it was JL Skinner too who put the hit stick on reigning Super Bowl MVP to save the game. Have a game ball, all three of you dudes! – Tim Lynch Big time play here by @JlJlskinner to keep the Chiefs out of the end zone. It will get overlooked due to the final play but he came up big there 💪 pic.twitter.com/2j7Hol00ap — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Malcolm Roach Malcolm Roach gets my game ball for sacking the whiniest baggy-eyed punk the NFL has to offer and helping seal the win for the Orange and Blue. Roach has been with this team for a few years now and tends to fly under the radar, but he’s a baller up front. He had 4 tackles including a tackle for loss in the game and a quarterback hit to his credit as well. The big thing we see from Roach consistently is his ability to attack gaps and peel off blocks to create pressure up front. Give this man some love, Broncos Country! – Sadaraine MALCOLM ROACH YOU'RE A FUCKIN BADASS pic.twitter.com/FVPJ7sBnBQ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Alex Singleton Alex Singleton gets my game ball. While he was far from perfect, and still got gashed in the passing game, he played a great game. He had one of the Broncos two sacks, and he finished the game with 14 tackles (6 solo), 1 TFL, and 1 PD. His sack was the sack that pushed the Chiefs out of range for Butker. I may rag on him but he played terribly in the first game against KC, and he made up for that with one of his best games when the Bronco defense needed it the most. – Joe Mahoney SACK SINGLETON pic.twitter.com/AwAr2hgFx5 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Wil Lutz Will Lutz might not be an obvious choice for a gameball, but consider this; he did not miss. The Broncos kicker was 2/2 on FG attempts, and 2/2 on his extra points. Harrison Butker put the Chiefs in a tough spot when he missed his 54 yard attempt late in the 4th quarter. The Broncos went on to score, and Lutz hit the extra point to force the Chiefs into a tough spot, needing a TD to win, and no possibility of kicking a FG to extend the game. Big Nutz Lutz coming through big, helping to seal the win. – Adam Malnati Offensive Line The Broncos’ O-line has gotten a lot of flak this season, and often deservingly so. But the difference in protection between the 1st & 2nd games against the Chiefs is staggering: from pressuring Nix on 48.5% of dropbacks in Week 1 to pressure on just 5.9% of dropbacks in Week 8. The O-line kept Nix clean enough to make the comeback possible. – Taylor Kothe ESPN Research: Chiefs pressured Bo Nix on 2 of 34 dropbacks (6%), the lowest for any team since 2024 Week 5, and the lowest for the Chiefs since 2012 Week 8 Chiefs had a 48.5% pressure rate on Nix in Week 1 — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 2, 2026 Sean Payton A tip of the cap to Head Coach Sean Payton. It hasn’t always been pretty, but Broncos keep finding ways to win under his leadership. Yesterday’s impressive comeback victory over the Chiefs was the 200th of his storied career. It couldn’t have come at a better moment beating a rival to reclaim the top spot in the AFC West. Cheers to Payton on the milestone. – Chris Hart Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Chiefs game? Share in the comments section below.

title: Sean Payton becomes sixth fastest head coach to 200 wins
summary: It’s another week and another insane comeback win for the Denver Broncos. This time it came against the previously AFC West leading Kansas City Chiefs. With 15-unanswered points in the fourth quarter and a heck of a goal to go stand to send the Broncos into first place in the division and the second seeded […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton and Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid shake hands after the game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s another week and another insane comeback win for the Denver Broncos. This time it came against the previously AFC West leading Kansas City Chiefs. With 15-unanswered points in the fourth quarter and a heck of a goal to go stand to send the Broncos into first place in the division and the second seeded spot in the AFC . The win was also a milestone for head coach Sean Payton who notched his 200th career win and became the sixth-fastest to do it. Shula. Halas. Lambeau. Belichick. Brown. 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐭𝐨𝐧. Historic win for @SeanPayton . pic.twitter.com/qn6pjEY4j3 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 2, 2026 What a way to reach that milestone too. Payton was asked about his range of emotions during the final moments of that 200th win and he hit a bit on how special it is to be a part of a great NFL team and the great wins that come with that. I’m screaming at Vance one second and then I’m hugging Vance and shaking Andy’s hand. There’s nothing like it. Sean Payton “Every one of us at some point has to get off this thing, but you don’t want to,” Payton said after the game. “We’re all better having been on it than never at all. So I’ve been fortunate to have been a part of a lot of good players and a lot of good organizations. People that make that happen. So it was emotional. The timing of the game and everything else. I’m screaming at Vance [Joseph] one second and then I’m hugging Vance and shaking Andy’s [Reid] hand. There’s nothing like it. I think the little bit of the curse is that I hate losing probably more than I like winning. So this was a good win.” The ending was special, but what made it so was who they did it again. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs have been dominant when holding a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter. In fact, they were 80-2 before today. Eighty and Two. The Chiefs were 80-2 with Patrick Mahomes when they had a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter before the 28-24 loss to the Broncos. — Rob Maaddi (@RobMaaddi) November 2, 2026 This is a statement win for the Broncos. It’s a win that can catapult a team down the stretch. For all of the criticism the media and fans have thrown at them, this team is 6-2 and in firm control of their destiny. Maybe its time for all of us to just enjoy this ride…

title: Jonah Coleman makes statement as Broncos RB of the future
summary: During Sunday’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs, it became clear a shakeup was underway at the running back position. When the game began, JK Dobbins was given plenty of opportunity to lay the ground game foundation on which Bo Nix’s passing attack would be predicated. None of Dobbins 7 carries would go for longer […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos rushes for a touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs in the fourth quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Imagine if they’d given those Dobbins carries early on to Coleman… pic.twitter.com/2R3LphoGA1 — Mile High Broncos Podcasts (@MHBroncosPods) November 2, 2026 During Sunday’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs, it became clear a shakeup was underway at the running back position. When the game began, JK Dobbins was given plenty of opportunity to lay the ground game foundation on which Bo Nix’s passing attack would be predicated. None of Dobbins 7 carries would go for longer than 6-yards and he would finish his night running for just 13-yards, averaging an unacceptable 1.9 yards per carry. His long of 6-yards was only eclipsed by the -8-yards he managed during a backwards run in the 2nd quarter. It was clear last week against the Cardinals, with his 10 carries for 39-yards and at touchdown, that rookie Jonah Coleman was poised to take a hammer to the running back depth chart. Against the Chiefs on Sunday, he did just that. While patiently waiting for Dobbins to self-immolate on the field, Coleman muscled out 41-yards on 11 carries for a touchdown. While a 3.7 yards-per-carry isn’t anything to get excited about, it’s nearly twice the 1.9 that Dobbins offered. When you factor in Coleman’s receiving stats, 4 receptions for 63-yards compared to Dobbins’ grand total of zero, Broncos Country should have no doubt just whom their bell cow will be going forward. So, why did it take so long for Sean Payton to embrace what all of Broncos Country knew early in the 1st quarter? Coleman was unable to hide his ’it’ factor just as much as Dobbins couldn’t contain the ‘not-it’ oozing from his every pore. Sure, Dobbins is a seasoned veteran who has earned every amount of respect and efference he’s been given, but in the face of the 100+ yards that Coleman produced (especially with carries primarily given to him in the second-half), there is no putting the toothpaste back in the tube. Jonah Coleman is the Broncos future at running back. This doesn’t mean that Dobbins shouldn’t play, be released, or anything like that. If anything, having an explosive playmaker like Coleman in the backfield is a good thing for him. With Coleman, defenses will have to show a greater respect the run and that will translate to better opportunities on the ground (and not to mention in the air) when Dobbins is in. With RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on IR, it’s going to be the Coleman-Dobbins show for the foreseeable future (barring some blockbuster move as we close in on the NFL trade deadline). Broncos Country saw what JK Dobbins was capable of during a solid performance before being injured last season. While he’s struggled to regain that form and dominance this season, it’s not impossible to think that he can’t regain some of that form in the coming weeks. That Kansas City defense, with all the deflected balls and constant pressure Bo Nix endured, managed to play the Broncos as tough as anyone with Dobbins being the primary victim. The Broncos schedule gets less difficult going forward and with opposing teams keying in on Coleman, Dobbins might find some opportunities to get his game going. However, that maturation will be up to Dobbins. The Broncos have found their star back and it’s Jonah Coleman. Will Dobbins shrink and pout in the face of competition or will he jump in and embrace the future with both legs churning? The future of the Broncos running attack is looking exceptionally bright. Dobbins will have to find a way to complement that or he’ll end up watching from the sideline.

summary: Playoffs? Yes, we’re talking playoffs. We are through 8 weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, and the playoff picture is starting to take shape. After their thrilling victory over the Kansas City Chiefs, the Denver Broncos have moved into first place in the AFC West and are currently the number 2 seed in the AFC. Through 8 games, the Denver Broncos are 6-2, lead the AFC West and are currently the number 2 seed in the AFC. pic.twitter.com/pX4CiRhXb2 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 AFC Playoff Picture Buffalo Bills (6-1) Denver Broncos (6-2, 3-1 AFC) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, 3-2 AFC) Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) Kansas City Chiefs (5-2, 5-1 AFC) Cincinnati Bengals (5-2, 4-2 AFC) New England Patriots (5-3, 5-1 AFC) In the hunt Cleveland Browns (5-3, 3-3 AFC) Las Vegas Raiders (4-4, 3-3 AFC) Baltimore Ravens (4-4, 2-3 AFC) Houston Texans (2-5) New York Jets (2-6, 2-3 AFC) Indianapolis Colts (2-6, 1-5 AFC) Miami Dolphins (1-6) Tennessee Titans (1-7) Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Looking ahead The Denver Broncos had a brutal stretch to start the season and made it through that with an impressive 6-2 record. Now, the second half of their schedule is MUCH easier on paper, which doesn’t always mean much. Broncos upcoming schedule Week 9: @ Carolina Panthers Week 10: BYE WEEK Week 11: vs. Las Vegas Raiders Week 12: @ Pittsburgh Steelers (Black Friday Game) Week 13: vs. Miami Dolphins Week 14: @ New York Jets Week 15: @ Las Vegas Raiders Week 16: vs. Buffalo Bills (Christmas Game) Week 17. @ New England Patriots Week 18. vs. Los Angeles Chargers The three big games to circle are the Black Friday game on the road vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers, who currently lead the AFC North and are the 3rd seed in the AFC; the Christmas game vs. Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, who are currently the number one seed; and a road game vs. Drake Maye and the New England Patriots. All three teams are in the playoffs right now and could be potential postseason matchups for the Broncos. These games will likely be crucial in seeding when everything is all said and done. So, these are the three most important games remaining on the Broncos’ schedule, but they must take it one game at a time and take care of business on the road vs. the struggling Panthers and head into their BYE with a 7-2 record.

title: Broncos are reportedly doing everything in their power to trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor
summary: Could the Broncos end the night with a big splash? According to DNVR’s Broncos insider Zac Stevens, the Broncos are doing everything in their power to trade for Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor. Stevens adds that this deal could go down at any moment and that Broncos Country may not want to go […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Running back Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs for a first down in the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Could the Broncos end the night with a big splash? According to DNVR’s Broncos insider Zac Stevens, the Broncos are doing everything in their power to trade for Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor. Stevens adds that this deal could go down at any moment and that Broncos Country may not want to go to sleep just yet. The Broncos want Jonathan Taylor, per @ZacStevens 🗣️ "I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor. This could happen at any moment. You might not want to go to sleep Broncos Country." "The Broncos are going to try to pull this… pic.twitter.com/ixzuSTSsYy — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) November 2, 2026 Stevens goes on to say that the Broncos WANT Jonathan Taylor now. “I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor. This could happen at any moment. You might not want to go to sleep Broncos Country. The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now.” After a huge, thrilling win to improve to 6-2 on the year and take the lead in the AFC West, the Broncos could be on the verge of making a big-time splash trade to improve their offense. The Colts are imploding and started their fire sale this past week, and the Broncos have been named a potential suitor for Taylor from the start. Now, with them sitting as the number 2 seed in the AFC, they could be going “all in” and add one of the best backs in the NFL to their offense. The Broncos do have rookie Jonah Coleman who had over 100 yards from scrimmage which included a 50+ yard catch in run to get the Broncos inside the 5-yard late in the game. Coleman would go on to score the go-ahead touchdown, which ultimately ended up being the difference in the game. However, the rest of the Broncos’ runners are either struggling or currently on the injured reserve. Veteran JK Dobbins’ struggles continued this game, and he apparently unfollowed the Broncos on social media last week and would later get into a kinda heated back-and-forth with 9NEWS Broncos insider Mike Klis. The Broncos also placed second-year back RJ Harvey on the short-term IR this week, joining Tyler Badie. So, you can make the case that they should add to their running back room. Hypothetically, if the Broncos were to acquire Taylor, Coleman would become the Broncos’ 1B and give the Broncos one of the better run games in the NFL. Their run game has really struggled in recent years, so this could be a big time boost to their offense and make life easier for quarterback Bo Nix. We’ll see if this trade goes down tonight or in the coming days, but it sounds like the Broncos want to make a splash addition to their offense ahead of the trade deadline.

title: Winners and Losers from the Broncos’ thrilling 28-24 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs
summary: Your AFC West-leading Denver Broncos did it again. They trailed the Chiefs 24-13 at one point late in the game but would go on to have another thrilling fourth-quarter comeback and score 15 unanswered points to take the lead. Mahomes and the Chiefs attempted to lead a game-winning comeback and got very close, but the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Jonathon Cooper #0 and Malcolm Roach #97 of the Denver Broncos sack Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs in the fourth quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your AFC West-leading Denver Broncos did it again. They trailed the Chiefs 24-13 at one point late in the game but would go on to have another thrilling fourth-quarter comeback and score 15 unanswered points to take the lead. Mahomes and the Chiefs attempted to lead a game-winning comeback and got very close, but the Broncos’ defense tightened, and Malcolm Roach had a game-ending/winning sack. It was a wild roller coaster of a game against a hated divisional rival, but the Broncos worked their Mile High Magic once again. As for winners and losers, it was a tale of two games (when isn’t it?) with the Broncos. The offense kinda sucked at times, and the defense could not stop Mahomes or rookie Emmett Johnson. Yet, in the end, the Broncos made enough plays to win. My blood pressure and heart rate still haven’t returned to normal. WINNER – QB Bo Nix Was it perfect? No. He had some good plays, stretches of bad plays, some passes batted at the line, a few misthrows, but at the end of the day, he came up big in the end. He led the offense to 15 unanswered points, converted a two-pointer, and had yet another 4th quarter comeback and added another victory against Mahomes and the Chiefs. He finished the game going 20 of 32 for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns. TOUCHDOWN NATE ADKINS!! pic.twitter.com/gqRBVv6C1X — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 At the end of the day, Nix went head-to-head with Patrick Mahomes and once again came out on top. Led his team to yet another 4th quarter comeback, and now the Broncos are 6-2 and at the top of the AFC West. Has it been pretty? No. Has it been perfect? No, but here we are again. Despite all the doubters, the Broncos and Nix are simply winners, and they proved that once again tonight. WINNER – RB Jonah Coleman While trade rumors continue to swirl, Jonah Coleman announced himself in a big way on the national stage. All eyes were on the Broncos-Chiefs game, and Coleman came up clutch late in the game to give the Broncos the lead and eventually, the win. He finished the game with 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, while also adding 4 catches for 63 yards, which included the game-changing 51-yard reception late in the game. That’s 15 touches for 104 yards and a touchdown for the Broncos rookie running back. JONAH MFING COLEMAN!!! pic.twitter.com/PgsLaqppkH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 The Broncos are among the teams in the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes and could be tempted to go all in after this big win. If they do, Coleman will be a very good 1B to Taylor or whoever, but if not, Coleman proved he can be the guy in the biggest game and come up big in the biggest moment. WINNER – DL Malcolm Roach The big man called game. MALCOLM ROACH YOU'RE A FUCKIN BADASS pic.twitter.com/FVPJ7sBnBQ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Roach has been excellent for the Broncos this season and came up big on the final play of the game. This will be one of those plays you look back on once the season is over as one of the Broncos’ biggest moments of the season. This sack gave the Broncos the lead of the AFC West. A loss would have been devastating and likely ended all hope of winning the AFC West. Big-time play. WINNER – S JL Skinner His contributions might be overlooked, but he stuffed Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker on 3rd down. Walker, the back who they couldn’t tackle at all in Week 1 and the back who was making defenders miss once again in this game. This stop brought up 4th down and the rest was history. Big time play here by @JlJlskinner to keep the Chiefs out of the end zone. It will get overlooked due to the final play but he came up big there 💪 pic.twitter.com/2j7Hol00ap — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 On top of that, Skinner came in late after Brandon Jones left the game with a hamstring injury. The Broncos were down both starting safeties, and Skinner, who is primarily a special teams player, made one of the biggest run stops of the season. Big play in a big moment. WINNER – Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle The stat lines will not wow you, but both of the Broncos’ wide receivers made impact plays in this game. Sutton had 4 catches for 53 yards, which included a circus catch off a deflected pass, while Waddle had 3 receptions for 39 yards, 1 touchdown, and a 2-point conversion. TOUCHDOWN WADDLE 🐧 pic.twitter.com/eFjvuAIKTd — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 1, 2026 Again, neither player had a big WOW game, but they both left their mark on the game, and Waddle scored a touchdown and had a clutch 2-point play. WINNER – LB Alex Singleton Does Singleton have issues with coverage? Sure, but we cannot deny how good he has been playing lately. He has been excellent in the run game, making big hits each and every game and hasn’t been missing many tackles. Like Skinner’s big play, Singleton’s big play is likely lost in the shuffle, but he had a big impact on the outcome. He sacked Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes late in the 4th quarter and put the Chiefs in 50+ yard field goal range. Well, Harrison Butker, a not-so-good person, was put in a big spot to extend the Chiefs’ lead. Well, he continued his struggles and shanked the kick and put the Broncos in GREAT field position to attempt a comeback. Jonah Coleman would go on to score the go-ahead touchdown, and none of this would have been possible without Alex Singleton. SACK SINGLETON pic.twitter.com/AwAr2hgFx5 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 He is also my star IDP player in fantasy football. His 14 tackles extend his league-leading tackle numbers (not an important stat, but he’s on pace for 200+, so that’s kinda cool). WINNER – AFC WEST LEADERS With this win, the Broncos are now at the top of the AFC West and are currently the number 2 seed in the AFC. THE DENVER BRONCOS ARE YOUR AFC WEST LEADERS 👑 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 More notable Winners and Losers LOSER – RB JK Dobbins: It’s over. Dobbins had 7 carries for 13 yards and saw Jonah Coleman take 90% of the snaps in the second half. Rumors are swirling about an addition at running back, and if that does happen, Dobbins days in Denver could be numbered. LOSER – Broncos coverage of Emmett Johnson – If they did not win this game, the plays they allowed to Emmett Johnson would be the talk of the game. They could not tackle him, and he had multiple chunk plays. LOSER – Offensive struggles: They went cold for a period of time and had 3 or 4 straight three-and-outs. Nix and the offense went nuts in the 4th quarter; still, the inconsistencies and poor play are there. LOSER – Deflected passes: I lost count, but at least 4 of Nix’s passes were deflected at the line. Can’t have that. LOSER – Special teams: They nearly gave the game away when they allowed a long kick return on the final drive, where the Chiefs started at midfield WINNER – TE Nate Adkins: Caught yet another touchdown! WINNER – Run defense vs. Kenneth Walker: Walker embarrassed the Broncos in Week 1, but they held the talented back to 21 carries for 69 yards and a yard per carry of 3.3. Big time improvement!

title: Instant reaction: Broncos rise to first place in AFC West with thrilling victory over Chiefs
summary: The Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs squared off in a gridiron battle that would determine the AFC West leader. After four quarters of back-and-forth football, the Broncos reigned victorious after an incredible goal line stand to earn them a 28-24 victory. Here are some instant reactions from today’s game. Broncos’ offense rallies in fourth […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the football past Nohl Williams #20 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs squared off in a gridiron battle that would determine the AFC West leader. After four quarters of back-and-forth football, the Broncos reigned victorious after an incredible goal line stand to earn them a 28-24 victory . Here are some instant reactions from today’s game. Broncos’ offense rallies in fourth quarter, Jonah Coleman makes a big impact Last week against the Arizona Cardinals, the Broncos had a handful of game-changing splash plays on offense. That was a big reason they were able to earn their third victory in a row. It’s been an up and down year for the Broncos on offense, so finding a way to have a few more big plays was a must to win this afternoon. With RJ Harvey out, the Broncos relied heavily on J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman. Both struggled on the ground in the first half with Steve Spagnuolo’s defense swarming to the ball. However, Coleman was able to heat up in the second half and was a huge boost for Denver’s offensive attack. Coleman finished with 104 all-purpose yards. He had 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown and added four receptions for 63 yards—including a key 51-yard reception late in the fourth quarter. Quarterback Bo Nix was able to help lead another comeback victory. Nix finished the game going 20-of-32 for 222 yards and 2 passing touchdowns. It wasn’t pretty for the first three quarters, but the Broncos’ offense made the right adjustments and came up clutch when it mattered most. I’m pleased with the way they finished and am really optimistic to see what they can do moving forward. There is no doubt Coleman deserves a big role in the second half of the season. Broncos’ defense had issues, but the goal line stand made up for it After what transpired in Week 1, finding a way to shut down running back Kenneth Walker was an absolute must. For the most part, Denver’s defense did just that. They halted Walker to 26 rushing yards on seven carries in the first half . He would finish the game with just 69 rushing yards total. However, rookie running back Emmett Johnson was sensational for the Chiefs in the first half. He had multiple big plays and notched 119 receiving yards on 3 catches in the first half—including a 73-yard catch-and-run for a touchdown in the second quarter. The rookie also made an impact for them on special teams. Denver didn’t have an answer for his speed when he was on the field. Moreover, the missed tackles continued to be an issue for the Broncos’ defense in this matchup. The Broncos weren’t tested deep, but Patrick Mahomes was able to find success in the short game and over the middle of the field most of the evening. Nevertheless, they rose to the occasion and were able to stop the Chiefs on an epic goal line stand to win the game. It certainly wasn’t a great performance overall, but Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and the players executed when they need it the most. They have a lot to clean up before next week’s matchup, but I’m thrilled with how they came up clutch at the end of the game. The Broncos are now the top team in the AFC West Had the Broncos lost this game, they would have been in a multi-game hole in the AFC West and lost important ground in the playoff race. Now? They’re at the top of the division and will ride a four-game winning streak into their Week 9 battle against the Carolina Panthers. If Denver is able to take care of business next weekend, they will be 7-2 going into their bye week. I certainly didn’t think that was possible given their slate of opponents to start the season. It’s great to see the team respond and come away with a huge victory. On a side note, congratulations to Head Coach Sean Payton on his 200th victory as a Head Coach—quite the accomplishment and a great game to earn it in.

title: Broncos comeback preserved; defense with incredible goal line stand to beat Chiefs
summary: BRONCOS WIN! BRONCOS WIN! BRONCOS WIN! Both sides of the ball struggles for the Denver Broncos in this game against the Kansas City Chiefs. However, in the fourth quarter both offense and defense came alive. Bo Nix and the offense scored 15-unanswered points to take the lead with less than two minutes to go. Then […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos looks to pass during the first quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images BRONCOS WIN! BRONCOS WIN! BRONCOS WIN! Both sides of the ball struggles for the Denver Broncos in this game against the Kansas City Chiefs. However, in the fourth quarter both offense and defense came alive. Bo Nix and the offense scored 15-unanswered points to take the lead with less than two minutes to go. Then the defense made one of the most incredible goal line stands to secure the win over Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs to take the AFC West lead. Broncos vs. Chiefs final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Final Kansas City Chiefs 7 10 7 0 24 Denver Broncos 3 10 0 15 28 First Quarter The Broncos defense came out to play to start the game forcing the Chiefs into three-and-outs in two of their three first quarter drives. However, the one drive ended in a touchdown with a Patrick Mahomes pass to Rashee Rice on a slant who beat Alex Singleton pretty badly on the play for the touchdown. PS2 should be on Rice. Shadowing him. Not Alex Singleton. Come on Vance … — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 1, 2026 That play call on defense isn’t on Singleton, though. He shouldn’t be put in that situation against the Chiefs most dynamic receiving threat. The Broncos did answer to that score. After putting up a field goal on their opening drive, they got a big play to Courtland Sutton on the final play in the first quarter to get the team into field goal range again on their third possession of the game. Chiefs 7, Broncos 3. Full first quarter recap . Second Quarter Chiefs’ running back Emmet Johnson exploded in the pass game in the second quarter burning the Broncos’ linebackers in coverage to the tune of three receptions for 119 yards and a touchdown. His two big plays accounts for a total of 10 of the Chiefs 17 points in the first half. Vance Joseph had no answer for him early in this game. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense kept things close with a long drive of their own in the second quarter capping a 12-play, 69 yard drive with this fourth down pass to Jaylen Waddle for their first touchdown of the game. TOUCHDOWN WADDLE 🐧 pic.twitter.com/eFjvuAIKTd — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 1, 2026 After giving up so many big plays on defense to Johnson, the Broncos being down by four points at halftime felt like a minor win. Chiefs 17, Broncos 13. Full second quarter recap . Third Quarter Denver’s offense came out and stacked three-and-outs to start the second half. It’s been a predictable tendency by them this season and the boo birds came out after the second one as fans realized the momentum was shifting towards the Chiefs. And it did. The next drive had the Chiefs march down the field to put Kansas City up by two scores as the third quarter came to an end. Noah Gray turns it into a two-score game ‼️ KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FQZ8EW4aM6 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The frustration with the offense was mounting in the stadium. Chiefs 24, Broncos 13. Full third quarter recap . Fourth Quarter When the Broncos finally got the ball back in the fourth quarter after three straight three-and-outs to start the second half, they got the run game going behind Jonah Coleman and then had big plays to Adam Trautman and Marvin Mims Jr. to setup a first and goal at the five yard line. They’d face a fourth and goal from the two where Bo Nix found a wide open Nate Adkins for the touchdown. TOUCHDOWN NATE ADKINS!! pic.twitter.com/gqRBVv6C1X — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Nix would then find Waddle in the back of the end zone for the two point conversion to close the gap to 3-points with over half the fourth quarter left down 24-21 to the Chiefs. The defense needed a stop and got one, but not before giving Harrison Butker a 54-yard field goal attempt that he missed to give Denver the ball near midfield with 2:32 left in the game down by three points. Nix dumped it off to Jonah Coleman on the first play who ran it all the way down to the four yard line to instantly set the Broncos up in scoring position on a 52-yard catch and run. JONAH MFING COLEMAN!!! pic.twitter.com/PgsLaqppkH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Coleman would punch it in on the very next play just after the two minute warning to give Denver their first lead since the first quarter to put the Broncos up 28-24. Of course Emmett Johnson would return the kickoff 45 yards to their own 44-yard line to give Mahomes and the Chiefs offense a short field to work with in their two minute offense. A big play to Travis Kelce set them up inside the red zone where they would punch it their ticket down to the four yard line to run the clock down to less than 15 seconds at the one yard line where they would have a goal line chance to win but the Broncos defense put together an incredible goal line stand to move to 6-2. Broncos 28, Chiefs 24 .

title: Detroit Lions grades, report card: The run game finally arrives vs. Vikings
summary: Let’s hand out some grades for the Detroit Lions’ gritty 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Quarterback: B Jared Goff’s final statline isn’t all that impressive, but he commanded the offense to a relatively successful day. After shaking off a first half of four sacks, Goff successfully avoided negative plays against this harrowing defense. Obviously, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 01: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) celebrates after gaining a first down during the fourth quarter of a regular season NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions on November 1, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s hand out some grades for the Detroit Lions’ gritty 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Quarterback: B Jared Goff’s final statline isn’t all that impressive, but he commanded the offense to a relatively successful day. After shaking off a first half of four sacks, Goff successfully avoided negative plays against this harrowing defense. Obviously, the interception wasn’t on him. You could argue he held onto the ball a little too long in the first half, but the Vikings’ coverage was often very good on those plays. Ultimately, I was impressed by Goff’s ability to stay calm and disciplined despite the tough start. We’ve seen him—and just about every NFL quarterback—get rattled by this defense before, but Goff kept his head, found the open receivers in the second half (7-of-9 for 66 yards, 1 TD) and even threw his body around a little in the run game. Running backs: A+ Per NextGenStats, Jahmyr Gibbs forced 12 missed tackles on his 25 touches on his way to a 153-yard rushing day. But it was Sione Vaki who got a ton of attention for his breakout performance. His 11 carries for 65 yards may not seem like much, but it felt like he was the key to opening up the run game against the Vikings. His downhill running style led to an impressive 45% success rate on runs (Gibbs was 42%). As a team, Detroit produced 10 rushes of 10+ yards against the Vikings—who had given up just 14 for the entire season prior to this game. And a lot of that had to do with the backs’ performances: Entering today, the Vikings defense had just 16 missed tackles on rush attempts on the season In just today's game, they had 15 missed tackles on rush attempts including 12 in the second half (Data: @SumerSports ) pic.twitter.com/iBtQYr611I — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 2, 2026 Tight ends: B Early in the game, it felt like the Lions’ tight ends were largely responsible for some protection busts. Sam LaPorta and Tyler Conklin looked directly responsible for one sack each in the first half. However, this unit rebounded in a huge way in the second half. Having one or two tight ends in the backfield really seemed to neutralize the Vikings pass rush, and it opened up some massive rushing lanes, as well. Just look how impactful it was to have some sort of skill position player in the backfield (most often a tight end): Lions had 14 under center run plays today with 2 or more skill players in the backfield. Those runs went for 125 yards, 1 TD, and 11 were successful, per @NextGenStats . — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 1, 2026 Wide receivers: C+ Jameson Williams now has five touchdowns in his last three games, as he continues to be a weapon at every point on the field. Amon-Ra St. Brown’s statline is modest (seven catches, 46 yards), but that was on eight targets. His impact was still felt in key moments. Both players were tagged with taunting penalties, and there were times it didn’t feel like they were getting open quick enough. And Williams’ untimely slip on his route not only cost Detroit an opportunity to convert a third down but led to Goff’s only interception on the year. It was far from a bad day from the receivers, but we know they can play better than this. Offensive line: A- It felt like some of the early pressures weren’t on the Lions offensive line, although there were certainly some missed assignments and lost one-on-ones in the run game early. However, everything cleared up in the second half. Despite facing a blitz on 26-of-29 dropbacks (89.7%), the Lions offense allowed a pressure rate of just 24.1%—the third-lowest of any team in Week 8 and Minnesota’s lowest pressure rate of the season. The Vikings’ previous low was 41.3%. I’ve already gone through a lot of the impressive rushing stats, but here’s a few more. The Lions had the sixth best rushing success rate (47.4%) of the week, which was also the highest mark the Vikings have allowed all season. Detroit’s rushing game has been decent all year, but this was the first time it looked like where it was at during its peak days under Ben Johnson. Defensive line: C+ According to PFF, the Lions produced just 12 pressures and NFL Pro had them at a 33.3% pressure rate (14th of the week) with an average time of 3.26 to pressure (third slowest of Week 8). They were fine against the run, but Detroit’s pass rush has slowly been fading a bit over recent weeks. Thankfully, the Lions dialed up a few successful blitzes in this game, and in the rare occasions Kyler Murray was able to escape the pocket, he didn’t do much damage. The interior of the defensive line continues to carry the load. Alim McNeill and Skyler Gill-Howard both had a sack, while Tyleik Williams is a force in the run game and drew a holding penalty. Linebackers: B+ The Lions found a little spark with Jimmy Rolder, who had a sack and a tackle for loss on the game. And coverage didn’t seem to be as big of an issue this week as in previous weeks. While T.J. Hockenson was a bit of a problem, the Lions mostly used defensive backs on him. Secondary: C+ We need to talk about the rebound D.J. Reed is currently going through. He had three pass breakups in this game, and PFF credited him with just a single catch allowed on five targets for 11 yards and an interception. Since Week 5, Reed is the No. 1 graded cornerback by PFF (90.7) with the best coverage grade (91.0). Unfortunately, the rest of the secondary was very up and down. Granted, they often forced Murray to hold the ball long, they still gave up too many big plays and there are still too many coverage busts. Roger McCreary missed a key tackle on Aaron Jones that immediately led to a touchdown. Brian Branch, Chuck Clark, and Christian Izien all had issues on the back end. Obviously, the mistakes didn’t hurt them too much against a Vikings pass attack that just can’t find its identity, but against a better team, Detroit will need to be much cleaner on the back end. Special teams: B Detroit’s coverage units were fantastic against one of the biggest return threats in the NFL. Myles Price managed just 24.0 yards per kick return, well below his 29.7 average. He also didn’t gain a single yard on his one punt return. Jake Bates was okay. He had two touchbacks on kickoffs, although I’m certain the last one was intentional, and his missed his first field goal of the year. But Jack Fox picked up the mantle, putting three of his four punts inside the 20-yard line. Coaching: B+ There were some in-game decisions I didn’t approve of much. At the end of the first half, I think the Lions bled too much clock. Dan Campbell likes to make sure they have the final possession in each half, but when you’re going up against a bad Vikings offense, I think the priority needs to be maximizing your own points rather than being fearful of giving Kyler Murray too much time. I also believe Campbell was wrong to go for a two-point conversion with five minutes still left in the third quarter. Considering the Vikings notoriously score field goals and not touchdowns, being up six rather than five is a pretty significant difference. I don’t think there was enough motivation to try to be up by seven with that much time left. But, a ton of credit goes to offensive coordinator Drew Petzing for a game plan that found actual, real solutions to Brian Flores’ defense. The tight ends in the backfield gave Detroit a numbers advantage in both the run and pass game. Some of the toss action caught the Vikings off kilter, like on Detroit’s 30-yard rushing touchdown. Jahmyr Gibbs races into the end zone to give the Lions the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus…

title: The Detroit Lions’ rushing attack broke Minnesota Vikings’ defense
summary: The Detroit Lions may have only scored 19 points against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but what they were able to do to a previously impenetrable defense was jaw-dropping. Especially because going into this game, the Vikings were talked about as one of the best defenses in this league’s history. The Lions’ second-half running game—23 […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki (33) runs against Minnesota Vikings safety Harrison Smith (22) and defensive line Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (90) during the fourth quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions may have only scored 19 points against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but what they were able to do to a previously impenetrable defense was jaw-dropping. Especially because going into this game, the Vikings were talked about as one of the best defenses in this league’s history. The Lions’ second-half running game—23 carries for 164 yards (7.1 YPC) and 1 touchdown—not only broke through the 2026 Vikings defense, but they did some stuff that has almost never been done to a Vikings defense led by coordinator Brian Flores. According to Shawn Syed, the Lions’ 16.2 explosive play rate on Sunday was the highest mark of the Flores’ era with the Vikings . According to the FOX broadcast, the Lions forced more missed tackles than any team against this Vikings defense. Colton Pouncy was the first to point out that Detroit’s 230 total rushing yards were the second-most ever allowed by any Flores-led Vikings defense. Or, if you’re a more visual learner, just look at the butt whooping the Lions put on the Vikings via most advanced metrics: my god lmao https://t.co/joOx5v13jU pic.twitter.com/HLwYCqEkEn — Arif Hasan, but NFL 🏈 (@ArifHasanNFL) November 1, 2026 To recap, in the second half, the Lions: Had a 31.7% higher success rate than Minnesota Had 1.25 more points per drive Had 0.765 higher EPA/designed run Had 4.4 MORE yards per carry Had a 51.2% higher rushing success rate than Minnesota It was a truly outstanding performance from the Lions offense, despite the low score. On this week’s PODcast, we break down how the Lions broke through the Vikings’ fortress. We also talk about our thoughts on the Jack Campbell injury, the strides the defense continues to make, and the odd officiating in the game, as well. Check out the entire show on your favorite podcasting platform, or listen using the Spotify embed below: As always, you can catch the video version of the podcast—where we talk about some of the coaching decisions made in this game plus other NFL action from Sunday—over on our YouTube page and Twitch channel . There you’ll also see some of our Movember celebration in action, including me doing 10 up-downs and eating “dead fish” flavored jelly beans. title: Lions vs. Dolphins odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
summary: The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins […]
full_text: Aug 16, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa (18) scores a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Eamon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. title: Discussion: What was the most impressive part of the Detroit Lions’ victory over the Minnesota Vikings?
summary: The Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings have been a litmus test for each other for a few seasons now. These NFC North divisional tilts have shed light on the true identity of each team. Last season, the Lions floundered against the Vikings defense on both occasions, while the Vikings offense did enough to eke out […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 01: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs wide with Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) out blocking for him during the Detroit Lions versus Minnesota Vikings game on Sunday November 1, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings have been a litmus test for each other for a few seasons now. These NFC North divisional tilts have shed light on the true identity of each team. Last season, the Lions floundered against the Vikings defense on both occasions, while the Vikings offense did enough to eke out points for a win. In 2024, the Vikings and Lions duked it out for the division crown all season, yet it was a Week 18 Lions victory that ended the Vikings’ nine-game win streak. That Vikings loss set the stage for their Wild Card exit. How would the first leg of this rivalry play out in 2026? Could Detroit beat a defense playing at an elite level under one of the best defensive minds in the league? Could Minnesota legitimize their 6-0 start by beating a talented foe in decisive fashion? The answer was thankfully in Detroit’s favor, but it was not always pretty. It was an emotional game for the Lions on multiple levels, but at the end of the day, they walked away with a win. Even before the season started, many viewed these games versus the Vikings as a challenge for the Lions. With the Vikings starting undefeated, there was an extra level of satisfaction by delivering them their first loss of the season. Amid a game with plenty of impressive moments, what stood out the most to you? Today’s Question of the Day is: What was the most impressive part of the Detroit Lions’ victory over the Minnesota Vikings? My answer: The adaptability of the offense under Drew Petzing. This game started out rough. In the first half, here is a quick summary of each Lions offensive drive: Punt—Seven plays for 4 yards, including two sacks and a taunting penalty Field goal—12 plays for 57 yards, including a sack, another taunting penalty, and an overturned touchdown Interception—three plays for 2 yards Punt—six plays for 18 yards, including two false starts and a 2-yard loss on third-and-1 Punt—three plays for 1 yard, including a sack Field goal—seven plays for 43 yards, including a holding penalty Simply put, very little was working. Jahmyr Gibbs had little room to run, while Jared Goff had little time to throw. When the Lions can’t get those two going, things get rough for the offense. Under previous coordinators like Anthony Lynn or John Morton, a slow start like this would have been a death sentence for the Lions. Those coordinators rarely managed a mid-game turnaround—if the offense started slow, odds are the offense would finish slow. Even when Ben Johnson was coordinating a high-flying Lions’ offense, they were a team that needed to avoid slow starts—that cost them in the playoffs against the Washington Commanders during the 2024 season. Part of that was due to the Lions fielding a porous defense, but it was also because the Lions have thrived by punishing their opponent by running the football and controlling the clock. Naturally, falling behind in games makes that more difficult. Yet despite the rough first half, the Lions’ offense came to life in the second half. It wasn’t by airing it out for Jameson Williams, one of the Lions’ typical sparkplug plays. It wasn’t by forcing the ball to Amon-Ra St. Brown, the reliable right-hand man of Goff. Instead, things started working because Petzing learned from his earlier failures and adapted. In the first half, the Vikings were bringing a ton of blitzes and crashing towards the line of scrimmage. That led to two things: there was little time for the deep routes to develop and there was very little room to move laterally. Early on, the Lions tried running towards the perimeters a fair bit—normally a strength of Gibbs—but because of the Vikings playing so many players close to the line, there was nowhere for him to move. In the second half, Petzing used the Vikings’ hyper-aggressiveness against them. No room to get St. Brown moving in space? Dial up a creative play where he lines up 20 yards back to get a sprinting start on the screen . The Vikings are crashing the edges often? Run more Iso plays up the middle against a weaker Vikings interior with Brock Wright leading the charge (Wright played a season-high 55 snaps on offense with 17 of those coming in the backfield). A lot of the Lions’ success in the run game came with at least one player operating as a fullback: Lions used their TEs in the backfield very effectively today against the Vikings defense. Adding and changing gaps for the defense to account for to get to zone runs and change-ups off of that. The sidecar look on the first few clips has seen an uptick in the NFL the past month pic.twitter.com/7iTkKJ7pLz — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 1, 2026 Look at the run direction (largely up the middle) and look at the clock—most of these clips are from the second half. I have admittedly not re-watched the game yet, but I strongly suspect that play designs like these were not happening in the first half. Early in the game, Petzing’s offensive approach was not working, but he demonstrated his ability to change on the fly based on what Minnesota was showing him. I also think adding Sione Vaki to the running back rotation gave the Lions an extra wrinkle (and a breather for Gibbs too). Of course, not to be forgotten was the impressive outing from Kelvin Sheppard’s defense. Complementary football sealed this victory for the Lions. Despite the slow start, Detroit remained in the game because the defense was holding firm—after a touchdown early in the second quarter, Minnesota would go scoreless until the middle of the fourth quarter. As mentioned before, the reason why the Lions of the past struggled with early deficits was because the defense could not stem the bleeding. Petzing’s crew had a phenomenal turnaround in the second half, but that might not happen if the defense doesn’t keep the Vikings at bay. A hat tip to Sheppard after a difficult start to the season. With Petzing helming the offense, this team looks like it can run the football at any moment—and best of all, succeed while doing it. Those final two drives were prime Lions football—they ran the ball down the throat of the Vikings and won themselves this game. The Lions demonstrated a lot of grit against the Vikings in their pivotal NFC North victory. What part of the team stood out the most to you? Let us know in the comments below.
author: John Whiticar

title: Detroit Lions RB Sione Vaki takes ‘huge step’ vs. Vikings, earns ‘a lot of trust’
summary: When a team has a full roster of offensive superstars, sometimes it’s the role players who pave the way to success. Against the Minnesota Vikings’ vaunted defense, the Detroit Lions tried multiple approaches to find success, but ran into several roadblocks. Entering the half, the Lions trailed 7-6, and while they were moving the ball, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki (33) celebrates a play against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co When a team has a full roster of offensive superstars, sometimes it’s the role players who pave the way to success. Against the Minnesota Vikings’ vaunted defense, the Detroit Lions tried multiple approaches to find success, but ran into several roadblocks. Entering the half, the Lions trailed 7-6, and while they were moving the ball, penalties and missed assignments held them back. Over 30 minutes, Jared Goff was 11 of 16 for 110 yards (and an interception following a Jameson Williams slip), and Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 11 times for 37 yards, averaging 3.4 yards per carry. Sione Vaki also contributed on five carries, producing 29 yards and a clean 5.8 yards per carry. While Gibbs draws a ridiculous amount of attention, Vaki found more chunk yards on the ground in the first half, mainly because of the blocking scheme they ran. With Gibbs, offensive coordinator Drew Petzing called a variety of plays, both inside-the-tackles and stretch plays in outside zone, and the results were mixed. With Vaki, more inside gaps and traps let him get downfield quickly and take advantage of the Vikings’ aggression. Coming out of the half, the Lions started incorporating more of the Vaki blocking scheme with Gibbs as a runner, and they began to take control of the clock. The Lions duo gained another 55 yards on the ground in the third quarter (plus another 10 from Amon-Ra St. Brown on a lateral), then asserted their will in the fourth. Inside trap after inside trap led to Vaki gaining another 34 yards on five carries (6.8 yards per carry) and Gibbs running six times for 63 yards (10.5 yards per carry), as the Lions literally ran out the clock. Lions used their TEs in the backfield very effectively today against the Vikings defense. Adding and changing gaps for the defense to account for to get to zone runs and change-ups off of that. The sidecar look on the first few clips has seen an uptick in the NFL the past month pic.twitter.com/7iTkKJ7pLz — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 1, 2026 “Vaki was one of the guys we challenged this week going into this game,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said in his post-game press conference. “We were going to need him. He needed to show up. He was going to need to get some carries for us, some significant carries. They needed to be real yards, and he was going to need to be able to pass protect for us. And I thought he took a big step today. That’s a huge step. He gained a lot of trust today, a ton. ” In the locker room after the game, Vaki was quick to credit the Lions offensive line for opening holes for him, and downplayed the idea that his success led to a change in approach with the blocking scheme, citing better execution as an offense, but he did note that he was told earlier in the week that his role would increase and that he felt prepared for the moment. “I knew I was going to be called on, especially in blitz pickup, but I was glad I was prepared for the moment. We really harped on grit and resiliency all week, and that’s what we showed today,” Vaki told Pride of Detroit in the locker room, later adding, “I just tried not to get outside of myself, tried to stay under control. Make sure that when I’m blocking, that I’m letting my eyes rest on a single point, and overall, trying to be the aggressor (as a runner).” In total, Vaki’s downhill approach helped him rank up 65 yards on 11 carries, 5.9 yards per attempt—along with one reception for 5 yards—including being the running back on the final two plays that earned the Lions their final first down and the win. If you thought the Lions were still in need of an RB2 to back up Gibbs, rest easy tonight, folks; he’s already on the roster.

Hockenson. On the play, Campbell appeared to get bent awkwardly back. Campbell was down on the ground for […]

Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions’ Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings came to a screetching halt after the first play of the fourth quarter, when Lions All-Pro linebacker appeared to go limp when tackling Vikings tight end T.J. UPDATE 4: The Lions announced Sunday night that Campbell is resting and will remain at a local hospital overnight for continued evaluation. No further update on his status was given. Here’s the team’s latest full statement: Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them. — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 2, 2026 UPDATE 3: Campbell provided a few more details on his post-game appearance on Lions radio. Dan Campbell says Jack Campbell was breathing and alert when he left the stadium but had no further updates. — Al Karsten (@FootballGuy_Al) November 1, 2026 UPDATE 2: After the game, Dan Campbell said that the team has no new information regarding Jack Campbell’s injury. “Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family,” Campbell said. “He’s being taken care of. We don’t have any new information.” UPDATE: The Lions announced Campbell has been transported to a local hospital. Jack Campbell is being transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. — Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) November 1, 2026 Campbell is obviously one of the Lions’ most important players, as he’s an All Pro, and receive a big four-year, $81 million extension this offseason. While we wait for more updates, if you’re the praying or well-wishing type, the entire Campbell family could use your thoughts.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: 11 winners, 8 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the Minnesota Vikings
summary: One week after a stressful NFC North divisional tilt, the Detroit Lions were faced with a similar situation. The undefeated Minnesota Vikings came to town boasting a historically dominant defense led by a coordinator that had given Detroit fits over the years. Despite the pressure on- and off-the-field, the Lions kicked off November with a […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions reacts during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images One week after a stressful NFC North divisional tilt, the Detroit Lions were faced with a similar situation. The undefeated Minnesota Vikings came to town boasting a historically dominant defense led by a coordinator that had given Detroit fits over the years. Despite the pressure on- and off-the-field, the Lions kicked off November with a win and gave Minnesota their first taste of losing. The game as a whole wound up being overshadowed by a disturbing injury to star linebacker Jack Campbell . Players put their bodies on the line to win football games, yet freak incidents like these highlight why these athletes are people first and foremost. Jared Goff said it best: Jared Goff says the Jack Campbell injury was a dose of reality. You remember in those moments that he's a husband and a father. — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) November 1, 2026 Although Detroit walked away with a win today, the team had to weather a scary circumstance to the heart and soul of their team. For the sake of analysis, I will delve into “Winners” and “Losers”, but we need to remember that in the grand scheme of things, they do more for this franchise and fanbase than just play football. Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Winner: Drew Petzing, OC Football is a chess match of player versus player and, more importantly, coach versus coach. The key matchup in this game was Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing versus Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. For Petzing, he boasted one of most potent offenses entering the week. For Flores, his defense had singlehandedly carried the Vikings to an undefeated record. The outcome of this heavyweight tilt was arguably a split decision win for Petzing. Flores landed his fair share of punches (four sacks and a below-average passing day from the Lions offense), but it was a darn good fight from Petzing. Best of all, it showed resilience and adaptability. After the first half, I was ready to crown Petzing as a loser, but the halftime adjustments worked wonders. In the first half, the Lions tried to run too many plays horizontal to the line of scrimmage. The Vikings capitalized, often tackling the Lions players for losses. The Lions only ran a few deep shots (mainly a 46-yarder to Jameson Williams) because there was rarely time for downfield routes to develop. In the second half, the tune changed. Instead of running east-west, Jahmyr Gibbs broke free on a north-south carry and sprinted for a 30-yard touchdown. On the play prior, the Lions ran a Canadian Football League-coded play in which Amon-Ra St. Brown lined up deep on a screen play so he could get a running start. Something kicked in for the blocking up front and the offensive line went from getting pushed back to plowing their way downfield. The Lions’ seven-play, 69-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter was vintage Lions football. They enacted their will against the NFL’s best defense, getting production from Gibbs (as expected) and Sione Vaki (unexpected). Just look at this turnaround: my god lmao https://t.co/joOx5v13jU pic.twitter.com/HLwYCqEkEn — Arif Hasan, but NFL 🏈 (@ArifHasanNFL) November 1, 2026 On a day when the offense looked stuck in the mud at the start of the game, you have to credit Petzing for a complete 180 turnaround when it mattered most. Loser: Jared Goff, QB It was a subpar day for Goff, and I’m hardly factoring in his first interception of the season (a play in which his receiver fell down). In a game where the Vikings were bringing pressure nearly every snap, Goff looked out of sorts. He took too many ill-timed sacks, struggling to sense the pressure and throw the ball away in time. The Lions offensive line was getting worked by the constant blitzing and dynamic looks, but the burden ultimately falls on Goff to avoid drive-killing sacks. Holding onto the ball for too long is a death sentence in the NFL, especially against a defense like Minnesota. Pressure aside, Goff was uncharacteristically inaccurate. His slight overthrow of Amon-Ra St. Brown in the endzone resulted in an overturned touchdown grab. Later on that same drive, Goff turfed an easy swing pass to Gibbs, a catch that would have been an easy touchdown jog for Gibbs. Later in the third quarter, he missed Jameson Williams for a sure-fire first down. In the fourth quarter, with a chance to extend the lead, Goff missed Sam LaPorta on third down (although the play would have been overturned due to a hold). Thankfully, unlike in his early years, Goff avoided self-destruction down the stretch, limiting his turnovers to just that one pick. Goff delivered with a sharp touchdown throw to Williams to secure the lead, plus a beautiful block on a pair of Gibbs runs. However, I think he would be the first to tell you that he was not at his best on Sunday. Winner: D.J. Reed, CB With the Lions struggling to find a shutdown corner amid injuries and poor play, the pressure was on Reed to step up. Over the last month, Reed has quietly been the top defender that the Lions paid him to be. Sunday’s game against the Vikings was perhaps his finest work, doing a phenomenal job of smothering the Vikings receivers. Justin Jefferson in particular had a quiet first half due when covered by Reed, only getting on the scoreboard due to a touchdown grab over Roger McCreary. Reed was credited with three passes defended and made a pivotal interception to set up a field goal late in the first half. The unfortunate news is that Reed left the game in the fourth quarter after breaking up a fourth-down attempt, landing awkwardly on his hip. The Lions would certainly be worse for wear if he has an extended absence. Winners: Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki, RBs At first, the run game was floundering. At the half, Gibbs and Vaki had combined for 66 yards on 16 carries, but a bulk of those yards came on a 19-yarder by Gibbs and a 10-yarder by Vaki. On a majority of their touches, they were getting stopped at or behind the line of scrimmage. The Lions were drawing up a lot of sideways-moving plays and the Vikings were smothering it accordingly. The rushing attack exploded in the second half. Petzing deserves credit for getting creative with his play calls, but the truth of the matter is that Gibbs and Vaki simply started churning out hard-fought yards. On the day, Gibbs finished with 22 carries for 153 yards and a touchdown, while Vaki finished with 11 carries for 65 yards (a career-high). Gibbs is already cemented as a weekly “Winner,” yet Vaki’s rushing ability today showcased the proof of concept for him as a RB2. We had seen his blocking on display before, but now we got to see him shine with the ball in his hands as well. There was some speculation that the Lions could acquire a veteran running back via trade as insurance, but Vaki’s growth could make that moot: Dan Campbell on Sione Vaki: "He gained a lot of trust today." — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) November 1, 2026 Losers: Sam LaPorta and Tyler Conklin, TEs Against a blitz-heavy defense, you often need your tight ends to pull double duty as blockers. As expected, the Lions leaned on Sam LaPorta, Brock Wright, and Tyler Conklin often to help protect Goff. While Wright was serviceable in that capacity, it was a fairly disastrous day for LaPorta and Conklin. LaPorta and Conklin each allowed a sack of Jared Goff in the first half. Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel in particular gave the Lions fits with his ability to both rush the passer and drop into coverage. LaPorta was often left guessing where the pressure was coming from. Conklin, meanwhile, only played a…
