title: Jaguars Run Colts Out of Duval in Dominant Win
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars entered their 2026 Rivalry Week wearing their sandy beach jerseys for the first time, in front of the Jacksonville home crowd. On the field, the Duval ‘House of Horrors’ continued for the Indianapolis Colts, as Indianapolis failed to make this one even remotely competitive from the opening quarter on, cementing 12 consecutive […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Bhayshul Tuten of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs with the ball during the NFL London Series match between Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars entered their 2026 Rivalry Week wearing their sandy beach jerseys for the first time, in front of the Jacksonville home crowd. On the field, the Duval ‘House of Horrors’ continued for the Indianapolis Colts, as Indianapolis failed to make this one even remotely competitive from the opening quarter on, cementing 12 consecutive home wins over the 2-6 Colts. 11 of the 12 wins occurred in Jacksonville, with one taking place in London. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 8 42-7, 35-point domination of the Indianapolis Colts. P lay(s) of the game: Nate Boerkircher’s second touchdown of his rookie season was one of beauty, with the “Consensus Board All-Star” locating the ball in flight over his opposite shoulder for the touchdown, extending the lead to two scores. Trevor Lawrence finds a wide open Nate Boerkircher for his 2nd TD pass of the first half! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H3ubmhXBZo — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Post-game notables: Jaguars Backfield Goes Wild Running backs Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez combined for 217 total yards and three touchdowns, as Tuten made his mark in the run and passing game, going 16 carries for 104 yards and a touchdown, with an additional 55 yards and a touchdown in the air. Chris Rodriguez added another 58 total yards and a touchdown. The two backs combined for 145 rushing yards on 22 carries (6.59 per carry), with the game clearly in hand by halftime. A Clean Day Following back-to-back weeks with 13 penalties during weeks five and six, the Jacksonville Jaguars have seemed to correct this early-season issue, with just 6 penalties against the Houston Texans and 7 on Sunday. Travis Hunter: Punt Returner? Early in the first quarter, Jacksonville sent cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter back to return a punt for the first time in the 2026 season. While the team has toyed with this in training camp, it was somewhat shocking to see Parker Washington, a Pro Bowl-caliber punt returner, taken off the field. My question: Is this move more indicative of the value that Washington holds as a wide receiver building block for the future? Or is the move more about finding every opportunity available to get the ball into the hands of the explosive Hunter? Interestingly, the return in question was right after the opening punt return when Indianapolis downed the ball at the two-yard line. Davon Hamilton Loss Looms Huge While the game outcome clearly takes precedence, the wet Duval weather wasn’t the only thing to place a damper on the celebration at EverBank Stadium. The Jacksonville Jaguars dominated their AFC South rival on a rainy Sunday afternoon. However, defensive tackle Davon Hamilton being carted off the field with a first-half knee injury was the immediate focus of many following the final seconds. The league-leading defense at stopping the run losing their dominant nose tackle is certainly news. The immediate question surrounds the severity of Hamilton’s injury, with secondary questions resting on Jacksonville’s options moving forward, with the approaching November 10th trade deadline. Hamilton was carted from the field following the defense’s fumble recovery on the failed trick play. The trick play goes awry and the Jaguars get it back! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AinguLvhQi — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 In-Game Injuries As a note, the following Jacksonville players left Sunday’s game due to injury: DT Davon Hamilton (knee) S Eric Murray (elbow) RG Ezra Cleveland (ankle) DE Travon Walker (ribs) In Case You Missed It The outcome of Sunday’s AFC South matchup seemed extremely clear by the end of the first quarter, after Jacksonville took an early 7-0 lead via a 12-yard Brian Thomas Jr. reception. Brian Thomas Jr. starts the scoring in Jacksonville! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TSkI5R33VG — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Before Indianapolis could blink, it seemed that the score was already out of reach, with explosive scores from Nate Boerkircher and Bhayshul Tuten. However, an Indianapolis opportunity to create a two scores matchup was quickly extinguished as Ray Lane returned the redzone interception 92 yards for a touchdown, confirming the rout. RAYUAN LANE III PICK-SIX INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bZN2FaLptY — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Halftime Stats: Score: 28-0 Jacksonville Third Down Defense: 16.7% Jacksonville (1/6) to 66.7% Indianapolis (4/6) Defensive Sacks: 2-2 Turnovers forced: 2-1 Jacksonville Rushing yards: 118 to 42 Jacksonville Passing yards: 118 to 57 Jacksonville Redzone: 100% (1/1) Jacksonville to 0% (0/1) Indianapolis Penalties: 8 for 49 yards for Indianapolis to 3 for 25 yards for Jacksonville Points off turnovers: QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half 7/11 for 138 yards and two touchdowns (146.8 passer rating), while RB Bhayshul Tuten had 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown. Following the half, Chris Rodriguez joined in on the fun with a 28 yd touchdown run to extend the third quarter lead to 35-0. Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s turn to score! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1yCUmnx74m — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Jacksonville defense took advantage of the positive game script, collecting 4.5 sacks, a fumble recovery, and two interceptions (including the previously mentioned pick six). Game balls: Special Teams: Punter Logan Cooke: 6 punts, landing 50% (3) inside the 20-yard line, and a long of 55 yards Defense: LB Foye Oluokun: 9 tackles, 5 solo, 1 sack, and 2 tackles for loss Offense: RB Bhayshul Tuten: 159 total yards, two touchdowns, and a 6.5 YPC average Pre-Game Inactives For the Jaguars: S Antonio Johnson (ankle) WR CJ Williams (healthy scratch) CB Alijah Huzzie (healthy scratch) LB Jamal Hill (healthy scratch) DE Wesley Williams (healthy scratch) DT Albert Regis (healthy scratch) For Indianapolis: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) WR Anthony Gould (concussion) CB Justin Walley (knee) TE Pharaoh Brown DT Kevin Givens OT Charlie Heck QB Riley Leonard Live blog: Recap each of the big plays from tonight’s game in our live blog ! What are your thoughts from tonight’s game, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments!

title: Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Indianapolis Colts game discussion, live chat
summary: Good morning, Big Cat Country! The Jacksonville Jaguars are back off their bye and looking to extend their home winning streak against the Indianapolis Colts. Kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST; you can find out how to watch/listen here. Game updates can be found on our X/Twitter, Bluesky, and Facebook. Inactives Live Blog First quarter […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - DECEMBER 28: Parker Washington #11 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs the ball during the third quarter of the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Big Cat Country! The Jacksonville Jaguars are back off their bye and looking to extend their home winning streak against the Indianapolis Colts. Kickoff is at 1:00 p.m. EST; you can find out how to watch/listen here . Game updates can be found on our X/Twitter , Bluesky , and Facebook . Inactives The following players will be inactive for the Jaguars in today’s game: 6 S Antonio Johnson 18 WR CJ Williams 21 CB Alijah Huzzie 54 LB Jamal Hill 90 DE Wesley Williams 98 DT Albert Regis — JaguarsPR (@JaguarsPR) November 1, 2026 Our inactives for #INDvsJAX . pic.twitter.com/r9EcbfGhT6 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 1, 2026 Live Blog First quarter Indianapolis began the game with the football. Jonathan Taylor suited up — perhaps for his last time as a Colt — and on the first play of the day, he broke a tackle in the backfield before scooting for 19 yards down the sideline. The tide turned in Jacksonville’s favor from there. The defense quickly forced a 3rd-and-4, and Foye Oluokun forced a punt by tackling Taylor for a 7-yard loss on a checkdown pass from Daniel Jones. The Jaguars’ offense started at their own 2-yard line but marched 98 yards downfield. A well-schemed pass play to Brenton Strange for 46 yards did most of the damage, though Parker Washington and Travis Hunter also had solid gains, and Bhayshul Tuten had several nice runs. Trevor Lawrence found Brian Thomas Jr. on 3rd-and-12 for the first touchdown of the day! Way to boost that trade value! Brian Thomas Jr. starts the scoring in Jacksonville! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TSkI5R33VG — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Jaguars 7, Colts 0 Indianapolis went three-and-out on their next possession, thanks to a 2nd down sack by Travon Walker and another 3rd down tackle by Oluokun. Lawrence connected with Jakobi Meyers over the middle for a 16-yard pickup before the Jags punted back to the Colts. Second quarter After a pretty smooth first quarter, things got sloppy at EverBank Stadium. The Colts picked up a 1st down due to a facemask penalty against Ruke Orhorhoro, but consecutive false starts by the OL turned a 3rd-and-10 into a 3rd-and-20. The Colts punted, but a 1st down blitz resulted in a 10-yard sack of Lawrence. The Jaguars were backed up and ended up punting back to the Colts. Indianapolis showed some life by converting on 3rd-and-7 against an all-out blitz, but on the next play, a double reverse was botched by Josh Downs, and Jaguars rookie defender Bryan Thomas Jr. jumped on the loose football! The trick play goes awry and the Jaguars get it back! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AinguLvhQi — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Unfortunately, DaVon Hamilton sustained a knee injury during the play and was carted off the field. (Also, Eric Murray was ruled out early in the game.) The good news is that Jacksonville’s offense was able to carry over the momentum from the takeaway. On a “leak” play concept, Lawrence found Nate Boerkircher wide open for a 31-yard touchdown! Trevor Lawrence finds a wide open Nate Boerkircher for his 2nd TD pass of the first half! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H3ubmhXBZo — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Jaguars 14, Colts 0 Jacksonville’s defense forced yet another punt, helped by a Colts pre-snap penalty on 4th-and-1. Washington had a 16-yard catch on 3rd-and-6 to move the chains, then Tuten thundered for a 39-yard touchdown run! A new career high for the second-year back! BHAYSHUL TUTEN RUNNING THROUGH DEFENDERS FOR A 39-YARD TD INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d2MvvxMdPw — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Jaguars 21, Colts 0 With less than two minutes remaining, the Jaguars forced a three-and-out to get the ball back for one more scoring opportunity before halftime. But Lawrence was strip-sacked on the first play by J.T. Tuimoloau. The Colts were immediately in field position, and a Keenan Allen catch put them inside the redzone, but Tyler Warren dropped a pass that went straight into the hands of Rayaun Lane III — who returned it 92 YARDS TO THE HOUSE! Rayuan Lane III reached a top speed of 21.83 mph on a 92-yard pick six of Daniel Jones, the fourth-fastest speed by a ball carrier this season. #INDvsJAX | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/nZLh1meRgI — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) November 1, 2026 Jaguars 28, Colts 0 Third quarter An 11-yard sack of Lawrence on 3rd-and-6 forced the Jaguars to go three-and-out to start the second half. But the defense got the ball by forcing a three-and-out via a 3rd down sack of their own, shared by Josh Hines-Allen and Arik Armstead. Two plays later, Chris Rodriguez Jr. took his fourth carry of the game all the way to the endzone! Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s turn to score! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1yCUmnx74m — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Jaguars 35, Colts 0 Indianapolis put together a 10-play, 65-yard drive that ended with a 6-yard touchdown catch by Josh Downs. The shutout was awesome while it lasted. Jaguars 35, Colts 7 Tuten said, “It’s my turn again!” His second score of the day gets the Jaguars to 42 points! Bhayshul Tuten ends the 3rd quarter with his 2nd TD! @Jaguars are in the 40s! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ShxRF0caiJ — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Jaguars 42, Colts 7 Fourth quarter Branson Combs interception? Branson Combs interception! WHAT A DAY FOR THE JAGS! Branson Combs gets his first career INT INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/N23nx9IBIP — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 FINAL Jags fans, let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ snap counts in the 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 8. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Mike Caliendo, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Jaylon Moore, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Kenneth Walker, TE Travis Kelce and TE Noah Gray Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, DT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Kristian Fulton, CB Nohl Williams, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: QB Justin Fields, OT Joshua Ezeudu Inactive: QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), CB Mansoor Delane (Shoulder), FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, DE Tyreke Smith and OT Diego Pounds The big takeaway: Cyrus Allen is moving up the depth chart In Denver, wide receiver Xavier Worthy led all skill-position players in snaps (64) by playing 94% of the time the unit was on the field. It felt like wideout Rashee Rice (38 snaps, 56% of the offensive snaps), in his return from the hamstring tweak, was playing on a pitch count due to the soft-tissue injury Rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allens stepped up to play 30 snaps, including 22 reps on pass plays. He out-snapped second-year wideouts Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong by 8 snaps, although those two saw more action in run-blocking situations. Allen caught two passes on three targets, but the miss was nearly a huge play downfield; it appeared Allen wasn’t anticipating the ball in tight coverage, so he slowed down on his route. He may not have been as open as it appeared due to that hesitation, but he still could’ve had a chance at a tight-window completion, a similar play as the ones he made in training camp to originally start the hype train. Allen’s 20 yards over the two catches were more than Worthy (13 yards) produced in less than half the playing time. The Offensive takeaway: Emmett Johnson is earning more and more touches Lead back Ken Walker played 55 snaps and dominated the run share, but rookie Emmett Johnson had his breakout game despite just 13 offensive snaps. He saw just one handoff, but gained 15 yards on the tackle-breaking, highlight-reel play. Johnson saw 12 snaps on pass plays and ran routes on 11 of those snaps (staying in for pass protection just once). He caught all five of the passes thrown his way and totaled 128 yards, including the 73-yard touchdown catch-and-run in the first half. With 143 yards from scrimmage, Johnson out-produced Walker (84 yards) in 1/4 of the playing time. He also played nine snaps on special teams and gained 44 yards on his only kickoff return of the afternoon. With return specialist Nikko Remigio struggling, Johnson should be strongly considered as the primary returner moving forward. The Defensive takeaway: Jadon Canady emerges as L’Jarius Sneed replacement The primary slot defender moving forward is Chris Roland-Wallace, and that seemed to be the case even before L’Jarius Sneed was placed on the Reserve/Injured list on Saturday. Roland-Wallace played 49 snaps in Denver and dominated the slot snaps. However, rookie cornerback Jadon Canady was active for the second time this season and made an impact for the first time on defense. As the sixth defensive back in the Chiefs’ Dime defense, a pass-down package predicated on coverage, Canady took seven snaps and made two tackles on third downs that were short of the sticks. He only defended pass plays; he may not be ready to man the slot on neutral downs and defend the run, but he looks like an asset for the Chiefs’ coverage moving forward. title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ heartbreaking collapse in Denver
summary: Last week’s loss sucked. The Kansas City Chiefs were dominated and outplayed in every phase of the game. This one hurt more. Not just because the Chiefs should have beaten the Denver Broncos, but because of how they lost and what was at stake in the AFC West. It felt like the defense played well […]
full_text: (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week’s loss sucked. The Kansas City Chiefs were dominated and outplayed in every phase of the game. This one hurt more. Not just because the Chiefs should have beaten the Denver Broncos , but because of how they lost and what was at stake in the AFC West. It felt like the defense played well enough to win. It also felt like the offense moved the ball well enough to win. It wasn’t the 90% of the plays that cost the Chiefs; it was the minutiae . The little things that all add up to a team coming up one play short when they needed it the most. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs losing to Denver 28-24 in Week 8. 1. Sack Nation is dead The Chiefs’ pass rush isn’t bad. It’s non-existent. \We’re almost halfway through the season, and the Chiefs have recorded a total of eight sacks. It’s tough to come to grips with the fact that Chris Jones is no longer the game wrecker he once was. Peter Woods left early with a neck stinger , but he hasn’t been a difference-maker in his short time in the NFL. And that’s about it for interior pass rushers who still have a shot at getting to the quarterback. The edge rushers are faring a little bit better, getting the occasional pressure, but close only counts in horseshoes and hand grenades. “George Karlaftis got close there” – feels like a perpetual theme. Always so close — Sterling Holmes (@HomestretchKC) October 26, 2026 It’s embarrassing to still refer to the Chiefs’ pass rush as “Sack Nation.” Especially when one of the few things they do well is knock down passes. So I’m proposing we retire the moniker Sack Nation and come up with a more fitting one. I propose: The Batting Cage. 2. The coaching staff needs to make better choices The choice to trot Harrison Butker out to attempt a 58-yard field goal in the rain when he has failed to convert anything over 50 yards, when you’re up three with two and a half minutes left to play, is a wild decision to make. I get trying to show faith in your guy who has shown up for you in the past. But part of being a head coach is having the huevos rancheros to know when a guy is cooked or in a slump, and make the tough/sometimes unpopular choice to adjust accordingly. The same goes for defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s refusal to adjust his scheme and game plan to attempt to generate more pass rush. Or the unforgivable crime of slipping into prevent defense when Kansas City was up by two scores late in the fourth quarter. I won’t get into special teams coordinator Dave Toub here, because those huevos went bad two seasons ago; now they’re just stinking up the chicken coop. There was a lot of pressure on Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker coming into this game after Justin Tucker was signed after what I’m told was an outstanding tryout. Butker went 1/2 and missed a crucial kick late. pic.twitter.com/sbuTghT6HM — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) November 2, 2026 We’ll see if the Chiefs make the move to call up Justin Tucker this week. Speaking of huevos. I hope the organization finds the internal fortitude to skip plan B (Tucker) and find a less slimy solution to their kicking woes than a sleazeball who is no better than Deshaun Watson. Perhaps a guy like free agent Tanner Brown, who was the UFL’s Special Teams Player of the Year in 2026 , making three field goals from 60+ yards this past season. 3. Emmett Johnson deserves a bigger role There were a few bright spots in this game. But for my money, the brightest was rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who at times seemed to be single-handedly trying to will this team to victory. Johnson finished the day with 128 yards receiving and a touchdown. He also had a clutch kick return late in the fourth quarter that set up the Chiefs with a short field and a chance to win. Going back to making questionable decisions — you have to wonder, on their final drive, if Andy Reid and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy should have ridden the hot hand a little bit more and fed Johnson. Maybe it wouldn’t have mattered. Maybe they would have gotten in the endzone; we’ll never know. Regardless, Johnson needs to be an explicit part of this team’s game plan moving forward. 4. Situational football matters Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was brought in to enforce discipline and improve the Chiefs’ situational football. So, seeing a game-winning touchdown wiped off the board by a false start on what should have been the final play is disheartening. Jaylon Moore on the False Start Penalty and more from Travis Kelce on how the team just has to be better and some honest words on how he's been the past couple weeks. pic.twitter.com/mh6oXIaU5Z — Harold R. Kuntz (@HaroldRKuntz3) November 2, 2026 These are the things Bieniemy was brought back to clean up. We’ll see if he’s up to the task. 5. If Brett Veach doesn’t make a move, it’s on him I like Brett Veach as a general manager, but let’s be real for a second. If he doesn’t make at least one, maybe even two, significant moves between now and the trade deadline, he is letting this team down. I’m not usually one for going all in for a championship run. But this is probably tight end Travis Kelce’s last season. This might be the last time to get Chris Jones another ring if his decline continues. The Chiefs need help at wide receiver. Rashee Rice is really good at doing one thing, but it’s still just one thing. Why waste this season by waiting for rookie Cyrus Allen to develop? Allen’s ceiling is that he evolves into a player like Josh Downs. You have the chance to go get Josh Downs, so go get him. The same goes for a pass rusher. Some really bad teams have really good pass rushers. After finishing with six wins last season and losing back-to-back games, it’s clear that this team needs a player or two to get them over the hump. With where things stand, Veach’s actions are the only ones that may put them over the top.
author: Rocky Magaña

title: Chiefs News: Brett Veach is looking for receivers before trade deadline
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs wouldn’t be fixing everything by adding a wide receiver, but regardless, general manager Brett Veach is actively looking for one with just over a week before the NFL trade deadline. Just before Kansas City blew the 11-point lead in the fourth quarter, CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson made sure to share […]
full_text: Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Kansas City Chiefs wouldn’t be fixing everything by adding a wide receiver, but regardless, general manager Brett Veach is actively looking for one with just over a week before the NFL trade deadline. Just before Kansas City blew the 11-point lead in the fourth quarter, CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson made sure to share a report with the nearly-national audience about her conversation with Veach. “I had a chance to speak with GM Brett Veach, who told me that, with Tyquan Thornton being out for the season and Rashee Rice having a history with soft tissue injuries, they will explore what’s available at the wide receiver position.” “You’ve heard Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr. being mentioned, but over the next week, they will make calls and see where everything stands and who is available.” Wolfson’s report was accompanied by a graphic labeled “Wideout Woes” that showed the Chiefs’ rankings among NFL teams’ wide receiver rooms: 27th in receptions (59) 30th in yards (735) 31st in percentage of team receiving yards (49.9%) Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs, Steelers, Commanders have interest in Brian Thomas Jr. | Pro Football Talk 2024 first-rounder Brian Thomas Jr. has interest in a fresh start. And multiple teams are believed to be interested in acquiring him. Currently, the Chiefs, Steelers, and Commanders have interest. The Steelers, we’re told, have greater interest in Colts receiver Josh Downs. Downs, however, is Kansas City’s Plan B, if they can’t get Thomas away from the Jaguars. Five things that stood out about the Chiefs’ loss to the Broncos in Denver | The Kansas City Star The Chiefs’ initial third down never stood a chance. Because the center, of all players, never gave it one. Creed Humphrey has something of the yips with his shotgun snaps. They’re significant plays. The eventual incomplete pass was worth minus-1.5 points, per the RBSDM model. And an incomplete pass was best-case scenario after Patrick Mahomes scrambled just to collect the ball and alertly fire it out of bounds. Broncos score 15 unanswered to win as Chiefs stopped at goal line | The Athletic “The reality of things is we got to fix a lot,” tight end Travis Kelce said after the game. “The little things, mistakes — and it starts with the person you’re looking at. I’m one of them. I’ve been frustrated with myself on how long I’ve been in the league, and the procedural stuff that’s happened for the past three games, really — since the bye. It’s frustrating. You just can’t f—ing do it, excuse my language. I’ve got to be better for my teammates, and that sets the tone for a lot of people in this room.” It looked like more Mahomes magic. Then the Broncos won a nail-biter — again. | NBC News When Denver’s goal-line stand held firm after it sacked Mahomes on the final play, the game became the 35th of this season with a game-winning score in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter or in overtime. (The NFL record through eight weeks is 36.) Perhaps the ending, as wild as it was, should have been expected. Over the past two seasons, Denver’s 16-2 record in one-score games is the league’s best. “It has to come from we’ve done it before,” Broncos coach Sean Payton said. Andy Reid defends Harrison Butker, but the numbers don’t | CBS Sports Here’s the thing, though: 54 yards isn’t really within Butker’s range anymore. It may have been during his prime, but these days, he is not nearly consistent enough from that distance to justify trying that kick. Here’s what we wrote just last week, for example, when Butker missed a pair of field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ loss to the Seattle Seahawks: Through 2023, he made 89.1% of his total field goals, and 28 of 40 (70%) from beyond 50 yards. Since then, though, Butker has made just 82.2% of his kicks, and only 8-of-18 (44.4%) from beyond 50 yards. He missed one of those 50-plus-yard kicks short by several yards in this game, making him just 1-of-5 from 50-plus this year, and he missed another from 45 yards out, pushing it wide to the right. ‘Dogfight for division’: Chiefs face key stretch against trio of sub-.500 teams | KSHB 41 Aside from games on Nov. 27 at Pittsburgh (6-2), Dec. 25 against Buffalo (6-1) and Week 17 at New England, every other team on the Broncos’ schedule has a losing record except Las Vegas (4-4), which might be feisty enough to take a game off their longtime rivals. Meanwhile, Kansas City faces a stretch beginning on Thanksgiving with five straight games against teams at .500 or better before wrapping up the season at the Los Angeles Chargers and against the Raiders at Arrowhead. Around the NF L Ravens’ Lamar Jackson needs thumb surgery, will be placed on IR | ESPN “Obviously, it sucks the way this game is kind of cruel like that,” Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said. The Ravens are dealing with a run of injuries at quarterback and are unsure who will start Thursday night’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Backup quarterback Tyler “Snoop” Huntley left the game in the second quarter and didn’t return because of a right toe injury. Minter said he’s not sure of Huntley’s status. Buccaneers’ Todd Bowles on zero-completion win over Falcons: There’s a ‘first time for everything’ | NFL.com Tampa Bay instead outlasted the Falcons, 16-0, in a rain-soaked affair at Raymond James Stadium despite Mayfield attempting only three passes and converting on none of them, as the Bucs became the second team (1974 Bills) in the Super Bowl era to win a game without a single completion. “I have not,” head coach Todd Bowles said when asked if he’s ever won without a completion, per the team’s transcript, “but there is a first time for everything.” Lions All-Pro linebacker to remain in hospital after scary neck injury | USA Today Campbell went down after making a tackle against Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson in the fourth quarter. He remained down on the field as the training staff and medical personnel surrounded him and the cart arrived. Campbell was loaded onto a backboard before the cart took him off the field. Lions teammates took a knee and looked concerned as staff attended to him. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was in tears while the game was paused. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs-Broncos: The Big takeaway from a Big loss in Denver A false start by right tackle Jaylon Moore negated a potential game-winning touchdown by Rashee Rice, which was a theme of this game. According to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press , the Chiefs committed eight penalties for 75 yards in the first half — the fourth time a Chiefs team has done that with Andy Reid as head coach. Overall, the team finished with 11 penalties and 105 penalty yards going against them, but there was still a chance on fourth-and-6. With nowhere to go with the ball, Mahomes succumbed to a sack, and the game was over. title: 5 Winners and 5 Losers from the Chiefs’ loss in Denver
summary: Your Kansas City Chiefs are good enough to win a game like Sunday’s against the Denver Broncos fairly comfortably. But a series of ill-fated decisions and mistakes allowed the Broncos to play the role of closer. Somehow, with an MVP quarterback, a Super Bowl MVP running back, and an offense that ran for 220 yards […]
full_text: (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Kansas City Chiefs are good enough to win a game like Sunday’s against the Denver Broncos fairly comfortably. But a series of ill-fated decisions and mistakes allowed the Broncos to play the role of closer. Somehow, with an MVP quarterback, a Super Bowl MVP running back, and an offense that ran for 220 yards against this same defense six weeks ago, Kansas City couldn’t get a yard with the game and the division lead on the line. At the end of the day, they’re still 5-2, and in a strong position in the AFC. But they could’ve — and maybe should’ve — won this game. Here are a few Chiefs who stood out in the team’s second-straight loss. 5 Winners Running back Emmett Johnson: When teams focus all of their energy on stopping Kenneth Walker, the Chiefs need a counterpunch to emerge. On Sunday afternoon, it came in the form of a breakout performance from Emmett Johnson. The rookie from Nebraska led the Chiefs in receiving (128), had the game’s biggest play (73 yards), scored a touchdown, made a special teams tackle, and returned a kick 44 yards to set up what should have been a game-winning score. Perhaps the Chiefs should have gone back to the kid at the end? Defensive end George Karlaftis: The conversation all week will be about Kansas City’s lack of pass rush, but we shouldn’t overlook Furious George’s efforts. Continuing an underrated season, Karlaftis had three batted passes, a sack, a tackle for loss and force fumble. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: The best quarterback in the NFL had a great statistical game and delivered what should have been the game-winning score on a short pass to Rashee Rice. This loss isn’t on Mahomes. Wide receiver Rashee Rice: Mahomes needs reliable receivers that can create yards after the catch. The return of Rashee Rice was a reminder that they have (more than) one in-house already. It was a solid game for Rashee, one that could have gone better, and something to build upon. Tight end Travis Kelce: A middle-aged married man was still the team’s best option on the game’s final drive— Travis Kelce’s 32-yard catch and run was exactly what makes this QB/TE duo the best in history. Kelce caught 5 of 7 targets for 67 yards, continuing his strong start to 2026. Losers Kicker Harrison Butker: The pressure was on, and the kick was wide— again. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: At this point, should they just give him a package of trick plays and punt returns? The Chiefs offensive line room: What is going on with Andy Heck’s guys? The left side of the line should be loaded with talent; instead, they mysteriously miss multiple games. The All-Everything Center has a low snap every game. The right side of the line had costly penalties in the biggest moments. And the depth still leaves a lot to be desired. Can they field a championship offensive front for the next four months? Defensive lineman Chris Jones: Eventually, the lack of production from the future Hall of Famer in the middle would outweigh the wins from the edge. Sack Nation needs a better version of their CEO to win in the second half of the season. Head Coach Andy Reid: The buck stops with Big Red. Once again, Reid benched the starting left guard, putting the offensive game plan at risk before kickoff. Then, the Chiefs wasted a very good performance from Mahomes (321 yds and 3 TDs). They lost more penalty yards (11-105) than they gained running the ball (24-90). They couldn’t capitalize on a breakout game from their rookie running back and instead let Denver’s do the heroics. They again struggled with short-yardage situations and left points on the field. They still led 24-13 in the fourth quarter, and seemed poised to grind the clock out with a solid victory. But then there was that punt on 4th and 1 from the 41 (questionable decision)… leading to a long Broncos drive that nearly ended in a goal-line stand. Instead, Bo Nix found wide-open receivers in the end zone (execution failures) on 4th and 2 and on the two-point conversion. On the ensuing drive at the Denver 30, up by a field goal, Mahomes gets sacked (bad play call and execution), and Butker missed a long field goal (everyone outside the coaching staff saw this coming, right?). This comedy of errors led to another Broncos touchdown at the two-minute warning. But even then, the Chiefs would have first and goal from the four-yard line with plenty of time to get out of Colorado with a win. Ken Walker got them to the one, but even more mistakes ended their chances as time expired — a failed pass attempt (predictable play call), a touchdown nullified by a penalty (undisciplined play), and a sack (fittingly terrible end). When one player struggles, we can call them out. But this game showed a lack of discipline, poor execution, and questionable coaching decisions leading to a fourth-quarter collapse. One could argue Andy Reid was outcoached two weeks in a row. Note: Applying the labels “losers” is not meant to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s just a simple way to grade their job performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.
author: Matt Stagner

title: Andy Reid points to ball spotter on Chiefs’ fourth-and-inches punt
summary: On fourth-and-goal from the Denver Broncos’ one-yard line, with four seconds on the game clock, the Kansas City Chiefs were down by four and needed to score. It appeared the team succeeded with a quick pass over the middle to wide receiver Rashee Rice, but it was negated by a false-start penalty on right tackle […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images On fourth-and-goal from the Denver Broncos ’ one-yard line, with four seconds on the game clock, the Kansas City Chiefs were down by four and needed to score. It appeared the team succeeded with a quick pass over the middle to wide receiver Rashee Rice, but it was negated by a false-start penalty on right tackle Jaylon Moore. The pre-snap penalty was the team’s 11th of the game, and set Kansas City up for failure. Needing six yards now, Mahomes had a longer, drawn-out dropback and was eventually sacked by defensive tackle Malcolm Roach to end the game. At the podium after the game, head coach Andy Reid was asked if he felt the penalty on Moore met the criteria for a false start immediately after his opening statement. Reid shared “one man’s opinion” on the game-deciding play. “I didn’t see it,” Reid said. “That’s one man’s opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see ‘false start.’” “I saw him moving his head a little bit,” Reid later clarified. “Now, my eyes went off after that, looking at the setup with the secondary and everything else. I didn’t see anything else move.” JAYLON MOORE WITH A COSTLY FALSE START THAT MADE IT 4TH AND GOAL FROM THE 2 TO THEN THE 7-YARD LINE CHIEFS FOLD IN THE 4TH QUARTER AGAIN pic.twitter.com/YFjULU0qVQ — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) November 2, 2026 It was a polarizing play, but one that decided the game. The Chiefs were one of the least-penalized teams for false starts heading into this matchup. Reid implied he didn’t see a penalty — but Moore’s back foot twitched before he turned his head. #77 definitely twitched lol good call pic.twitter.com/apK5ElYJCY — Dmoney #ElijahWilliamsFC (@JoshCaronIsHim) November 2, 2026 The penalty was deserved, and Moore took accountability in the locker room after the loss. Chiefs' Jaylon Moore on the late false start: "I've got to go back and look at it. Still haven't got a chance to look at it, but regardless, just got to be better." Did he think the flag was on him in the moment? "Just got to look at the tape. It was called. There's nothing else… — Jesse Newell (@jessenewell) November 2, 2026 It wasn’t the only time Reid didn’t “see” the situation on the field: earlier in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs ran into fourth-and-inches from their own 41-yard line. Kansas City punted away, but may not have if the officials gave Reid a clearer picture of the distance needed. “The guys that was holding the ball, spotting the ball, was two yards away from the ball,” Reid said. “So that’s where it’s supposed to be spotted. Then, clock’s running, and they moved the ball up to a foot for a fourth down. So that’s what happened. Mechanically, I wasn’t sure exactly how they were operating with that.” “That’s all hindsight, but it would’ve made for a good decision right there,” Reid said. The head coach was asked about a potential fourth-and-2 if Mahomes hadn’t taken a sack on the second-to-last drive; it was third-and-2 from Denver’s 30-yard line, but a rolling-to-the-right Mahomes let himself be tackled for a six-yard loss. Still, Reid justified the 54-yard attempt from kicker Harrison Butker that followed. “It ended up being what it was, but it’s within Harrison’s range,” Reid said. The miss ignited a touchdown drive from Denver, and the whole fourth quarter reignited questions about Reid’s late-game management.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: The Chiefs’ pass rush, batted balls and all, doesn’t get home
summary: It felt like the Kansas City Chiefs were executing the bend-don’t-break defense for most of the afternoon before the fourth quarter, when the Denver Broncos scored 15 points and stole the game and the AFC West lead from the Chiefs. Kansas City’s defense stuffed the run and didn’t give quarterback Bo Nix much room to […]
full_text: (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images It felt like the Kansas City Chiefs were executing the bend-don’t-break defense for most of the afternoon before the fourth quarter, when the Denver Broncos scored 15 points and stole the game and the AFC West lead from the Chiefs. Kansas City’s defense stuffed the run and didn’t give quarterback Bo Nix much room to throw, whether through coverage or batted balls. Defensive end George Karlaftis batted down three passes, and rookie R. Mason Thoma and nose tackle Khyiris Tonga each added one. At one point, CBS play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz noted that the Chiefs led the NFL in batted balls. “It’s something we emphasize throughout the week,” Defensive tackle Chris Jones said at the podium after the loss. “To make sure you get your hands up if you can’t get there.” However, batting balls down at the line of scrimmage only helps so much. The team still needed the pass rush to get Nix to the ground, and that didn’t happen as it did in Week 1. ESPN Research: Chiefs pressured Bo Nix on 2 of 34 dropbacks (6%), the lowest for any team since 2024 Week 5, and the lowest for the Chiefs since 2012 Week 8 Chiefs had a 48.5% pressure rate on Nix in Week 1 — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 2, 2026 ESPN NFL analyst Benjamin Solak pointed out that, by ESPN’s analytics, the Chiefs pressured just two of 34 dropbacks (6%), which was the lowest of any team in over two years. It was also the lowest pressure rate Kansas City has generated in a game in the era of head coach Andy Reid. Chris Jones knows the team has to execute in pass-rush situations more. “We blocked a couple balls, but I don’t think we got him down today, and I put that on the defensive line,” Jones said. “One-on-one, we have to win on one-on-ones. There’s a big emphasis on winning one-on-ones; we have to take advantage of that. We get a one-on-one — we have to win it.” Denver had an effective game plan by using Nix’s legs: according to NFL Next Gen Stats , Nix completed 5 of 7 passes for 67 yards and two touchdowns on “designed rollouts.” He also completed 5 of 6 passes against man coverage after entering the week with the NFL’s lowest completion percentage in man-on-man matchups (41%). The team missed cornerback Mansoor Delane on the outside, but this speaks to the lack of disruption the Chiefs caused on the Broncos’ signal caller. Karlaftis (1) was the only Chiefs defensive lineman who recorded a quarterback hit; linebacker Nick Bolton also had one, but was beat in coverage across the middle by Nix — who has struggled to attack the field over the middle in past games this season. Whether it was an in-rhtyhm, on-time quarterback like Sam Darnold last week or a mobile, off-script gunslinger like Nix this week, the Chiefs aren’t finding ways to get to the passer before he throws. While multiple factors contributed to a demoralizing loss in Denver, the lack of sacks was a big deal and gave Nix confidence to make the plays needed late. Maybe the blitzes will be more effective with a healthier secondary, but there doesn’t seem to be a direct solution for generating more sacks in Kansas City.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs vs. Jets odds: Kansas City opens as 9.5-point favorites in Week 9
summary: After a very tough two-game losing streak to teams that made conference title games a year ago, the now 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs will return home to Arrowhead Stadium to host the 2-6 New York Jets in Week 9. A rare noon kickoff will see Kansas City face a struggling Jets squad coming off of […]
full_text: Oct 1, 2023; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) scrambles against the Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con After a very tough two-game losing streak to teams that made conference title games a year ago, the now 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs will return home to Arrowhead Stadium to host the 2-6 New York Jets in Week 9. A rare noon kickoff will see Kansas City face a struggling Jets squad coming off of three consecutive losses. Head coach Aaron Glenn is firmly on hot seat watch as the NFL coaching carousel gets in motion. Speculation on the Jets is now heavily tied to what they will do with three first-round selections in next April’s draft. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Kansas City opened as a 9.5-point favorite in the game. Kansas City has now opened as a favorite in seven of their eight contests in 2026. This will be the first meeting between the two teams since the Chiefs won 23-20 in a 2023 primetime showdown at Met Life Stadium in New Jersey. The Jets fall to 2-6 on the season after losing to the Raiders pic.twitter.com/mv7KpEgy8P — SNY Jets (@snyjets) November 1, 2026 The Chiefs are coming off of a heartbreaking 28-24 road loss to the Denver Broncos in which they blew a double digit lead in the fourth quarter. title: Andy Reid, again, says it’s between Kingsley and him after benching
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs started Sunday’s eventual 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos down one of their two first round rookies after cornerback Mansoor Delane was ruled out before departing for the road contest on Saturday. Early on, the Chiefs lost their other first round pick as defensive tackle Peter Woods left the game with […]
full_text: Aug 9, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Kansas City Chiefs offensive tackle Kingsley Suamataia (76) against the Arizona Cardinals during a preseason NFL game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Kansas City Chiefs started Sunday’s eventual 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos down one of their two first round rookies after cornerback Mansoor Delane was ruled out before departing for the road contest on Saturday. Early on, the Chiefs lost their other first round pick as defensive tackle Peter Woods left the game with a neck injury. Woods was initially listed as questionable to return, but he was eventually ruled out after halftime . After the game, head coach Andy Reid confirmed that Woods had suffered a stinger. That was the coach’s only postgame injury note. The most curious absence from the lineup had nothing to do with injuries. For the second time this season, left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched — with CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson calling it “a coach’s decision.” As in Week 4’s contest against the Las Vegas Raiders, Suamataia was active for the contest but watched from the sideline as backup Mike Caliendo took every offensive snap. Reid never confirmed the reason for Suamataia’s benching. He had nothing more to say on Sunday. “It’s just between Kingsley and I,” was Reid’s only comment on the situation. The Chiefs will return to practice on Wednesday hoping to get right from a two-game losing streak with the 2-6 New York Jets coming to town. We will monitor the practice status of Delane and Woods and pass along any further developments with Suamataia.

title: Chiefs-Broncos: The Big takeaway from a Big loss in Denver
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs built a 24-13 lead against the Denver Broncos before a 15-point fourth quarter gave Denver the win in a pivotal AFC battle; final score: 28-24. Here’s the biggest takeaway from the game: The (5-2) Chiefs were the better team on Sunday afternoon… until they weren’t. It was an all-around effort to […]
full_text: (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs built a 24-13 lead against the Denver Broncos before a 15-point fourth quarter gave Denver the win in a pivotal AFC battle; final score: 28-24. Here’s the biggest takeaway from the game: The (5-2) Chiefs were the better team on Sunday afternoon… until they weren’t. It was an all-around effort to blow a 24-13 lead in the fourth quarter and screw up two potential game-sealing possessions. There goes the massive lead in the AFC West standings; the (6-2) Broncos now have the leg up on winning the division for the second consecutive season. This article was supposed to highlight a solid defensive performance and an offense carried by the running backs and tight ends as pass-catchers to reach the finish line. Together, those positions accounted for 17 receptions, 231 receiving yards, and two scores. The headliner was supposed to be rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who totaled 143 yards from scrimmage, scored his first career touchdown, and also had a 44-yard kick return late in the fourth quarter. He was tremendous anytime he touched the ball, including one run where he shed at least five tackles while moving the chains. We were supposed to be talking about which wide receiver on the trade market could elevate the offense; CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson shared word that general manager Brett Veach will be active before the trade deadline targeting that specific position. However, this article is now about everything that went wrong after Johnson and lead back Kenneth Walker muscled their way into a third-and-2 situation from Denver’s 30-yard line with 2:44 to go after an effective, long possession. It all went south once Mahomes took the snap on that play; a roll-out right that the Broncos were all over, leading to a flustered Mahomes eventually taking a sack. Instead of punting to Denver and making their offense drive the length of the field, the Chiefs elected to kick a 54-yard field goal in the rain, trusting Harrison Butker — who has struggled so much recently that the team brought in competition this week. When the kick was missed, a 51-yard catch-and-run by the Broncos’ rookie running back Jonah Coleman followed it, and suddenly Denver was up by four points. The heroic rookie Emmett Johnson tried to spark a game-winning possession with a long kick return following the score — and tight end Travis Kelce found room for 32 yards down the right sideline as well — but the Chiefs failed to reach the end zone despite getting to the four-yard line with 35 seconds remaining and a timeout. A false start by right tackle Jaylon Moore negated a potential game-winning touchdown by Rashee Rice, which was a theme of this game. According to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press , the Chiefs committed eight penalties for 75 yards in the first half — the fourth time a Chiefs team has done that with Andy Reid as head coach. Chiefs have 8 penalties for 75 yards. Only other times under Andy Reid that had 8+ penalties for 75+ yards in a 1st half: Super Bowl 55 vs Bucs 8-95 Week 11 2018 vs Rams 10-95 Weel 13 2016 vs Falcons 8-95 — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) November 1, 2026 Overall, the team finished with 11 penalties and 105 penalty yards going against them, but there was still a chance on fourth-and-6. With nowhere to go with the ball, Mahomes succumbed to a sack, and the game was over. So the big takeaway is… This team still has some of the same situational issues that plagued them in 2025. It doesn’t feel like a wide receiver will fix that. Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes deserve a lot of blame for not managing this winnable game to the finish, and these types of games will only become more frequent as the team navigates the rest of the regular season into a (now) potential playoff run.

title: Chargers-Rams Game Recap: Bolts fall to Rams, fail to find end zone yet again
summary: The Chargers spent two weeks self-scouting, re-evaluating, and reflecting on their first six weeks of the season during a bye week that couldn’t have come at a better time. With a league-worst offense and just about everyone on that side of the ball looking like a shell of their old selves, answers were needed and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 01: Head coach Jim Harbaugh, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers before a game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers spent two weeks self-scouting, re-evaluating, and reflecting on their first six weeks of the season during a bye week that couldn’t have come at a better time. With a league-worst offense and just about everyone on that side of the ball looking like a shell of their old selves, answers were needed and they were needed immediately. Through the first 28 minutes and 30 or so seconds, the Chargers defense had held Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense to zero total first downs. Despite that, they only led 9-3 when the Rams took over shortly after the two-minute warning following Cameron Dicker’s third field goal of the game. On the second play of the two-minute drill, Stafford found wide receiver Tutu Atwell for a 40-yard gain after he beat cornerback Tarheeb Still up the left sideline. Three plays later, running back Kyren Williams leaped into the end zone from one yard out to give the Rams a 10-9 lead into the break. This was the beginning of the end for the Chargers and their hopes of earning their first win of the season. Justin Herbert and the offense would go on to score zero points in the final 30 minutes of the game and ultimately fell to the Rams 24-9. After having a time of possession and total yardage amount that doubled the Rams’ in the first half, the wheels didn’t just fly off, they completely evaporated into thin air. Herbert threw two more interceptions to add to his league-high total. He now has 10 interceptions through the first seven games of his season, an unprecedented fact when you compare it to his 2024 campaign in which he threw three over the entire season. The first came in the opening quarter when he stared down tight end Charlie Kolar on a short out route. Instead of letting it rip just before Kolar made his cut, Herbert waited for Rams safety Quentin Lake to start his drive on the route to let it rip. Lake easily undercut the pass and took it back for 45 yards. That led to the Rams’ first points of the game on a field goal. His second came in the third quarter when he seeming through it straight to cornerback Trent McDuffie who was doing nothing but sitting in his zone and watching Herbert. At the time Herbert threw the pass, he likely saw Kolar coming across the field from left to right over the middle. Fullback Scott Matlock was in front of Herbert blocking a defender and the end zone angle of the replay showed McDuffie was likely out of Herbert’s view behind the blocking Matlock. However, that’s not an excuse for yet another blatant mistake. Hall-of-Fame quarterback Drew Brees, who famously became one of the best pure passers in the NFL despite his 6’0 frame, was in the booth calling the game with FOX Sports’ Adam Amin. At 6’6, Herbert should have some of the best field vision possible. That wasn’t the case here and it was yet another nail in a coffin carved for the Chargers’ seventh consecutive loss. Herbert did throw for a season-high 257 yards, but it was also his second game this season in which he failed to throw a touchdown pass, joining their loss in Week Six where the offense put up a season-low six points. After that rock-bottom outing, the Chargers chose to retain Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator during their extended break. Despite being the league’s worst offense in EPA/play and overall points per game, Jim Harbaugh showed the football world that he did not expect to have to use a Plan B. He tied himself to McDaniel and vice versa. McDaniel hoped to lobby this opportunity in Los Angeles with Justin Herbert into his next head coach gig. Instead, he’s turned Herbert into a turnover-machine that can’t stop delivering the ball to the wrong team. At this rate, McDaniel will be lucky to find himself an analyst job in the NFL. For a complete recap of Sunday’s loss, check it out below. First Quarter The Chargers received the opening kickoff and it nearly went south from the very start. Derius Davis dropped the kickoff and was late to getting up field once he corralled the ball, ending in a short return of nine yards to the 23-yard line. Justin Herbert and the offense’s first possession of the game was a short three-and-out that ended with a pass deflected at the line on third down. On the third play of the game for the Rams, Stafford threw an errant pass towards the left sideline but cornerback Tarheeb Still undercut the ball and took it away to give the Chargers possession as the Rams 47-yard line. Unfortunately, the Chargers offense once again went three-and-out after Mike McDaniel called three consecutive screen passes for a combined -3 yards, the last of which was dropped by Ladd McConkey. The Chargers defense continued their strong start by forcing a three-and-out by the Rams after pushing them back three yards before the punt. But as they’ve done all year thus far, things went off the rails on their ensuing drive. On third-and-five, Herbert took the snap and looked towards his cluster of three receivers to his right. Tight end Charlie Kolar ran an out route at the first down line but Rams safety Quentin Lake was in his hip pocket the whole way. Herbert took a short drop and fired directly into the hands of Lake who took the ball 45 yards the other direction. The Rams ran four plays for eight yards only and the Chargers managed to keep the damage to just field goal. Herbert and the Chargers responded with a nine-play, 56-yard drive that ended in a 34-yard field goal by Cameron Dicker. The highlight play that helped push the Bolts into field goal range was a 30-yard catch-and-run from Herbert to McConkey. Quentin Johnston also caught a pass for 10 yards on the drive. Second Quarter The Rams’ struggles on offense continued with their first drive of the second quarter. Stafford and Co. was once again held to another three-and-out by Chris O’Leary’s defense, including a sack by Tuli Tuipulotu on second down. McDaniel brought out the trickery early in the second quarter with a fake end-around flea-flicker in which Herbert found Kolar for a gain of 20. That play came right after Herbert linked up with Tre’ Harris for a gain of 15. After the Chargers managed just seven yards on the next three plays, Dicker came on once again and converted from 46 yards out to give his team a 6-3 lead. Following the fifth consecutive Rams drive where they failed to convert a first down, the Chargers marched down the field once again on an 11-play, 58-yard drive that ended in Dicker’s third field goal of the game which gave the Bolts a 9-3 lead. Johnston grabbed a 21-yard pass on the first play of the drive while tight end Oronde Gadsden II added a 15-yard catch-and-run. With 1:50 remaining in the first half, the Rams took just two plays to get to the Chargers17-yard line thanks to a a 40-yard pass to Tutu Atwell who beat Tarheeb Still up the left sideline. That play was also the first first down by the Rams against the Chargers. Running back Kyren Willliam took a handoff and hopped into the end zone untouched from the one to give the Rams their first lead at 10-9. After a lopsided first half yardage-wise in favor of the Chargers, they still somehow trailed at the break. Right before time ticked off the clock, the Chargers tried a Hail Mary attempt that ended up bouncing off Johnston into the arms of McConkey but the latter got possession short of breaking the goal line. Third Quarter The Rams offense found a whole new beat to march to coming out of the half. After finding their groove right before the half, Stafford led his group right back down the field with an eight-play, 74-yard drive that ended in a 23-yard rushing touchdown by Blake Corum. The score extended the Rams’ lead to 16-8 with 10:42 in the quarter.…

title: Rams’ optimism growing for Myles Garrett’s return
summary: The reported level of optimism around the Los Angeles Rams and the potential return of Myles Garrett is growing. The hope is that Garrett is back sooner than later, and though he may not be back in Week 9, he could be back any time after. The Rams will likely need Garrett if they hope […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 01: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett (95) looks on during the NFL game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on November 01, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The reported level of optimism around the Los Angeles Rams and the potential return of Myles Garrett is growing. The hope is that Garrett is back sooner than later, and though he may not be back in Week 9, he could be back any time after. The Rams will likely need Garrett if they hope to make a serious postseason run. To be clear, it’s reported optimism with regard to the Rams and Garrett. Until Garrett actually suits up for a game, the team and their fans are going to have to wait. It’s encouraging that the Rams think Garrett is heading back to the lineup, but it’s speculation. The Rams thought that Garrett’s knee would be fine for the season too, it hasn’t been. All this to say that even if the Rams are optimistic, they can be wrong. This is a developing situation as time will tell if the Rams optimism pays off, and if it’s fairly placed. Or, if the team’s excitement will lead to more disappointment as the team, the fans and Garrett wait for him to take the field. LA Rams Get New Myles Garrett Update Before Chargers Game (heavy.com) “Once again, there is optimism that Myles Garrett returns to practice this week,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported on “ NFL GameDay ” on X on November 1. “I know there was optimism last week. Much more this week. He should practice and should be on the field playing relatively quickly.” Rams On SI’s Blaine Grisak offered a “key note” in the wake of Rapoport’s latest report. “Even if Garrett returns to practice, that doesn’t mean he will play vs. WAS,” Grisak posted . “It only means Rams would open up his 21-day window…which would expire after the bye.” Rams Head Coach Sean McVay Hilariously Says He Will ‘Crush’ Aaron Donald (heavy.com) “McVay was asked about the play after the game and he said the following: “Aw man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that. I mean, I saw what he was thinking because it’s going right in front of you and he’s thinking, ‘I’m going to scoop and score,’ and he knocks that [expletive] out of bounds, I mean, what the [expletive]. So, his face he couldn’t even look at me and make eye contact after that.” He also reportedly said, “I’m gonna crush him for that,” per J.B. Long.“ Matthew Stafford and Rams overcome slow start, rally past winless Chargers 24-9 (foxsports) “INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Aaron Donald sprinted after Justin Herbert’s loose fumble with almost nothing but open turf between him and his first touchdown for the Los Angeles Rams . But footballs bounce funny, and this one skittered out of bounds before the diving, scrambling Donald could scoop and/or score. The 35-year-old superstar stayed down in exaggerated exhaustion, and his teammates applied some fake first aid before the Rams finished up their victory. “Oh man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that,” coach Sean McVay said. “He couldn’t even look at me. At least we can laugh about it right now.”“ 3 initial takeaways from Rams’ Week 8 win: offense sputters early, defense locks in (ramblinfan) “The passing offense was largely ineffective throughout the game. With the exception of a handful of plays, the Rams sputtered. Failing to attempt many runs early in the game allowed the Chargers to control the clock, double the home team in yards gained, and keep the Horns on their heels throughout the first half. Fans didn’t need that type of scare. Could LA somehow find a way to get back to running the football? 3 initial observations from Rams’ 24-9 win over Chargers 1. Run game fixed early offensive sputters The Rams ran for miles in Week 7 against the Raiders. But against a similarly poor Chargers run defense, they continued to pass. That’s very questionable play calling, as the offense entered the game without tight ends Colby Parkinson and Terrence Ferguson, or wide receiver Davante Adams.“ Rams send Chargers to 0-7 for first time since Jim Harbaugh was their QB (sports.yahoo) “The Rams overcame a slow start to beat the Chargers, 24-9 , evening their record at 4-4. The Chargers remain the NFL’s last winless team, falling to 0-7. After some early offensive struggles, the Rams dominated the middle eight minutes of the game to win an ugly one. They scored the go-ahead touchdown just prior to halftime and increased their lead on their opening drive of the second half, keeping the Chargers at arm’s distance for the rest of the game. It’s the worst start to a season for the Chargers since 2000, when Jim Harbaugh was quarterback.“ Matthew Stafford and Rams overcome slow start, rally past winless Chargers 24-9 (espn.com) “Herbert has thrown an interception in all seven games this season, but the Chargers also struggled to run the ball. McDaniel, who retained play-calling duties despite the Bolts’ winless start, called back-to-back successful flea-flickers to get the Chargers moving toward their second field goal in the second quarter. “I think the turnovers are what’s stopping us, and that’s something we have to clean up,” Herbert said. “When we’re not converting on third down and not scoring points in the red zone, it’s tough in that regard.” The Chargers haven’t scored a TD in their last nine quarters of play, yet the Rams were pretty terrible themselves early on at SoFi.“ Rams Player Facing Potential Discipline From NFL After Chargers Game (heavy.com) “The Los Angeles Rams’ win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8 could be punctuated by the NFL dishing out punishment for Braden Fiske . Fiske drew a flag for a penalty that is on the NFL’s list of fineable offenses. During the fourth quarter on a third-and-9 play from the Rams 41-yard line in the eventual 24-9 victory, Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert attempted a pass to running back Kimani Vidal that fell incomplete. Omar Speights was credited with bringing the play to an end.“ Sean McVay’s unusual kicker experiment leaves Rams with little margin for error (sports.yahoo) “Keep in mind, it’s exceedingly rare for an NFL team to carry two kickers. Roster spots are too valuable. But we’re talking about the Achilles toe of a team with championship expectations. Sunday’s results were, well, meh. Karty is still dialing in the so-called “dirty” kickoffs, and two of them fell short of the landing zone — the area between the goal line and the 20 — which gave the Chargers the ball on the 40, prime position to start a drive. And a third kickoff just eked into the landing zone, hitting the ground at the 19. “Probably the worst kickoff day I’ve had since last year,” said Karty, who until this week had been back at his alma mater, Stanford, working on his kicks. “I think I was trying to do too much on a couple of those.” 2026 NFL season, Week 8: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Rams rumble over Chargers in battle of L.A. Sean McVay’s offense got off to an ugly start, failing to record a first down in its first five drives. The Rams finally broke through with less than 90 seconds remaining in the first half on a Matthew Stafford 40-yard bomb to Tutu Atwell . The home squad skated from there, scoring 21 straight to blow out their SoFi Stadium mates. The Rams came out at halftime and saddled up the rushing attack. After just 10 yards on the ground through two quarters, Blake Corum and Kyren Williams blasted their way for 129 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries for the game. title: Winners & Losers: Rams win ‘Battle for LA’ pillow fight
summary: The Los Angeles Rams got the win they needed against the Chargers in the “Battle for LA”, but not much else. This is the NFL. You cannot set the bar at a blowout even against the bottom feeders of the league, which the Chargers are at now 0-7. The Rams also did little to inspire […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams got the win they needed against the Chargers in the “Battle for LA”, but not much else. This is the NFL. You cannot set the bar at a blowout even against the bottom feeders of the league, which the Chargers are at now 0-7. The Rams also did little to inspire confidence moving forward as the schedule grows more difficult. The offense feels disjointed and untalented. The defense was stifling, although Justin Herbert may as well have worn royal and sol for as often as he gave the ball to the Rams. Most importantly, the mission was accomplished. The Rams are now 4-4 and have dug themselves out of the hole they put themselves in amid early season struggles. Two very winnable games are on the horizon against the Washington Commanders and the Arizona Cardinals. Keep stacking boxes and LA could soon find themselves at 6-4. But before we turn the page, let’s revisit the individual contributions that made the difference in the win over the Chargers. Winners Blake Corum & the run game The offense goes as Blake Corum does. For most of the season the Rams have searched for a spark plug on offense, and the answer may have been right in front of our eyes this whole time. When Corum is involved and productive, the offense operates at the highest levels we’ve seen from them so far. Corum rushed 11 times for 73 yards (6.6 average), including a 23-yard touchdown that flipped the momentum in the third quarter. Kyren Williams added a less efficient 16 carries for 56 yards (3.5 average) with a short touchdown, although his average was hurt by closing out the game late into the fourth quarter. This is always worth mentioning: anytime two running backs produce, you must give credit to the offensive line. Matthew Stafford was sacked only a single time. While the Rams seemed reluctant to lean into the ground game in the first half, it came alive in the second half to flip the script and then closeout the contest. Blake Corum with the smooth move and TD! LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YP3lqMMQYg — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Puka Nacua, WR The offensive game plan feels like it boils down to two options: feed the ball to Puka Nacua or ask Corum to make something happen. Nacua has battled injury all season long. He doesn’t look like the version of himself we saw a year ago. Even then, the Rams run the offense through him. He had another heavy workload in the game with 11 catches on 12 targets for 80 yards. Nacua also scored a touchdown on a screen. If we are nitpicking, Nacua’s ability to stretch the field vertically has disappeared. It’s the added element that made him an offensive player of the year candidate in 2025. Can the Rams and Nacua regain his value in this facet? Puka Nacua finds his way to the end zone for a TD 🔥 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rYQeocKgJN — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Defensive secondary Quentin Lake stepped in front of a pass to intercept Herbert in the first quarter. Trent McDuffie stole another throw in the second half. In addition, rookie Wesley Bailey forced the ball out of Herbert’s hands on a sack but Aaron Donald and the defense were unable to recover the ball. It was effectively the game’s third turnover and all three plays easily could have resulted in defensive touchdowns. That’s not a bad day at the office. Ladd McConkey and Oronde Gadsden were efficient targets in the passing game with four catches on six targets for 86 yards and five of five for 52 yards, respectively. Outside of that, the Chargers had very little going offensively. 54 of McConkey’s yards came on a single catch and run. And the secondary accomplished these results despite Jaylen Watson suffering a shoulder injury and leaving early. Josh Wallace, who continues to step in and rise to the occasion in big moments, relieved Watson and did not miss a beat. McDuffie also suffered a back injury late. Both injuries are worth monitoring moving into next week. Leading receivers for Justin Herbert today by yards: 1. Ladd McConkey – 86 rec yards 2. Rams Defenders – 71 INT return yards 3. Quentin Johnston – 36 rec yards — NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) November 1, 2026 Nate Landman & Omar Speights, MLB The defensive line deserves credit for helping bottle up the Chargers’ run game, of course. Nate Landman and Omar Speights were a forceful tandem in bringing down ball carriers. Kimani Vidal was held to 23 yards on eight carries (2.9 average), Omarion Hampton had just nine rushes for 20 yards (2.2 average), and Keaton Mitchell contributed just six yards on four carries. That’ll get the job done in run defense, especially in light of the recent injuries to Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. Losers Penalties & discipline… again The Rams were flagged eight times for 40 yards. Between turnovers and penalties, self-inflicted issues can help bad teams stick around. That was at least the case through two quarters, and it’s a concerning continuation of a troubling pattern. Matthew Stafford & the pass game Stafford completed 17 of 25 passes (68%) for 157 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. The numbers are OK in a vacuum and he did not lose the game. They also do nothing to quiet the larger questions about the Rams’ disappearing deep passing attack or whether this offense can generate explosive plays against better defenses. Winning against the Chargers while throwing for under 160 yards is not the same as fixing the problems that have shown up against stiffer competition. I wouldn’t be surprised if Stafford finished with an average depth of target below five yards. Fortunately for Stafford, Herbert was even worse. The Rams QB deserves credit for taking care of the football outside of an opening drive interception. Intercepted by Tarheeb Still ‼️ LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/N3Iqc8430g — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Any receiver not named ‘Puka Nacua’ I’ve written about the Rams’ lack of a third receiving option entering the season ad nauseum. Barring an ill-advised trade acquisition, help isn’t walking through the door—and the Rams are without Davante Adams for perhaps the remainder of the season. Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington are not getting the job done. Tutu Atwell made an important 40-yard catch down the sideline that setup a score, although he basically vanished thereafter. It’s hard to feel optimistic about the Rams’ passing game on a going forward basis with their evidently inadequate firepower.

title: Rams Takeaways: What We Learned From Win Over Chargers
summary: The Los Angeles Rams may have found the missing ingredient to their offense, and Blake Corum is proving to be the secret sauce behind their success. Sunday’s victory over the Chargers showcased how the second-year running back’s explosive playmaking and physical running style can elevate an already dangerous offense. While the Rams have leaned heavily […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams may have found the missing ingredient to their offense, and Blake Corum is proving to be the secret sauce behind their success. Sunday’s victory over the Chargers showcased how the second-year running back’s explosive playmaking and physical running style can elevate an already dangerous offense. While the Rams have leaned heavily on their established stars, Corum’s emergence provides another dimension that opposing defenses must account for. His ability to create opportunities, complement the ground game and keep the offense moving could prove vital as Los Angeles pushes toward the postseason. The Rams-Chargers matchup offered plenty of takeaways , but Corum’s growing impact might be the biggest development of all. For what it’s worth, I suggested Corum should be the team’s lead running back back after Week 2… READ HERE 1st Down: Rams are wisely leaning more on Blake Corum’s explosion For two straight weeks, Blake Corum has drawn the “start” as the Rams running back on the first series. The team still splits the carries between Blake Corum and Kyren Williams but Corum is providing something that the team has desperately needed: shiftiness and explosive ability. LA’s drive to open the third quarter was a heavy dose of Blake Corum. Corum had runs of 5, 6, 13, 8, and 23, with the final carry being for a touchdown to go up 17-9 . The Rams prioritize 2nd & short and 3rd & short situations and Corum gave them exactly that. As for Corum’s explosive ability, check out this chart… Blake Corum has the 2nd best explosive run rate since 2025 💥 #ramshouse 📸 @Scott_Spratt pic.twitter.com/ESr2ToUqav — FTN (@FTNFantasy) November 1, 2026 2nd Down: Running the ball more works For the second straight week… where have you heard that before… Sean McVay called more run plays than pass plays. Stafford had 25 passing attempts while Corum and Williams had a combined 27 rushing attempts. A lot of those rushing attempts coincidentally came in the second half where the Rams began to run away with the game. So if you are keeping record, the Rams are now 2-0 in 2026 when they call more run plays than pass plays. Perhaps Sean McVay should stay with it until it doesn’t result in a win…… The Rams have the second-best success rate on designed runs this season (48.3%). Yet they continue to not run the ball (37.7% designed run rate coming into today ranks 21st). pic.twitter.com/agGI0O2jJN — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 1, 2026 3rd Down: Wesley Bailey needs to play even when Myles Garrett returns Even though the Rams and fans want Myles Garrett want their superstar offseason acquisition to rejoin the team, the team shouldn’t make undrafted free agent Wesley Bailey the guy that sees the field less. Bailey has been as good if not better than 2025 third rounder Josiah Stewart. When the Rams utilize their “cheetah” package, Bailey might be the third edge rusher they want to employ alongside Byron Young and Myles Garrett. Wesley Bailey became the first undrafted rookie since Javelin Guidry in 2020 to record multiple forced fumbles in a season, and the first undrafted Rams rookie to do so since Troy Reeder in 2019. #Rams | #RamsHouse | @wesfresh23 pic.twitter.com/biDCkf2U3N — Los Angeles Rams PR (@TheLARamsPR) November 1, 2026 4th Down: Defense pitches 2nd half shutout The Rams have a reputation for pitching second half shutouts. And they produced another one in Week 8. When the Rams offense starts slow like they have done a lot in 2026, it helps to have a defense that gets stronger as the game further unfolds; giving the Rams offense more and more opportunities.
