title: Rams dominate Chargers: 5 key plays that push LAR to .500
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are back to .500 after delivering a 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8. Several pivotal key moments ultimately separated the two teams, swinging momentum firmly in the Rams’ favor and helping Los Angeles secure a convincing victory. The Rams dominated the Battle of Los Angeles after its […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 01: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against the Los Angeles Chargers in the third quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are back to .500 after delivering a 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8 . Several pivotal key moments ultimately separated the two teams, swinging momentum firmly in the Rams’ favor and helping Los Angeles secure a convincing victory. The Rams dominated the Battle of Los Angeles after its first touchdown, even shutting out the Chargers in the second half. Here are five key plays that helped the Rams dominate the Chargers and get back to .500. 1. Tutu Atwell hauls in 40 yard pass during two minute drill Many Rams fans have criticized the pick and play of Tutu Atwell. But sometimes you can’t measure a player by the box score. Such is the case for Tutu Atwell. He opens up a lot of throwing lanes in the intermediate because of his deep threat ability. Against the Chargers, we finally got to see that big play ability as Atwell hauled in a 40 yard pass from Stafford. It was the longest play of the game up to that point and it kickstarted the Rams offense that had struggled in its first four drives. Matthew Stafford launches it to Tutu Atwell 🚀 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ccnqqgtjya — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 2. Chargers hail mary comes up 1/2 yard short before halftime The Rams were able to get into the endzone with just :19 left in the 2nd quarter. But Joshua Karty’s botched knuckleball kickoff gave the Chargers the ball at their own 40 yard line. After one play and a second down spike to stop the clock, Herbert dialed up a hail mary attempt. Ladd McConkey actually hauled in the deep ball from Herbert after a deflection but he didn’t secure possession until he was a 1/2 yard outside of the goal line. The Rams caught a huge break and the play could have swung momentum in the Bolts favor had it been a touchdown. Instead it was Rams 10-9 going into halftime. The chargers offense is so bad they completed the Hail Mary and still couldn’t score pic.twitter.com/qqlsIxsKWt — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) November 1, 2026 3. Blake Corum caps off scoring drive with rushing touchdown Coming out of halftime, Sean McVay finally committed to the running game that worked in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Blake Corum showed off his twitchiness on a few runs including this one… Blake Corum so shifty 😮‍💨 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3Om4ewYd55 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 He then made this nice cutback on 1st & 10 at the Chargers 23 yard line to give the Rams an 8 point lead in the early 3rd quarter. Blake Corum gets it in from 23 yards out for the Rams! Corum continues to see a bulk of the RB workload and is making good on it. pic.twitter.com/MHLBfVswvw — The Goal Line Grind (@theGLgrind) November 1, 2026 4. Trent McDuffie picks off Justin Herbert in 3rd Quarter Anytime you can create turnovers, you are giving the offense more opportunities. Trent McDuffie’s late third quarter interception gave Stafford and Co. the ball back to add onto their lead. The McDuffie interception set up an 18 yard Puka Nacua touchdown. Scoring points off turnovers makes those turnover plays even more significant. Trent McDuffie gets the pick on Justin Herbert 🙌 pic.twitter.com/XTBoW00crN — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 1, 2026 5. Chargers can’t convert on 4th down (after replay assist) Up by two possessions, the Chargers put together a long drive midway in the 4th quarter. On 4th & 8, the Chargers had no choice but to go for it with only 6:42 remaining. Josh Wallace was able to bring down Orande Gadsden just shy of the first down marker. The initial call on the field was a first down but for the first time all year, the Rams got replay assist to help them!!! View Link

title: Rams vs. Chargers final score: Trent McDuffie powers defensive win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams (4-4) beat the Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) by a final score of 24-9 in Week 8 of the NFL season, as Trent McDuffie got his second pick of the season and led a defensive win over L.A. at SoFi Stadium. The Chargers kept this one close for a time as the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams (4-4) beat the Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) by a final score of 24-9 in Week 8 of the NFL season, as Trent McDuffie got his second pick of the season and led a defensive win over L.A. at SoFi Stadium. The Chargers kept this one close for a time as the Rams only led 10-9 at the end of the second quarter, but the other L.A. team showed they are winless for a reason. The second half was mostly dominated by the Rams in this not so marquee battle for L.A. The Rams weren’t wholly dominant as their offense struggled for about half the game, the special teams struggled on kickoffs as Joshua Karty earned a couple penalties for failing to kick the ball in the landing zone. Yet, the Rams overcame any errors for a clean win to move to a 4-4 record, and stay afloat in the crowded NFC playoff picture. The Rams offense failed to convert a first down on their first five offensive drives. L.A.’s offense beginning games sluggishly is a real trend as Sean McVay hasn’t seen his team score a touchdown to open a contest all season. The Rams relied on their defense, and the defense answered the call as the group was as stout as they’ve been all year by forcing two turnovers (Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie each had an interception), and the defense held the Chargers to only field goals. McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were hurt in this game, the severity is not known, but players like Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace stepped up as Chris Shula’s unit bought time as McVay tried to figure out the right rhythm for Matthew Stafford and the offense. Rams Injury Update: CB Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable. — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 1, 2026 Rams Injury Update: CB Jaylen Watson (shoulder) downgraded to out. — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 1, 2026 By the end of the second quarter, the Rams were starting to find their groove on the ground as Kyren Williams found the endzone right before the half came to a close. In the third quarter, the Rams were able to lean on Blake Corum who added another rushing score on the ground for the Rams. KYREN HURDLES IN FOR SIX! 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/8RxkBhjeTo — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 1, 2026 BLAKE TO THE HOUSE! 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/i4ykHPNjZo — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 1, 2026 Williams and Corum combined for over 100 yards on the day as for the second week in a row, L.A.’s ground game worked as both backs scored to help take pressure off of Stafford who threw an early interception, and has struggled in 2026 by comparison to his MVP season in 2025. Stafford ended the day with just over 150 passing yards, one passing TD to Puka Nacua, and an interception. He’s still the QB1 for L.A. and in L.A., but you have to wonder if the Rams make jump to Ty Simpson in 2027. But that’s a problem for 2027. In 2026, the Rams won in Week 8 over the Chargers, and that’s the most important thing. At the same time, if the Rams don’t improve, they may not be able to matchup with the best teams in the NFL. The 4-4 record matches what the team is, inconsistent. A win is still a win though, and the Rams will take this one. WHOSE HOUSE!?!? pic.twitter.com/4tcnxpmsVU — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 1, 2026

title: Chargers a trap game for Rams?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are 3-4 and climbing back into the NFC playoff picture after a slow start to the season. They are expected to finish with wins in each of the next three weeks against teams with losing records. A 6-4 record puts them back in the contention conversation, especially as Myles Garrett, Terrance […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are 3-4 and climbing back into the NFC playoff picture after a slow start to the season. They are expected to finish with wins in each of the next three weeks against teams with losing records. A 6-4 record puts them back in the contention conversation, especially as Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson, and Kobie Turner could all return around Thanksgiving. Meanwhile the Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and looking for their first win of the season. The Rams cannot let the “Battle for LA” become a trap game. Justin Herbert and the Chargers will likely pull out all the stops in order to finish in the win column for the first time all year. One added complexity? The Chargers are coming off their bye week. According to Sports Illustrated—across the NFL from 2019 to 2025— teams posted a 102-91-1 record immediately following their bye . That’s good for a .528 winning percentage, when in theory that should be a perfect .500 record in a large sample size. The Chargers need all the help they can get, so they will welcome the bye week boost. Jim Harbaugh’s tenure in Los Angeles is on thin ice. He has yet to win a playoff game in two entries. After hiring former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel as the offensive coordinator, the bottom has fallen out of the offense. Last year’s defensive coordinator, Jesse Minter, was maximizing the Chargers’ defensive talent. They are now equal or performing below the sum of their parts. But a bye week can be handy in correcting coaching and scheme, and this was a chance for the Chargers to look themselves in the mirror and course correct. This is a team that has more talent than their 0-6 record. It’s only a matter of time before they catch an opponent by surprise. The Rams cannot allow that to happen. Sean McVay’s team must finish the season 7-3 or better in order to have a realistic chance at a wildcard berth that isn’t left up to tie breaker chance. Using one of their three lives on a winless team would be a difficult pill to swallow, although that is what happened just a couple weeks ago when the Rams dropped a game to the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals. The jury is still out as to how good the Rams are this year, despite sky-high expectations and a super star roster. One thing is certain: they currently have no margin for error. They must keep as much gas left in the tank as possible ahead of a late-season gauntlet against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, and Seattle Seahawks (twice). The Rams must take care of business over the next three weeks to give their path from narrowing before their pre-playoff playoff stretch begins. It all starts with the Chargers. The Rams cannot fall victim to another trap game a couple weeks after being surprised by Arizona.

full_text: Jauan Jennings spent five years with the San Francisco 49ers and apparently he had enough of Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch. The 49ers had agreed to a trade with the Minnesota Vikings to reunite with Jennings, according to Jay Glazer, but they wanted Jennings to FaceTime with Shanahan and Lynch first. Jennings said something along the lines of “no thanks” and opted to stay with the Vikings, per Glazer. That’s a rejection unlike any rumor we’ve ever heard before. Glazer: 49ers had trade worked out for Jauan Jennings contingent on a FaceTime with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch but Jennings said he wanted to stay in Minnesota. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 1, 2026 Despite Jennings only having four catches for 43 yards with the Vikings this season — and the team agreeing to trade him — the receiver rejected the 6-1 49ers. It’s a bold statement from someone who had almost 1,000 receiving yards with Shanahan in 2024 and caught nine touchdowns for the 49ers in 2025. Jennings hasn’t had anything near that success with Kevin O’Connell’s team this season, but apparently likes it more in Minnesota than in San Francisco. The Los Angeles Rams haven’t tried to trade for Jennings — that we know of — but maybe this would be the perfect opportunity for them to try. If for no other reason than trolling the 49ers.

Chiefs vs. Broncos Score: 28-24 Chiefs win KC Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 30/41 (73.2%), 321 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs RB Emmett Johnson: 1 carry, 15 yards, 5 catches, 128 receiving yards, 1 receiving TD WR Rashee Rice: 7 catches, 53 yards, 1 TD EDGE George Karlaftis: 2 tackles, 1 sack, 3 PDs LB Nick Bolton: 9 tackles, 1 QB hit DEN Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 20/32 (62.5%), 222 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs RB Jonah Coleman: 11 carries, 41 yards, 1 TD, 4 catches, 63 receiving yards WR Jaylen Waddle: 3 catches, 39 yards, 1 TD LB Alex Singleton: 14 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PD DT Malcolm Roach: 4 tackles, 1 sack After the Chiefs cruised to a 31-10 victory over the Broncos in the season opener, Denver managed to even the season series with a huge fourth-quarter comeback. Down 11 points heading into the final frame, the Broncos scored 15 unanswered points to pull off the win. It took a missed field goal by Harrison Butker and a goal line stand to finish the job, but Denver made it happen to take control of the division heading into the second half of the season. For the second week in a row, Kansas City’s opponent managed to keep Walker in check. The running back was held below 70 rushing yards for the second time this season and didn’t eclipse triple digits for just the third time. Instead, the focus was on each team’s rookie back, with Johnson serving as the Chiefs’ leading receiver and Coleman amassing more than 100 yards from scrimmage. KC Next week: vs. Jets DEN Next week: @ Panthers Chargers vs. Rams Score: 24-9 Chargers lose LAC Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 24/32 (75.0%), 257 yards, 0 TDs, 2 INTs RB Kimani Vidal: 8 carries, 23 yards, 2 catches, 7 receiving yards WR Ladd McConkey: 4 catches, 86 yards CB Tarheeb Still: 3 tackles, 1 INT EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu: 4 tackles, 1 sack What’s there to say about the Chargers at this point? They’re litterally the worst team in the league, sitting as the only winless club through eight weeks. The offense is attrocious, failing to score a touchdown while Herbert looks like a shell of himself. One might think that would lead to a change at offensive coordinator, but it seems like head coach Jim Hargbaugh is content rolling with Mike McDaniel moving forward. Laube was the first NFL player this season to return a kick for a score.” Ashton Jeanty on reduced workload: “We won. It doesn’t matter how I feel about how much times I get the ball. Whatever it takes for the team to win, I just want to win. That’s all,” via The Athletic’s Sam Warren , who also noted that Jeanty was aware heading into the game that he’d be getting fewer carries. Klint Kubiak post win: “We have to keep stacking wins,” the coach said in the locker room (h/t Raiders’ X/Twitter account ). “I’m happy, I’m fired up, I’m proud of you, I’m proud to be your coach. full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders managed to end their four-game losing streak in Week 8 against the New York Jets , evening out their record at 4-4 and keeping their slim postseason hopes alive. Additionally, the Raiders got some help on Sunday, as we take a look at the AFC Playoff picture below. AFC playoff standings 1. Buffalo Bills 6-1 2. Denver Broncos 6-2 (3-1 in AFC for tiebreaker over PIT) 3. Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 (3-2 in AFC) 4. Jacksonville Jaguars 5-2 5. Kansas City Chiefs 5-2 (5-1 in AFC) 6. Cincinnati Bengals 5-2 (4-2 in AFC) 7. New England Patriots 5-3 (5-1 in AFC for tiebreaker over CLE) 8. Cleveland Browns 5-3 (3-3 in AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders 4-4 (3-3 in AFC for tiebreaker over BAL) 10. Baltimore Ravens 4-4 (2-3 in AFC) 11. Houston Texans 2-5 12. New York Jets 2-6 (2-3 in AFC for tiebreaker over IND) 13. Indianapolis Colts 2-6 (1-5 in AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins 1-6 15. Tennessee Titans 1-7 16. Los Angeles Chargers 0-7 The Raiders got help from the Bills, who took down the Ravens 36-10. But the bigger storyline is that Baltimore could be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season after Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will place him on injured reserve and require surgery. The Ravens also had backup quarterback Tyler Huntley go down in the game, leaving them with a lot of question marks at the most important position on the field. That could remove one more team from being “in the hunt”, but Las Vegas still has some work to do. The Titans almost did the Silver and Black a favor, narrowly losing to the Cincinnati Bengals. But the Bengals managed to avoid the upset and climb up to the second AFC Wild Card spot, putting another AFC North team in the seventh seed competition: The Browns. However, the Patriots’ win over the Dolphins gives New England the nod right now, which means Vegas is 1.5 games out of the playoffs since the Pats have the head-to-head tiebreaker. Las Vegas heads to Cleveland at the end of the month, but first has a matchup in San Francisco next Sunday. Meanwhile, the Browns will be in New Orleans, the Patriots host the Packers, and the Ravens take on the Jaguars this Thursday.

title: Raiders-Jets: 17 things we learned
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders showed they are better than the league’s worst teams Sunday as they ended a nasty four-game losing streak. In a game that was similar to Week 3 at New Orleans (Las Vegas’ last victory), the Raiders outplayed the Jets in the second half, outscoring them 24-10 to win a 38-33 game […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders showed they are better than the league’s worst teams Sunday as they ended a nasty four-game losing streak . In a game that was similar to Week 3 at New Orleans (Las Vegas’ last victory), the Raiders outplayed the Jets in the second half, outscoring them 24-10 to win a 38-33 game Sunday to even their record at 4-4. The Jets fell to 2-6. Going into this week, the three teams the Raiders beat to open the season had a combined 3-16 on the season. So, this win tracks. The key is for Las Vegas to start beating some good teams. If they want to stay in the Raiders must win a couple of the next three games, against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. They all have winning records. Sunday’s win at New York was crucial and the Raiders deserve credit for turning it around after a 23-14 halftime deficit. But if they fall to 4-5 next week wit a loss to the 49ers, they will have some decisions to make at the November 10 trade deadline. Here are some key aspects to Sunday’s victory: Jeanty plays backup role: Raiders second-year running back Ashton Jeanty didn’t get his first carry until the second quarter. He had just two catches for nine yards. He did contribute with 64 receiving yards on three catches, including a crucial 45-yard screen pass. Rookie fourth round pick Mike Washington led the way with 23 carries for 83 yards, including a 15-yarder. In the end, the Raiders’ ground game was still lacking. Coach Klint Kubiak said Jeanty will still be a big part of the offense. He said Jeanty’s disparaging words about some of the Jets’ defenders last week didn’t play a roe in his lack of carries. It will be something to monitor next week. Second half seals it: The Raiders trailed 23-14 at halftime after being outplayed by the Jets, But the Raiders scored on three straight drives to overtake the Jets. It was a big response. Kirk Cousins strong again: There has been a lot of noise about the Raiders potentially starting No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza soon. Kirk Cousins did his best to quiet that talk. He was 19 of 26 and threw three touchdown passes for the fourth time this season, which is tied for the league lead. The Raiders were 4-for-4 in the red zone after going 3-for-10 in the past two games. That was a key. Also, the Raiders were 7 of 11 on third down after going 3 for 14 last week. Defense in a mess: The Jets scored on their first six dries and the Raiders have allowed 30 or more points in five straight games. That is the longest streak in the NFL since 2020. The Raiders allowed 27 points to the Saints the week prior to the streak beginning. On a positive note, the Jets and Geno Smith, who shredded his former team, were just two of six in the red zone, which was a difference maker. Las Vegas’ opponents had been eight of 10 in the red zone the past two games. Nailor not tucker makes some plays : Starting wide receiver Jalen Nailor had a relatively solid game with four catches and a touchdown. Tre Tucker, who had been on fire the past two games, didn’t have a catch. According to Next Gen Stats, Brock Bowers had six catches for 87 yards as a receiver and one catch for five yards as a tight end. Laube strikes: Raiders’ kick returner Dylan Laube has been flirting with breaking a kick return all season as he led the NFL in kick return average going into Week 8. Sunday, in the second quarter, the third-year backup running back returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown It was the Raiders’ first kick return for a score since Jacoby Ford did it 15 years ago. Laube was the first NFL player this season to return a kick for a score. It was crucial to this one-score victory. Raiders buck trend: The Raiders score don their opening drive of the second quarter for the first time this season as Kirk Cousins hit Brock Bowers for a short score to cut the Jets’ lead to 23-21. They then scored on their second drive of the third quarter. Jets’ actually have success in last two minutes of first half: Since Aaron Glenn took over as coach last year, the Jets were outscored 106-7 in the final two minutes of the first half. It was, by far, the worst percentage in NFL history. the Jets broke that spell Sunday as they outscored Las Vegas 3-0 in that time span. Tush-push problems continue: The Raiders failed to convert a Connor Heyward tush-push in the second quarter on fourth down at Jets’ 46. It has been a season-long problem. They’ve had better success with having Cousins sneaking the ball. McCoy plays: After not playing on defense for most of the season, fourth-round pick Jermod McCoy replaced Darien Porter at an outside cornerback spot when the starter was injured on the first play from scrimmage. So, at least for now, McCoy has replaced brief starter Zeke Masses, a fifth-round pick, as the primary backup to Porter. McCoy was picked on often Sunday and Masses replaced him for a bitin the second quarter, but McCoy did return in the third quarter. Zuhn starts: Rookie, third-round pick Trey Zuhn made his starting debut, at right guard. Previously, the Texas A&M product played on offense sparingly in Jumbo packages. Kubiak hinted last week a young player would get a chance on the offensive line. He replaced Caleb Rogers, who replaced Jackson Powers-Johnson two weeks ago. Now, Zuhn, is the latest high draft pick on the offensive line to get a chance. Injury advantage again: As has been the case in nearly every game this season, the Raiders entered as the more healthy squad. Every starter was healthy for Las Vegas, while the Jets were missing running back Breece Hall, run-stuffing defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat and standout rookie defensive end David Bailey. Two young wide receivers sit: 2025 Fourth-round draft pick Dont’e Thornton was in inactive in his first game on the on the 53-man roster. He had been on the injured reserve. Rookie sixth-round pick Malik Benson was a healthy scratch for the first tine. Jack Bech is back from the injured reserve and the team, at least for this week, value Cody White and Dareke Young more than Thornton and Benson. They were both training camp heroes as rookies, but neither has done much in the regular season. Slone was active: Undrafted rookie Cian Slone was active for the first time. He has been elevated from the practice squad the past three weeks, but was not active the past two games. Slone can’t not be elevated for a game anymore this season. He must be part of the 53-man roster if he plays again. Back to deferring: The Raiders won the coin flip and they deferred to the second half, allowing the Jets to get the ball to start the game. Last week, in a loss to the Rams, the Raiders di the opposite and it didn’t work well. DT rotation: It seemed like 2025 sixth-round pick J.J. Pegues would have a game-day role after Jonah Laulu was waived last week. But Pegues was inactive Sunday after being active the past two games. Tim Keenan was elevated from the practice squad for the second straight week and he was active. He had a sack in the third quarter. If JPJ a center again? Powers-Johnson was warming up behind Tyler Linderbaum at center in pre-game warmups. It maty be an indication he is back to being a center with him losing his starting guard spot. But, with this line, it seems like everything is fluid.

Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter The Raiders won the coin toss and deferred to the second half, giving the Jets the ball first. The Jets had three big plays early including a 31-yard pass play from Geno Smith to Garrett Wilson on the first play from scrimmage. The Jets stalled in the red zone and settled for a field goal with 12:50 remaining to take a 3-0 lead. Rookie safety Treydan Stukes made a big play on third down to force the field goal. Jalen Nailor, who had a quiet start to the season, had two big catches on the first drive. Rookie running back Mike Washington got the first six carries over starter Ashton Jeanty. Another great catch by Brock Bowers, touchdown Raiders. They lead 7-3 with 7:23 to go. The Jets cruised down the field, but stalled in the red zone again, settling for another field goal to make to a 7-6 game. Second quarter: . The Raiders had to punt. The Jets went down the field and scored after picking on the Raiders cornerbacks. However, Dylan Laube responded big time with a kick return for a score to give the Raiders a 14-13 lead with 10;44 to go. The Jets responded as Smith picked apart his former team. Jets uow up 20-14 with 6:18 to go in the quarter. Ashton Jeanty didn’t get his first carry until six minutes remained in the quarter. Jets settle for another field goal after a Maxx Crosby sack. They lead 23-14 with nine seconds to go. The Jets have scored on every drive. The Raiders get the ball to start the second half. Third quarter: The Raiders scored on their opening drive of the third quarter for the first time as Kirk Cousins hit Bowers for a short touchdown. Bowers had a previous big play and Mike Washington had two nice runs on the drive. The Jets lead 23-21 with 9:59 to go. The Jets responded by easily going down the field and scoring. They have scored on all six drives, the first time they accomplished that since 2008. They lead 30-21. The Raiders have allowed 30 points or more in the past five games. It’s the longest such streak in the NFL in six seasons. The Jets had not scored more than 25 points in a game this season before Sunday. The Raiders responded with some big plays from Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer. Cousins scored on a sneak to make it 30-28 with 4:14 to go. The Raiders’ defense finally gets a stop. Fourth quarter: Jeanty made his presence felt, finally, with a big catch and a run. Nailor had his third first-down conversion of the game and the Raiders score to take a 35-30 lead with under 12 minutes to go. The Raiders with the stop. They can try to put this away. Nope. They go three and our. New York has the ball on its own 19 with 9:09 to play. The Jets score a field goal after stalling in the red zone. The Raiders lead 35-33 with 4:31 to go. Las Vegas can close it out here. Matt Gay with a 53-yard field goal in the final seconds. Jeremy Chinn seals with with interception. Final score: Raiders 38, Jets 33 Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 4-5. The New York Jets are 2-6. What the win/loss means for the Raiders: The Raiders snapped a four-game losing streak and showed they can continue to beat bad teams. Turning point of the game: The Raiders outscored the Jets 24-1o in the second half. Injury report: Raiders’ cornerback Darien Porter was helped off the field on the first scrimmage play of the game with a groin injury. He did not return. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was injured in the first quarter. Hemingway returned in the second quarter. What’s next for the Raiders: The Raiders are playing at the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers, who are on their bye week, next Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT. Raiders Week 8: Meet the Jets

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 8 loss to the New England Patriots
summary: The Miami Dolphins entered Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots looking to build on their first victory of the 2026 season. For 30 minutes, it looked like Miami might actually be capable of putting together back-to-back wins. Then the second half happened. The Dolphins took a 13-3 lead into halftime before watching the Patriots […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots tackles Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter of a game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins entered Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots looking to build on their first victory of the 2026 season. For 30 minutes, it looked like Miami might actually be capable of putting together back-to-back wins. Then the second half happened. The Dolphins took a 13-3 lead into halftime before watching the Patriots score 21 unanswered points to take control of the game. Miami’s offense disappeared, its defense couldn’t find an answer for Drake Maye, and running back Ollie Gordon II provided an unfortunate reminder that the Dolphins still have some growing up to do. The Dolphins and head coach Jeff Hafley are now left wondering what could have been after another frustrating afternoon. Let’s take a look at the good, bad, and ugly from Miami’s 24-19 loss to the Patriots. GOOD Miami’s first half performance Miami entered halftime with a 13-3 lead over New England with strong performances on both sides of the football. The defense created an early turnover when Jacob Rodriguez forced an Efton Chism fumble with a thrilling peanut punch, and Miami’s offense took advantage of the opportunity with a field goal. Malik Willis and the offense eventually put together a touchdown drive late in the second quarter when Willis completed a one-yard touchdown pass to Malik Washington with eight seconds remaining in the half, giving Miami a 10-point advantage. It was the type of drive the Dolphins desperately needed. The touchdown gave Willis and the offense some much-needed momentum heading into the locker room. Unfortunately, the momentum quickly faded, as did the Miami Dolphins’ lead… BAD Miami’s second half performance For as good as the Dolphins played in the first half, the second half saw the team come crashing back down to earth. Miami was outscored 21-6 in the second half, allowing Drake Maye and the Patriots to walk (and throw) all over them en route to a crushing loss. Maye and the Patriots stormed out of the locker room looking like a completely different offense. The Patriots’ quarterback connected with Kyle Williams for a long 43-yard touchdown early in the third quarter, then led another scoring drive that ended with a two-yard touchdown run of his own. The biggest problem wasn’t that the Patriots scored 21 points during the final two quarters of play — it was how quickly Miami lost control of a game it had spent the first half controlling. Hafley and his coaching staff will need to go back to the drawing-board to figure out how to keep Miami from losing another double-digit halftime lead as the season progresses. UGLY Ollie Gordon II has ugly display on Miami’s sideline following penalty There is a difference between being frustrated and allowing that frustration to boil over into something that costs your team. Ollie Gordon II crossed that line on Sunday. Early in the third quarter, Gordon was called for a taunting penalty after a short run against the Patriots. The 15-yard penalty was crushing, and head coach Jeff Hafley responded by pulling Gordon to the sidelines and admonishing the young player for his mistake. Gordon did not take kindly to that decision. The running back was seen screaming at Hafley on the sideline, with Malik Willis also getting caught up in the confrontation. Nobody is going to criticize Gordon for being competitive. The young man plays hard and wants to win. Those are good things. But there is a time and a place for that kind of emotion. Gordon had just committed a penalty that hurt his team. Instead of accepting the consequences and moving on, he turned the situation into an ugly sideline spectacle. Gordon has been thrust into a significant role following De’Von Achane’s season-ending knee injury, and the Dolphins need him to be productive. But they also need him to be accountable for his actions. Gordon has shown plenty of promise this year — he has the talent to become an important piece of Miami’s offense, not just this season, but moving forward as well. Now he needs to show that he can handle the emotional side of the game too. ___ The Dolphins snatched defeat from the jaws of victory on Sunday against the Patriots. The loss drops the team’s record to 1-6 on the year. Do you think they can get back on the right side of the scoreboard with a victory against the visiting Detroit Lions next week? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up .

summary: The Miami Dolphins entered Week 8 with a 1-5 record after defeating the New York Jets on the road last week to earn their first victory of the season. Sunday’s game against the visiting Patriots was a much tougher battle — even without wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson. Of course, the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Gabe Jacas #50 of the New England Patriots sacks Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter of a game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins entered Week 8 with a 1-5 record after defeating the New York Jets on the road last week to earn their first victory of the season. Sunday’s game against the visiting Patriots was a much tougher battle — even without wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson. Of course, the Dolphins weren’t completely healthy either, as they were missing their starting left guard, rookie Kadyn Proctor. The Dolphins played the Patriots tough in the first half — taking a 13-3 lead into halftime despite the offensive line’s inability to keep quarterback Malik Willis upright. Miami’s gunslinger was corralled four times through the first two quarters of the game, but connected on a short touchdown pass to Malik Washington with eight seconds left in the second quarter. The Patriots would find success early on in the second-half, with Drake Maye throwing a deep bomb to Kyle Williams for a 43-yard touchdown to cut the Dolphins’ lead to three points early in the third quarter. A taunting penalty from Ollie Gordon II would put Miami’s offense in a third and long situation on the team’s next drive — a down and distance they would not convert. Momentum swung in New England’s favor from there — as Miami was outscored in the second half 21-6. Miami’s offense stalled time and time again, while the Patriots moved the ball at will — hitting on multiple backbreaking chunk plays. Ultimately, the test proved to be too much for Jeff Hafley’s squad and the Dolphins fell by a score of 24-19. Final Score Patriots – 24, Dolphins – 19 Immediate reactions Snap Winners and Losers Winners Jacob Rodriguez, linebacker – Dolphins’ rookie sensation at linebacker, Jacob Rodriguez, forced the first fumble of his NFL career — peanut punching the football from the grasp of tight end Efton Chism midway through the first quarter. The Dolphins would get three points as a result of Rodriguez’s signature play. Chop Robinson, EDGE – Miami’s best pass rusher looked the part on Sunday against the Patriots. Chop Robinson sacked Drake Maye two times on the afternoon — consistently wreaking havoc in New England’s backfield. After a slow start to the season, Robinson has turned it on as of late and the Dolphins are reaping the benefits. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred. Ollie Gordon II, running back – Ollie Gordon needs to get his emotions in check. After being called for a taunting penalty in the second half of Sunday’s game that proved quite consequential, Gordon was seen yelling at his head coach, position coach and quarterback on the sidelines. Jeff Hafley will need to hand down some punishment if he doesn’t want to lose the respect of his locker room. The refs – A critical fourth-down play looked to go in Miami’s favor late in the third-quarter, only for the refs to change the spot of the ball during the television time-out, giving the Patriots a first down instead of a turnover on downs. On replay, it still didn’t look like the Patriots receiver got the nose of the football over the line to gain… but New England was awarded a new set of downs anyway, allowing them the chance to put another touchdown on the board. Immediate thoughts The weather was a factor Rain in Miami? What a surprise! Prior to the start of Miami’s clash with New England, it rained three inches in soggy South Florida. The deluge would continue throughout the entire game. As a result, the contest was of the slower variety, with clock control a big factor in how the game was played. That worked to Miami’s favor in the first half. The Dolphins possessed the football more than the Patriots did and had multiple long drives that resulted in points. The second half was another story… The Patriots came out of halftime firing on all cylinders. Drake Maye had a passing touchdown and a rushing touchdown in the third quarter and Miami’s offense couldn’t answer, with multiple ineffective drives giving New England’s offense the opportunity to control the clock through the final two quarters. A missed 43-yard field goal by Zane Gonzalez with 6:41 left in the game certainly didn’t help things — especially considering the Dolphins did score a late touchdown on a Willis throw to rookie receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. — the pass catcher’s second as professional. It was a hard-fought game, but it was not enough The Patriots were the AFC’s representative in the Super Bowl last season. Despite Miami’s roster limitations due to the massive amount of dead cap the organization is dealing with this season, the Dolphins kept it close against New England for a majority of the contest. Unfortunately, close doesn’t cut it in the National Football League and the warm and fuzzy feelings Miami gave their fanbase with last week’s victory have evaporated quicker than the rain puddles will in the hot Florida sun.

title: Miami Dolphins offensive line review: Tracking the guards in Week 7
summary: Do my eyes deceive me, or did the Dolphins just win their first game of the Hafley/Sullivan era? Doing it against the Jets is an added bonus, but while wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent. That is especially true along the offensive line, […]
full_text: Do my eyes deceive me, or did the Dolphins just win their first game of the Hafley/Sullivan era? Doing it against the Jets is an added bonus, but while wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent. That is especially true along the offensive line, where rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor and second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea are important pieces of the team’s future. How are they performing this season? Each week, we take a closer look at the guards and what is being said about their most recent performance. Kadyn Proctor Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 1 71.2 79.0 63.4 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 2 62.0 72.4 39.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 57.5 51.1 71.3 10/4, @ Vikings 39 (100%) 0 51.2 48.6 64.9 10/11, vs. Bengals 66 (100%) 0 72.7 74.9 52.2 BYE 10/25, @ Jets 65 (100%) 0 59.6 58.2 61.3 Jonah Savaiinaea Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 0 47.6 50.9 38.2 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 0 65.9 68.5 46.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 56.6 58.4 47.5 10/4, @ Vikings 39 (100%) 0 49.5 44.6 77.5 10/11, vs. Bengals 18 (27%) 0 45.4 44.7 78.4 BYE 10/25, @ Jets 65 (100%) 0 49.4 53,5 31.4 What We Learned The last time we looked at the guards, we were concerned over Jonah Savaiinaea’s ankle injury. With the extra week of rest, he was fine to play – but now we’re worried about Kadyn Proctor. Proctor has been ruled out for Week 8 against the Patriots due to a concussion, which hurts the team’s efforts to secure their second consecutive win and interrupts Proctor’s development. So far this season, the offensive line has been one of Miami’s biggest strengths, paving the way for five consecutive 100-yard rushing performances, and individually Proctor has yet to surrender a sack through six games. Proctor will likely be replaced by Jarrett Kingston, who filled in admirably during Savaiinaea’s injury in Week 5. Looking at the two guards’ PFF grades for this week, you wouldn’t think the Dolphins as a team had played especially well. Neither player earned a PFF grade of 60, generally considered league average, despite the Dolphins scoring four offensive touchdowns and controlling the game on the ground when it mattered most. That disconnect speaks to the difference between evaluating individual assignments and evaluating the offense’s overall success. Grades notwithstanding, the eye test reinforces what we’ve seen so far this year: Proctor is already an offensive force to be reckoned with. Physically, the athletic ability, power, and movement skills are already NFL-caliber: Locked On Dolphins’ Kyle Crabbs called Proctor’s performance against the Jets “ his best graded game of the season by a fairly comfortable margin.” There’s still room for growth, but the biggest opportunities are mental: recognizing defensive looks more quickly and becoming more consistent with his assignments. For Savaiinaea, it seems like he is still making progress and is light years ahead of where he was a year ago, but Proctor’s development appears to be further along at this stage (something the PFF grades would attest). He’s more consistently doing the things you want to see – washing defenders down the line, keeping his feet moving, not getting distracted by unexpected movements by the defense. He still played hesitantly at times against the Jets, which feels normal in the course of offensive line development. What is very clear on tape is that both Proctor and Savaiinaea were instrumental in Miami’s success on the ground. Time and again, they displaced Jets defenders and created cutback lanes for Ollie Gordon. More importantly, when the Dolphins needed to salt away the game in the fourth quarter, the coaching staff trusted the offensive line to win at the point of attack. That may be the most encouraging sign of all. The tracker will be updated each week throughout the season. For a more in-depth breakdown of Proctor’s and Savaiinaea’s performance, check out offensive line Coach Eric Smith’s film analysis of the game, which you can find on his YouTube channel, Focused on Fins .

title: Dolphins fan confidence rockets to near all-time high in Week 8; Patriots game looming
summary: The Miami Dolphins, 1-5, beat the New York Jets in Week 7, putting together a complete performance in every aspect and looking like a team that can compete on any Sunday. The team is still in the midst of a complete roster rebuild, and it will continue to make the mistakes expected of the league’s […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 25: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins scores on a 1 yard run during the first half of the National Football League game between the Miami Dolphins and the New York Jets on October 25, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. (Photo by Joshua Sarner/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins, 1-5, beat the New York Jets in Week 7, putting together a complete performance in every aspect and looking like a team that can compete on any Sunday. The team is still in the midst of a complete roster rebuild, and it will continue to make the mistakes expected of the league’s youngest team, but its potential was on full display last weekend. This weekend, the Dolphins face their second straight AFC East rival, this time hosting the New England Patriots. Miami hopes to back up its Week 7 win as it heads into Week 8, while the Patriots hope to avoid back-to-back losses for the first time this year. New England, 4-3, fell to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night to start Week 7, giving them 10 days to sit with the loss. The Patriots are hoping to stay within reach of the division-leading Buffalo Bills, who are 5-1 to start this year. According to FanDuel Sportsbook odds , the Dolphins are seven-point underdogs as the Patriots come into Hard Rock Stadium. Dolphins fan confidence Each week of the season, we use our SB Nation Reacts survey to gauge fans’ confidence in the Dolphins’ direction. Despite the team starting the season with five straight losses, Dolphins fans recognized the situation this season and accepted that Miami is a rebuilding team. The fan confidence survey has averaged around 75 percent positive responses throughout the year, hitting a low of 63 percent in Week 2 and a high of 87 percent in Week 5. Fan confidence in the team after their Week 7 win did not just rise; it leaped to a near all-time high. In Weeks 4 and 11 of the 2022 season, 99 percent of fan responses indicated they felt positive about the Dolphins’ direction. After Miami’s win last weekend, the 2026 fan confidence survey jumped from 72 percent in Week 7 to a new season-high of 97 percent in Week 8. What will happen on the field this week at Hard Rock Stadium? Will fan confidence in the Dolphins’ direction keep rising? Miami Dolphins 2026 Season Fan Confidence Results: Preseason – 80% Week 1 – 79% Week 2 – 63% Week 3 – 65% Week 4 – 79% Week 5 – 87% Week 6 – 71% Week 7 – 72% Week 8 – 97% Dolphins fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Dolphins polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Phinsider readers. Then discuss the results with other diehard Fins fans. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Win total Now that the Dolphins have their first win of the season, the next logical question is how many games they can win this year. We used the SB Nation Reacts survey to ask fans for their thoughts on Miami’s win total for the year. The preseason win total for Miami had been 4.5 games. Fans still think the Dolphins will land on the under side of that line, but they do think the Dolphins will come away with a few more wins over the remaining 11 weeks of the season. Asked whether the Dolphins will finish the season with 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5+ wins, three victories received the most votes, with 39 percent of responses. Four wins received 28 percent, and 5 or more wins picked up 21 percent of the vote. Together, 88 percent of fans expect at least two more victories. Two wins received 8 percent of the vote, while remaining at one victory this season received 4 percent ofresponses. Do you agree with the Dolphins’ fan confidence poll results? Let us know in the comments.

title: This Can’t Continue (But It Probably Will)
summary: On Sunday afternoon at Ford Field, the Minnesota Vikings finally ran into a situation where their defense couldn’t overcome what is becoming one of the worst offenses in recent team history. The Vikings’ offense had ten possessions on Sunday afternoon in Detroit (excluding their kneel down at the end of the first half). Only two […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings is sacked by Alim McNeill #54 of the Detroit Lions during the third quarter at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday afternoon at Ford Field, the Minnesota Vikings finally ran into a situation where their defense couldn’t overcome what is becoming one of the worst offenses in recent team history. The Vikings’ offense had ten possessions on Sunday afternoon in Detroit (excluding their kneel down at the end of the first half). Only two of those possessions lasted longer than three minutes. The Lions had a more than eleven-minute advantage in time of possession (35:43 to 24:17). Usually, those sorts of numbers are a recipe for a beatdown. That the margin of victory wound up being four points, and that the Vikings had a lead with five minutes left to go in the game, is a testament to the effort the defense was able to put up before they finally just got worn down. But this offense, quite simply, is just not a serious NFL offense right now. And, unfortunately, the path to any sort of a simple fix for this season just doesn’t appear to be there. There were those of us who spent this offseason screaming into the void that Kyler Murray was not a fit for what the Vikings have wanted to do offensively in the Kevin O’Connell era. Think, for a second, about the two quarterbacks who have really been successful in this offense since O’Connell became the head coach: Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold. What did those guys do well? Lined up under center, excelled in the play-action game, turned their back to the defense, didn’t run around a lot, manipulated the pocket and fired passes down the field. Or, to put it another way. . .roughly the exact opposite of everything Kyler Murray has done throughout his NFL career prior to now. Per a September article from Garrett Burroughs over at Vikings Wire , during his time in Arizona, Murray was lined up in the shotgun on approximately 85% of the Cardinals’ snaps, per numbers taken from Next Gen Stats. Since O’Connell became the Vikings’ head coach in 2022, only two teams in the NFL had a lower percentage of snaps out of the shotgun than the Vikings’ 53%. The style of offense that O’Connell has wanted to run since he became the Vikings’ head coach is not compatible with Murray’s skill set, and whatever adjustments needed to be made apparently have not been. But, here we are, continuing to attempt to jam the square peg into the round hole with entirely predictable results. And, respectfully, miss me with any sort of “Well, he had to split reps in training camp” excuse. Kyler Murray is approaching 100 career NFL starts. If he looks like this because he had to cede a few training camp reps. . .well, then there are a few other questions that need to be answered. So, what’s the fix? Honestly, I’m not sure if there is one. There probably isn’t a feasible trade scenario. Any quarterback that you’re going to trade for at this point is probably going to require you to pay through the nose and will require an adjustment period of some sort. There is one notable exception, and man, if you think people have thoughts about the quarterback situation now, just wait until the potential premiere of Kirko 2: Kirk Harder . Yes, Kirk Cousins could step into this offense immediately and be an upgrade. . .and, yes, I can’t believe that’s a sentence I’m typing in this, the year of our Lord 2026. But that comes with a hitch as well, that being that the Las Vegas Raiders have had the audacity to go out and actually be a competitive football team this season, largely due to Cousins’ play. Did you know that Kirk Cousins is currently second in the NFL in touchdown passes? He’s thrown more than Josh Allen, more than Patrick Mahomes, more than Matthew Stafford, and more than anyone else not named Joe Burrow. And outside of Brock Bowers, I can’t name three guys he’s throwing the ball to without going to ESPN or Pro Football Reference or something. So while a Cousins trade would help the Vikings. . .do the Raiders even want to move him? (Would it be wrong to point out that the Vikings could have signed Cousins this offseason? That would be wrong of me, wouldn’t it? Okay, then, I won’t do it.) For better or worse, the Vikings may be locked into their current quarterback depth chart for the rest of this season. Maybe I’ll be wrong on that, but I don’t see anything else that does anything for them this season at the quarterback spot. The Vikings have had other trade rumors around them as well, notably for Colts’ running back Jonathan Taylor. Our friends at Stampede Blue have said that the asking price for Taylor is a first-round pick and a defensive tackle, which is a price that the Vikings should absolutely not be entertaining, in my opinion. Jonathan Taylor doesn’t fix this offense if there’s no passing game, and in its current state, the Vikings need to be careful about expending too much draft capital. Why? Well, because this team has zero quarterbacks on the roster under contract beyond this season. Murray is here on a one-year deal and, as we know, hasn’t been making what you’d call a super compelling case for being the long-term guy anyway. Carson Wentz is on a one-year deal and also isn’t the long-term answer. And if you’ve looked at the 2027 free agent pool at the quarterback position, it’s a bit of a wasteland. Even in the aftermath of the J.J. McCarthy situation. . .and don’t get me started on that again. . .this team is probably going to have to take another swing at a quarterback in the draft sooner rather than later, and given that they already have six wins, if they want to make any sort of move for a top quarterback in 2027, they’re going to need picks to do that. I can understand Kevin O’Connell coming to the podium after games each week and telling us that the offense is close and that the breakthrough is coming any time now. I get it, honestly. But, you know. . .we’re halfway through the 2026 season. At this point, you sort of are what you are. And, at this point, the Minnesota Vikings are a bottom-five NFL offense by pretty much any objective measure, and I’m not sure that there’s a fix that’s going to change that for the second half of this season. But, as always, I’m more than open to Nolan Teasley and company proving me wrong.

title: Vikings Week 8 Stock Market Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings lost for the first time in their last twelve contests, falling 19-15 on the road against the Detroit Lions. It was a game that will bring more scrutiny and criticism of the Vikings offense, as the Vikings were unable to drive the field much on several occasions, or possess the ball very […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Kevin O'Connell head coach of the Minnesota Vikings greets Shane Steichen head coach of the Indianapolis Colts after the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Colts 16-10. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings lost for the first time in their last twelve contests, falling 19-15 on the road against the Detroit Lions. It was a game that will bring more scrutiny and criticism of the Vikings offense, as the Vikings were unable to drive the field much on several occasions, or possess the ball very long. That led to the Lions wearing the Vikings defense down and going with a heavy dose of heavy-formation running between the tackles to take and keep the lead in the fourth quarter. The Vikings elected to punt the ball on what turned out to be their last possession, facing a 4th and 5 situation on their own side of the field. It was a questionable decision that revealed O’Connell’s lack of confidence in his offense given that the Lions had been wearing down the Vikings defense and the Lions were also down five players on defense. As it was, the Vikings suffered a rare loss when tying the turnover battle. The Vikings have won 90% of the time when tying or winning the turnover battle. But credit also the Lions for having a good game plan on both sides of the ball- which the Vikings weren’t able to counter effectively. Stock Up Nobody . Stock Down Kyler Murray. It wasn’t any one thing with Murray, but it was at times holding the ball too long and taking a sack- putting the offense further behind schedule, and at times being off with his accuracy. But perhaps more than that, he seems to be playing with too much of a conservative mindset, looking more to not make a mistake versus making a play. This is the second game in a row that his adjusted completion percentage has been under 70%, meaning he had about 9 inaccurate passes in the game. There still is no rhythm in the Vikings passing game as Murray remains inconsistent. And this has been with fairly good pass protection and playing against defenses ranking near the bottom of the league. The Lions had a good game plan, however. They double-covered Justin Jefferson the whole game, and doubled T.J. Hockenson in some key situations as well. They played mostly man coverage as they like to do, but they were betting that the Murray-to-Addison (or Jennings) connection wasn’t going to beat them. And there was a reason for that. So far this season, Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson have been elite against man coverage- both grading over 90 according to PFF. But Jordan Addison has not. He has graded just 58.6 with only 4 receptions on 11 targets for 34 yards this season prior to the Lions game. Hence they doubled Jefferson and (at times) Hockenson. The Lions also doubtlessly benefited from having Murray’s former offensive coordinator, Drew Petzing, on their staff as he would have insight into Murray’s strengths and weaknesses that they could work into their game plan. It wasn’t an off-the-charts bad performance by Murray, who finished 17/29 for 210 yards, 2 TDs and 1 INT and an 89.7 passer rating, but more of a continuation of the same issues that have been hindering the offensive all season. Kevin O’Connell. Part of the problem with Kyler Murray comes from KOC, who has pivoted too much toward a conservative mindset. Maybe that’s justified from what he’s seeing in practice, but he doesn’t really seem to be gearing up the offense to play a bigger role when even he has said more from the offense will be needed against the Lions and other matchups coming this month. He talked about the offense “being close” last week, but it got farther away in Detroit. At this point in the season, and especially with a bye-week to assess things as well, the offense should be further along than where it is and be able to respond better to game developments. But instead the scheme seems stale with few answers and there still is little hint of rhythm and timing or consistency- and they are getting to the halfway point of the season. There needs to be more urgency. Perhaps the winning streak has led KOC to take a more relaxed approach to getting the offense from liability to asset, but shame on him for not being more proactive. In that sense maybe the loss to the Lions and the end of the win streak is just the kick O’Connell needs to get the offense on track. Something needs to change, and that has to start with O’Connell. I think he’s seen now that if the offense doesn’t get it together, the defense isn’t infallible against better offenses and a heavy-formation run game to counter Brian Flores’ pressure packages and wear them down. O’Connell got outcoached against the Lions as well. They had a better game plan against his offense that he wasn’t able to counter effectively- and I’m not sure there was much of an attempt to do so. The Vikings offense’s inability to possess the ball and score points- 8 of their 11 drives were 5 plays or less- particularly in the second half, led to the Lions shifting to a heavy-formation run game to take the lead and secure it in the fourth quarter. It was something the Lions hadn’t really shown much on tape. O’Connell wasn’t able to take advantage of Detroit’s injury-depleted defense in the second half either, and with three minutes left in the game, facing 4th and 5 at their own 33-yard line, down 4 points, O’Connell didn’t have confidence in his offense to convert against a Lions defense playing backups at half their positions. It was a telling decision. Buy The Vikings loss- and end of their winning streak- adding urgency to improving the offense. Sell The Vikings loss to the Lions effectively ending their season. summary: Sunday afternoon’s game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions at Ford Field had a very scary moment in the fourth quarter involving one of the Lions’ star defensive players. Early in the fourth quarter, Lions linebacker Jack Campbell made what looked, at first glance, to be a fairly routine tackle on Vikings tight […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 11: Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions stands on the sidelines prior to a game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday afternoon’s game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions at Ford Field had a very scary moment in the fourth quarter involving one of the Lions’ star defensive players. Early in the fourth quarter, Lions linebacker Jack Campbell made what looked, at first glance, to be a fairly routine tackle on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson on a third-down catch. Upon making contact with Hockenson, however, Campbell immediately went limp on the field and did not move, with players on both teams immediately taking a knee on the field after the play was over. Play was stopped for an extended period of time as medical personnel looked Campbell over. He was placed on a backboard and carted off the field, then taken to a local medical facility. The Lions have released a statement on Campbell’s medical condition. Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them. — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 2, 2026 The statement, in full, reads: Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them. I don’t want to read too much into the statement, so I won’t. Here’s hoping that Jack Campbell ends up being okay. Obviously, you hate to see something like this happen to anyone, and I’m sure that the medical professionals who are watching over him are doing everything they can for him. Hopefully there will be some positive news to pass along about his condition sooner rather than later.

title: Lions Run to Victory as Vikings’ Undefeated Streak Ends in Detroit
summary: You had to figure that, at some point, the Minnesota Vikings’ lack of offensive production would catch up with them. That’s what happened in Week 8 at Ford Field, as the Detroit Lions were able to put up enough points to end the Vikings’ undefeated streak. Jahmyr Gibbs put up yards and a touchdown, and […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 01: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings scores a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 01, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images You had to figure that, at some point, the Minnesota Vikings’ lack of offensive production would catch up with them. That’s what happened in Week 8 at Ford Field, as the Detroit Lions were able to put up enough points to end the Vikings’ undefeated streak. Jahmyr Gibbs put up yards and a touchdown, and the Minnesota offense once again failed to reach the 20-point mark as the Vikings finally fell from the ranks of the NFL’s undefeated by a score of 19-15 at Ford Field in Week 8. The Vikings got the football first after the Lions won the coin toss and chose to defer to the second half. That put Kyler Murray and company on the field right away, and they got off to a fast start as Murray found Ben Yurosek for a gain of 24 yards on the game’s first play to put the ball into Detroit territory. The drive stalled out after that, and the Vikings then called on Will Reichard to attempt a 57-yard field goal, and Reichard uncharacteristically pushed it wide to the right, leaving the Vikings empty on their opening drive. It appeared that the Lions’ first drive was going to result in a three-and-out, but the officials flagged Levi Drake Rodriguez for roughing the passer on Jared Goff to extend the drive for the Lions. But after the Vikings collected two sacks on Goff, courtesy of Andrew Van Ginkel and Eric Wilson, the Lions were forced to punt after all and the Vikings took over at their own 11. Minnesota started the next drive with Jordan Mason taking a handoff for about 10 and a first down, but that was all they could get before they called on Brett Thorson to punt it away. His boot went out of bounds at the Detroit 35 for the home team’s second possession of the afternoon. The Lions converted on a third down on a pass from Goff to Amon-Ra St. Brown despite Jalen Redmond deflecting it, and on the next third down, Goff found Jameson Williams down the seam for a big 46-yard gain. Williams was then called for a taunting penalty to push the Lions out of the red zone to the Lions’ 24-yard-line. The Lions then appeared to have a touchdown pass from Goff to St. Brown, but it was overturned on review when it was determined that St. Brown didn’t control the ball all the way through the catch. The Lions ultimately ended up settling for a field goal attempt from Jake Bates, who connected from 25 yards out to give the Lions a 3-0 lead with just over two minutes left in the first quarter. The ensuing Vikings’ possession got off to a nice start after D.J. Reed was called for pass interference on a pass to Jordan Addison to move the ball into Detroit territory at the 45-yard-line, and a few plays later Murray found the former Lion, T.J. Hockenson, for a 22-yard gain down to the Detroit 16. Aaron Jones then took a screen pass and plowed down to the 1 to make it first-and-goal, and then Justin Jefferson went and did Justin Jefferson things. . @JJettas2 is just different. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/tao9TbfnRO — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 1, 2026 The ridiculous one-handed catch gave the Vikings a 7-3 lead after the Reichard extra point less than a minute into the second quarter. Detroit’s next possession started with decent field position despite the Lions’ return man muffing the initial attempt at fielding the return. On the next third down, however, Jared Goff did something that he had not done all season before now. . .throw an interception. James Pierre picks it off! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XZ8sQnAqCx — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 James Pierre’s second interception of the year ended the Lions’ drive, but the Vikings’ offense couldn’t capitalize, and they quickly went three-and-out. Brett Thorson’s punt put the Lions at their own 8-yard line to start their next possession. The Lions picked up one first down, but ultimately punted it back to the Vikings with six and a half minutes left before halftime. The Vikings’ offense responded with an ugly three-and-out that featured Murray getting sacked, and Thorson got away a bad punt that allowed the Lions to start at midfield. The Vikings forced another Lions punt and had the ball at the two-minute warning. Murray then got out of the pocket and got the ball to near midfield, but then overthrew Jefferson on a pass and was intercepted by D.J. Reed to kill the drive. The Lions then pushed the ball into Minnesota territory and got a long carry from Gibbs to set up another field goal attempt by Bates, a 37-yarder that split the uprights to make it 7-6 going into the locker room at halftime. The Lions got the ball to start the second half, and got into Minnesota territory in just three plays, thanks largely to Gibbs. They managed to push into Minnesota territory at around the 30, but their drive stalled, and they faced a 4th-and-5 from the Minnesota 28. Bates came on for a 46-yard field goal attempt, and he bounced it off the left upright, and it fell no good, keeping the Vikings on top at 7-6 just over five minutes into the third quarter. Minnesota started their first drive of the second half with Murray getting sacked again, this time for a seven-yard loss. The drive wound up in yet another three-and-out, and the Vikings punted it away again. On the Lions’ next drive, the dam finally broke, as the Lions got into the end zone on a 30-yard touchdown run from Gibbs to put the Lions back up on top by a score of 12-7 after the two-point conversion attempt failed. The next drive saw Jordan Mason break a nice run to midfield on the first play that was called back for a hold on Will Fries. The Vikings overcame the 1st-and-20 after the hold, and converted another big third down on a seam throw from Murray to Hockenson to move into Detroit territory. After a lengthy injury timeout following an injury to Lions’ lineback Jack Campbell, the Vikings went for it on a 4th-and-5 from the Detroit 25-yard-line, and Murray’s pass for Jordan Addison fell incomplete for a turnover on downs. Detroit then quickly went three-and-out on their next possession, putting the Minnesota offense back on the field around their own 15. A few plays into the drive, the Vikings’ offense finally hit on a big play, as Murray hit Addison for a huge 51-yard gain to put the ball down at the Detroit 10-yard-line for a first-and-goal. A couple of plays later, the Vikings found the end zone again, as Murray connected with Hockenson for an 8-yard score to make it 13-12. Murray then found a wide-open Addison in the end zone for the two-point conversion to make it 15-12 with just under nine minutes left in regulation. TJ Hockenson for the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cPj2oQQZzU — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Lions’ next drive got started with a big play, as Gibbs took a handoff, reversed field, and picked up 17 yards to put the Lions near midfield. The Lions’ run game just shredded the Vikings’ defense all the way down the field and quickly found themselves with a first-and-goal from the Minnesota 7. Goff then found Jameson Williams in the back of the end zone for a 7-yard touchdown, and just like that the Lions were back on top by a score of 19-15 with four and a half minutes to go in regulation. The ensuing drive for the Vikings was a quick three-and-out, with Brett Thorson’s punt being fielded by the Lions at their own 17 with just under three minutes to play. Gibbs then broke another big run and the Lions got to the two-minute warning with a short-yardage situation. The Vikings started calling their timeouts, and eventually the Lions converted and went to victory formation, taking home the victory and handing the Vikings their first loss of the 2026 season. Kyler Murray, once again, looked awful for the most part against a Detroit defense…

title: Report: Vikings Had Trade In Place With Niners for Jauan Jennings
summary: The NFL’s trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and the Minnesota Vikings reportedly had a deal in place for a player who has been underperforming this season, but the trade fell through. Per Jay Glazer of FOX Sports (via Air Meirov of The 33rd Team), the Vikings had a deal in place to send wide receiver […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 25: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings (14) runs off the field after a NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and the Minnesota Vikings on October 25, 2026 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The NFL’s trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and the Minnesota Vikings reportedly had a deal in place for a player who has been underperforming this season, but the trade fell through. The #49ers and #Vikings recently had a trade agreement in place for WR Jauan Jennings to return to San Francisco, but Jennings made it clear he didn’t want to go back, and the deal fell through, per @JayGlazer . pic.twitter.com/aqCgTn5l0M — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 1, 2026 Per Jay Glazer of FOX Sports (via Air Meirov of The 33rd Team), the Vikings had a deal in place to send wide receiver Jauan Jennings. . .who has been the subject of recent trade rumors, back to the San Francisco 49ers, but the deal fell through when Jennings made it clear that he did not want to go back to San Francisco. Jennings spent the first six seasons of his NFL career with the Niners after they selected him in the seventh round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Tennessee. During his time in San Francisco, he caught 210 passes for 2,584 yards and 22 touchdowns. He signed a 1-year deal with Minnesota this offseason, and thus far, he has been a significant disappointment, catching just four passes for 43 yards. No word has been given on why Jennings did not want to go back to San Francisco or anything like that. . .just that he didn’t want to go back to his former team. At this point, it’s not clear if Jennings would be open to a trade to any other team or if he just didn’t want to go back to San Francisco. The NFL trade deadline is a week from this coming Tuesday. We’ll be keeping an eye on what the Vikings are doing and whether or not they make any moves for the stretch run of the 2026 NFL season.

full_text: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first two months of the regular season. While the expectation is that they will get several players back from injured reserve at some point, they also could go for a more radical approach in hopes of improving their team and gearing up for a stretch run in 2026. Like they have done multiple times in 2026 already, they could look at the trade market. Will there be additions to a list that already includes the likes of A.J. Brown, Jaylen Reed, Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse? Or could they move on from some of their players, like they did in 2025 ? We will know soon: the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET.
