title: Eagles-Commanders final score: Philadelphia loses sixth straight game
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-6 after losing to the Washington Commanders in Landover, Maryland on Sunday night. Final score: 27 to 10. Well, the Eagles got out to a 1o to 0 lead in this one. That was nice. But then they played like the bad and dumb team that they are as the Commanders […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Charles Omenihu #90 of the Washington Commanders recovers a fumble by Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the third quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-6 after losing to the Washington Commanders in Landover, Maryland on Sunday night. Final score: 27 to 10. Well, the Eagles got out to a 1o to 0 lead in this one. That was nice. But then they played like the bad and dumb team that they are as the Commanders took control of the game to score 27 unanswered points. The Eagles have now lost SIX games in a row. It’s their longest losing streak since 2012, which was Andy Reid’s final season in Philly. The Eagles are now 5-11 in their last 16 games. This team stinks. They’re a real tough watch. Are they even going to win another game this season? Next up for the Eagles: a Week 9 home game against the NFC East-leading New York Giants, who enjoyed a bye in Week 8. Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also, check me out talking about this game on the PHLY Eagles postgame show. FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Commanders had a 44-yard kick return to set up at midfield. Facing 3rd-and-inches after two runs, the Commanders easily ran up the gut into wide open space for a first down. So easy. Facing 3rd-and-6, Jonathan Greenard jumped early to give Washington a free play, which was a Jayden Daniels pick to Andrew Mukuba. Facing 3rd-and-1, the Commanders false started. Facing 3rd-and-6, the Commanders false started again. Facing 3rd-and-11, Cooper DeJean had good coverage on Stefon Diggs and the pass was wide anyway. The Commanders settled for a 55-yard field goal attempt … that went wide right! The Eagles took over at their 45-yard line and began with a Saquon Barkley run for two yards. Facing 3rd-and-3 after a Tanner McKee scramble for four yards, McKee scrambled and lofted up a ball to Darius Cooper, who couldn’t make an impressive leaping grab as the ball was a bit too high. Facing 4th-and-3, Nick Sirianni should’ve gone for it but he did the stupid shit where the offense pretends to snap the ball only to take a delay of game penalty. Does the defense ever fall for that against this team?! 3 plays, 1 yard, punt. The Commanders took over at their own 12-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-3, Treylon Burks dropped a sure first down to bring up a punt. The Eagles took over at their own 38-yard line. McKee hit Makai Lemon for 20 yards on a nice play-action connection. Then McKee hit Darius Cooper over the middle for another first down. Facing 3rd-and-6 from just outside the red zone, McKee’s throw for Cooper was off target with the quarterback not looking on the same page with his receiver. The Eagles brought in Jake Elliott for a 40-yard field goal make. EAGLES 3, COMMANDERS 0. The Commanders took over at their own 20-yard line after Elliott’s kickoff bounced into the landing zone before going into the end zone. Nice kick. The Commanders got knocked back to 1st-and-20 after two five-yard penalties. Chig Okonkwo caught a pass over the middle but Mukuba put his helmet on the ball to knock the ball out! Mukuba’s first career forced fumble. FLIPPING THE FIELD pic.twitter.com/hfqKnSxz0C — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 2, 2026 The Eagles took over at the plus 26-yard line. A McKee play-action pass to Barkley went for 24 yards! Two plays later, Barkley in the wildcat formation (with fullback Willie Lampkin and sixth offensive lineman Fred Johnson on the field as extra blockers) picked up a touchdown! Takeaways? Touchdowns? Who is this team? EAGLES 10, COMMANDERS 0. Alllll Saquon 🙌 pic.twitter.com/3CFDYmpGmz — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 2, 2026 Eagles have scored 10 points in the first quarter for the first time since Week 12 of last year. — Tucker Bagley (@TBagleySports) November 2, 2026 The Commanders took over at their own 35-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-6, Daniels hit a crossing Burks for a first down. Facing 3rd-and-4 after Jalen Carter tipped a Daniels pass, Washington went with a bubble screen to pick up another first down. Facing 3rd-and-4 after Moro Ojomo picked up a TFL, Daniels’ pass was wide and off target. The Commanders brought in Drew Stevens for a 56-yard field goal make. EAGLES 10, COMMANDERS 3. The Eagles took over at their own 29-yard line. An Elijah Mitchell run for five yards brought up the end of the first quarter. SECOND QUARTER Another Mitchell carry resulted in a first down. Facing 3rd-and-2, Mitchell took a carry up the middle for another first down. The offensive line looks … good?! Or not. Landon Dickerson left Shy Tuttle unblocked to sack McKee. Facing 3rd-and-12, pressure forced McKee into a short completion to bring up a punt. The Commanders took over at their own 11-yard line. Daniels hit Burks with Riq Woolen trailing for 21 yards. Facing 3rd-and-4 a little shy of midfield, Daniels hit Antonio Williams for a first down. Then Daniels took off running upfield into a wide open lane for an easy first down. Austin Ekeler broke a run 18 yards to the left edge (no contain by Arnold Ebiketie) to get to the 8-yard line. Then Daniels hit Diggs for a touchdown. 11-play, 89-yard TD drive to tie the game. Not a great showing from the defensive line. EAGLES 10, COMMANDERS 10. Diggs for six 👏 📺 #PHIvsWAS NBC pic.twitter.com/AKQ5IPsbEb — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 2, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 27-yard line. Barkley re-entered the game and gained four yards. The Commanders got flagged for a very dumb unnecessary roughness penalty by hitting McKee late to give the Eagles a first down. But then the Eagles got knocked back by a TFL and a delay of game penalty. Facing 3rd-and-12, McKee overthrew Mitchell on a dump off to bring up a punt. 5 plays, 17 yards. The Commanders took over at their own 10-yard line with 2:31 on the clock and three timeouts to work with. Jalen Carter jumped offside as the clock was going down to the two-minute warning. No discipline. Facing 3rd-and-2, Rachaad White gained just one yard after it was originally ruled he got the first down. The Commanders punted from 4th-and-inches. The Eagles took over at their own 27-yard line with 1:32 on the clock and three timeouts to work with. Facing 3rd-and-2 after Mitchell inexplicably ran out of bounds before the marker, McKee’s downfield throw to Lemon was incomplete with the receiver failing to make a tough catch against tight coverage. Low percentage throw there. Why is that the call? The Commanders took over at midfield after a 27-yard punt return with 0:50 on the clock and three timeouts to work with. Washington quickly moved into field goal range. Facing 3rd-and-1 after Nolan Smith had Jayden Daniels hurting with a QB hit, Daniels was pressured into another off target throw. The Commanders settled for a 39-yard field goal make to take the lead. EAGLES 10, COMMANDERS 13. The Eagles took over at their own 31-yard line with 0:12 on the clock and three timeouts to work with. They inexplicably gave Saquon Barkley a carry and exposed him to an extra hit for no real reason to end the second quarter. Why not just take a knee? Or why not use Mitchell or Jaydon Blue if you want to run? What are you doing?! THIRD QUARTER The Eagles took over at the 20-yard line to begin the second half. Eli Stowers (!) awkwardly made his first career catch to give the Eagles a second first down on the drive. Facing 3rd-and-3, a handoff to Mitchell was stopped in the backfield for a loss. Facing 4th-and-6, Sirianni opted for a punt. No attempt to draw them offside that time. The Commanders took over at their own 4-yard line after Braden Mann’s punt took a favorable Philly bounce. Facing 3rd-and-6, Okonkwo made a sick one-handed grab for 21 yards that would’ve been a first down anyway if it wasn’t caught because Woolen got flagged for…

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Cole Payton #18 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Gardner Minshew II #15 of the Arizona Cardinals looks on before a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles got some good news ahead of their Week 8 Sunday Night Football game against the Washington Commanders with the Dallas Cowboys choking and losing to the Arizona Cardinals! It seemed like the Cowboys were cruising to a win. They took a 14-point lead late in the third quarter and Arizona was not seriously threatening to come out on top: But the Cardinals made a quarterback change from Jacoby Brissett to former Eagles backup Gardner Minshew. And that change clearly paid off with Minshew going 17/23 for 188 passing yards, three touchdowns, zero interceptions, and a 137.3 passer rating. It was then the Cardinals who nearly had the game won; they scored a touchdown with just six seconds remaining in the fourth quarter … but Chad Ryland missed the go-ahead extra point to keep it tied at 30 points each. The Cardinals then went three-and-out to begin overtime, allowing the Cowboys to win the game with a field goal make. But former Eagles edge rusher Josh Sweat came up with a huge third down sack to force Dallas into a punt. From there, the Cardinals drove into field goal range for the win! Some quick thoughts: Can’t wait to talk about this loss with RJ Ochoa on The NFC East Mixtape this week! Lololololololololololololol Cowboys. The Cowboys truly are owned by the Cardinals. So funny that that’s their boogeyman. Man, this Dallas defense is DREADFUL. Former Eagles defensive assistant Christian Parker might not survive this season. Might get fired as soon as this week? This Cowboys loss helps to keep the Eagles alive in the division, though the Birds need to do their part and actually beat Washington on Sunday night. Or else any talk of winning the NFC East is silly. Cowboys lose! title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns
summary: In a Week 8 battle for the AFC North lead, the Steelers let their play do the talking in a dominant win over the rival Cleveland Browns in Pittsburgh on Sunday. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. Some things never change It’s been a year of change in the AFC […]
full_text: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images | Getty Images In a Week 8 battle for the AFC North lead, the Steelers let their play do the talking in a dominant win over the rival Cleveland Browns in Pittsburgh on Sunday. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. Some things never change It’s been a year of change in the AFC North as three teams have new head coaches. Pittsburgh is no longer under the long-time leadership of Mike Tomlin, while the Browns, with Todd Monken replacing Kevin Stefanski, shocked the world by leading the division through seven weeks. But the Browns haven’t won a regular season game in Pittsburgh since 2003, and all that offseason turnover didn’t do anything to change that. History continued. Emphatically. The Steelers won 27-6 in their most lopsided victory yet this season. The Browns were repeatedly punched in the mouth in a game that never felt particularly close. Much in the way that it’s easy to dismiss what happens in a Steelers’ Thursday Night Football loss in Cleveland — in what feels more like an annually-scheduled night of disappointment rather than a football game with free will — I believe it’s a bit of an overreaction to suddenly declare the Steelers as Super Bowl contenders in a win as clearly telegraphed as this one was. But at the same time, the story of the game is less about the win and more about how the Steelers won. The pass rush was masterful. The run game was relentless. Pittsburgh’s roster seemed to relish every moment of punishing its rival. The team culture seems to be in a great place, and the Steelers have their most established identity of the season on both sides of the ball after the big win. When the Steelers hired Mike McCarthy, it was clearly in part a decision to try to keep a similar status quo from the Mike Tomlin era. Yes, plenty has changed in terms of scheme and other details, but the macro-level results: an above-average team, rebounding from brutal losses such as the Patriots in Week 2, and of course, routinely defeating the Browns at home, remains the same. 2. The Steelers dominate the trenches Eight sacks. Fourteen quarterback hits. Nonstop pressure. The Steelers’ pass rush was absurdly good Sunday afternoon, defeating the Browns’ offensive front with speed and power and making Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson distribute the ball from a war zone. What was even more impressive for Pittsburgh was how the production was spread across the board, with seven different defenders recording 0.5 sacks or more. The box score doesn’t do it justice, either. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was arguably the team’s MVP against Cleveland, logging just a 0.5 sack but generating six pressures against Browns left tackle Spencer Fano, including two quick pressures. He also drew three holding calls, per NFL Pro. I’ve been as critical as any in regards to the Steelers’ spending choices on defense in recent seasons, and even skeptical at times of the plan to extend (and properly use) all three of T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, and Nick Herbig. But Sunday’s game was an occurrence when all that star power clicked on at once. It’s one of the most dominant, fun-to-watch performances from a pass rush I’ve seen in recent memory, and although such gaudy numbers are an unrealistic expectation moving forward ( this wasn’t even the first time the Browns have given up eight sacks this season ), it’s still a promising sign for a group that has already been excellent for much of the year. Simply put, if the Steelers want to be any sort of contender come late-season, the pass rush, as the best position group on the team, is going to have to be the engine of that effort. Sunday was overwhelmingly a strong step in that direction. Equally as encouraging was the Steelers’ offensive line on Sunday, particularly in the run game. Pittsburgh averaged a strong 6.1 yards per rush, gaining 14 of the team’s 20 total first downs on the ground against Cleveland. One of the highlights of the game was Pittsburgh taking advantage of a pass-expecting Browns front on third and 13 to move the sticks on an interior run. Trap again! On 3rd-and-13 no less. Steelers dipping into the Wing-T playbook… pic.twitter.com/xP7GDZjZ0R — Kevin Smith (@KTSmithFootball) November 1, 2026 I feel like I’ve talked ad nauseam about how much Jaylen Warren has meant to this Steelers offense in the takeaways column this year, so there’s no reason to rehash those same points. But it’s also no secret that Warren’s star turn largely correlated with Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor joining the starting O-line on the right side earlier this season, and Pittsburgh continues to reap the benefits. In recent weeks, notably against the Saints and now the Browns, Pittsburgh has also turned to a higher dose of gap concepts in the run game along with more use of an extra offensive lineman jumbo package to further up its production on the ground. With that in mind, it’s probably not surprising to hear those two games have also resulted in Pittsburgh’s best two rushing performances of the year thus far (148 and 200 yards, respectively). Entering Week 8, the Steelers’ offense ranked 11th in yards before contact per carry and seventh in yards after contact per carry. That’s the sign of a true team effort between blockers and backs in the run game, and I’d only expect both statistics to improve after Next Gen Stats updates for Week 8. But moving back to the Browns game, it might be even more impressive that the Steelers ran for 200 given that the passing game (more on that later) only mustered 161 yards. Despite failing to achieving balance on offense, Pittsburgh still pulverized Cleveland on the ground and scored nearly 30 points. The Browns had every reason to sell out against the run and still couldn’t stop it. That’s the sign of a truly successful run game. 3. Still some passing game concerns Here’s the point in the column where I do my usual “Well, the Steelers weren’t entirely as good/bad as they might’ve looked” bit and try not to come across as annoying. Yes, it was a great win! Yes, the pass rush and run game looked elite! But those two incredibly bright spots covered up a lot of issues. I’m still mildly confused with the “complete” game narrative ( Aaron Rodgers also pushed against this ) floating around given just how incomplete parts of the team still looked on Sunday. Namely, the passing game. As mentioned above, the Steelers managed just 161 yards on the air. They didn’t have to throw it much on Sunday, to be fair, but Aaron Rodgers still just completed barely over half of his passes (13/25), averaging an uninspired 6.2 yards per pass. While the passing game to the tight ends worked (Darnell Washington logged three grabs for 94 yards), the team’s wide receiver core only combined for 43, with WR1 D.K. Metcalf contributing a paltry four. Once again, the Steelers’ passing game was largely restrained to short throws and quick-game screens and dump-offs. And no, this is far from a critique of just Aaron Rodgers. When the deep ball finally was an option, this happened: Rodgers looks deep for DK Metcalf, who bobbles it and it's intercepted by Denzel Ward. Works out to be a long punt, but man, what a missed opportunity. pic.twitter.com/FP1CZFWjxf https://t.co/jNrlt8aLT7 — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 1, 2026 The Steelers’ unreal running game success made their passing game struggles somewhat negligible, but that won’t always be the case. If the Steelers want to rise to Serious™ contender status, the passing offense is still several tiers away from looking the part. But to be fair, while neither have been game-breakers, even getting one of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson back soon after the bye would be a boost for a team awfully short-handed on starting-caliber wide receivers. 4. A tale of two red zones The Steelers’ strong defensive performance last week was still met with the cautionary title of “bend don’t break” — and against the Browns,…

title: Steelers make Jared Verse eat his words
summary: In the lead up to the Week 8 matchup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns, Jared Verse did a lot of talking. The Browns’ edge rusher said that some Steelers players were “dirty,” and called out Cam Heyward after the Steelers’ captain responded to those comments. “I’m not worried about Cam,” Verse said. “I’m […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the lead up to the Week 8 matchup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns, Jared Verse did a lot of talking. The Browns’ edge rusher said that some Steelers players were “dirty,” and called out Cam Heyward after the Steelers’ captain responded to those comments. “I’m not worried about Cam,” Verse said . “I’m not worried about their offensive line. I’m not worried about anyone on their team.” And, to be fair, Verse shouldn’t worry about the Steelers. He should, however, worry about not having a sack through eight games. He should worry that Steelers undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity now has more sacks than him, despite Sunday being just the second game he’s appeared in. He should worry that his tackle total was lower than his body slams received total. And he should worry that the Steelers ran it to the tune of 200 yards against his defense. Steelers running back Jaylen Warren heard what was said all week, and brushed off Verse’s comments when asked about them after the game. “Some walk, some talk,” Warren said . Safety Jaquan Brisker was a bit more blunt. “He should have kept his mouth shut,” Brisker said via Ashley Wenskowski. All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles, that’s bad. He’s gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better.” Offensive tackle Troy Fautanu added that the Steelers purposely weren’t saying anything once they took a big lead. “We were kinda not talking on purpose just to piss them off,” Fautanu said via Alan Saunders . “They wanted us to start chatting a little bit. We were just trying to finish the game.” Edge rusher Nick Herbig echoed this sentiment. “We let the pads do the talking,” Herbig said. The Steelers made it clear throughout the week that they had no interest in engaging in Verse’s battle of words. They were more concerned about winning the war on the field. Now at 6-2, the Steelers control their destiny. Take care of business in the second half of the season, and the AFC North will be theirs for a second straight season. title: Steelers ‘right where we want to be’ entering bye week
summary: Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers remained somewhat terse in his postgame press conference following Pittsburgh’s 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Despite the big win over a divisional foe, Rodgers seemed reluctant to give too much praise to the Steelers offense, saying their performance was “not very complete” and that there “should’ve been a lot […]
full_text: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images | Getty Images Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers remained somewhat terse in his postgame press conference following Pittsburgh’s 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Despite the big win over a divisional foe, Rodgers seemed reluctant to give too much praise to the Steelers offense, saying their performance was “not very complete” and that there “should’ve been a lot more points.” Still, with the Steelers now 6-2 on the season, in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, and entering a midseason bye week on a four-game winning streak, Rodgers acknowledged the team is in a good spot. “We’d like to play our best and still win. We also like to win,” he said. “We’re 6-2 going into the bye, first in the division. We’re right where we want to be.” Both Cleveland and Pittsburgh were 5-2 entering Week 8, with the Browns having already defeated the Steelers earlier in the season in a Thursday Night Football matchup at Huntington Bank Field. But back at home in Acrisure Stadium in Sunday’s rematch, the Steelers ran for 200 yards on Cleveland while only allowing 34 yards on the ground en route to a lopsided, 21-point victory. Despite the AFC North being arguably the NFL’s most competitive division in 2026 with not one team under .500, the Steelers are in the best spot of the group at midseason. The now 5-3 Browns lost in blowout fashion. The Bengals (now 5-2) won on Sunday to jump into second place in the division, but it took overtime to defeat the hapless 1-7 Titans. And the Ravens, the consensus preseason pick to win the AFC North, are now in last place at 4-4 after a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. To make matters worse for Baltimore, Lamar Jackson was injured again and is now headed to IR with an upcoming thumb injury. The Steelers’ first game after the bye will be a Sunday Night Football matchup on Nov. 15 against the Bengals in what will be another matchup between top AFC North teams. “Winning is the most important thing — 2-1 in the division now,” Rodgers said. “Either way, that game in two weeks is going to be really important.” The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 earlier in the season. The black and gold have split their series with the Browns in 2026 but still have both matchups against the Ravens due later in the season. While the Steelers players acknowledged there’s a lot of football left to play, T.J. Watt said he’s been encouraged by how the team has found ways to win thus far. “I like that we’ve won games many different ways. We’ve come from behind. We’ve been able to hold leads. We’ve played games where we haven’t looked great. We’ve played games where we’ve looked great,” he said. “We just need to continue to grow and build off this performance … There continues to be young guys (contributing), and I think (Derrick Harmon) is coming back soon too, hopefully, so I think this bye week comes at a great time for us.” AFC North standings after Week 8 Steelers (6-2; 2-1 division) Bengals (5-2; 1-1 division) Browns (5-3; 2-1 division) Ravens (4-4; 0-2 division)

title: Steelers stock report after Week 8 win over Browns
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 on Sunday. Pittsburgh will go into the bye week 6-2 overall and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The streak continues, as the Browns haven’t defeated the Steelers in Pittsburgh since 2003. As always, here is my weekly stock report after the Steelers’ […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 on Sunday. Pittsburgh will go into the bye week 6-2 overall and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The streak continues, as the Browns haven’t defeated the Steelers in Pittsburgh since 2003. As always, here is my weekly stock report after the Steelers’ dominant win over Cleveland. Stock Up RBs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle Coming into the contest, Cleveland struggled to defend the run. The Steelers took that to heart, as Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle set the tone offensively. Dowdle got the scoring started for the Steelers with a nine-yard touchdown run. Warren posted over 100 yards rushing in the first half, while getting into the end zone himself in the third quarter. The Steelers’ 160 first-half rushing yards is the most by any team in a half this season. The Steelers had a vision of a two-headed monster at running back when they signed Dowdle this offseason. That vision finally seems to be coming to fruition as the team enters the bye. TE Darnell Washington Darnell Washington has emerged as one of the Steelers’ best options in their passing attack. Washington only caught three passes today, but recorded 94 receiving yards with 64 yards after the catch. Washington needs only a few targets to make a big impact. Whether it’s in the red zone or on a wheel route, Washington is simply a matchup nightmare that defenses have to account for on every snap. Defense Defensive coordinator Patrick Graham deserves a ton of credit for the way the Steelers defense has played over the course of the last month. Today, the Pittsburgh defense sacked Deshaun Watson eight times. Cleveland posted just 34 rushing yards as a team, and averaged 2.3 yards per attempt. The inside linebacker duo of Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson played very well today. Queen posted 1.5 sacks today, while Wilson made several quality run stops, one for a loss. Rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings got things going for the defense by forcing a fumble on the game’s opening drive. It was a complete and total dominance by the Steelers defense today. Stock Down WR DK Metcalf Metcalf is an incredibly frustrating player to watch. On his six targets, Metcalf brought in just one of them for four yards. Late in the third quarter, Metcalf was targeted downfield by Aaron Rodgers. The ball hit Metcalf right in the hands, but he bobbled the ball as Browns corner Denzel Ward ran by and grabbed it out of Metcalf’s clutches. As good as the Steelers moved the ball down the field today, it had absolutely nothing to do with the highest-paid player on their offense. Metcalf is well on his way to another underwhelming season in Pittsburgh. Red zone offense Speaking of frustrating, the Steelers’ red zone offense is puzzling to watch. In the first half, the Steelers had two drives go first and goal inside the ten. Of the six plays they ran inside the ten in those drives, the Steelers elected to pass the ball on five of those six plays. Despite how well the team was running the ball, they continued to pass and utilize fade routes in those situations. While it ended up being a comfortable win for the Steelers, their red zone offense will need to be more efficient in the second half if they want to clinch a second straight AFC North title. title: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren celebrates birthday with all-time performance
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers just put the finishing touches on a 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns, in which the Steelers running back helped set the tone for what was a true butt-kicking from start to finish. Happy 28th birthday, Jaylen Warren. While there were still some questionable decisions by the offense early in the game, […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers just put the finishing touches on a 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns, in which the Steelers running back helped set the tone for what was a true butt-kicking from start to finish. Happy 28th birthday, Jaylen Warren. Happy Birthday @Nunless2 ‼️ pic.twitter.com/6PZOaF85L5 — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 While there were still some questionable decisions by the offense early in the game, especially in the red zone, Pittsburgh eventually embraced the bullyball DNA of their roster. On the day, the Steelers hammered the Browns with 200 yards on the ground. Leading the charge was Warren, who tied a career high with 143 yards rushing on 17 attempts, good for an average of 8.4 yards per carry. Warren reached that same rushing total last December against the Lions. Warren created explosive play after explosive play, with three runs of 15 yards or greater, including a 51-yard scamper that helped convert a 3rd-and-13. Jaylen Warren just went 51 yards on 3rd and 13 😳 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YD1Naon9lN — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 But Warren wasn’t just simply outrunning defenders; he was running through them. According to PFF, Warren totaled 118 yards after contact, an average of 6.94 per rush. He forced five missed tackles as well. And, of course, the Steelers couldn’t let their dominant running back’s birthday end without a trip to the end zone. Jaylen Warren increases the Steelers' lead CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QNrPIbaQDk — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Warren isn’t just a dominant force, though. He’s been a great teammate during his career, and he made sure to shout out his offensive line during a pregame interview. The Steelers’ offensive line deserves just as much credit for this win, naturally, and they made sure to come through for their guy so he could not only celebrate a win on his birthday, but have a career day as well. The Steelers are on bye next week and will have a rematch against Cincinnati in Week 10. Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries (7.47 YPC) when the teams last played in Week 3. title: Steelers sack Deshaun Watson eight times, defeat Browns 27-6
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have now won 23 straight regular season home games over the Cleveland Browns, defeating their division rivals 27-6 to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers’ defense made its imprint very early on in the game, as Pittsburgh had two fumble recoveries on Cleveland’s first two drives. […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have now won 23 straight regular season home games over the Cleveland Browns, defeating their division rivals 27-6 to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers’ defense made its imprint very early on in the game, as Pittsburgh had two fumble recoveries on Cleveland’s first two drives. While the Steelers went three-and-out following the first fumble, they wouldn’t make that mistake the second time around. Rico Dowdle recorded his first touchdown of the season to put Pittsburgh up 7-0. Dowdle would finish the day with 56 yards on the ground. The next drive would begin the terrific day of Jaylen Warren. Pittsburgh’s rising star continued his incredible season, getting the Steelers downfield with a 51 yard run. The Steelers, however, would stall in the red zone and settle for a field goal. The teams would exchange field goals over the next three drives, making it a 13-6 Steelers lead, and then Aaron Rodgers put together a terrific drive to end the half. With just 44 seconds left, Rodgers led a six-play drive featuring a 23-yard Jaylen Warren run and completions of 28 yards to Pat Freiemruth and 15 yards to Germie Bernard. On the final play of the half, the Steelers punched the ball in with a Freiermuth run at the goal line to take a 20-6 lead into halftime. On their second drive of the second half, Rodgers hit Darnell Washington for a 58 yard catch-and-run, and Jaylen Warren would put an exclamation point on his day with a touchdown, which is where the scoring would end. Warren tied his career high in rushing yards with 143 and a touchdown, while the defense put up an astounding eight sacks, two of which came from T.J. Watt. The former Defensive Player of the Year now has 7.5 sacks on the season, topping his season total of seven from 2025. Alex Highsmith only had half a sack, but was applying constant pressure to Watson all day. Nick Herbig, Kevin Jobity, Cam Heyward, Patrick Queen, and Keeanu Benton all teamed up for the remaining six sacks. The Steelers are now 6-2, and hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North heading into the bye week. Additionally, the Buffalo Bills defeated the Baltimore Ravens, putting Baltimore at 4-4 on the season. Pittsburgh will return from its bye week in Week 10 to take on the Cincinnati Bengals. title: How and why this 2026 Seahawks offense could change
summary: Don’t look now… the Seattle Seahawks offense is evolving. Don’t push ‘B’. Seattle pulled off a blockbuster to secure the services of All-Pro guard, Quenton Nelson. One that many speculated about after Indianapolis signaled to the league that they were ready to embrace their rebuild already. Terron Armstead thinks that his impact will be on […]
full_text: Don’t look now… the Seattle Seahawks offense is evolving. Don’t push ‘B’. View Link Seattle pulled off a blockbuster to secure the services of All-Pro guard, Quenton Nelson. One that many speculated about after Indianapolis signaled to the league that they were ready to embrace their rebuild already. Terron Armstead thinks that his impact will be on par with that of JSN’s in the receiving corps. "Quentin Nelson, he adds a level of impact and playmaking. It's as massive as JSN." 👀 @T_Armstead72 on the Seahawks OL addition. #justfootball pic.twitter.com/e39VtO0VxW — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 28, 2026 In the short term, with no Charles Cross at LT (ankle), new surroundings for Nelson, a new position for new RG, Grey Zabel and the returns of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet: expect the Seahawks to lean into the run game before settling in to let this line gel. Former Colts center, Jeff Saturday ,discussed what it would be like for Grey Zabel moving to the right side. “Conceptually, it all makes sense. There are times when you’re uncomfortable in your set. But, as well as Zabel has played already, I would not think it would be overly challenging.” Indy’s former interim Head Coach went on to talk about how muscle memory will build, but until then: “I’m probably telling the center to look right a little bit, early. Just peek so that he gives up that inside.” Offensive coordinator, Brian Fleury made his expectations for Grey Zabel flipping sides clear, saying that “he’s had a lot of experience with that in college. He’s got a lot of versatility, so I’m sure the learning curve will evaporate pretty quickly.” Sometimes the antidote to OL uncertainty is to just let your guys go out there and MASH. Good thing that’s exactly the way the Hawks want to operate, to alleviate situations for Sam Darnold and the 3rd-down efforts of the point-scoring unit. What else can we expect? Cooper Kupp was asked about Sam Darnold getting through his progressions, and he spoke to how receivers are also responsible for that. Kupp said that “you might not have time to be creative in your route. You might need to just get to your spot, and if you’re not there, then there’s an opportunity for Sam to move on, for you to pull coverage. and for other guys on the back end to be creative and have time to find the open space. We all work in conjunction with that. So, it’s not just Sam playing fast — which I thought he did an unbelievable job — but it’s also all of us really owning what we’re trying to get done.” One of the receivers who was criticized for a lazy route that could’ve led to an OT INT against the Broncos, and a drop against the Chiefs was Tory Horton. Mike Macdonald on Horton filling in for Rashid Shaheed (knee) this week was succinct: “He’s got more of an opportunity. We expect him to take advantage of it.” Seattle likely does not want to take the ball out of JSN’s hands, but distributing the ball a bit more seemed to work well against Kansas City. Fleury was asked about heightened TE involvement last week, and he refused to make it just about that position, even though A.J. Barner played a pivotal role (his 42 yards were second only to Smith-Njigba, adding to his 3 “Barn-Yard” tush push conversions). “There’s been a deliberate approach to try and get everybody a little bit more involved”, Fleury explained. Remember how the acquisition of Rashid Shaheed changed how defenses played the Seattle offense last year? He didn’t even play well, and it still changed the defensive structures that Seattle saw! The run game took off and produced a Super Bowl MVP. They are trying to flip the script and dictate terms on offense, halfway through the season once again. The Seahawks would love to knock teams out of cloud coverage, and get them to commit more to stopping the ground game. View this post on Instagram Mike Macdonald, during his weekly radio show , talked about JSN getting doubled: “We’re getting a lot of ways to allocate two people to him, as they should, and he’s still finding ways to get open. We got to still keep finding ways to manipulate those coverages so that either the ball goes somewhere else — I’ve got a great opportunity to hit Tory on the in-cut early in the game, and I really expect Tory to make that play. We’ve really got to hit on those types of plays if teams are going to play those types of coverages against us, we can make them pay.” If there’s any legitimate thought about trading for Jonathan Taylor, Price and Charbonnet will be under the microscope over the next two games against the Bears and Cardinals. If Charbo doesn’t look the same after a serious injury and Price displays a continues problem with either fumbles or injury, the Taylor talk could get louder. Ultimately, the offense is attached to a defense that is putting up historical numbers. They just had unprecedented success against a Sean Payton-led offense and handed Patrick Mahomes the biggest beatdown of his professional offensive life. If the Seahawk offense can control the ball, move it forward and play complimentary ball, this could be a very dangerous team. With Nelson and Jones playing key roles this week, we can expect more bully ball. The type of ball that will punish those who seek to go all in on stopping the reigning OPOY, Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Seattle is far more banged up than Chicago, with Rashid Shaheed and Charles Cross both out, while Uchenna Nwosu is unlikely to play. He was drafted by the Giants in 1978 in the seventh round from Washington State University and was traded to the […]
full_text: Former Seattle Seahawks running back, Dan Doornink, passed away on Saturday. The team announced his passing on Sunday afternoon. We’re saddened by the passing of former Seahawk Dan Doornink. Our thoughts are with his family, friends and loved ones. pic.twitter.com/jvwRiPXS3m — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 1, 2026 Doornink played seven seasons for the Seahawks after being traded from the New York Giants. He was drafted by the Giants in 1978 in the seventh round from Washington State University and was traded to the Seahawks prior to the 1979 season. Throughout his playing career, he averaged 3.5 yards per carry, 5.5 yards per reception, had had 15 rushing touchdowns and 11 receiving touchdowns. Fans may remember the 1984 Wild Card game against the Los Angeles Raiders at the Kingdome where he ran for 123 yards and helped the Seahawks win 13-7. He also caught a touchdown in Seattle’s AFC Championship Game loss to the Raiders in the previous season. After his NFL career was done, Doornink went on to graduate from the University of Washington with his Doctorate of Medicine. He then returned to his hometown of Yakima, Washington where he practiced medicine, giving back to the community that raised him. Dan Doornink was 70 years old.

title: Will Mac Jones be a trade target for QB-needy teams?
summary: According to Ian Rapoport, the Baltimore Ravens will look to add help at quarterback after Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could sideline him for the rest of the season, and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss an extended period with turf toe. That leaves Baltimore with only a QB3. “I do expect the […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Ian Rapoport, the Baltimore Ravens will look to add help at quarterback after Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could sideline him for the rest of the season, and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss an extended period with turf toe. That leaves Baltimore with only a QB3. “I do expect the Baltimore Ravens to go out and consider some QB trades, and kinda discuss, ‘How bold do you wanna be?’ Do you want to go out and spend a lot of capital for a quarterback in a season that may be lost because you don’t have Lamar? Or is it going to be a stopgap, and then you end up a seller? These are real decisions that general manager Eric DeCosta and the rest of the Ravens brass.” Rapoport mentioned Tyson Bagent, who was the backup for the Bears under now-Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle last year, as an option. He also brought up Jacoby Brissett, who was benched in Week 8 by the Arizona Cardinals. “There are some options. There aren’t great options, but there are some options out there.” Mac Jones has an expiring contract. He has no ties to Doyle and the Ravens, but he has starting experience and proved he can win last season. The San Francisco 49ers still might value Jones more than those on the outside think they should, given how much they relied on a backup in 2025. It’s a move that doesn’t make sense, but the Vikings, despite their record, are struggling at quarterback. Surprise, surprise: Kyler Murray doesn’t look the part. But why would the 49ers make a playoff contender better? That’s essentially the landscape for quarterback-needy teams in the playoff hunt. It’s slim pickings, and that means Mac Jones is likely here to stay.

title: Jauan Jennings nixed a trade to return to the 49ers
summary: According to Jay Glazer, the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings recently had a trade agreement in place to bring wide receiver Jauan Jennings back to the Niners, but the deal fell through after Jennings made it clear he didn’t want to return to the team that drafted him. Jennings, who was targeted twice this […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jauan Jennings #14 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts against the Indianapolis Colts in the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Jay Glazer, the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings recently had a trade agreement in place to bring wide receiver Jauan Jennings back to the Niners, but the deal fell through after Jennings made it clear he didn’t want to return to the team that drafted him. Jennings, who was targeted twice this past week and caught two passes for 11 yards — bringing his season total to four receptions for 43 yards — reportedly likes the direction the Vikings are headed and wants to be part of that organization. Here’s what he posted on his Instagram after the Vikings suffered their first loss: Jauan Jennings recent IG post: pic.twitter.com/i2X7nsiqkJ — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) November 1, 2026 Here’s what Glazer had to say before kickoff on Sunday morning on Fox: “Here’s a little scoopage that nobody knew. The 49ers, who traded for DeForest Buckner, also had trade terms worked out for Jauan Jennings, their former receiver, with the Vikings. But it was contingent on him hopping on a FaceTime with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch and saying, ‘OK, yeah, I wanna come back.’ But he didn’t. He actually said, no, I wanna stay here in Minnesota. Hey Vikings fans, he likes what you have going on over there.” Jennings would give the Niners a big-bodied, gritty blocker you can trust on third and medium. The problem with Jennings is that everything shrinks when he’s on the field from a passing-game perspective. But familiarity would have been key here, as the Niners, assuming whenever they agreed to this trade, were short at wideout and could plug and play Jennings in multiple roles. Jennings got into a heated argument with Kyle Shanahan on the sideline in the first half of 2025 . Jennings is no stranger when it comes to wearing his emotions on his sleeve. He had an incident with Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell. We’ll see if any more details come out about this nixed trade, like the potential compensation. If Jennings is the only receiver the Niners are eyeing, or if it’s a player of similar value, then that’s the team telling us they are counting on some of the other injured wideouts to return to the lineup, including De’Zhaun Stribling.

full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Texans are reuniting with veteran defensive tackle Naquan Jones, per Aaron Wilson . Jones appeared in three games for the San Francisco 49ers this season at defensive tackle after the team suffered a rash of injuries at the position. Jones last appeared in Week 5. But with the return of James Thompson and Mykel Williams, the team no longer needed a nose tackle in the next two games. Jones was with Houston in training camp. The Texans released him in August before he joined the Minnesota Vikings. That’s where the Niners poached Jones from a little more than a month ago . This opens a practice squad spot for the 49ers, who will inevitably feel ahead of this week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Defensive tackle CJ West, out since September 23 with a bone chip in his knee , is one of the candidates to return from injured reserve once the team returns from its bye. West could return to the active roster, and Sebastian Valdez could head back to the practice squad. Valdez was promoted to the active roster to begin October . You run the risk of losing him to another team, but it’s a numbers game, and somebody will be out of a job once more bodies return from injury in the second half. The 49ers practice on Monday, so we could find out the roster move as soon as Monday morning.

full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers didn’t play this week, but still found a way to win. They can thank the Detroit Lions for that. San Francisco 49ers (6-1, strength of victory .427) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1, strength of victory .409) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-4) 5. Detroit Lions (5-2, 2-0 NFCN) 5. Chicago Bears (5-2, 0-2 NFCN) 7. Green Bay Packers (5-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 9. Los Angeles Rams (4-4) 10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5, win over ATL, 1-0 vs DAL+ARZ, 3-2 NFC) 11. Atlanta Falcons (3-5, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC record) 12. Arizona Cardinals (3-5, 1-0 vs DAL+ARZ, 2-4 NFC) 13. Dallas Cowboys (3-5, 0-2 vs TB+ARZ, loss to ARZ) 14. New Orleans Saints (2-5, 1-3 NFC) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (2-5, 1-4 NFC) Sunday Night Football 16. Washington Commanders (1-4-1) Sunday Night Football Explaining the cluster of NFC teams at 3-5 First, you get to one team per division, so the Falcons and Buccaneers are against each other. Tampa has a win over Atlanta, so they have the tiebreaker. Tampa vs. Arizona vs. Dallas is a head-to-head tiebreaker where Atlanta and Arizona move on since they both have wins over Dallas. The Bucs are 3-2 in the NFC vs. the Cardinals at 2-4, so Tampa is the 10 seed. Then the Falcons go into a three-way tiebreaker with the Cardinals and Cowboys. It goes straight to NFC record, where the Falcons are 3-3 and the Cardinals and Cowboys are 2-4. Atlanta is the 11 seed. The Arizona Cardinals beat the Cowboys, so they win the head-to-head tiebreaker in the two-way decision. Arizona is 12th, and the Cowboys are 13th.

title: Report: “No way” the Jets trade Garrett Wilson in 2026
summary: Well, the Garrett Wilson-to-49ers hope that a (very) few of you have can come to an end. Adam Schefter reported Saturday that a well-placed source said there’s “no way” the Jets trade Garrett Wilson: Maybe it’s surprising to some that Wilson won’t be moved. It’s not surprising that any chance the 49ers had for him […]
full_text: (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the Garrett Wilson-to-49ers hope that a (very) few of you have can come to an end. Adam Schefter reported Saturday that a well-placed source said there’s “no way” the Jets trade Garrett Wilson: One well-placed source told ESPN this weekend that there is "no way" the Jets will trade Garrett Wilson by the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline, despite any interest from other teams. pic.twitter.com/tzyCeBabNS — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 31, 2026 Maybe it’s surprising to some that Wilson won’t be moved. It’s not surprising that any chance the 49ers had for him is gone—I doubt they’d even do a trade for a wide receiver, but there’s a lot out there to suggest otherwise. The 49ers have a banged-up wide receiver room. Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans missed last week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons, and De’Zhaun Stribling has been on injured reserve since Week 1. The thing is, Samuel and Evans should be back after the bye (hopefully), and Stribling is back in December. So Wilson, if he was actually acquired, would come to San Francisco with no knowledge of the offense and have to produce. Something Brandin Cooks had to do weeks earlier. So the 49ers give up draft picks for a player whose cap number will climb past $35 million in 2028. Many of us hope DeForest Buckner finishes his career in San Francisco; that’s no way to do it with those salary cap hits. And let’s not forget players like Dominick Puni are eligible for an extension in 2027—we know how guards get poached from the 49ers, and Wilson coming to the 49ers would make the odds of that happening again more likely. From a financial and personnel perspective, it just doesn’t make sense to make a trade for Wilson. Yes, I say this crossing my fingers that the substation has moved on to other positions to injure. However, even if the 49ers manage to get a deal done, he’s still unfamiliar with the offense and has no time to build chemistry with Brock Purdy. Maybe he does it in a day? Maybe he takes until February? I don’t know. We don’t know who this source is: someone inside the Jets organization? Someone around the league? An agent? So we don’t know where the “no way” comes from. Whether the Jets have too high an asking price, are too dysfunctional to get it done in time, or no team wants to trade for that contract. Without context, we can only take this at face value, and “no way” means “no way” Now there is good in this for the 49ers. This also means some NFL squad in contention for an opening at productive wide receiver can’t get Wilson either. Which means he can’t be a problem for the 49ers defense later on. Wilson will stay with the New York Jets, and the Jets will…do Jets things.

title: Buccaneers Week 8 Top Performers vs. Atlanta Falcons
summary: Entering Week 7, the Buccaneers faced roughly a 1% chance to make the playoffs and needed to secure two straight wins against division opponents. Well, after steamrolling the Carolina Panthers last week, the Buccaneers did nearly the exact same to the Falcons in a 16-0 victory that was not as close as it appeared on […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Kenny Gainwell #1 and Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering Week 7, the Buccaneers faced roughly a 1% chance to make the playoffs and needed to secure two straight wins against division opponents. Well, after steamrolling the Carolina Panthers last week, the Buccaneers did nearly the exact same to the Falcons in a 16-0 victory that was not as close as it appeared on a rain-drenched afternoon in Tampa. Tampa became the first first team since 1974 to win without completing a pass — Baker Mayfield went 0 for 3 — and the first one to score double-digits in said type of win since 1945. This total absence of a pass game comes just one week after…largely not needing to throw the ball, as Mayfield went 7-of-11 for 64 yards and a touchdown. So that is fewer than 15 pass attempts and 75 yards in 8 quarters. In the year of our lord 2026. The Buccaneers have lived the old school way — opportunistic defense and a ground-shaking run game — and it’s worked to incredible effect. How well? Try 4 interceptions of Michael Penix Jr. and a franchise-record 324 yards rushing. It’s not going to sustain forever, as they’ll need to actually utilize the forward pass to keep pace with a dynamic Bears offense next week, but the team is fully back in the fight. Everyone involved deserves a lot of praise when so many close losses could’ve torpedoed the team’s confidence. Offensive Top Performer: RBs Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell The Bucs have become the NFL’s premier rushing attack over the last two weeks, and you need to give credit to Zac Robinson for not only leaning into it, but doing so in a very diverse way. He’s featured an eclectic mix of outside zone, inside zone, and gap blocking schemes, as well as different formations and wrinkles. All three tight ends, Cade Otton, Payne Durham, and Bauer Sharp, have absolutely feasted, as has the entire offensive line. Of course, the ones churning out the yards have been extremely effective as well. Bucky Irving set a career-high, slashing the Falcons for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries. He ripped off multiple explosives (including a 46-yard burst) and averaged a whopping 6.3 yards per carry. He’s led the league in rushing over the last 4 weeks and looks fully back to his rookie form. Bucky Irving TD! He's up to 169 yards! ATLvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PsIV3YPlxE — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 His running mate, Kenny Gainwell, closed out the game with aplomb. Handling a majority of the carries in the fourth quarter, Gainwell smashed Atlanta for 140 yards on 25 carries to completely erase any chances of a comeback. After a slow start, Gainwell is gelling now as RB2. Kenneth Gainwell living up to his last name ATLvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/O3GLOc23uJ — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 This rushing attack with regress to the mean at some point, but even then it’s clear they’ve established themselves as high-quality producers even without a consistent pass attack. The Bucs’ playoff hopes will depend on it. Defensive Top Performer: LB Alex Anzalone Make no mistake, Alex Anzalone has been a net negative for this defense all season. But still, it’s not fair to let that taint one game, and in this one game he delivered results. No. 34 recorded two huge interceptions within Penix’s first four passes, one of which being an athletic high-point grab that had me thinking it was 6-foot-7 Anthony Nelson (No. 94) making the jump to snag the throw. He then read Penix like a book in zone to secure another one that the offense unfortunately squandered via a fumble out of the end zone, but both early turnovers set a hugely positive tone. The Bucs proceeded to intercept Penix twice more, and it could’ve been higher. They had the third-year passer (8-of-24, 125 yards) in complete hell all afternoon long. Alex Anzalone INT for the Bucs! ATLvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9XQl4g5mcJ — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Parrish built on his NFL lead in passes defensed while snagging his second interception of the season, and McCollum continued his excellent start with another pick as well. Add in Keionte Scott and Tykee Smith making a couple standout plays in their own right, and the secondary continues to be excellent. The pass rush wasn’t as active this week, more so due to lack of opportunities, but still notably affected plays more than once, including a couple standout rushes from rookie Rueben Bain. It will be fascinating to see how this defense handles the best offense they’ve faced all year in the Chicago Bears. It’s prime opportunity to assert themselves as the elite unit they’ve been playing like. WIDE OPEN JACOB PARRISH ‼️ 📺: #ATLvsTB on FOX pic.twitter.com/LcZ3BpvEul — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 1, 2026 Special Teams Top Performer: K Chase McLaughlin Money McLaughlin is inevitable. Shortly after Falcons kicker Nick Folk, a former Buccaneer from a lifetime ago, completely shanked his only attempt of the day, McLaughlin responded with an effortless 46-yard make. He then hit two more to build a lead on afternoon where yards and points were extremely hard to come by. Again, extension for him now, Jason Licht. Chase McLaughlin converts from 42 yards out to add to Tampa Bay's lead, 9-0. McLaughlin's 73 kicking points this season leads all kickers. — Buccaneers Communications (@BuccaneersComms) November 1, 2026 And some credit must be given to punter Riley Dixon, who has been mostly bad this season but loosed some huge punts later in the game (downed at the 7- and 2-yard lines) to help maintain the pivotal field position.

title: Week 8 Game Recap: Buccaneers run game does it again in run-first shutout victory
summary: Coming off of a running bonanza against Carolina for their second win of the season, week eight was set to feature more running, a downpour, and no Baker Mayfield glove. Would a second consecutive game of relentless running by the Buccaneers’ offense be enough for the Buccaneers to climb out of their early season hole […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) hands the ball to running back Bucky Irving (7) against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Coming off of a running bonanza against Carolina for their second win of the season, week eight was set to feature more running, a downpour, and no Baker Mayfield glove. Would a second consecutive game of relentless running by the Buccaneers’ offense be enough for the Buccaneers to climb out of their early season hole and to the top of the NFC South? First Quarter: It was Todd Bowles’ defense up first on Sunday. Battling on a water-logged field, Tampa’s strongest unit took the field and bent a bit, however, there was no break. The Falcons pushed into Tampa territory before ultimately needing to settle for a long field goal attempt. Weather conditions not favoring Nick Folk, the kick was missed and missed badly. Converting turnovers into points or this case missed field goals into points gave Tampa the first lead of the day. 3-0, Buccaneers. The response from the Falcons was quite mild, an interception by Alex Anzalone. Penix looking for Drake London on a slant, found Anzalone for his second interception of the season. Turnovers into points would fail Tampa on their next drive— Bucky Ivring, breaking into space on a broken play, was met by Jessie Bates at the goal line for a 2023 Antoine Winfield Jr.-esque forced fumble stripping the ball out at the goal line which rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Rest assured, Tampa’s defense understood the assignment. Back on the field, following an Alex Anzalone pick that didn’t result into points, fans watched Michael Penix drop back and throw another Alex Anzalone interception— His second of the day and third of the season. One more field goal off of an Alex Anzalone interception and the Buccaneers expanded their lead. 6-0, Tampa Bay. Second Quarter: The difference between the start of the game’s first quarter and its second? Not much. More rain and more Micheal Penix interceptions. For the start of quarter number two, Penix, under pressure from Rueben Bain Jr., decided to spread the wealth tossing a fourth down interception to Jacob Parrish. Back on the field after another turnover, Tampa Bay’s offense stayed consistent. Run, run, run, and run. The Buccaneers’ only pass attempt of the drive would actually wind up as a rush attempt as well after Baker Mayfield scooped up his third fumble of the day and scurried forward for a short gain. Tampa’s first drive of the second quarter ended with 4:04 left in the half and three more points on the scoreboard. 9-0, Buccaneers. The Bucs and Falcons would each exchange run-first, slow-paced, non-scoring drive to close out half number one and head to the intermission— The only first half since 1978 to feature less than three completed passes. Third Quarter: With zero first half completions and a two-score lead, Baker Mayfield was under center at the 30 yard line to start the third quarter— Run, run, third down drop, and a punt. Tampa Bay, still repping their signature no completion streak, sent their defense back out onto the field for another three-and-out stop. The third quarter was nothing but rain and punts until the final five minutes. Bucky Irving ripped through Atlanta’s defense for a 45 yard rush— Two plays later, it was Kenny Gainwell’s turn. Gainwell, with his second break away run in as many weeks, put the Buccaneers inside the 10 yard line. It would be another two plays until Bucky Irving put the Bucs inside the end zone. 16-0, Tampa Bay. Fourth Quarter: The Falcons seized some bits of momentum in the waning moments of the third quarter. With the final quarter beginning at the Tampa Bay 30 yard line and an Atlanta decision. Neglecting a short field goal the Falcons opted for a forth down attempted and converted with a Michael Penix tush push. Unfortunately for Falcons’ fans, the team would ask Penix to throw next and he would once again throw to a Tampa Bay defender. Penix’s fourth interception would be tossed to Zyon McCollum. Atlanta’s next bite at the apple would be from their 12 yard with just over seven minutes to go— Three-and-out. Tampa’s response— Three-and-out. Backed up from their own two, Michael Penix found Atlanta’s biggest spark of the day— Jahan Dotson for 76 yards. Dotson’s catch and run was the only chink Todd Bowles’ armor, the Falcons’ drive was immediately stalled afterwards and the Buccaneers salted away the rest of the clock and the game. Tampa Bay, despite their 0-4 start, is 3-5 and very much in contention of the NFC South.

full_text: The Daily Slop – 2 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Fans are pumped. pic.twitter.com/fasK0xkzzS — George Carmi (@Gcarmi21) November 2, 2026 Articles Commanders.com Instant Analysis: Rocky start, strong finish, key NFC East win The Commanders (2-4-1) emphasized the importance of being competitive for all four quarters coming out of their bye week. They still have some work to do there; head coach Dan Quinn said he thought they played well in three. They were still plagued by pre-snap penalties — they committed four fouls in their first nine plays — and had a fumble and a missed field goal on their opening two drives. Once the Commanders started to pick up steam, however, it was difficult for the Eagles to slow them down. They outgained the Eagles 318-201 for the rest of the night, recording 16 first downs and averaging nearly six yards per play. “After that TD drive [from the Eagles], I thought, ‘Okay, that’s it. There we are,'” head coach Dan Quinn said after the game. It still was not pretty; the Commanders had to send Drew Stevens out to kick four field goals — an issue Quinn said must be cleaned up — but their defense bought them time by putting consistent pressure on Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee and the rest of Philadelphia’s offense. The Commanders generated pressure on 46.5% of dropbacks — a season high, according to NFL+. It led to five sacks from the unit, one of which resulted in a fumble and recovery deep in Eagles territory. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN Can this win ignite a turnaround for Washington? The Commanders needed this win if just to settle a nervous building, knowing they couldn’t afford to lose to a wounded Eagles team at home. But if the Commanders beat the Rams at home next week, then they can talk about turnarounds. Washington committed nine penalties, one of which wiped out an interception deep in Philadelphia territory and continued a season-long theme. Quarterback Jayden Daniels wasn’t that sharp, but he made big plays and averaged 13.5 yards per completion against a defense that was healthier than it has been. Daniels got his first win since Oct. 5, 2025, and Washington’s defense hounded Tanner McKee all night and held Philly to 3.4 yards per play until late completions boosted that average to 3.9. Maybe this win doesn’t represent a turnaround, but the Commanders did what was necessary. Trend to watch: With Terry McLaurin done for the season, Washington needs other receivers to help more. Sunday night, Treylon Burks, who is taking over for McLaurin at the X spot, caught three passes for 81 yards, including a 53-yarder. Rookie slot receiver Antonio Williams caught a career-best five passes for 54 yards, including a 30-yard grab. Both receivers set up field goals with their long catches. — John Keim To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Instant Reaction: Depleted Front Delivers the Biggest Answer Against Eagles The penalties didn’t disappear after the bye , but Washington’s pass rush took over, and Rachaad White finished the job on the ground. With McLaurin out and three defensive tackles unavailable , Washington needed contributions from the players taking on more work. Antonio Williams got involved early , Charles Omenihu made his return count, and Stevens answered his opening miss with four straight makes. Those contributions helped the Commanders overcome another night of costly mistakes and keep their season alive. Washington’s defensive front finished this game. Dorance Armstrong was still making plays against the run, and Odafe Oweh beat Jordan Mailata off the edge for a late sack. A season-high five sacks is the production Washington has needed from this group; Washington did it without Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, and Jer’Zhan Newton, while holding Saquon Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries. K’Lavon Chaisson’s late sack helped put Philadelphia in a desperate situation, and Rasul Douglas took advantage when McKee floated a ball up for grabs. Chaisson’s penalties were costly, but he also helped Washington close this game. After having an earlier interception erased by a flag, the defense made this takeaway count. Washington Post (paywall) Commanders take care of business against flailing Eagles in prime time For the Eagles (2-6), it was their sixth loss in a row. They were without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, No. 1 wide receiver DeVonta Smith and a bevy of other core players because of various injuries. While Philadelphia had a better record before kickoff — and Washington has a lengthy injury report of its own — the Commanders were the superior team on paper. Daniels started to get groove back in the second quarter. He completed 7 of 10 passes for 70 yards and one touchdown in the period. Despite being shorthanded, the defensive line thrived. It generated consistent pressure on Philadelphia quarterback Tanner McKee and sacked him five times. While it must be noted that Barkley was playing through injury, Washington still deserves credit for limiting the Eagles to 3.1 yards per carry. With the D-line rolling, the secondary locked down Philadelphia’s passing attack. McKee only passed for 212 yards and threw an interception. It was easily the best performance of the season for defensive coordinator Daronte Jones’s group. The defense held the Eagles scoreless for eight consecutive possessions, forced two turnovers and was instrumental in the Commanders’ comeback. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Commanders hand Eagles sixth straight loss. Can Washington build off this win? The Commanders didn’t seek outside help after losing Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season because of a patellar tendon injury. They relied on their in-house talent and, for the most part, their prudence paid off. Early mistakes by Washington’s pass catchers — a dropped pass, a fumble — turned into a standout performance from the Commanders’ skill players. Tight end Chig Okonkwo, who earlier fumbled after a short catch deep in Philadelphia’s territory, had perhaps the catch of the year on a third-and-6 in the third quarter. Receiver Treylon Burks led the way with 81 receiving yards on three catches, veteran Stefon Diggs caught the team’s lone passing touchdown and rookie wideout Antonio Williams had five catches for 54 yards. All had grabs that could’ve been incompletions To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) The Commanders, after an awful start, shut down Philly’s offense and won a critical divisional game Quinn got the complementary football he constantly talks about — good plays by the defense feeding into scoring drives by the offense. Luke McCaffrey had his best night of the season returning kicks. Drew Stevens nailed a huge 56-yard field goal late in the first quarter to get the Commanders on the board. If he’d missed, the Eagles would have taken over near midfield, ready to add to their lead. And Daniels came back from a big hit by Eagles linebacker Nolan Smith late in the first half that knocked the wind out of him. In the second half, he hit tight end Chig Okonkwo for 21 yards on a great catch by Okonkwo, found Treylon Burks on a double-move for a 53-yard strike that set up another Stevens field goal, and got Antonio Williams on a 30-yard vertical route in the…

title: How Jayden Daniels sideline speech impacted Commanders win over Eagles
summary: The Commanders offense did not start Sunday’s game well, by the eye test or any proven metric. Washington’s attack, point blank and pulling no punches, was awful.  They went just 18 yards on seven plays following an excellent Luke McCaffrey opening return, and then missed a field goal largely due to consecutive false starts taking […]
full_text: The Commanders offense did not start Sunday’s game well, by the eye test or any proven metric. Washington’s attack, point blank and pulling no punches, was awful. They went just 18 yards on seven plays following an excellent Luke McCaffrey opening return, and then missed a field goal largely due to consecutive false starts taking a third-and-1 to a third-and-11 . The second series went three-and-out. The third started with two more penalties, an ineligible man downfield and a false start. Daniels threw a rocket to Chig Okonkwo to make up some ground, who caught it in stride and then coughed it up. Daniels had seen enough. The normally mild-mannered and even-keeled quarterback pulled his offense together after three series, four penalties and zero points. The Commanders were down 10. Daniels was not thrilled. He responded in a way that was both atypical and justifiable. Jayden Daniels having words with the Commanders’ offense after Chig Okonkwo fumbled and set the Eagles up inside the 30-yard line. Before that play, Washington received ineligible man downfield and false start penalties. Not a strong start. pic.twitter.com/g03T7PjQHW — Jake Kauderer (@jakekauderer) November 2, 2026 Daniels had something to say. And he was forceful about it. “Honestly, it was complete B.S. how we started and what we were doing,” Daniels said in his postgame presser . “We had a promising drive the first drive and then had mental lapses like penalties and stuff like that. And then on the second drive, we get behind the sticks with a lot of pre-snap penalties and then a fumble. “At that point, it just wasn’t our brand of football we as players want to showcase. It was at that point, you kind of just get frustrated and you have to speak your mind. That’s what I did, and just helped snap everyone back into place.” Jayden Daniels spoke to the team after the "Complete BS" start in the 1st quarter…it worked! pic.twitter.com/vb6NjVAKtj — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) November 2, 2026 The discussion worked. The Commanders rattled off 27 unanswered points to win a crucial game against the Eagles on Sunday night at Northwest Stadium that ended 27-10. Washington scored on six of the next eight drives after that sideline speech – there were still too many field goals in that stretch – and the defense was essential to closing this vital victory out. Also, it should be noted that the Commanders had just two penalties (both false starts) the rest of the way. That sideline talk helped the Commanders get right. “He brought the offense up and was getting us mentally reset, ‘Hey, we know if we don’t stop ourselves, we can score points,'” said veteran running back Austin Ekeler, via ESPN reporter John Keim, who played with Daniels when he was a rookie and for a short time last year “It’s hard being a leader in this league, especially at quarterback. You have a lot on your plate. The older you get, the more you understand your role, so it’s cool to see him bring us up like that.” Daniels was frustrated most by the unforced miscues. The Commanders were frequently beating themselves early on and, considering the stakes, that was untenable. The third-year quarterback, without getting into specifics (or expletives), explained what he said to the group in his postgame press conference. “We were having miscommunication on a number of different things, so it was frustrating,” Daniels told on-site reporters. “I was telling everybody, in a PG way, to lock in, focus and overcommunicate. It doesn’t matter if they know the snap count or whatever, just make sure everyone knows that we don’t have those mental lapses.” Daniels wasn’t just demanding better from others. He knew he had to tighten things up. He did. He was 4-for-11 for 26 yards in the first quarter. He was 12-for-18 for 191 yards and a touchdown after that. The penalties went down and production went up. Was that all due to one sideline talking to? Certainly not. Football games aren’t fairy tales. This isn’t Charles S. Dutton in Rudy . But the fact Daniels gathered everyone and made such an impassioned speech, and it wasn’t regular or lip service, clearly had a positive impact on the team as it surged ahead and clearly contributed to Sunday’s outcome. “What I see a lot from him is the poise,” Quinn said. “The accuracy and the toughness – he took a real shot towards the end of the first half. To see him go make a bunch of plays was a real step. Offensively, I thought we started off slow, but at the end of the first half and into the second I thought we were in control.” Let’s be real here. How impactful was Jayden Daniels’ speech? And, why do you think the Commanders turned things around in Week 8? Let us know in the comments blow:
