 Oct. 30: Packers' ground game cause for concern 
 

 By Adam Rank 

 Jordan Love throws multiple touchdown passes. Matthew Golden looks good. I mean, Christian Watson left and arrived back at Lambeau Field from an ambulance in a move that would make Triple H say, "no way this is real." And yet, I get a note from my editor (a Packers fan, mind you) complaining about the (lack of a) Green Bay Packers running game. 

 I mean, the Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series , but we need to focus on the Packers' rushing attack? Well, I guess that is the best place to start.

 

 The Packers won the game despite rushing for just 66 yards . They have been held to fewer than 90 rushing yards in all eight games, the club's longest streak in the Super Bowl era. The Packers' 485 rushing yards are the fewest by any team through eight games since the 2019 Bengals. I mean, what in the name of Eddie Lee Ivery is going on here?

 The short answer is the offensive line is bad. The playcalling is bad. I mean, you think the guy who favored Dion Lewis over Derrick Henry when he was offensive coordinator in Tennessee  was ever going to have a solid running game in Green Bay? It's just the facts.

 And it's not going to get much easier in the coming weeks, either. The New England Patriots , Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Rams aren't great matchups. It's not until the New Orleans Saints in Week 13 that the schedule softens for Josh Jacobs . If you kept him on your roster all this time, you're likely going to be compelled to start him, but the matchups aren't ideal.

 Some other notes from Thursday night: 

 

 
 Love has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all eight games this season, but this was his first game of the season with three touchdown passes. He's a set-and-forget quarterback moving forward. It is wild to think he wasn't drafted as a QB1 this year. 
 Watson is nearing ace territory this season. He recorded his 12th reception of 20-plus yards, second in the league behind  Jaxon Smith-Njigba . 
 Golden is also a must-start, but he registered two drops Thursday. Love has seen 20 drops by his receivers this season. I feel like that total would double if you counted the number of interceptions that are dropped. Or maybe it just seems that way to me, a Bears supporter. 
 Is the " Bryce Young as a QB1" era over already? Well, for starters, the Carolina Panthers need to do a better job of protecting him. He was hit. A lot. I'm not rushing him back into my lineup next week against the Denver Broncos . You might want to take a look at the waiver wire right now for a streamable option if Young is your only quarterback. Kyler Murray against the Buffalo Bills next week could do the trick. 
 Chuba Hubbard was good, however. He scored a touchdown, rushed for 81 yards and caught seven balls for 38 more yards. Again, playing the Bills next week makes him a prime RB1. 
 

 

 Oct. 29: Week 8 streaming guide 
 

 By Michael F. Florio 

 Kyler Murray has used his legs more lately, with 51 and 34 rushing yards in his past two games. This week, he gets the Detroit Lions , who have allowed the most pass yards per game, most fantasy PPG to QBs and second-most passing touchdowns. Every QB but one who faced them has finished in the top eight and scored at least 21 fantasy points. Plus, if you stream him this week you can use him again next week against the Buffalo Bills .

 Jacoby Brissett is in play due to the matchup. He faces the Dallas Cowboys , who have allowed the sixth-most fantasy PPG and eighth-most passing touchdowns to QBs. Plus, the Arizona Cardinals likely will be trailing, which means added volume.

 Deeper QB plays: 

 
 Malik Willis is coming off his two best fantasy games of the season and has been running effectively. 
 Geno Smith gets a revenge game against the Las Vegas Raiders , who have allowed the sixth-most fantasy PPG and second-most passing touchdowns to QBs. 
 Michael Penix Jr . has thrown three touchdown passes in two straight games and faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , who are much easier to throw on than run against. 
 Tanner McKee faces the Washington Commanders , who are top five in passing yards per game and touchdowns allowed to quarterbacks. Overall, they have allowed the second-most fantasy PPG to the position. 
 
 Blake Corum played 43% of the snaps with 18 touches last week. He went for 101 yards and a touchdown, while having two called back due to penalty. He has picked up explosive runs at the seventh-highest rate in the NFL and faces the Los Angeles Chargers , who give them up at the eighth-highest rate. The Chargers are also top seven in rushing yards allowed per game and touchdowns allowed to RBs.

 Rhamondre Stevenson has 24 targets on the season, which by far leads the New England Patriots ' backfield. That is big this week as the Miami Dolphins are top 10 in catches and receiving yards allowed to backs. In total, they have allowed the third-most fantasy PPG to RBs.

 Jonah Coleman returned last week and led the Denver Broncos backs in snaps (50%), carries (nine) and rushing yards (54). He is by far their most explosive runner and I believe is their best dual-threat back as well. Even in a tough matchup, he is in play as a flex option.

 Rachaad White played just under 70% of the snaps in his first game without Jacory Croskey-Merritt . Volume wins out here, and the Eagles have allowed 275 rushing yards and two touchdowns to opponents' RB1 in the past two weeks.

 Carnell Tate is in play as long as he suits up. He has had at least a 25% target rate in five of his past six games. He has the fourth-highest target share against man coverage, which the Bengals play at an above-average rate. Tate, who has shown to have a safe floor, could show his upside this week as well.

 Keenan Allen has nine or more targets in three of four games. That has led to him scoring 16-plus fantasy points in two of those games. Now he faces the Jacksonville Jaguars , who allow in the top five in most yards and fantasy points per game to opposing WRs. The Indianapolis Colts will likely be in catch-up mode, so expect volume to go Allen's way.

 Ja'Kobi Lane and Rashod Bateman are in play due to the matchup against the Bills. Buffalo has allowed the most fantasy PPG and touchdowns to wide receivers this season. The two have split targets against zone coverage, which the Bills play 81% of the time. Lane is the preferred option, but Bateman brings upside this week.

 Chig Okonkwo saw a team-high seven targets in the Commanders' last game, and he turned them into seven catches for 69 yards. I expect him to be a top-two target moving forward for the Commanders. The volume has him in play as a streaming option.

 T.J. Hockenson is in play due to the matchup against the Lions. Detroit has allowed the most yards, touchdowns and fantasy PPG to tight ends. Plus, the Minnesota Vikings may have to put up more points than normal in this one.

title: Larry Csonka, member of undefeated '72 Dolphins, celebrates Vikings' first loss
summary: The Minnesota Vikings' loss Sunday ensured that another NFL season will pass without an undefeated team.
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings ' 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday ensured that another NFL season will pass without an undefeated team. It prompted celebration from one Pro Football Hall of Famer: Larry Csonka, a member of the 1972 Miami Dolphins .

 

 The Vikings entered Week 8 with a 6-0 record as the last unbeaten team. Their loss continues the Dolphins' 54-year streak as the only team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to complete a regular season and postseason undefeated. The Dolphins went 17-0 in the 1972 season en route to a Super Bowl VII win.

 Csonka commemorated the feat on social media. He shared an image of himself raising a glass with a cigar in hand to celebrate another year that the Dolphins' undefeated record stands alone. Csonka rocked his Super Bowl ring, too.

 

 The fullback posted a similar photo in 2024 when the Kansas City Chiefs ' undefeated season ended with a loss in Week 11.

 Csonka had a key role in Miami's invincible campaign. He led the team in rushing with 1,117 yards and scored six touchdowns, second most on the Dolphins. Csonka had 119 yards on the ground in Super Bowl VII, including a 49-yard scamper.

 The closest any team came to taking down the Dolphins' record was in the 2007 campaign when the New England Patriots entered Super Bowl XLII at 18-0 but were upset by the New York Giants .

 Arguably the league's most unbreakable record extended into one more campaign -- and Csonka made sure to acknowledge it.

title: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
summary: The Pittsburgh passer is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
full_text:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

 In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots . In Week 6 of 2026, he moved into a third-place tie with Peyton Manning with 539.

 "Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

 

 Rodgers supplanted Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025. But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

 Among the milestones for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 8 he has appeared in 295), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 8, he needs 1,855 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards . 

 This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

 
 Weeks: 
 Preseason | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 
 Remaining schedule 

 
 

 

 
 Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INT, 0 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

 

 Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

 
 

 Week 1:  Steelers 20, Falcons 13 
 Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard 
 Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth  for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the  Green Bay Packers , per ESPN Research.

 After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

 "No, keep doing it," Rodgers said, urging his coach to keep calling passes. "Keep doing it."

 And although Rodgers and the Steelers got the win, the quarterback struggled under the pressure from the Falcons' front. He completed 3 of 12 attempts under pressure and was sacked twice. And continuing the trend from last season, Rodgers was also 3-of-12 on throws of 15 or more air yards. Some of those incompletions, though, were the result of drops by his receivers.

 

 "I liked the plan from Mike," Rodgers said. "I liked the playcalling. We took some shots. I felt like we had really close to having one of those really good games. If we come down with a couple of those, it obviously looks a little different on the scoreboard and stat sheet and stuff, but love my guys, love  DK [Metcalf] .

 

 

 Week 2: Patriots 20, Steelers 3 
 Rodgers' stat line: 187 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT, 4 sacks, 1 rush for 5 yards 
 Rodgers set two personal Steelers milestones in the team's Week 2 loss -- and not in a good way. Rodgers was off target on 26% of his throws (nine attempts) in the loss, his worst as a Steeler. The Patriots frustrated Rodgers with heavy pressures and blitzed on 19 of 44 dropbacks (43%), the second-highest rate he has faced with Pittsburgh. Against the blitz, he was 8-of-17 for 42 yards with two sacks and an interception. And he had his first interception against the blitz as a member of the Steelers.

 

 "It's frustrating, for sure," Rodgers said of not getting into the end zone at New England on Sunday. "The defense has been playing great. They've been holding [opponents to] 13 points a game in two games, and offensively I think we're averaging like eight points a game. That's not winning football."

 

 

 Week 3: Steelers 30, Bengals 27 
 Rodgers' stat line: 292 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for 10 yards 
 It turns out Rodgers still has plenty left in the tank. A week after one of his worst performances as a Steeler, Rodgers bounced back with three passing touchdowns to help the offense put up a season-best 30 points and 411 yards in the win against the Cincinnati Bengals . Rodgers aired it out in the first quarter with two touchdown throws and 143 passing yards -- the most he has thrown in the first quarter since Week 6 of 2018 against the 49ers (170). Each of his touchdown passes traveled at least 20 air yards, marking his first time with multiple touchdowns of 20-plus air yards since he joined the Steelers. Entering Sunday's game, Rodgers was 0-of-9 on pass attempts of 20-plus air yards.

 "We definitely needed it because it was just uncharacteristic of us," Steelers wide receiver Ben Skowronek said of the offense's bounce-back performance. "Throughout camp, we felt really confident in what we were doing, moving the ball. And the first two weeks we just weren't us. So credit to the coaching staff, the guys in the building, we locked in this week and we knew we had to have it. We knew we could do it."

 

 After two weeks without much movement in the record books, Rodgers is starting to make some headway. Sunday's win marked the 165th of his career, tying him with Ben Roethlisberger for fifth most by a starting quarterback since positions were first tracked in 1950. With his first-quarter 38-yard touchdown throw to Roman Wilson , Rodgers also recorded his 233rd career game with at least one passing touchdown, tying Peyton Manning for the fourth most such games in NFL history.

 

 

 Week 4: Browns 27, Steelers 24 
 Rodgers' stat line: 299 yards, 3 TDs, 2 INTs, 5 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Rodgers spent a lot of time on the turf at Huntington Bank Field in what's scheduled to be his final Thursday night game (barring a late-season flex). Rodgers took 10 quarterback hits thanks to Cleveland's aggressive game plan, protection breakdowns and the quarterback's decisions to hold on to the ball as he looked for his pass catchers to get open against man coverage.

 

 All five of the sacks against Rodgers came as he faced man coverage, and on the season, he has been sacked an NFL-worst 12 times when facing man coverage -- seven more than any other quarterback. And while the offense largely stagnated through the second and third quarters, it came alive in the fourth as Rodgers aired it out with 43-, 28- and 22-yard completions to wide receiver DK Metcalf and a 21-yard touchdown throw threaded to Darnell Washington .

 Rodgers even tied the score at 24 with a quarterback sneak for a successful two-point conversion with less than two minutes to go.

 "I felt like there was no chance they'd be expecting that," Rodgers said. "So I just told them in the huddle, if I can this one, I'm going to sneak it.'"

 

 With the loss, Rodgers still has 13 wins on Thursdays and remains tied with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott for second most all time.

 

 

 Week 5: Steelers 34, Colts 22 
 Rodgers' stat line: 235 yards, 3 TDs, 1 sack, 1 rush for 6 yards

title: Can Seahawks' Rashid Shaheed become a complementary WR to Jaxon Smith-Njigba?
summary: Shaheed was a big part of the Seahawks' Super Bowl run as a returner and earned a new three-year contract. But he has been quiet as a receiver since his trade to Seattle.
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. -- When the Seattle Seahawks hosted the  San Francisco 49ers  in the divisional round of last season's playoffs, smoke from pregame introductions had not yet dissipated when Rashid Shaheed sent Lumen Field into a stadium-rattling frenzy.

 His 95-yard return for a touchdown on the opening kickoff set in motion a 41-6 Seahawks rout and provided one of the most indelible moments of their run to Super Bowl LX . It was Shaheed's third score on special teams since he'd arrived in a midseason trade, a move that would prove critical to Seattle claiming the second Vince Lombardi Trophy in franchise history.

 As a return man, Shaheed has been everything the Seahawks (4-3) hoped he'd be when they acquired him from the New Orleans Saints  and re-signed him in March to a three-year, $51 million deal .

 But as a wide receiver, he has not.

 Shaheed -- who has been ruled out (knee) of Monday's game against the 5-2  Chicago Bears  (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN) -- has 16 catches on 30 targets for 163 yards in seven games this season. He has one rushing touchdown, which is his only score from scrimmage since the Seahawks gave up 2026 fourth- and fifth-round picks to get him on Nov. 4 last year.

 The speedy receiver remains an underutilized target who rookie offensive coordinator Brian Fleury -- like his veteran predecessor, Klint Kubiak -- has yet to unlock. Because of it, the Seahawks are still waiting for someone to emerge as a secondary receiving threat to Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who continues to carry their passing game at a historic rate.

 

 "I think there's more there," coach Mike Macdonald said of Shaheed's production. "It's not for a lack of effort or a lack of trying. I think that's part of our process of keeping the ball distributed and finding better ways to get him the ball that might be more in his sweet spot."

 When the Seahawks re-signed Shaheed after he tested free agency, it was a clear sign that they expected him to produce more offensively than he did after his arrival in Week 10 of last season, when his biggest contributions came on special teams.

 Including playoffs, Shaheed totaled 352 scrimmage yards and no touchdowns on 29 touches over 12 games as the third receiver behind Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp in Seattle's run-heavy offense. Those numbers were especially underwhelming given his preexisting knowledge of Seattle's playbook, as Kubiak was New Orleans' coordinator in 2024. His per-game average of 29.3 yards with Seattle was significantly less than his average of just under 52 scrimmage yards over 3½ seasons with the Saints, who signed him as an undrafted free agent in 2022.

 So far this season, Shaheed's 28.9 scrimmage yards per game are a hair under his post-trade average last season. His lone touchdown came in a win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4, when he lined up in the backfield, took a pitch and found the end zone from 28 yards out. It was part of a package that Fleury had installed over the offseason, reminiscent of how the 49ers often used  Deebo Samuel Sr . as a running back during the coordinator's time on San Francisco's coaching staff.

 When rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price landed on injured reserve a day earlier, Fleury broke the play out against the Chargers in an attempt to inject some speed into Seattle's backfield. Shaheed gained 5 yards on another carry in that game.

 The Seahawks haven't gone back to it since, though Fleury says those plays have been in the game plans and won't be abandoned once Price and Zach Charbonnet return to Seattle's backfield. Shaheed's only carry over the past three games came on an end-around that resulted in a lost fumble in Seattle's overtime loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 6.

 

 "It's opponent-based on how we see them pursuing to fast-flow plays, what the blocking schemes are to get him out on the perimeter and in space and be able to read it like a punt returner," Fleury said of Shaheed, whose career average of 12.9 yards per punt return is third best in NFL history.

 Shaheed's only official drop this season came on a scramble throw 20 yards down field. He nearly made a diving catch for 33 yards on a go route in the Denver game, too, but couldn't secure the ball as he hit the ground. That continued a head-scratching trend.

 One of the NFL's best deep threats during his time in New Orleans, Shaheed has not been nearly as impactful in that regard for Seattle. In 19 games with the Seahawks, he has two catches on balls thrown at least 25 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. He had 21 such catches -- 10 of which resulted in touchdowns -- in 42 games with the Saints, which was tied for the league's third-highest per-game average in that span.

 The drop-off is partly explained by fewer opportunities, as Shaheed averaged over a target per game on deep throws with New Orleans compared to 0.6 such targets per game with Seattle. His timing with quarterback Sam Darnold is another factor. Even on their two deep connections -- a 51-yarder in the NFC Championship Game and a 42-yarder against Denver -- Shaheed had to break his stride enough for the defensive back to prevent any yards after the catch.

 "It's going to happen at some point," Darnold said of Shaheed becoming more of a factor on deep throws. "He does such a good job with the intermediate routes and the shorter routes as well, being able to catch and knife and get up the field in a hurry, which also presents a problem to the defense. I think it could be a coincidence.

 

 "But at the same time, even that deep ball in Denver, I should have put the ball out there a little bit further for him to go catch. He even had a chance at a go that I overthrew in Denver as well. So there's some opportunities there that I've missed as a quarterback."

 Neither Darnold nor Drew Lock -- who filled in for most of the first two games -- have struggled to connect with Smith-Njigba. The reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns, which puts him on pace to become the first player in league history to top 2,000 receiving yards in a season.

 Just as eye-popping is how much of the Seahawks' passing game the production represents. Smith-Njigba has 53.9% of their receiving yards. According to the Elias Sports Bureau, that's the second-highest percentage of a team's receiving yards through seven games in the past 75 seasons. (Lance Alworth had 54.6% for the Chargers in 1965.)

 In 2025, Smith-Njiba's 35.9% team target share was the highest the NFL has seen since 2012. With 78 targets so far this season, his target share of 36.6% again tops the league by a wide margin. If he leads the Seahawks in receiving yards against Chicago, it'll be the 13th consecutive regular-season game he has done so. Per Elias, that would be tied for the longest streak in NFL history.

 Fleury has made no secret of his desire for the ball to be spread around more.

 "It's becoming more and more obvious the way that teams are trying to take away Jax," he said. "So being a little bit more deliberate and not just allowing them to do that and giving the other guys an opportunity to take advantage of some of the matchups that they're being given."

 During the mini-bye that followed the Thursday night Denver game in Week 6, Macdonald and Fleury came to the realization that they needed to narrow their focus offensively. The result was a pared-down game plan that leaned into their strengths and, as players put it, allowed them to play more freely in their 20-3 win over the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs .

 

 Seattle's offensive line, coming off its best performance of the season, got a significant upgrade this week with the trade for All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson . That addition plus the impending returns of Price and Charbonnet give the Seahawks a chance to build a strong run game that could take pressure off Darnold, who has thrown eight interceptions in the past five games.
